abstract: The Internet of drones (IoD) has emeregd as a hot topic in the technology industry and is deemed important and useful to several applications and fields where we see dozens of drones deployed to achieve a particular mission. The huge benefits sometimes can be a mask for some of the crucial issues that can affect this field of the UAVs crucially and we are talking about security and privacy. The internet of drones comes to connect between drones making them smart but leaving an open door for intruders to exploit. This paper will uphold a model that utilizes the wonders of deep learning to improve it greatly. In this proposed model, a LSTM algorithm is applied to further enhance the capability and reliability of the deep learning model. Using evaluation factors such as accuracy, precision, and etc. we can see that our model outperforms other ML algorithms and classifiers while having a low training time which showcases the efficiency of LSTM-based deep learning model.

articleTitle: The smart analysis of energy optimization for sensor nodes in Ad-Hoc networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks have become increasingly common in various fields, including environmental monitoring, commercial automation, and healthcare. Sensor nodes in those networks are regularly powered through constrained energy resources, leading to the need for power optimization techniques. Advert-hoc networks, which are self-organizing networks without a hard and fast infrastructure, are mainly at risk of electricity constraints because of the sporadic nature of the verbal exchange between nodes. In this project, we propose a clever analysis technique for electricity optimization in sensor nodes in ad hoc networks. Our technique entails using intelligent algorithms and gadgetmastering techniques to analyze the power intake patterns of sensor nodes and make dynamic changes to their operations. This permits the optimization of energy utilization while assembling the community’s preferred targets. Through vast simulations, we show the effectiveness of our proposed approach in prolonging the community lifetime and improving the general electricity efficiency of sensor nodes in ad hoc networks. Moreover, our clever evaluation method permits flexibility and adaptability to changing environments, making it suitable for various packages.

articleTitle: Optimizing Air Quality Monitoring in Educational Institutes: A Protocol-Centric Approach for Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Monitoring air quality in educational institutions, especially in enclosed classrooms where student numbers significantly impact air quality, is vital. While hardware implementation has been proposed to enhance classroom productivity, this study introduces a protocol-centric approach to improve efficiency. Optimizing process of air quality monitoring in educational institutions is the focus, emphasizing the importance of efficient and reliable communication. Implementing Classroom Air Quality Monitoring systems requires careful consideration of communication protocols. However, selecting the most efficient protocol is challenging, particularly in educational institutes spanning $100 \times 100$ meters and six floors. This study serves as the focal point for experimentation and analysis in protocol selection. Utilizing the Three-Stage communication model, sensor nodes are deployed to monitor CO 2, Temperature, and Humidity across multiple classroom floors. Each floor employs one, edge node within 10 meters, bolstering data transmission to the central fog node. The fog node aggregates data from all edge nodes, accessible via the Internet. Sensor nodes operate on batteries, while edge and fog nodes are mains powered. After analyzing existing protocols, ZigBee emerges as the optimal choice for communication between battery-operated sensor nodes and mains-powered edge nodes. Integrated with ZigBee, MQTT enables efficient data transfer and scalability. This study prioritizes low power consumption and protocol reliability.

articleTitle: Yolo-based Deep Learning Techniques for Identifying Floating Bottles in Inland Water: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Floating trash like bottles are one of the main causes of the serious environmental threat posed by the growing pollution of inland water bodies. Conservation efforts are hampered by the lack of effective and affordable techniques for locating and retrieving these bottles. Real-time object detection algorithms in conjunction with unmanned boats can offer ways to remove floating trash from rivers. A popular real-time object detection model is the You Only Look Once (Yolo) Series. Based on efficacy and accuracy rate, each YOLO model gets better than the other. articleTitle: Speed Optimization For Fly Ash Brick Machine

abstract: Over the years, fly ash bricks have evolved significantly from rudimentary production methods to sophisticated manufacturing processes. Analysis reveals that the bottleneck lies in the hydraulic system, where a single valve regulates oil flow to both the hydraulic compressor and the rotating table, leading to decreased machine efficiency. To mitigate this challenge, a double valve system is proposed, offering a solution to enhance machine speed and meet growing demand. Furthermore, the study explores the loading and unloading process, which relies on metal detectors to sense a metallic rod attached to the table rotator. However, withthe implementation of the double valve system and subsequent increase in machine speed, the accuracy ofmetal detection becomes compromised. As an alternative, the study recommends the utilization of inductive proximity sensors, capable of accurately detecting metal atany speed without physical contact, thereby ensuring precise control of the table rotator. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for enhancing production efficiency and meeting the demands of the burgeoning market for sustainable building materials. demands of the burgeoning market for sustainable building materials.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Sensing Capabilities of Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes for Urea Detection through Optical and Electrical Characterization

abstract: Detecting the nitrogen content present in urea is of utmost importance in determining its suitability for agricultural applications. This specific research paper explores a method that employs Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes (MWCNT) as the sensing material. The study revealed promising results, showcasing that the MWCNT-based sensor achieved its peak sensitivity, detecting urea concentrations with good precision. Specifically, it demonstrated a maximum sensitivity of 0.49% at a urea concentration of $\mathbf{1 0 ~ m M}$. Moreover, the sensor exhibited impressive sensitivity, with a rapid response time of 46 seconds and an efficient recovery time of just above 7 minutes. The sensing mechanism was initially confirmed through analytical techniques such as Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR). By observing the change in intensity of the CO2 signal upon exposure to urea solution, the involvement of oxygen ions in the sensing process was validated. Furthermore, the confirmation of this mechanism was reinforced through detailed electrical characterization. Overall, the development of this sensing film represents a significant advancement in the field of urea detection as it offers a cost-effective solution that is non-enzymatic in nature, yet possesses good sensitivity. This breakthrough has the potential to greatly benefit agricultural practices by providing farmers and researchers with a reliable tool for assessing the quality of urea fertilizers efficiently and accurately.

articleTitle: Improved Detection Rate of Breast Cancer Using 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Feature Representations for Topic Modeling with Latent Dirichlet Allocation

abstract: Topic analysis is also known as topic detection or topic extraction, refers to ML method that categorizes larger text datasets into categories based on the individual text. It employs natural language processing to analyze human communication by breaking it down into components such as speech, words, sentences, and context, aiming to identify patterns and unveil underlying meanings within texts. This process aids in deriving insights and facilitating data-driven decisions. Within topic analysis, the primary machine learning techniques employed areas of focus include topic modeling and topic classification within this field. However, topic modeling encounters various challenges, specific to document properties. NLP is an integrative subject that merges CS, AI, and linguistics to construct systems capable of comprehending and processing human language. The prevalent machine using labeled data to categorize unlabeled data. This process relies on the knowledge gained during training to classify new data. In general, text classification methods handle predefined and finite categories such as predicting labels like credible or not credible for credibility assessment, or determining movie ratings (bad, okay, good) based on reviews. The difficulty in text classification arises from the predetermined set of topics or labels. When the topics are not known in advance, the concept of topic modeling becomes crucial. This statistical modeling approach is designed to identify abstract topics within a set of documents that lack predefined labels. By analyzing labelled data, this method extracts underlying topics.

articleTitle: Soil Fertility Mapping Utilizing Wireless Sensor Network Applying Tree-Based Topology

This study addresses the urgent need for precision farming methods in the face of problems such as soil deterioration and population increase by designing and implementing a wireless sensor network system combining the Internet of Things with sensor nodes set up in a tree topology network for mapping soil nutrients, focusing on assessing the efficacy of the proposed network system. The results show a 100% success rate of data transmission for all the sensor nodes in a tree topology configuration up to 5 meters distance apart and started to have minimal errors in transmitting at $\mathbf{6}$ meters up to 10 meters and have an average time of 3 to 4 seconds data transfer regardless of the number of nodes and distance. articleTitle: Proportionate Conjugate Gradient Algorithm for Sparse Systems

abstract: For colored input, the Recursive Least Square (RLS) technique is employed to achieve a higher computational complexity but a faster convergence rate. Recently, For lesser computational complexity, the conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm has replaced the RLS algorithm as it yields a similar convergence rate with. In this paper, a sparse CG algorithm is proposed by introducing a proportional gain matrix in its update equation to obtain further improvement in the convergence rate for identifying sparse systems with colored inputs. The proposed algorithm provides a better convergence rate as the active taps (AT) get higher step size and thus converge fast. Incorporation of the gain function is made tactfully to obtain improvement in its overall performance. Simulation findings demonstrate that the suggested technique considerably increases the steady-state error and convergence rate.

articleTitle: Design of Novel Phase Frequency Detectors for Low Phase Noise Frequency Multipliers

abstract: Phase frequency detectors (PFDs), which are utilized in Delay Locked Loops (DLLs) and Phase Locked Loops (PLLs), are an essential component of any frequency synthesizer systems. DLL is made up of four parts: PFD, CP, VCDL, and EC, with PFD playing a crucial role in identifying phase differences between the reference and feedback signals. Having a lot of parameters controlling the PFD output, it becomes necessary to understand each of them and have a balanced design, which determines having low trade-offs. This research proposes four innovative PFDs that outperformed their parent PFDs. Analysis on power, phase noise, corner analysis, and sweep analysis (frequency) are performed to offer a clear picture of trade-offs. PFD performance is demonstrated using a gpdk90 nm CMOS technology and voltage range between $1 \mathrm{~V}-\mathbf{1. 8 V}$. The analysis findings demonstrated a 39.12% reduction in power consumption for the suggested NL-PFD, as well as a 55.5% decrease in dead zone operating frequency for the buffer-based PFD, while in terms of phase noise we see a decrease of 9.7% for NL-PFD design. Other two unique designs have also demonstrated considerable results in terms of transistor count, power consumption, and dead zone trade-offs.

articleTitle: Advanced Source Privacy: DQ-NN and Phantom Routing in IoT-Integrated Multiple-Source and Destination Wireless Sensor Networks

abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) and Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have brought about revolutionary opportunities for many areas, they have also raised serious security issues, especially with relation to source node location privacy in IoT-enabled WSNs. Through the strategic selection of phantom nodes, our method establishes various routing paths from source to sink nodes via these phantoms, taking into account factors such as neighbour lists, energy levels, distances, and trust heterogeneity. The use of DQ-NN, a combination of Deep Q-learning Network (DQN) and Deep Neural Network (DNN), is essential to our approach since it guarantees source node location privacy protection in addition to effective and reliable data transfer through IoT-enabled WSNs, strengthening the privacy and security environment of IoT networks and facilitating easy integration with everyday life. The suggested DQ-NN performs better than other current methods.

articleTitle: Diabetic Retinopathy using OCT Images

abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a serious microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus and a very prevalent cause of vision loss worldwide. Fundus Images till now is used as gold standard for DR diagnosis. However, Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) has emerged as a better option for imaging modality for the early detection, monitoring, and management of DR other than fundus imaging. By providing high-resolution cross-sectional images of the retina, OCT enables visualization of microstructural changes associated with DR, such as retinal thickening, intra-retinal cysts, and disruptions in the retinal layers. The study demonstrates the potential application of two-phase machine learning algorithm techniques for OCT picture classification, leading to more accurate and efficient diagnosis of DR. In recent years, advancements in OCT technology, particularly Optical Coherence Tomographic Angiography (OCTA), have further enhanced ability to assess the retinal microvasculature non-invasively. This paper presents a thorough review of OCT imaging’s function in Diabetic Retinopathy, highlighting its value for treatment monitoring, disease stage, and early identification.

The strategy tries to improve sentiment classification performance by utilizing the advantages of both models. The complexities of social media text are often difficult for traditional sentiment analysis models, like rule-based systems and machine learning algorithms like logistic regression and support vector machines, to capture because of issues with contextual understanding, linguistic complexity, inherent data variability, and noise. Labelled data and an innovative training approach are combined to train the model. Reporting accuracy metrics is part of the performance evaluation process when using a test dataset. articleTitle: Analyzing Cross-Layer Design Approaches for Quality of Service in Wireless Networks

articleTitle: Enhancing the Parkinson’s Disease Detection Through Machine Learning and Feature Engineering

articleTitle: Design and Comparative Analysis of Various Antenna Array Structures for 5G Applications

abstract: The emergence of the 5G technology has ushered in a system that offers data rates, low latency, and improved wireless communication. This project focuses on investigating array structure configurations specifically designed for antennas with a primary emphasis on their applications in the realm of 5G. The study involves the design of multiple MIMO antennas to determine the most suitable array structure. These MIMO antennas are designed to operate within a Frequency for 5 G Applications with sub-band 6 GHz and 5 G Frequency range spanning from 3.5 GHz to 6 GHz. Additionally, the performance of array configurations is meticulously compared, taking into account factors such as directivity, gain, VSWR (Voltage Standing Wave Ratio), and polarization ratio. A Chair-Plane antenna is designed. At the top substrate, a chair-shaped patch with etched out. At the bottom of the antenna, a rectangular shape is placed. An array of microstrip feed lines feeds the antenna. FR4, identified by a dielectric continuous ($\varepsilon$ r) of 4.4 as well as a loss tangent $(\tan \delta)$ of 0.02 is the structure that is made use of. The measurements of the antenna are $50 \times 39 \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm}$ in overall. Simulated values of return loss at resonating frequencies are 3.5 GHz, and 5 GHz are observed at -23.59, and -20.91dB respectively. The Chair-plane antenna exhibits 5.01 dB gain and 5.38 dB directivity and a VSWR value of 1.15 and 1.19GHz is obtained. This Chair-Plane antenna is resonant at the C band. Thus, utilizing this suggested antenna it can be made use of for real-time 5 G applications that utilize C band as a reverberating regularity.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Jute Pest Detection Using Improved VGG-19 and XAI

abstract: Jute, an important crop in many regions of India faces significant threats from pests, a local survey found that 18% of the harvest was damaged by pests. articleTitle: Partitioning-Based Filtering Technique for Accelerated Speckle Reduction in SAR Images

abstract: Partitioning-based total filtering is a way to lower speckle noise in synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) pics. This technique uses a brand-new mass-spring analogy to partition a photograph into present-day homogenous areas. A hard and fast state-of-the-art policy is then hooked up to pick out the speckle-loose pixels’ present-day place and build a statistical model of today’s speckle-free pixels from them. This statistical version is applied to the alternative pixels within every region to generate a speckle-decreased picture. This approach ends in an improved noise reduction effect compared to SAR denoising strategies while keeping the edge features inside the picture. Additionally, it requires no prior information approximately the speckles and, therefore, can be used for any SAR image without tuning the parameters. As a result, this technique can boost the denoising procedure and convey proper consequences with much less computational complexity.

articleTitle: Exploitation of SQL Common Language Runtime Assemblies: A Novel Attack Vector for Compromising Microsoft SQL Server Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research investigates a novel attack technique employed by cybercriminals to compromise Microsoft SQL (MS SQL) servers. The attackers leverage the functionality of MS SQL Common Language Runtime (CLR) assemblies to establish persistent backdoors on targeted systems. Given the elevated privileges and trusted status of MS SQL servers, traditional security measures often fail to detect such intrusions. This work explores the attack methodology, detailing the exploitation of SQL CLR assemblies for crafting malicious backdoors. The attackers employ a multi-stage approach that includes brute-forcing publicly accessible SQL servers, creating backdoor user accounts, and deploying custom-designed CLR assemblies. These CLR assemblies are subsequently executed via SQL stored procedures or functions, granting the attackers comprehensive control over the compromised server. The research further explores post-exploitation activities conducted by the attackers which includes, but not limited to, cyber espionage, ransomware deployment and crypto-currency mining. Additionally, it proposes comprehensive mitigation strategies to safeguard MS SQL servers against this emerging attack vector. By highlighting this novel technique and emphasizing the importance of securing exposed database instances, this work contributes to a more robust defence posture against evolving cyber threats.

articleTitle: Reliability and Power Supply Scaling Effects on Nanoscale Comparators for Future Flash/SAR Analog to Digital Converter (ADC) Applications

abstract: The most of mixed-signal applications, including ADC and DLDO (digital low drop-out regulators), depend on the dynamic comparators. The comparator operated with a $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{DD}}$ of 0.7 V demonstrated a delay & power consumption of $15.45 \mathrm{pS} \ \& \ 12.77 \ \mu \mathrm{W}$ under $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and a $\Delta \mathrm{Vin}=\operatorname{VinP}-\mathrm{VinN}$ of 0.7 V. At $107^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the comparator shown a delay & power consumption of 24.13 pS & $11.48 \ \mu \mathrm{W}$ at same $\Delta$ Vin. However, when $\Delta$ Vin is reduced to 0.1 V, the comparator demonstrated a delay & power consumption of $\mathbf{1 8. 2 3} \ \mathrm{pS} \ \& \ 14.05 \ \mu \mathrm{W}$ at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and 30.16 $\mathrm{pS} \ \& \ 12 \ \mu \mathrm{W}$ at $107^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The same comparator when operated with a $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{DD}}$ of 1.2 V demonstrated a delay & power consumption of $9.689 \ \mathrm{pS} \ \& \ 101 \ \mu \mathrm{W}$ under $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and a $\Delta \mathrm{Vin}$ of 1.2 V. At $107^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the comparator shown a delay & power consumption of $14.5 \ \mathrm{pS} \ \& \ 84.86 \ \mu \mathrm{W}$ at same $\Delta \mathrm{Vin}$. However, when $\Delta \mathrm{Vin}$ is reduced to 0.1 V, the comparator demonstrated a delay & power consumption of $12.29 \ \mathrm{pS} \ \& \ 112.3 \ \mu \mathrm{W}$ at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $21.66 \ \mathrm{pS} \ \& \ 93.6 \ \mu \mathrm{W}$ at $107^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.

This paper provides an investigation into modern-day identification-primarily based authentication algorithms and their packages for community safety. It outlines the inspiration of identity-primarily based protocols and examines distinct authentication algorithms along with uneven key authentication, challenge-reaction authentication, comfortable key exchange protocols, and zero-information authentication. It also evaluates the risks associated with every technique, consisting of capacity weaknesses and vulnerabilities. Furthermore, it presents suggestions for the maximum suitable authentication algorithms for unique varieties of networks and programs. In the end, identity-based total authentication algorithms are an important tool for securing a network and offer a sturdy level of authentication for users.

articleTitle: Automatic Food Billing System of Indian Food using YOLOv8 model
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Automatic food analysis has gained significant interest in the realm of dietary choices as individuals become more aware of their nutritional intake. Particularly in the context of self-service restaurants, this technology not only aids in retrieving information from selected food items but also speeds up the process by solving the congestion problem existing at the cashiers during peak demand periods. This research paper introduces an innovative approach to tackle the challenges associated with automatically analyzing food platters in canteens and restaurants. We have developed a specialized automated billing system tailored specifically for Indian cuisine. Our system leverages computer vision techniques to process food item images and extract vital information like food item names and prices by employing a state of the art object detection algorithm known as YOLO (You Only Look Once). Whether it’s a waiter or a customer, a simple photograph of a food order suffices for our system to extract the necessary details and generate an itemized bill. This eliminates the need for manual item entry, reducing errors and saving time for both customers and businesses. Our approach demonstrates a substantial improvement in food detection, surpassing the state-of-the-art performance on the publicly available IndianFood10 dataset by achieving an impressive 91.9% mAP score. This represents a significant technological advancement in the domain of automatic billing within restaurant settings.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Master Slave D Flip Flop Using Pass Transistor
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)

By utilizing pass transistors strategically, our design minimizes the propagation delay and power consumption, making it well-suited for high-speed and low-power applications and analyzes the impact of process variations and parasitic capacitances on the flip-flop’s performance, highlighting its robustness. We implement this concept in (digital schematic circuit designing software) DSCH and Microwind layout editor software tool.

articleTitle: An intelligent routing protocols for Vehicular networks using machine learning

articleTitle: Real-Time Reconstruction of 3D Space using Holographic Video

articleTitle: Enhancing Healthcare through Real-Time Big Data Analytics in the Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Actual-time massive information analytics in the Cloud can provide healthcare agencies with the opportunity to correctly reveal, assess, and improve the excellent of patient care. The procedure of gathering and processing healthcare facts from diverse resources within the Cloud offers a unique task due to the want to combine a couple of facts assets and to hit upon and analyze events in actual time. In reaction, they are being used to improve the overall performance of analytics in the Cloud, including in-memory analytics, graph databases, streaming analytics, and gadget mastering equipment. Inmemory analytics allows for velocity-of-idea evaluation of massive volumes of information. By temporarily storing records inside the system’s reminiscence, organizations can speedy respond to patient records and healthcare occasions without looking ahead to the information to be transferred to and from disk-based storage. Graph databases are also beneficial in Healthcare, as they permit easy navigation of relationships between records entities, which include sufferers, physicians, healthcare groups, medications, and medical gadgets. articleTitle: Mixed User Grouping for Downlink NOMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The paper addresses several important issues regarding the performance of non-orthogonal multiple access systems in terms of sum rate capability with numerous users divided among several clusters sharing the same channel resources. Previous studies revealed that NOMA with 3 users in each cluster performed better with respect to sum rate under high channel gain conditions, whereas NOMA with 2 users in each cluster excels where the channel gains are on the lower side. It has been observed that a conventional NOMA system consisting only similar type of user grouping technique may not be the best choice to address diverse channel conditions for different types of applications. The issue is addressed by introducing mixed user grouping in NOMA systems, with both 2-user and 3-user grouping techniques applied at the same time to group users in several clusters depending upon their channel gain conditions to improve the sum rate capacity. It also bridges the gap between the average sum rates of proximate and distant users with a significant increase in the average sum rate of distant users. Results for mixed user grouping are simulated and compared with the existing user grouping techniques. This research work indicates a basis for additional research on dynamic user grouping in NOMA systems.

articleTitle: Evaluating AODV Routing Protocol Performance in UAV Networks for Search-and-Rescue Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With the rapid advancement and widespread adoption of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) across various sectors, effective communication among these vehicles has become indispensable. Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Networks (UAVNETs) are recognized as pivotal for facilitating cooperative and synchronized operations among UAVs. Routing protocols play a vital role in optimizing the efficiency of UAVNETs given the dynamic nature of these networks. Ad-hoc On-Demand Distance Vector (AODV) routing protocol is evaluated in this study for its efficacy in a variety of mobility scenarios, with an emphasis on its use in search-and-rescue operations. Different mobility models including Random Waypoint, Gauss Markov and Paparazzi are employed for the evaluation

articleTitle: Authentication for Access Mechanisms for Cloud Services Based on Improved Elliptic Curve Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In an era where cloud computing has become ubiquitous, ensuring robust security measures is imperative to safeguard sensitive data and maintain user trust. Traditional methods of authentication, such as passwords, are susceptible to various security threats, including phishing attacks and brute-force attempts. Biometric authentication offers a promising solution by leveraging unique biological characteristics of individuals, such as fingerprints, iris patterns, or facial features, for identity verification. This paper proposes a novel biometric authentication model tailored specifically to enhance the security of cloud systems. The proposed IECC performs better with a lower encryption time of 9.85 sec and decryption time of 7.58 sec. Also, with a key generation time of 2.12 sec and an execution time of 23.21 sec, the model integrates biometric data acquisition, processing, and authentication mechanisms within the cloud infrastructure, offering a seamless and secure user authentication experience. By leveraging biometric traits, the proposed model mitigates common vulnerabilities associated with traditional authentication methods, thereby enhancing overall system security.

articleTitle: Machine Learning in Motion: Enhancing Human Activity Recognition with Smartphone Sensor Data and Performance Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The goal of this undertaking course, is to enhance the efficiency and outcome performance in Human Activity Recognition (HAR) using smartphone sensor data and machine learning (ML) approaches. This field of study is located at the interface between pioneering computational techniques and practical technical implementations. The rising demand for high-performance, robust and user friendly HAR systems is the driver behind this initiative. The importance of such systems is increasing not only in the fields of medicine, training, and cities development but also aided by these areas. This investigation will have a primary goal for appraising many ML models. The models include different types of neural network architectures, including support vector machine (SVM), decision trees (DT), convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM). In training and validation procedures, the models were given datasets based on information from sensors in smartphones accelerometers and gyroscopes. Precisely, the goal was to provide a precise identification and value of wide range human behaviors. One of the key components that make this course meaningful is its clear-cut inclination towards practical application in real world situation. To do this, giving priority to the accuracy of models is paramount while simultaneously taking into consideration parameters such as speed of processing and practical aspects when using most smartphones. For HAR tasks, CNN and LSTM achieve better results as opposed to other deep learning approaches. They have amazing ability to harness more or less characteristics of the vibrations, which naturally happen in sensor data. The findings from the studies show that deep learning approaches perform better than traditional ML models.

articleTitle: Investigating the Feasibility of Encryption as a Risk Mitigation Strategy for Machine Learning Algorithms in Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In current years, the usage of system learning algorithms for clinical purposes has become more and more ubiquitous, and the privacy and protection of affected person records have emerged as more vital topics of debate. As such, it is vital to explore diverse threat mitigation techniques. In this summary, we inspect the possibility of the usage of encryption as a danger mitigation strategy for gadget-mastering algorithms in medical programs. We first overview the specific forms of encryption to be had, after which we examine the feasibility of the use of encryption to guard patient records in a system-learning context. We examine the overall performance effects of encrypting data before the application of a machine studying the set of rules, in addition to capacity vulnerable factors that encryption by me might not be able to shield towards. Sooner or later, we speak about the quality practices for enforcing and the usage of encryption for medical programs regarding device getting-to-know algorithms. The outcomes of this analysis show that even as encryption is a feasible threat mitigation approach, quality practices nonetheless want to be set up for its implementation.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-AF: A Novel Customized YOLOv8-Accurate Fast Deep Learning Model for Enhancing Border Security in Various Global Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The proliferation of ground-pit tunnels along international borders poses significant security threats, including illegal immigration, smuggling, human trafficking, and potential terrorist activities. To address these challenges, this paper presents an innovative surveillance system that integrates drones equipped with high-resolution cameras and a deep learning-based object detection model, specifically the YOLOv8-AF (You Only Look Once v8-Accurate Fast) variant. The proposed model has been designed to autonomously identify ground pits from aerial imagery, providing real-time alerts to security authorities. The YOLOv8-AF model, trained on a publicly available comprehensive Ground Pit Image Dataset (GPID), demonstrates superior performance with over $95 \%$ accuracy and a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.895, outperforming other models like Faster-RCNN, Fast-RCNN, and SSD. The proposed model ability to process 116.28 frames per second makes it highly efficient for real-time applications, offering a cost-effective and robust solution for enhancing border security in various global regions.

articleTitle: Object Detection and Land-marking for Human Action Recognition in Single to Multiplayer Sports by Hybrid Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Sporting events require strategic planning and proper analysis of the performance of players. Decision-making before or after a game helps the coaches to provide the players with appropriate guidance and training. Human Action Recognition models are the best tool to implement in this scenario. It not only helps improve the gameplay but also focuses on other factors. The broadcasting team can use it to show the highlights and Physicists can have a look into how a player is getting injured and prevent any future mishaps. Our paper proposes the use of two different algorithms to detect and estimate players, positions during a match in any sport. Firstly, object detection is done using YOLOv7 model then the pose is estimated using OpenPose. Additionally, we delve into a comparative analysis of different pose-estimation algorithms. Furthermore, we assess the performance of YOLOv7 in both single-player and multiplayer sports contexts, providing valuable insights into its efficacy and applicability.The average detection time per frame is $\mathbf{1. 4}$ seconds, with a peak accuracy of $\mathbf{0. 9 9}$ for single sports and 0.871 for multiple sports involving player and object detection, resulting in an overall accuracy of 0.8649 for the proposed framework. Through this comprehensive approach, we aim to revolutionize sports analytics and elevate the standard of performance analysis in the realm of athletics.

articleTitle: Feature Guided Convolutional Neural Network for Face Recognition of NewBorn Babies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The latest technological advancements offer methods for identifying individuals, with facial matching or facial image recognition being prominent among them. This technology is widely utilized worldwide for various purposes. The primary objective is to establish the absolute and definitive identity of a newborn baby at the earliest possible and increase the recognition rate and decrease the false alarm rate during the recognition process of an infant. The implementation of face matching for babies serves as a preventive measure against incidents like exchange, mixing, and kidnapping, among others. It also holds significant importance in the field of medical science, addressing long-standing challenges. With a rising number of such cases worldwide, face matching emerges as a viable solution to mitigate these issues. The dataset for the newborn babies has been collected from the Mandya Medical College, Mandya for three continuous days once the baby is born. Preprocessing of Images is done to remove unwanted information. Convolutional Neural Network is used for face matching. This paper offers a comparison of different facematching techniques, aiming to assess their respective efficiency and accuracy within the system.

articleTitle: Harnessing LLMs for Medical Insights:NER Extraction from Summarized Medical Text
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The rapid growth of medical text presents a significant challenge for healthcare professionals to stay updated with current research and clinical guidelines. Effective text summarization is essential to facilitate access to knowledge, improve clinical decision-making, and ultimately enhance patient outcomes. This study aims to fine-tune and assess a medical text summarization system utilizing large language models (LLMs). The objective is to produce concise, coherent summaries of medical literature, prioritizing clinical relevance. Additionally, automated named entity recognition (NER) is employed to extract vital entities from the summaries generated by GPT3, T5, PEGASUS LLMs. These LLMs are trained on benchmark PubMed dataset which are evaluated under standard metrics such as ROUGE (1, 2, L) and BERTScore metrics. The model pipeline demonstrates summarization and NER performance over precision of $\mathbf{6 5 \%}$ on medical text data. The resulting entity-annotated summaries provide condensed representations, enabling efficient information extraction and knowledge discovery. This automated approach accelerates biomedical research by large-scale medical text analysis.

articleTitle: Voice based gender recognition using deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Predicting age through audio is essential for tailored user experiences, such as content recommendations and targeted advertisements. Better accessibility features for those with age-or gender-specific needs are also made possible by it. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to gender classification using voice data, employing deep learning techniques such as Long Short Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neyral Network (CNN), and Residual Network (ResNet) models. The work begins with the preprocessing of audio data, extracting Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) as features. To address class imbalance, Random Oversampling and Random Undersampling techniques are applied. Then, using the resampled data, LSTM, CNN, and ResNet models are built and trained. Model evaluation includes metrics such as classification reports, confusion matrices, and (Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve) ROC curves. The outcomes show how successful the suggested models are, with considerations for oversampling and undersampling strategies. The results, based on training the model on the SLR45 dataset, demonstrate an impressive accuracy of approximately 99% for gender classification by CNN.

articleTitle: SkillSync: Evaluating Candidates for Communication and Problem-Solving Proficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In contemporary work environments, effective communication, collaborative problem-solving, and positive attitude are pivotal for success. However, conventional hiring approaches often struggle to accurately evaluate these essential competencies. SkillSync presents a groundbreaking solution to this challenge by introducing an innovative assessment platform tailored to measure candidate’s communication skills, problem-solving abilities, and positive demeanor. This project investigates the development of a comprehensive assessment tool designed to analyze an individual’s disposition and adaptability across diverse workplace situations. The tool will leverage a user-friendly interface and a novel algorithmic approach to evaluate an individual’s inherent characteristics. The algorithm will focus on analyzing the relevance and efficacy of candidate responses, with the primary objective of furnishing employers with valuable insights into a candidate’s content writing proficiency and their capacity to approach workplace challenges with a positive outlook

articleTitle: Unveiling Domain Generation Algorithms in DNS Log Traffic: A Next-Generation Intelligent Framework for Dynamic Anomaly Detection and Mitigation through Machine Learning Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Pioneering the forefront of network security innovation, this study embarks on an exhilarating exploration of DNS log data sourced from the esteemed Anna University, propelled by the cutting-edge prowess of the “Adaptive Ensemble Anomaly Detection” (AEAD) technique. DNS logs serve as a treasure trove of network activities, encapsulating intricate domain resolution requests and responses. Through the transformative lens of AEAD, a pioneering and dynamic machine learning paradigm, this research endeavors to illuminate hidden patterns and anomalies lurking within the intricate fabric of DNS log data. AEAD’s adaptive prowess situates it at the pinnacle of anomaly detection and mitigation methodologies, perpetually evolving to confront the ever-shifting challenges of contemporary network landscapes. By meticulously dissecting DNS logs with surgical precision, this study lays the cornerstone for the development of resilient strategies in network management and security. Remarkably, this approach boasts an unparalleled accuracy rate of 99.98%, cementing its status as an indispensable tool for safeguarding digital ecosystems.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Dermal Cell-Sheet Wound Healing Model using B-spline collocation Scheme

The biological process of wound healing depends on a number of factors, including contamination of the injured area, wound dimension, oxygenation of the tissues and the rapid growth of the cell count, making the dynamic of wound healing quite intricate to study even for any prediction hence, a mechanistic mathematical model has been considered for the study of cell regeneration. And for the same dermal cell interaction model a numerical approach has been initiated in this study by implementing cubic b-spline collocation scheme.
