articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Video Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Anomaly detection in video surveillance is a crucial task for ensuring security and safety in various environments, and Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) networks offer a promising solution by capturing spatiotemporal dependencies inherent in video data. This comprehensive approach to anomaly detection integrates ConvLSTM networks without the need for additional object detection frameworks, enabling direct processing of video data for anomaly detection. Leveraging the inherent capabilities of ConvLSTM networks, the model can effectively distinguish between normal and anomalous behavior without relying on predefined object categories or region proposals. Additionally, a refinement process enhances the representation of features in the backbone network and addresses potential issues related to template variations, ensuring robust anomaly detection performance. Furthermore, attention mechanisms are integrated into the ConvLSTM framework to improve feature selection and generalize to new objects and scenarios, eliminating dependency on query labels during testing and enhancing efficiency in real-world applications. Overall, this approach provides a flexible and efficient solution for anomaly detection in video surveillance, capable of handling diverse and complex scenarios with improved accuracy and adaptability.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition Using Deep Learning Techniques for Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The idea of smart healthcare is gradually gaining traction with the rapid advancement in information technologies. Smart healthcare is the intelligent transformation of the current medical system to make it more reliable, efficient, and individualized through the intelligent use of next-generation technologies like artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things (IoT). This study offered the recent advancement of Deep learning (DL) techniques for healthcare systems, and the use of DL techniques to identify human physical activity with wearable sensors. In this paper, convolutional neural networks (CNN), CNN-LSTM, Multi Headed CNN-LSTM, and Multi Headed CNNBiLSTM are used. The obtained outcomes of these Deep Learning models are compared in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and F1 score. The Multi-Headed CNN-BiLSTM model exhibits better performance than the rest of the models when applied to the UCI HAR dataset.

articleTitle: 6T SRAM Cell Based Various Spillage Reduction Techniques for Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Static memory cells, sometimes called SRAMs, are used in various electrical systems. Compared to other memory cells, it consumes less energy, operates more quickly, and requires less frequent replacement. Thus, SRAM is the memory cell that VLSI designers use the most often. Mobile appliances employ octa-core processors, which have been available for 5 to 6 years in electronics. As a result, transistor density and capacity rise as size reduces. Also space-saving memory is being produced. Information can be kept in SRAM cells without being regularly restored as long as power is available. Due to its significant lead (DRAM), the purchase of SRAM was made feasible. In this research paper, different leakage reduction techniques were simulated to compare the static and dynamic power of SRAM cells. These techniques included DTMOS, LCNT, the tri-mode MTCMOS ground-gated approach, and the tri-mode MTCMOS power-gated approach. Various parameters, such as delay and static noise margin, have also been calculated. The Tri-Mode MTCMOS ground-gated method works 1.54, 1.92, 1.51, and 1.52 times faster than the 6T SRAM cell, DTMOS, LCNT, and Tri-Mode MTCMOS powergated methods. In terms of static power, it performs 2.12, 2.29, 1.68, and 1.073 better than the 6T SRAM cell, DTMOS, LCNT, and Tri-Mode MTCMOS power-gated method, respectively.

articleTitle: Differentiating Benign and Malignant Skin Lesions with 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging

Average, 3-D MRI has been located to be a powerful device for differentiating between benign and malignant pores and skin lesions because of its ability to produce high decision pix in a non-invasive way.

articleTitle: Malicious URL Detection: Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Malicious URLs can be detected by leveraging lexical analysis and machine learning, where the parsed components of the URL are parsed, and its features include domain reputation, URL length, and the presence of suspicious characters. Research on the detection of malicious URLs suffers challenges in keeping pace with the changing structural landscape of URLs. Adaptation to dynamic patterns and addressing the technical issues of efficient processing and scalability become important to stay one step ahead of the evolving threat landscape. This paper concentrates on addressing these challenges with the integration of Machine Learning and Lexical Analysis. Features extracted in this process are then fed into machine learning algorithms for the classification of URLs and are tested on unseen data. Research performance is measured using several metrics including Precision, Recall, F1-score and Accuracy during the Model evaluation. Out of all the models experimented, Extra Trees classifier stands out the best with 92% accuracy, showing effectiveness in accurate detection of malicious URL’s.

articleTitle: Automated Classification of Indian Watermelon Varieties Using CNN-PCA: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study shows a system using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with Principal Component Analysis (PCA). This helps to automatically sort major types of watermelons in India. These include Arka Manik, Sugar Baby, Pusa Bedana and Durgapura Kesar. A well-organized set of 8000 clear pictures was gathered and prepared for training the model. The new CNN-PCA plan used the feature-finding skills from CNN and PCA’s ability to reduce size. It did well, being 97.6% accurate on a special test group of information. Making tests helps show how well a model can classify things correctly. It’s very useful for telling apart closely looking types in visual views. The study of the confusion matrix showed very few mistakes, mostly because some types look too much alike. But these cases show chances to keep improving and adding more details to the models. The study shows how modern machine learning methods are mixed with farm uses. Not only is it very precise, but the model could make sorting easier and help those who grow plants to create special kinds of them. The study says it needs constant improvements. It suggests ways to make the data better and explore new designs, helping the model become more accurate and stronger. This work is a very important part of bringing technology into farming. It shows how it can help make better ways to manage crops, competes in markets, and improve types of watermelon plants.

articleTitle: Finding Direction of Arrival using Uniform Circular Array of Microphones and Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Estimating a sound source’s direction of arrival (DOA) has become a significant and crucial area of interest. It has gained recognition in various applications, such as telecommunications, robotics, and defense systems. In this paper, we propose estimating the DOA of a sound source using a uniform circular array (UCA) of microphones and a specific type of neural network called a recurrent neural network (RNN). The RNN was trained for multi-class DOA estimation problem, where 1400 noisy signal vector realizations are used for each class. We assessed the accuracy of RNN-based DOA estimation for UCA compared to a uniform linear array (ULA). Additionally, a comparison between UCA and ULA has been made regarding the DOA estimate accuracy of the Delay and Sum (DAS) beamforming technique. We concluded that DOA estimation via UCA, outperforms different techniques for DOA estimation using ULA.

articleTitle: RFECV-DT: Recursive Feature Selection with Cross Validation using Decision Tree based Android Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The internet is extremely valuable, but it is also vulnerable to assault. Malware is a persistent and dynamic danger. Malware assaults entail introducing malicious code into software. The task was handled using a variety of machine learning approaches. Previous research utilized various methods, such as chi-square, Fisher’s score, and Forward/Backward methods. A recent work used a wrapper strategy of Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation using the nonlinear Support Vector Machine (SVM) as an estimator. This lowered the number of features from 215 to 74, yielding an accuracy percentage of 95.58%. Our solution improves on the previous strategy by using the same dataset and a decision tree with Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation using Decision Tree to identify 53 out of 215 feature. Classifiers other than Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression are all obtaining the highest accuracy of 98 %. This paper decreases the number of features by using Gini Impurity and Cross Validation for detection of Android Malware.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effects of Channel Contention in Adaptive Communications Systems

abstract: This technical summary makes a specialty of the effects of channel contention in adaptive communication systems, and how this phenomenon influences communication performance. specifically, this summary examines how distinct channel rivalry techniques, including service experience more than one get admission to (CSMA), can be used to lessen interference and postpone in a wireless communication community. articleTitle: Enhanced Multi-Class Brain Tumor Classification in MRI Scans Using WPCA-LSTM Network
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Brain tumors pose a significant health threat, making accurate diagnosis crucial for effective treatment. Tumor types include gliomas, meningiomas, pituitary tumors, and benign tumors. Detecting and categorizing these tumors, especially when they consist of very few cells, is one of the most challenging aspects of brain tumor diagnosis. This study introduces a unique deep learning model named Wavelet-LSTM Classifier that combines feature extraction via Wavelet Decomposition-Based Principal Component Analysis (WPCA), Canny edge detection, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network that enhances multi-class tumor classification in MRI images. The experimental results finding demonstrates that the Wavelet-LSTM Classifier model effectively outperforms existing systems, achieves an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 8. 5 1 \% .}$

articleTitle: Design of a Bandgap Voltage Reference Circuit in 90 nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Due to the ability to produce a constant voltage that is unaffected by temperature fluctuations, Bandgap Reference (BGR) circuits plays a crucial role to provide a persistent power to Integrated Circuits. In this work, a BGR circuit is designed in 90 nm CMOS process. This circuit can operate in temperature range between $-40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $160^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The proposed BGR circuit shows stability of $0.7 \%$. At a supply voltage of 1.4 V, the circuit provides a reference voltage of 1.262 V. At this operating condition, the circuit draws $1.4 \mu \mathrm{~A}$ of current, which corresponds to $1.6 \mu \mathrm{~W}$ of power consumption.

articleTitle: Smart Compiler Assistant: An AST based Python Code Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: There are many challenges when it comes to compiling huge lines of code or codes with huge time complexity. Also, if there is an error in the last line of the code, for example, a simple syntax error or a syntactic error, all the time for compiling the code is wasted. To reduce the time and to compile an error-free code, The novel ‘Smart Compiler Assistant’, a tool is designed to revolutionize the coding experience for developers by learning the words and structure of code. The ‘smart compile assistant’ offers guidance in the optimization, completion, and correction of code, that in turn, improves productivity and the quality of the code. Equipped with smooth interoperability into commonly used development tools, ‘Smart Compiler Assistant’, lets developers produce cleaner, more efficient codes with greater accuracy and less hassle, boosting the overall efficiency of the software development cycle.

articleTitle: EEG Based Identification of Learning Disabilities using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A learning disability (LD) encompasses various learning challenges, characterized by difficulties in understanding words and poor reading skills. It affects many school-aged children, especially boys, often leading to poor academic performance and low self-esteem. Early detection and intervention are crucial in mitigating these adverse effects. Our research aims to develop a deep learning model to analyze EEG signals from individuals with learning difficulties, providing highly accurate results quickly. We employed Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Independent Component Analysis (ICA), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) for component analysis of the dataset and used deep learning algorithms such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), and Graph Neural Networks (GNN) for classification. The goal is to determine the most effective combination of data preprocessing techniques and deep learning algorithms for detecting learning disabilities.

articleTitle: Autonomous Drone Navigation in Closed Environments Using SLAM Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The improvement of independent navigation structures for drones has revolutionized severa industries, from agriculture to look and rescue operations. however, navigating drones in closed environments, consisting of warehouses and factories, poses unique demanding situations due to the limited outside cues and limitations. In this paper, we suggest a approach for the problem of self-enough drone navigation in closed environments using Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) strategies. SLAM is a well established method for robots to construct maps of unknown environments while simultaneously estimating their place within the map. inside the context of drones, SLAM algorithms use facts from onboard sensors, cameras, and LiDAR to create a map of the surroundings and track the drone’s role and orientation in actual time. This document is then used to plan a safe and green path for the drone to navigate via the surroundings. Our proposed tool uses function-based total SLAM and occupancy grid mapping strategies to gain robust and correct navigation in closed environments. characteristic-primarily based SLAM techniques extract and music extraordinary functions inside the surroundings to assemble a map. on the equal time, occupancy grid mapping strategies use probabilistic fashions to represent the occupancy of the environment. to evaluate the overall performance of our machine, we conducted experiments in simulated closed environment and assessment our effects with ground truth statistics.

articleTitle: Analyzing Regulations and Standards for Crypto currency Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cryptocurrency algorithms have evolved and are normally secured with the aid of cryptographic techniques or protocols. Cryptocurrency algorithms have evolved to facilitate relaxed transfers, exchanges, and garages of virtual currency values. As the cryptocurrency marketplace has grown, there has been an increase in the complexity of the algorithms and the character of the transactions. Consequently, it has become essential to evaluate the safety of the algorithms in addition to setting up a unified set of guidelines and standards. In this paper, we present a complete evaluation of existing policies and standards associated with crypto foreign money algorithms. We explore the key elements that need to be considered, consisting of economic implications, privateers, collaboration, and regulatory alignment. Further, we offer an in-depth dialogue of the related regulatory frameworks, inclusive of international requirements, existing and pending national guidelines, technology requirements, and quality practices. We also attempt to perceive the gaps in present guidelines and perceive regions in which modifications are needed. We also consider the numerous regulatory schemes which are being followed in extraordinary jurisdictions, which creates personal limitations and possibilities. Our findings suggest that there’s a need for a unified standard for crypto forex algorithms and to think about both the financial and security perspectives.

articleTitle: Classification of Foods based on Bijective Soft Set
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cuisine data is typically classified using images of the cuisine, cooking methods, cooking utensils, and, most importantly, ingredients. The vast amount of recipe data available on the internet necessitates the creation of specialised systems for storing, retrieving, and effectively utilising stored knowledge and data. Neural networks based expert systems are steadily being used to classify the cuisine data. But it lacks in dealing the vagueness present in the categorical cuisine data. Also, most of the popular recipes available online are mostly unhealthy. As a result, the Bijective soft set theory has been introduced into this study since it is an intelligent method for developing classification rules from food data and then recognising ambiguity and data reliance. The classification guidelines also address the necessity to select healthy/nutritious meals. The investigation outcomes from using bijective soft set analysis to a set of data samples are presented and appraised in this work. Furthermore, the classification rules derived from this approach provides valuable help for developing food recommendation systems. The accuracy of this classification scheme has got really influenced by application of the bijective soft set when compared to other state-of-the-art classifiers.

articleTitle: Investigation of AlGaN/GaN HEMT Device Performance with Variation of GaN Cap Layer Thickness along with Doping Concentration
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this paper, the AIGaN/GaN HEMT without and with GaN cap layer ($\mathbf{G}_{\text {cap }}$) along with variation in its thickness ($\mathbf{d}_{G a N}$) and doping concentration was presented. It is observed that $\mathbf{G}_{\text {cap }}$ thickness and doping concentration affects the electric field and two dimensional electron gas (2DEG). The formation of two dimensional hole gas (2DHG) at lower energy level of the device when $G_{c a p}$ is employed mainly influences the 2DEG at the interface of AlGaN/GaN. Our investigation found that the varying $\mathbf{d}_{G a N}$ from $10 \mathbf{n m}$ to $3 \mathbf{n m}$ with doping concentrations of $7 \times 10^{18}$ $\mathbf{c m}^{-3}$ and $8 \times 10^{18} \mathbf{c m}^{-3}$ improves the transconductance, ON state current, threshold voltage and current ratio. A device with a $G_{c a p}$ exhibits very low OFF-state current i.e leakage current that increases the ($I_{O N} / I_{O F F}$) current ratio.

articleTitle: Meta-Learning Framework for Coriander Variety Classification using CNN and DBN
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The proposed study focuses on sorting three main types of coriander, called Sadhana, Swathi, and Pant Haritima in India using smart computer methods. A big collection of very clear coriander pictures was carefully taken. It includes different places and growth stages to get many kinds of surroundings and how they look visually in the photos. The data set was carefully cleaned up and prepared for model creation. This included making it uniform and adding more information to it. The new model design combined Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Deep Belief Networks. It was made to find complex patterns in pictures of different coriander types. The data was split into three parts learning, checking, and testing. 70% was used to learn from it while both the other sections got 15%. The models did a great job with 97.6% accuracy, proving their skill at correctly sorting coriander kinds. Metrics like precision, recall, and F1-score gave a more detailed understanding of the models’ skills in classifying things. Also, the Confusion Matrix showed certain spots to improve and look into with models. This study provides a strong method for computers to classify coriander types. It can be used in farming, research, and checking the quality of products. The models’ great accuracy and careful study of their actions hint at how precise farming and handling crops can be in the future.

articleTitle: Crack Detection and Output Power Analysis in Solar Panels Using DANet Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Solar energy, derived from the sun’s radiation, is the best renewable resource powering various applications globally. Solar panels harness sunlight, generating clean electricity for residential and industrial sectors. Recent studies have indicated that cracks covering just 2% of a panel’s surface area can result in an efficiency decrease of around 6%. Moreover, severe cracks or damage can lead to even more significant reductions in output, potentially up to 20% or more. So efficient maintenance and timely detection of cracks in solar panels is critical for effective output. Manual crack detection in solar panels is hindered by the complexity of crack patterns, variations in lighting, and the potential for human error. It is time-consuming, lacks consistency, and may miss small or obscured cracks, impeding effective maintenance. So for effective crack detection deep learning model is used. Initially the images (obtained using EL imaging technique) is given as input to the model and then based on the crack segmentation power analysis is done. In this paper, DANet algorithm is used for segmentation of cracks in solar panel. Dual Attention Network enhances feature representation in deep learning by considering both spatial and channel-wise dependencies for improved performance. After the process of segmentation, it’s output is given for power analysis to know the severity of cracks.

articleTitle: EFFicient Water Jar Cleaning System FOR Industry: A COST-EfFective APProach USing Optical Setup and AUTOMATION
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The bottle washing machine is utilized across various industries for diverse purposes, facilitating efficient and rapid cleaning and purification of water jars to prevent water contamination. Water, being an essential resource, necessitates purification, and the water industry involves several processes such as water jar cleaning, water purification, bottle filling, and packaging. The objective of our project is to focus on the cleaning process of 20 -liter water jars. Employing the life cycle and cost method, we have implemented an optical setup. The project incorporates motors, pumps, Arduino, and motor drivers. Motors are employed to rotate the water jars throughout the process. Two pumps are utilized, with one delivering water solution and the other providing alkaline solution. The alkaline solution, a mixture of base solution and water, maintains a pH range between seven and eight. Arduino, functioning as an embedded system, oversees the entire process. The pumps are situated beneath a stainless steel frame to prevent rust formation. Additionally, electrical shock resistance is a crucial consideration in this project. The water cleaning process is completed in just 30 seconds, significantly reducing manual labor. Upon pressing the start button, the pump is activated, forcefully distributing water into the water jar. Within the jar, a brush is employed to remove any dust or contaminants. Following the process, the water is either collected or expelled through a pipe located underneath the bottle. The project does not entail complex Arduino programming; rather, it relies on simple programming for implementation.

articleTitle: AI Enabled Voice Assistant for Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In today’s world, everyone benefits from smart assistants, which allow us to speak with intelligent aides and ask robotic questions. The majority of people on the planet are pulled to technology in many different ways, whether it be through desktop computers, laptops, cell-phones, etc. It is a speech-recognition intelligent smart assistant that takes text or voice input from the user, processes it, and outputs the results in a number of ways, including speaking the user’s search results. A few instances of intelligent assistants are Alexa, Siri, and Google Assistant. They still have issues with human connection, and they are unable to recognize voices. In addition to requiring internet and $\mathrm{Wi}-\mathrm{Fi}$ access in order to interact with users, those Google Assistant issues also have a very narrow language set, which can cause a lot of difficulties for users. One feature of Android cell-phones is Google Assistant. Nevertheless, in order for this application to work, an Internet connection is necessary. Nevertheless, our suggested solution is also capable of operating without an Internet connection. In order to solve the problem and implement multiple languages, we are using a Raspberry Pi. On the Pi, data in multiple languages is loaded and stored, enabling the user to access any language through the voice assistant and obtain information about recently installed apps, daily news, geolocation, and Wikipedia, among other things. Utilizing automation technologies also benefits the user through voice assistance.

articleTitle: Realization of CNN Using Hybrid Multiplier With PYNQ-Z2
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Smart technologies namely Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) are evolved day by day to develop smart products for various applications. Deep learning is one of the recent technology, which is widely applicable for all kind of applications. CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) is the basic structure to simulate the deep learning algorithms. So various structure of CNN is studied and the selected structure is used for classification of images. Then the selected CNN structure is further analyzed for its performance in the FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) board. LeNet and EfficientNet uses MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets to analyse the performance in both software and hardware. By comparing the performance of EfficientNet, it takes 124 ms in software and 0.172 ms in hardware to classify a single image. Whereas LeNet takes 19 ms and 0.16 ms in software and hardware respectively. CNN performance can be highly improved by exploring the hardware resources of the FPGA chip. An efficient multiplier is designed here for LeNet to reduce the utilization of hardware resources. By implementing it, the area utilized is reduced by $51.2 \%$ than by using conventional multiplier for CNN.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of OMA and NOMA in VLC for 5G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of Orthogonal Multiple Access (OMA) and Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) techniques in Visible Light Communication (VLC) systems, focusing on their performance in the context of 5G and beyond technologies. Through extensive simulations, we analyze the impact of transmitted power on outage probability and total achievable rate for modulation schemes such as Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK), Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK), and Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM), considering both perfect and imperfect Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC). Additionally, we investigate the correlation between Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and sum rate under varying eta and Field of View (FOV) angles. Our study provides insights into the performance of existing OMA and proposed NOMA schemes, specifically in VLC environments, analyzing metrics like SNR and Bit Error Rate (BER). Notably, our findings demonstrate that the proposed NOMA system exhibits superior performance compared to existing OMA systems in VLC channels. These findings significantly enhance the proposed NOMA system for multiuser wireless communication systems, especially within the evolving landscape of 5 G and beyond technologies.

articleTitle: Cryptographic Protocols for Securing Internet of Things (IoT)
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cryptographic protocols are used to relax the ever-developing quantity of linked gadgets that make up the net of things (IoT). Those cryptographic protocols have been designed to make certain that IoT tool traffic stays cozy and personal, even while nevertheless allowing tool-to-device and cloud-to-tool communications. Examples of these protocols consist of TLS/SSL, PGP/GPG, IPsec, SSL VPN, and AES encryption. Every one of these protocols enables authentication, message integrity, and confidentiality via encryption and key trade. Moreover, a lot of these protocols are carried out in the form of diverse hardware and software answers, such as smart playing cards and gateways, to make certain that IoT traffic is secured. With the appropriate implementation of those cryptographic protocols, establishments can ensure that their IoT facts are blanketed and securely transmitted.

articleTitle: Visual Intelligence in Supply Chain Management with Power BI
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: An essential skill set for supply chain management is the ability to visualize and interpret data well. In addition to providing insightful information, these capacities are essential for directing decision-making procedures, which in turn improves the resilience and efficiency of the supply chain as a whole. A range of tools are frequently used in supply chain management to visualize and analyze data. The choice of a specific tool depends on factors like the organization’s preferences, the complexity of data analysis required, and the skill set of the users. In this paper, Power BI is explored for its use in visualizing and interpreting data in the context of Supply Chain Management. The database used here focuses on the supply chain complexities of fashion and beauty products. This work introduces an interactive visualization and analysis system to investigate the internal relationships between shipping costs, manufacturing costs, location-based revenue, and defect rates specific to skin care, hair care, and cosmetics products.

articleTitle: A Novel Contrast Enhancement Method for Low-Light Images with Non-Uniform Illumination Using the Entropy Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study addresses the challenging task of contrast enhancement for dark images with non-uniform illumination, where conventional methods fail due to the coexistence of both dark and bright regions. To overcome the inherent information loss in the bright regions during enhancement, we propose a novel method designed for low-light images. The suggested approach involves using the information related to individual grey levels and their corresponding averages and constructing a multidimensional entropy curve by selecting local pixel attributes. This results in the creation of a joint entropy curve that combines pixel intensity information from one image with the average pixel intensity information from the neighborhood. The application of suggested method yields an enhanced image without the loss of any information in the bright regions. A comprehensive evaluation, both qualitative and quantitative, confirms the superiority of proposed method over existing methods, establishing its effectiveness in addressing contrast challenges in low-light images with non-uniform illumination.

articleTitle: Android Controlled WI-FI Robotic Lawn Mower
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study was designed to clean the lawn field in an easier, faster, safer and more cost-effective way. This paper focuses on the design and implementation of a low cost and user-friendly remotely controlled lawn mower via an Android mobile application using a smartphone. This robot is operated through the $\mathrm{Wi}-\mathrm{Fi}$ module process. The robot has the heart of the NODEMCU controller, which is connected to the android application. The device has the following hardware such as NODE-MCU microcontroller, Wi-Fi module, two 12volt wiper motors as wheels, switch and two 12-volt 7 Ampere rechargeable lithium-ion battery that are connected in series. The device can be used using Android phone with installed Grass Cutter App. In controlling the lawn mower, Wi-Fi connection is used. The maximum distance of $\mathrm{Wi}-\mathrm{Fi}$ is up to 152 meters or 500 feet.

articleTitle: Utilizing Machine Learning for Predictive Sales Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The purpose of the study is to investigate the possibilities of machine learning methods for predicting revenue for a retail company. The significance of precise sales projections and the difficulties companies encounter in attaining it are covered in the opening section of the paper. The different machine learning techniques used in the research are then described, including neural networks, decision trees, random forests, and linear regression. The machine learning algorithms are trained and tested using past sales data from a retail company. The outcomes demonstrate that the random forest algorithm worked better than the other algorithms in terms of precision and accuracy. The research also finds crucial elements that have a big effect on purchases, like timing, marketing campaigns, and economic signs. The advantages of machine learning for sales projections, such as increased precision, speed, and scaling, are highlighted in the paper’s conclusion. The research’s conclusions provide useful information for companies looking to improve their capacity for sales planning and streamline their processes.

articleTitle: Tiny Object Detection for Marine Search and Rescue with YOLOv8n-Tiny
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Marine Search and Rescue (MSAR) operations are invaluable and vital in maritime traffic management, marine environment monitoring, and maritime security and defense efforts. Their prompt reactions also improve our marine environment’s security, safety, and sustainability. Accurately identifying tiny objects in images, such as boats, people, and swimmers, is essential for MSAR missions. We recognize the necessity for optimization in detecting particular categories of challenging-to-identify tiny objects present within images. However, MSAR operations come across challenges including the size of tiny objects, complex sea surface backgrounds, low signal-to-noise ratios, and the diversity and density of tiny sea target objects. To address these challenges, we proposed a modified YOLOv8-based model for classification and detection purposes. For experiments, we have selected the SeaDronesSee dataset to serve as the foundation of our research. For classification, the YOLOv8l-Tiny model demonstrates better results when compared to YOLOv8nTiny. On the other hand, the YOLOv8n-Tiny model outperforms the YOLOv8s-Tiny and YOLOv8m-Tiny models in detection tasks. The experimental findings indicate that a classification accuracy of $100 \%$ was achieved with losses reduced up to $75 \%$ using the YOLOv8I-Tiny model. For tiny object detection, the YOLOv8n-Tiny model attained a Precision score of 0.89, a Mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.27, and an F1 score of 0.45. Additionally, the cls_loss for detecting tiny objects was notably reduced to 0.10.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Classifier For Detecting Parkinson’s Disease Based on Voice Recordings
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease is a progressive neurological disorder that affects millions of people worldwide. Early detection is essential for effective management of the disease, as it helps in developing proactive treatment plans. In this paper, several classification algorithms are explored to identify the most effective one for detecting Parkinson’s disease. Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest, Decision Tree, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression algorithms are tested, and XGBoost emerges as the most accurate and powerful classifier. The XGBoost algorithm is a highly effective tool that can accurately identify Parkinson’s disease by utilizing multiple data sources. The present study utilizes the XGBoost algorithm and the MDVP Parkinson’s disease dataset to build a state-of-the-art machine learning model. The purpose method’s accuracy was remarkable at $95.918 \%$ through cross-validation, highlighting the effectiveness of the method. The XGBoost algorithm has the potential in the early diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease. The purpose method outperforms the state of art Parkinson’s detection Techniques.

articleTitle: A Study on Data Mining Techniques For Forecasting FMCG Product Sales
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Today era Sale forecasting is essential for any business organization. For forecasting sales, data mining techniques are used. Today’s era is full of information. And where there is information, data is there. The volume of data is increasing every day. With a huge volume of data, finding useful data is like finding a needle in a haystack. The mining process is used to find useful information from large amounts of data using different mining techniques. There are many techniques available to forecast the sales of business organizations. Sales of the FMCG product are affected by many of the variables. With accurate sales forecasting, businesses can get an idea of transportation, human resources, production, and cash flow requirements. This paper reviews some of the important data mining techniques: classification, clustering, regression, and decision trees, which are very useful to predict sales.

articleTitle: Real-Time Depth Map Upsampling for High-Quality Stereoscopic Video Display
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Real-Time depth Map Up sampling for Stereoscopic Video shows is a technology that allows the enhancement of the high-quality of a stereoscopic video for display. The technology improves the resolution of a depth map using deep mastering methods in real-time to up-pattern the map. This will increase the accuracy and niceness of the stereo video show due to the progressed depth perception it gives to the person. This generation is predicated on natural cues inside the video so one can generate an output of higher fidelity without alteration of the underlying geometry. This permits for a green transformation of depth information, which can be used in a myriad of tasks related to virtual fact and augmented fact programs. The rich and correct intensity facts are useful to each visible or audio simulation and optimization of digital camera views and algorithms to interpret 3-D content better.

articleTitle: An Approach Towards Highly Accurate Prediction of Parkinson’s Disease using Boosted Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Parkinson’s Disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized primarily by a blend of motor and non-motor symptoms. The onset of speech-related signs often emerges as an initial motor indicator, detectable in approximately ninety percent of individuals with Parkinson’s disease. The necessity for timely prediction of Parkinson’s disease based on speech-related manifestations has led to the utilization of machine learning methodologies to potentially impede the advancement of this condition. Several researchers have applied machine learning algorithms to various datasets linked to Parkinson’s disease for the identification of probable patients. In this field, ensemble machine learning methods like boosting algorithms display significant potential in promptly detecting Parkinson’s Disease. This scholarly article introduces an innovative Adaboost Model that employs decision trees as the primary estimator within the AdaBoost structure, integrating RandomizedSearchCV hyperparameter tuning techniques to boost the model’s effectiveness. Thorough computational simulations and analyses demonstrate that the machine learning models yield commendable outcomes across multiple performance metrics, including accuracy (95.91%), precision (1.00), recall (0.95), F1Score (0.97), and AUC (0.97), thereby underscoring the promising efficacy of the proposed approach in the realm of Parkinson’s Disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Alzheimer’s Disease Prediction using Machine Learning techniques with the help of Electroencephalogram Brain Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Changes in memory, cognition, and behavior may be symptoms of Alzheimer’s disease, a progressive and degenerative brain disease. The impact of this disease is felt not only by patients, but also by their families, caregivers, and society. This study uses machine learning on EEG data to classify new data as healthy or abnormal. Our experimental results show that combining EEG data with data augmentation techniques can provide 99% accuracy and reliable early detection and diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease. Our research contributes to the development of efficient and effective methods for diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease using machine learning. These techniques can lead to early diagnosis and treatment, ultimately improving the quality of life for those living with this debilitating disease.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion Battery SoC Prediction Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries, owing to their various advantages, are widely used as a primary source of energy for electric vehicles. For a battery management system (BMS), one of the most crucial tasks is to estimate state of charge (SoC). This paper proposes deep learning techniques to estimate the SoC of a battery in a BMW i3 electric vehicle (EV). The dataset consists of 70 trips and each trip has been covered for an average duration of 35 minutes with a sampling rate of 10 Hz. The LSTM network has been designed with 1 hidden layer and 256 nodes, having 3 features as input, and it achieved an overall MSE of 0.0427% on the test datasets. Further, the GRU network improved the prediction performance by achieving an overall MSE of 0.0176% on the same. The details of the implementation are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Bolstering Biometric Cryptosystems with Tailored Scale Invariance Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Biometric CryptoSystem(BCS) is the field of study that imparts the advantages of cryptography for providing secure access to the biometric based authentication systems. The two biometric samples from the same user can vary significantly, due to factors such as noise, orientation, scaling variability etc. These factors need to be addressed while developing any BCS method. Every BCS has three phases: enrollment, authentication and encryption/decryption phase. The core component of every BCS is key, which is used to encrypt/decrypt the data. The robustness of the key depends on the quality of extracted features. There are numerous methods available in literature for handling key. This work involves the construction of key from the biometric features of the user by offering it the scale invariance property. This property is achieved by exploiting Scale Invariant Feature Transform method for feature extraction. This key is further used to encrypt/decrypt the data. The proposed method is simulated on three datasets for three different biometric modalities to generalize its results. The results are evaluated using several performance measures and standardization is achieved by comparing its results with state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Building Fault-Tolerant Wireless Access Networks with Network Coding
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Network coding has been diagnosed as an approach to beautify the overall performance of access networks. In such networks, community coding permits a sure level of fault tolerance as each communication node can feature as a transmitter and a receiver. By means of enabling the nodes to perform simultaneous encoding and interpreting operations, network coding can ensure a reliable verbal exchange over wireless gets admission to the network even in the presence of unreliable links and nodes. It could be accomplished by sending redundant records across diverse parts of the network to boost the probability of recuperating the facts in case of any loss. Moreover, network coding can reduce the overhead generated by means of the retransmission of misplaced packets. It may lead to an advanced throughput of the communication. Wireless, due to its flexibility in managing screw-ups, network coding is a powerful technique to construct robust and fault-tolerant entries to networks.

articleTitle: Harnessing Machine Learning based sequence prediction for Industry 4.0 applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the utilization of gyro sensor data, particularly from the MPU6050 sensor, for sequence prediction and positional analysis for many Industry 4.0 application and asset monitoring. Leveraging machine learning algorithms such as Random Forest, Decision Trees etc., a robust classification model is developed to predict sequences of positions with notable accuracy. Data collection involves capturing gyro sensor readings across distinct positions, laying the foundation for subsequent analysis. Integration with the Thingsboard platform facilitates data processing and analysis, showcasing the effectiveness of this integrated approach. Additionally, a user-friendly interface is designed for streamlined data input and visualization of prediction outcomes, enhancing accessibility and usability. The model demonstrates high accuracy in predicting sequences of positions using Random Forest and Decision Trees algorithms. The Random Forest and Decision tree approach provides higher accuracy when compared with the other algorithms. A IoT based hardware is designed in Kicad and tested to validate the ML based prediction for shop floor applications.

articleTitle: Three-Port Converter System for Street Lighting with Advanced Power Flow Management
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper details the power flow management in a three-port converter (TPC) for a solar lighting system. Integrating a photovoltaic (PV) source, battery storage, and load, it optimizes energy use and ensures a reliable power supply. The TPC enables efficient power transfer, allowing seamless energy flow from the PV source to the battery for charging and from the battery to the load. The system, derived from traditional DC/DC converters, operates in buck mode for daytime charging and boost mode for nighttime LED power. Controlled by a Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) signal, the bidirectional converter ensures effective power flow. Simulation and experimental results validate the system, with prototype testing demonstrating performance under various conditions.

articleTitle: Reducing the delay of Non-volatile memory by Common centroid matching in sense amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Since memory is a storage component, it is the brain of the microprocessor and system on a chip. One of the important circuits in memory is the sense amplifier (SA), which is only active when stored data is being retrieved from memory. While designing analog and mixed-signal circuits, layout-dependent effects (LDEs) invariably result in performance reductions at low technology nodes. The three main LDE sources—the well proximity effect (WPE), length of diffusion (LOD), and oxide-to-oxide spacing effect (OSE)—have a substantial influence on transistor threshold voltage and carrier mobility. These have an impact on post-layout simulation, which increases sense amplifier delay.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Automatic Detection of Bike Riders with No Helmet
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Riding motorbikes with a helmet is very essential and important as they may help prevent fatal head injuries in case of an accident. Helmet detection is an important and challenging vision task in traffic surveillance to avoid accidents for bike riders. As motorbike accidents have been growing in many countries due to the lack of traffic law power and mainly due to the negligence of the bike rider. With the help of the proposed method, we can detect bikers with no helmet and extract their license number plate for issuing a fine. This paper presents an automatic helmet detection method combining, Feature descriptor and DNN-classifier. Where the system is trained with predefined datasets and DNN (Deep Neural Networks) classifier is used to classify the objects. Pre-processing, Feature extraction, and Classification make up the proposed method of operation. This study suggests a system for classifying whether or not the cyclist is wearing a helmet. Regarding robustness and effectiveness, this technique offers high rates of accurate detection.

articleTitle: Exploring the Landscape of Diabetic Retinopathy Diagnosis: Insights from Extensive Literature Review and Preliminary Fundus Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study conducts a thorough analysis of one hundred important publications regarding the diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy (DR), with a particular emphasis on retinal fundus and OCT (Optical Coherence Tomography) images. In this work initial results on eye retinal fundus images are provided, including scaling, grayscale conversion, and image improvement as a part of pre-processing work. Area under Curve models, distributive deep learning strategies, high-accuracy models, and novel techniques such deep learning ensembles and segmentation algorithms were all included in the initial study. Our analysis condenses the conversation to 15 key researches and clarifies the techniques used, dataset variances, and implications for diagnosing diabetic retinopathy early. It highlights effective tactics while recognizing current constraints, highlighting how crucial early intervention is.

articleTitle: Edge Computing Devices Authentication using Quantum Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Edge computing allows different technologies such as Internet of Things (IoT), vehicle-to-vehicle communications(V V), Industrial IOT (IIOT) to connect to the cloud computing to facilitate end users. The edge networks uses low bandwidth, and enhances the processing speed. With more number of IoT devices connected in the network the privacy of data stored at the edge server also under threat. Authentication is a major challenge which is be addressed to provide security and privacy to IoT devices connected in the network. The existing works uses cryptographic algorithms to solve the authentication problems, but with increase in growth of quantum computers and quantum computing, breaking the complex cryptographic algorithm is not an issue. Hence one should adopt the quantum approach to provide authentication in edge network. The proposed work uses quantum key and context information of IoT devices to store in the edge server using blockchain, which proves to be more secure. The performance analysis shows that it is better with respect to registration, encryption, decryption and authentication of IoT devices.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Online Machine Learning Frameworks for Anomaly Detection in IoT Data Streams
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With the rapid progress of technology, the Internet of Things (IoT) is vital in connecting real-time data sources. These sources generate a substantial volume of streaming data through various applications. When dealing with streaming data, there can be a significant amount of abnormal data, referred to as anomalies, which are completely unknown and can negatively affect the system’s performance. In this context, unsupervised anomaly detection methods are expected to perform better than supervised methods. In this paper, we evaluate the performance scores of nine unsupervised anomaly detection models belonging to two recently introduced online machine learning frameworks: River and Python Streaming Anomaly Detection (PySAD). The methodologies investigated in the River framework include Half Space Trees (HST), Quantile Filter One-Class Support Vector Machine (QF_OCSVM), Quantile Filter Half Space Trees (QF_HST), and Threshold Filter Half Space Trees (TF_HST). The Histogram-Based Outlier Scores (HBOS), Kitsune’s core Algorithms (KitNet), Robust Random Cut Forest (RRCF), Isolation Forest Anomaly Streaming Data (IForestASD), and K Nearest Neighbor Conformal Anomaly Detection (KNNCAD) belong to the PySAD framework. The models are compared in terms of Accuracy, Sensitivity, Specificity, and ROCAUC on the IoTID20 streaming dataset. The paper concludes with a comparative study through performance plots on both frameworks. The River models HST, QF_HST, and TF_HST attained the highest Sensitivity scores of 1.00, whereas only the PySAD model KitNet passed this Sensitivity level. articleTitle: Innovations In Hr Analytics By Using Swarm Based Ann For Employee Performance Prediction

articleTitle: Comparison of Encryption Time for Multi-level Authentication in Cloud using Lightweight Cryptography Method over Chipper Text-PolicyAttribute Based Encryption Algorithm

articleTitle: Time-Efficient Diagnostics Using AI/ML Algorithms in Smart Healthcare

articleTitle: Aggregate Rating Prediction for Restaurants using regression techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Food supply is a fast-growing industry, as the enthusiasm to taste different kinds of food increases in people, the industry develops itself. The development of any business requires learning, learning from past mistakes and never making the mistake that makes a good business. In this paper, we take the worldwide spread data of the restaurants and their cuisines with their locations from Zomato API an online food delivery service. Zomato provides the restaurant data with the Aggregate rating and the features that affect the rating. articleTitle: Exploring Neural Dynamics in a Recurrent On-Center Off-Surround Network: Insights from a Go/No-Go Task Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Understanding decision-making mechanisms is crucial in neuroscience. Here, we introduce a computational model employing recurrent on-center off-surround neural networks to simulate neural activity during go/no-go tasks. In our model, the beta parameter represents lateral inhibition, a critical factor in neural processing. Previous studies have shown that successful enumeration of numerosities at smaller (subitization) and larger (estimation) ranges requires high and low inhibition, respectively. We utilize signal detection theory (SDT) to analyze the simulation output, focusing on hit and false alarm rates to elucidate the model’s performance. Our model systematically explores the impact of beta on neural activity, considering different input stimuli configurations. By computing mean neural activity and deriving hit and false alarm rates, along with their corresponding z-scores, we unveil the model’s sensitivity and specificity. Furthermore, we integrate executive functions and enumeration in human perception, providing insights into how cognitive processes influence neural dynamics during decision-making tasks. Our findings contribute to understanding the neural basis of cognitive processes, highlighting the role of lateral inhibition in facilitating successful enumeration across different numerosity ranges.

articleTitle: Leveraging AI to Unlock the Potential of Data Science
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The application of synthetic Intelligence (AI) to records science has spread out a massive array of new possibilities. Via the combination of advanced evaluation strategies, effective understanding-pushed system gaining knowledge of algorithms, and modern computing architectures, AI is allowing researchers to quick and as it should be discover insights from huge and complicated datasets. Furthermore, AI tools are offering corporations with the ability to make higher and more knowledgeable choices from the evaluation of hundreds of thousands of statistics points. The skills of information technology powered by means of AI are revolutionizing industries which includes healthcare, finance, and manufacturing-producing savings, uncovering efficiencies, and identifying new opportunities.
