abstract: Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have emerged as an effective approach for photograph illustration and caption-era obligations. In this paper, we gift a singular GCN architecture for photo caption technology that models visible relationships in a photo. The proposed architecture consists of essential additives: a kernel-based photograph illustration based totally on graph convolutional networks (GCNs) and a caption generator primarily based on the generated picture representation. To generate image captions, the generated photo illustration is fed to the caption generator, which is skilled in the use of supervised brand new. We compare our method on commonly used datasets that require the ability to generate captions for pix and demonstrate that our architecture achieves overall performance. Our outcomes show that by exploiting the nearby structure of modern-day images, the use of GCNs can successfully improve photograph captioning overall performance and imply the path of state-of-the-art future research in this field.

articleTitle: Pattern-Aware Motion Tracking and Estimation From Low-Resolution Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Sample-conscious motion monitoring and estimation from low-decision using deep studying is an exploratory studies have a look at that makes use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and deep mastering strategies for actual-time movement estimation and monitoring from low-decision photo sequences. Particularly, the study’s objectives are to increase a CNN version to examine the input-output correlation of excessive-resolution motion supply sequences and coffee-resolution check sequences, after which use the found out model to appropriately song the motion of targets in low-resolution photograph sequences. The model is then evaluated over a large set of actual-world photo sequences, with promising effects showing accurate monitoring of goals from low-decision pictures. This technique can be used to facilitate actual-time movement tracking in imaging programs along with surveillance, independent riding, and augmented truth.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Early Detection of Liver Ailments: Comprehensive Analysis and Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Liver diseases are a major global health issue, causing about 2 million deaths every year and costing over ${\$}$1 trillion, as reported by the World Health Organization (WHO). Conditions like cirrhosis and liver cancer are among the top causes of death worldwide, emphasizing the critical need for better ways to detect and treat these diseases. The early stages of many liver ailments often lack noticeable symptoms, making proactive detection and therapy essential. This analysis aims to evaluate the potency of advanced artificial intelligence techniques in identifying liver diseases, with the goal of reducing the cost and complexity associated with traditional diagnostic methods. Utilizing a comprehensive dataset of Indian liver patients, we meticulously pre-process the data to address issues like missing values, categorical feature encoding, and standardization. Our investigation encompasses five distinct machine learning algorithms, among which Ensemble Learning emerges as particularly promising, achieving an impressive precision rate of 84% on the test set. The significance of our research lies in its demonstration of artificial intelligence’s ability to accurately predict liver diseases, providing a valuable tool for early diagnosis and intervention. By highlighting the potential of predictive modelling, our findings advocate for the integration of these technologies into clinical practice, facilitating proactive healthcare management and ultimately improving outcomes for individuals with liver diseases.

articleTitle: ML based Web Application Firewall for Signature and Anomaly Detection Using Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In today’s digital landscape, web applications have become indispensable tools for businesses, facilitating access to vital data and services. However, this ubiquity also exposes them to a myriad of cyber threats, ranging from SQL injection to cross-site scripting. Traditional Web Application Firewalls (WAFs), while essential, often struggle with rule-based detection methods, leading to issues like false positives and an inability to adapt swiftly to emerging threats. This paper introduces an advanced Web Application Firewall (WAF) fortified with Machine Learning (ML) techniques, specifically a Random Forest classifier. The proposed WAF achieved nearly $\mathbf{1 0 0 \%}$ accuracy in classifying requests as normal or anomalous and $\mathbf{8 9. 5 \%}$ accuracy in distinguishing between different attack types. Furthermore, it significantly reduces computational time compared to traditional WAFs. By harnessing ML, the proposed WAF enhances web application security, effectively identifying and mitigating attacks while minimizing false positives, showcasing a practical ML-driven solution for safeguarding online assets against evolving cyber threats.

articleTitle: An Empirical State-of-art Analogy on Heart Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: These days, cardiovascular disease it’s an international issue. However, it is a fortunate reality that early intervention can reduce the mortality rate from heart disease, for which early identification is crucial. The objective of this work is to develop a future machine learning model that can recognize important qualities and predict cardiac sickness in its early stages using a variety of feature selection strategies. Then, to determine which model was the most optimistic and which feature subset fit the best, six different machine learning models were used: decision tree (C5), random forest (C4), K-nearest neighbor (C3), logistic regression (C1), and support vector machine (C2). The suggested model offers a lot of promise for clinical usage to predict cardiac disease in its early stages at a low cost and in a shorter amount of time, according to the performance of the applied model paired with specific variables.

articleTitle: Voice Genius : IT’s Echoes of Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The dynamic technology of today requires a framework that makes task automation simple. This study presents a unique AI helper that can have conversations that go beyond voice orders. With the use of sophisticated voice synthesis and speech recognition, this intelligent system can comprehend user input and react appropriately. Imagine using an integrated speaker to ask questions like “How’s traffic?” or “What’s the weather?” and getting quick, tailored answers. Because of its user-friendly interface, manual interaction is eliminated, allowing for hands-free ease. The assistant’s capacity for learning and adaptation also guarantees ongoing development, which improves user experience even more. This work paves the path for a time when people will be able to use technology to help them naturally achieve their goals because it represents a major development in conversational AI.

articleTitle: ElectroGuard: The Next Generation Pesticide Pump
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Pest management remains an important part of agricultural production and environmental sustainability, necessitating ongoing innovation in pesticide application techniques. This study introduces “ElectroGuard: The Next Generation Pesticide Pump,” a unique gadget meant to change pest control techniques by combining modern technology, ergonomic design principles, and renewable energy sources. Drawing on interdisciplinary research in pest control, renewable energy, ergonomics, and environmental science, this study thoroughly investigates ElectroGuard’s design, performance characteristics, and implications for sustainable agriculture and environmental stewardship. The study begins by looking at the concerns with standard pesticide administration methods, such as efficacy, efficiency, and environmental impact. It then describes ElectroGuard as a transformative solution, emphasizing aspects such as solar panel technology, ergonomic design elements, and improved safety mechanisms. The study’s extensive research of ElectroGuard’s efficacy, efficiency, and usability indicates its capacity to offer precise and targeted pesticide application while limiting environmental impact and improving user comfort. The study also explores ElectroGuard’s implications for sustainable agriculture and environmental conservation. ElectroGuard takes a more environmentally responsible approach to pest management by utilizing renewable energy sources and reducing pesticide discharge, which aligns with the goals of sustainable agriculture and ecosystem preservation. Its ergonomic design elements lead to better operator well-being and productivity, hence increasing the overall sustainability of pest management operations.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Multi-Factor Authentication for Preventing Cyber Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: this article affords an outline of the effectiveness of multi-thing authentication (MFA) for stopping cyber attacks. MFA is an authentication procedure that combines or greater elements or traits to verify the identification of a character or user earlier than granting them access. This sort of authentication is increasingly being used to protect non-public data and to prevent unauthorized get admission to systems and services. Diverse studies have been carried out to evaluate the effectiveness of MFA as compared to traditional authentication methods, like passwords. The outcomes of these studies show that after properly implemented, MFA may be a powerful method to shield towards cyber-assaults. This article also presents satisfactory practices for implementing MFA to maximize its effectiveness and discusses risks related to using MFA.

articleTitle: Precision Agriculture: Enhancing Potato Disease Classification using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Potato, a highly cultivated and sought-after crop globally, ranks among the top crops alongside rice and wheat. Widely embraced as an occupation in over 125 countries, potato farming faces challenges, particularly infections and diseases. Typically, these problems fall into one of two categories: Both early and late blights have the potential to seriously damage crops and lower yield production. This research underscores the potential of Deep Learning (DL) methods in the categorization of potato diseases, providing valuable insights for the development of effective and automated disease management strategies. We employed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to conduct a classification of potato leaf diseases. This research study encompasses the preprocessing of leaf image data, the training of a CNN model on this data, and an evaluation of the model’s performance on a test set. Our tests indicate the CNN model excels in identifying potato leaf diseases-Early Blight (EB), Late Blight (LB), and Healthy conditions-with an impressive 97% accuracy.

articleTitle: Evaluating Recurrent Neural Network Architectures for Natural Language Understanding
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper examines and evaluates the effectiveness of recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures for natural language knowledge. The paper starts by imparting historical data on recurrent neural networks and their software to various responsibilities. It then goes on to talk about diverse RNN architectures, such as lengthy quick-time period reminiscence (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Bonior Recurrent Neural network (BONN). The paper then focuses on the efficacy of each RNN structure for textual content expertise obligations. A sequence of experiments is carried out to degree the overall performance of the one-of-a-kind fashions, the use of 3 preferred datasets-Wiki text, Squad and IMDB, as well as two newly created datasets. The paper analyses the empirical consequences of the various RNN architectures and finds that LSTM fashions are normally satisfactory performers, although BONN architectures can also be aggressive in some cases. The paper additionally looks at numerous techniques to enhance performance, which include pre-processing and hyper-parameter tuning. The paper concludes that, whilst RNN architectures are powerful for herbal language know-how responsibilities, the exact architecture and parameters can also need to be chosen cautiously, relying on the project and dataset to hand.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Performance of Lightweight Gradient Boosting and Random Forest Methods for Producing Effective Nutritional Diet Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The aim of the research is to recommend Efficient Nutrition and diet to patients using Light weighted gradient Boosting compared over Ensemble Random Forest to improve accuracy. In order to provide patients with food and nutrition recommendations, models were created that make use of a simple gradient boosting technique and Ensemble Random Forest. The suggested system is implemented with the help of a python programming tool. By using the Gpower 3.1 software (g power setting parameters alpha:0.05 and G power $=0.8$). Light Weighted gradient boosting is used for Group 1 and Naive Bayes with 10 sample sizes is used for Group 2. The outcome of the patients is monitoring the health conditions. The recommended light weighted gradient boosting algorithm classifier accuracy level is confirmed with 92.45%. Gradient Boosting Algorithm and Random Forest classifier’s processing time is also calculated. The recommended light weighted gradient boosting algorithm classifier accuracy level is confirmed with 92.45% with a significance of $0.001(\mathrm{p}{\lt}0.05)$. This recommended research process result says that it is finalized that the accuracy rate of Light Weighted Gradient Boosting Algorithm is 92.60% makes better results in Efficient Nutrition and the accuracy rate of Random Forest is 87.80%. The loss value of the light weighted boosting Algorithm is 7.58% and Random Forest loss rate is about 12.35%.

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of Security and Privacy in Machine Learning for Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Smart agriculture has currently become a closely researched and competitive field as it gives many methods to optimize farming operations. From monitoring crop and soil fitness to applying precise fertilizer and water input to yield prediction, device learning technology has been validated to be beneficial in largely enhancing the satisfaction of agricultural practices. But, as the evolved ML systems are increasingly integrated into one-of-a-kind factors of the farming technique, the interactions between ML algorithms and touchy information emerge as a challenge of vital interest. The position of safety and privateers in ML for smart agriculture is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the brought artifacts. Without proper safety and privacy measures, sensitive statistics, which include non-public data, private locations, and vital agricultural secrets and techniques, are at risk of malicious exploitation. Consequently, security and privacy strategies must be promoted to defend the machine from potential exploits or (interior) assaults and keep the privacy of all parties worried with the aid of not disclosing, enhancing, or disposing of personal statistics. There are numerous methods to address the safety and privacy problems in the context of ML for smart agriculture. Examples consist of using anonymization strategies for facts safety, the adoption of access manipulation mechanisms to defend facts availability, the implementation of pertinent encryption algorithms to keep integrity, and the development of specific protocols and records models to keep confidentiality.

articleTitle: A Blockchain-Based Scheme to Prevent the Sybil Attack in VANET
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Security and privacy are always major issues in Vehicular ad hoc networks. For ensuring privacy and avoiding tracking of the vehicle, recently some researchers proposed the idea of providing multiple pseudo identities to the vehicles. Although multiple pseudo identity approach provides anonymity, it could lead to a harmful type of attack called Sybil attack, in which a vehicle poses as multiple vehicles using the multiple identities at the same time. In this paper, a blockchain based decentralized approach has been proposed to mitigate the Sybil attack. In this approach, the blockchain utilization reduces the dependency on certificate authority which results in less computation and communication delay for verification of identities. Further, with the security analysis of this scheme, different security features of the scheme have been proved. Finally, for evaluating the performance and efficiency of the proposed scheme, simulation has been done using NS3 and SUMO environments.

articleTitle: Knowledge Retention in Incremental Learning using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: We are attempting to address the problem of catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, in which the model forgets previously learned information upon learning new information. So, we are trying to train a model on some tasks and then utilize the updated weights and parameters for the new task while preserving the model’s ability to perform classification of the old and new tasks correctly. Also, as the model must learn a vast amount of new information over time, it is impossible to store all the information as the model will have limited memory. Therefore, the model should also learn what to forget and what not to forget. This research proposed a new approach for continual learning that draws inspiration from the way Hebbian learning occurs in biological systems. The relevance of each neural network parameter is calculated during model training based on the sensitivity of the final output function that changes in the parameter. Modifying parameters during the training of a new task will impose penalties, thereby avoiding the loss of important knowledge from previous tasks. Using the AlexNet model, we are putting our strategy to the test on several object identification tasks.

articleTitle: Enhancing Indoor Navigation Efficiency with WiFi Signal Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the contemporary digital landscape, efficient indoor navigation has become imperative for large, intricate spaces like shopping malls, airports, hospitals, and universities. Traditional GPS-based methods often prove inadequate in these indoor settings due to poor reception and a lack of fine-grained location accuracy. To address these challenges, the work employs WiFi signals, pervasive in modern buildings, and harnesses their ubiquity and reliability for sophisticated indoor navigation. The team developed a Python package for collecting WiFi signal details, implementing robust preprocessing to filter out private networks, and storing the data in a database. The core of the system lies in a machine learning ensemble consisting of Gaussian Bayes classifier, decision tree, and K-nearest neighbors (KNN). This ensemble utilizes WiFi signal strengths to predict users’ real-time positions within large indoor spaces. The system aims to enhance user experiences and simplify wayfinding in complex indoor environments.

articleTitle: Autonomous UAV Navigation in Indoor Corridor Environments by a Depth Estimator based on a Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Indoor Navigation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is a challenging research problem that has gained attention in the present decade. This work proposes a system that facilitates a UAV with a monocular vision-based front camera to always face the vanishing point of an unknown corridor when it is at an equidistant position from the two walls. The proposed system utilizes the MiDaS depth estimator, which takes a monocular image and provides its corresponding depth map, which is then fed into a vanishing point locator that tries to predict the location of the vanishing point of the corridor by identifying and clustering the deepest areas within the image and choosing the region closest to the image center. The proposed approach was tested on the UAVCorV1 dataset and compared to other existing methods. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach for autonomous UAV navigation. When combined with a system that brings the UAV precisely in between the two walls, a complete corridor navigation system can be realized.

articleTitle: Bridging the Modality Gap: Generative Adversarial Networks for T1-T2 MRI Image Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: CycleGAN, a significant deep learning model, has transformed medical imaging by providing a remedy for translating MRI images between different modalities. Its ability to transform T1-weighted to T2-weighted images is crucial in healthcare environments where obtaining multiple scans can be time-consuming and burdensome for patients. This can be achieved by utilizing CycleGAN, which generates images that contains vital information that will help the healthcare professionals to diagnose the patient without exposing them to further radiations. This unleashes an effective and safer way of diagnosing patients. The adaptability of CycleGAN also allows scalability and the ability to customize it for different types of medical images, where scanning can be achieved with less exposure to radiation, without loosing or compromising any important information.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Crowd Density and Motion Direction Estimation for Real-Time Crowd Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Efficient crowd management is essential for ensuring safety and security in various societal gatherings, such as public events and transportation hubs. Traditional crowd surveillance methods often fall short in handling the complexities inherent in large-scale gatherings. To address these challenges, this paper explores the application of computer vision techniques for crowd density estimation and motion direction analysis. The proposed approach investigates the integration of advanced computer vision algorithms to monitor crowd dynamics in real time. Leveraging state-of-the-art techniques like YOLOv8 for object detection, for optical flow estimation, we aim to achieve unparalleled accuracy in crowd analysis. We use the Lucas-Kanade optical flow combining with corner to track moving target. We use a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract local features in the preprocessed video. These features are sequenced utilizing a Long Short Term Memory (LSTM). The results of the proposed approach showcase the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately estimating crowd density and analyzing motion direction across diverse scenarios. Using computer vision, our mechanism provides timely insights into crowd behavior, enabling proactive interventions to prevent potential incidents and ensure public safety. This work underscores the pivotal role of advanced computer vision techniques in revolutionizing crowd management strategies.

articleTitle: Enhancing Legal Document Summarization for Professionals: An Extractive Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The increasing volume and complexity of legal documents pose significant challenges for legal professionals who must extract relevant information efficiently. This paper addresses this issue by focusing on extractive summarization of legal documents, a technique that selects key sentences to create concise summaries while retaining the original language and structure. We utilize a labeled dataset of legal judgments and their summaries, employing both binary and multi-class labeling methods to categorize sentences based on their summary-worthiness and segment type (Facts, Arguments, Issue, Analysis, or None). To enhance our dataset, we convert abstractive summaries into extractive formats and fine-tune our models using a combination of pre-existing datasets and our labeled data. We train and evaluate various models, including traditional machine learning algorithms, neural networks, and transformer-based models, using metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, ROUGE, and BERTScore. Our findings highlight the challenges posed by class imbalance and the need for domain-specific adaptations in legal document summarization. The proposed methodology aims to improve the efficiency and accuracy of processing legal texts, ultimately aiding legal practitioners in their work.

articleTitle: A Robust Technique for Prediction of Dementia Using Ensemble Voting Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Dementia is an ordinary term used to describe the decline in memory, language, problem-solving, and other cognitive abilities that significantly disrupt activities of daily living. Dementia can be caused by an assortment of diseases. In a global society where the elderly population continues to increase, dementia is becoming an increasing concern. Every three seconds, somebody in the world gets dementia. It will reach $\mathbf{7 8}$ million in 2030 and 135 million in 2050 [1]. Dementia costs more than US ${\$}$ 1.3 trillion a year around the world, and that number is expected to reach US ${\$}2.8$ trillion by 2030 [2]. Despite its high prevalence within the community, this mental health condition remains inadequately identified, reported, and even partially comprehended. As a result of the exponential growth of computational power, scholars have created machine learning (ML) methods for the detection and diagnosis of neurodegenerative diseases. This paper aims to accelerate the prediction of dementia at an early stage in an individual’s development. Our experiment’s findings reveal that the Voting Classifier outperforms other methods, with an impressive prediction accuracy of 99.9%.

articleTitle: Study of Quantum Dot Solar Cell Including CdTe Quantum Dots Embedded in Al0.3 Ga0.7 As/GaAs Quantum Wells
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Intermediate Band Solar Cells were proposed in 1997 as an alternative to tandem solar cells to achieve high efficiency in a photovoltaic device. It has a proposed theoretical limit of $63.2 \%$, much higher than the 33% of a single-junction solar cell. In this study, we explore the photovoltaic performance of CdTe Quantum Dots embedded in $\mathrm{Al}_{0.3} \mathbf{G a}_{0.7} \mathrm{As} / \mathrm{GaAs}$ Quantum Wells for the first time using SCAPS-1D software. This arrangement leads to the formation of intermediate energy levels due to Quantum Confinement, which has been exploited to form a Hole Injection Layer and increase Quantum Efficiency. Further, a detailed study of the device’s band diagram in both illuminated and illuminated cases is provided, offering crucial insights into its performance and working. The best-optimized device yielded a maximum power conversion efficiency of $31.8 \%$, Quantum Efficiency (QE) of $\mathbf{8 0 \%}$ over the visible range, open-circuit voltage $V_{O C}$ of 1.36 and fill factor ($F=$ r) ranging between $\mathbf{7 7 \% - 8 5 \%}$.

articleTitle: Innovative Arduino-Based Solar Panel Cleaning System for Enhanced Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The objective of this project is to design and develop an Arduino based cleaning system for solar panel. As electricity rates rise and environmental concerns over fossil fuels grow, more and more renewable energy sources, including solar power, are being used. Solar power is mostly harvested using arrays composed of photovoltaic panels. The purpose of solar panels is to use the sun’s light as a source of energy to create electricity. The solar photovoltaic modules are typically used in dusty conditions. Dust and particle buildup on even one panel in an array significantly lowers the panels’ ability to generate electricity, underscoring the importance of maintaining the panels’ surfaces clean. The electrical parameters of a solar panel are susceptible to the density of accumulated dust, which can impact the panel’s absorption capacity and ultimately lower its efficiency. Cleaning the dust that has built on solar panels is one way to improve their performance. Manual cleaning of the solar panels is done, but it is not dependable or cost-effective because labor costs and time are rising. In order to get around the aforementioned problems, an Arduino UNO system with a sprinkler mechanism is suggested. This system offers an affordable and scalable solution to remove the dust accumulated on solar panel.

articleTitle: EEG-Based Scalogram Imaging and Deep Learning for Insomnia Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Insomnia is one of the most widespread sleep disorders described by the difficulties with falling asleep or staying asleep. Ensuring fast, accurate, and efficient diagnosis and treatment of the disorder is often quite challenging. Classical methods of diagnostics are quite expensive and are often limited to subjective observation and polysomnography, which is also expensive, time-consuming, and ineffective for various complicated sleep disorders. To address these issues, the following work offers a novel approach based on the pictures of the quarried scalograms, which are obtained after training the deep learning model called DenseNet-121 and learning the electroencephalogram signals.Our work aims to overcome the limitations of common clinical approaches through novel non-invasive techniques enabled by recent progress in machine learning and neuroimaging technologies. Scalogram images derived from the analysis of EEG signals implicated in sleep, provides an essential combination of the temporal and spectral information to depict sleeping patterns. Finally, while using the cutting-edge deep learning architecture DenseNet-121, which has proven a high classification performance in images to distill the critical features of scalogram images created through processing previously obtained EEG signals to successfully detect and classify the presence of insomnia.With a dataset consisting of EEG signals captured at 512 Hz and converted into 1024 scalogram pictures, we were able to identify insomnia with an astonishing 99.51% classification accuracy through careful experimentation and analysis. With this high degree of accuracy, our approach, called ScaloNet-121, exhibits promise as a reliable and workable replacement for diagnosing sleep issues, providing a promising path for data-driven, non-invasive sleep problem diagnosis.

articleTitle: Implementing Calorie Burnt Prediction Through XGBOOST Algorithm Compared Over Random Forest Regressor
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research aims to evaluate the XGBoost algorithm and the Lasso Regression approach for their respective abilities to forecast caloric expenditure during physical activity. Tools and Techniques for Scientific Investigation: Information such as calorie burn rates from different activities are included into the planned research. The XGBoost technique and state-of-the-art Lasso Regression were among the machine learning technologies used to ascertain these calories. The XGBoost method employs Innovative Lasso Regression sampling with a 10-sample size and a 0.8 G power value. According to an independent sample T-test, the two methods’ accuracy varies by 0.001 ($\mathbf{p}{\lt}0.05$). The average of the two approaches is 72.26, and the average detection accuracy is $\pm 2 S D$. In conclusion, the innovative Lasso Regression approach achieved a 72.35% accuracy rate, but the XGBoost strategy achieved an accuracy rate of 83.73%.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Smart Helmet for Responsible Driving and Accident Prevention
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The goal of this research work is to create a bike system that can be equipped with a helmet to stop collisions and injuries. In the event of an accident, the system will send the GPS module locations to pre-fed contacts and detect alcohol. The objective is to lower the number of accidents brought on by drunk driving, which is a significant accident cause in India. The goal of the development is to create an electronic circuit that stops intoxicated drivers from starting a vehicle, hence lowering the amount of accidents brought on by alcohol use.

articleTitle: Assessing the Progress of Natural Language Processing Algorithms in Drug Discovery
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This technical summary reviews recent improvements in natural language processing (NLP) algorithms and their use in drug discovery, with a focus on analyzing drug discovery fulfillment metrics. NLP techniques are being used to assist in exploring relationships amongst organic concepts consisting of protein-protein interactions, gene-gene interactions, and text mining for drug-disorder institutions. An expansion of research initiatives has emerged with the goal of applying NLP algorithms to drug discovery, and a lot of those initiatives have visible, tangible successes. Using a spread of methods, including category, facts extraction, and clustering, those algorithms demonstrate the potential to pick out novel drug and goal interactions. The effectiveness of those algorithms and the progress of modern-day drug discovery research are both evaluated and mentioned. In the long run, NLP algorithms are proving to be a beneficial tool in drug discovery research and have the potential for even extra destiny fulfillment.

articleTitle: Flexible and High Throughput Designs of 4-Stage Operational Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Operational amplifiers play a major role in analog and mixed signal integrated circuits. This paper proposes flexible and high throughput 4 -stage operational amplifier designs. The former case is flexible to perform the amplifications of 2-stage, 3-stage, and 4-stage. The later case performs two operational amplifications in parallel to improve the throughput. All the existing and proposed designs are implemented using 90 nm CMOS technology with Cadence. The synthesis results show the proposed high throughput 4-stage operational amplifier I achieves an improvement of 45.6% as compared with the conventional 4stage operational amplifier.

articleTitle: Interactive Smart Platform for Commodity Exchange
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the dynamic landscape of e-commerce, the evolution of web applications continually strives to enhance user engagement and satisfaction. This paper is mainly intended to deploy a website for in-campus trading and presents a novel approach to enriching the online shopping experience for the university students. The application facilitates seamless product uploads, wishlist management and others alongwith a groundbreaking feature enabling direct communication between users and product owners in real-time. The following introduction outlines the significance of this innovative approach and its potential impact on modern e-commerce platforms.

articleTitle: Investigating the Use of Virtual Private Networks on ATM Network Security
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Digital personal Networks have been increasingly utilized in ATM networks for ease of communication. This paper studies the use of VPNs over ATM networks, providing a synopsis of their features and advantages and discussing bible safety threats. The paper also explains VPNs, their sub-types, and how they may be implemented in ATM surroundings; observing takes place once they provide additional protection capabilities while used on ATM networks; we also talk about the fate of VPNs throughout ATM networks, precisely due to the risk posed by using Internet-based providers. These novel results are encouraging and indicate that VPNs may also offer a solution for securing ATM transactions and protecting network data from threat actors.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Hyperparameter Tuning in Deep Learning Models using Bayesian Optimization and XAI
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Plant disease detection is a crucial step in improving the quantity and quality of farm products since many plant diseases that arise in rice crops reduce the production of agriculture and cause financial loss. The manual evaluation of plant health is tiring and time consuming. Combining optimization algorithms with deep learning architectures can lead to more effective and efficient plant disease detection, with improved accuracy and generalization capabilities. This paper presents a comparison study on hyperparameter tuning of deep learning architectures for early detection of rice plant diseases. The hyperparameter tuning was performed by incorporating Bayesian Optimization algorithm on CNN, ResNet, MobileNet, InceptionNet and RegNet. The experimental study is conducted on dataset containing 1007 images of rice seed crop that contains 501 images of healthy samples and 506 unhealthy samples. Performance evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision and inference time are employed to compare models. Additionally, a comparative analysis using explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is conducted to visualize the interpretability of hyperparameter combinations and their impact on disease detection.

articleTitle: Restaurant Recommendation using Map-Reduce and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: There are a lot of restaurants to pick from these days, so it might be difficult for folks to locate a new location to eat. It can be challenging to choose one that precisely suits their preferences. Customers’ perceptions of a restaurant are greatly influenced by what other people have to say about its cleanliness and food quality. Unfavorable reviews may cause someone to question if they will like the dish or have a positive experience. People enjoy having a system that makes recommendations for them when they are looking through various products, especially those that are highly recommended. This saves time and money. However, it is crucial that this system only displays products that align with the user’s preferences. Our work proposes a novel recommendation system that combines two approaches: collaborative filtering (CF) and content-based filtering (CBF) to provide personalized recommendations to users. To determine what a user might like, CBF considers their past actions. However, in certain cases, insufficient data may make it difficult for it to distinguish between distinct products, which reduces the quality of its recommendations. Conversely, CF leverages user interactions to recommend related products that users may find interesting. However, in certain cases, insufficient interaction data among users also leads to issues. Although there are drawbacks to both of these approaches, we have been developing strategies to address these concerns in order to improve the recommendation system.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive and Comparative Examination of Machine Learning Techniques for Diabetes Mellitus Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Selecting the optimal machine learning (ML) approach is paramount in healthcare and medical informatics to ensure precise predictions that align with the dataset’s inherent characteristics. In this study, we explore the field of diabetes prognosis by employing five distinct ML models: Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), and k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN), to evaluate their efficacy in predicting future diabetic diagnoses. Our findings reveal that the RF classifier emerges as the most effective model, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of $\mathbf{9 2. 2 3 \%}$. This exceptional performance is attributed to its proficiency in navigating the intricate web of complex and non-linear relationships embedded within the input features. In contrast, the LR model demonstrated less favorable outcomes, with a comparatively modest accuracy score of $\mathbf{7 4. 4 2 \%}$. These results underscore the importance of utilizing sophisticated ML algorithms capable of discerning nuanced patterns in healthcare datasets, thereby equipping clinicians with robust predictive tools to enhance patient care and prognosis.

articleTitle: Return Loss and Bandwidth improvement of Circular ring antenna for 5G Sub-6GHz N77, N8 and, N79 band applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents a modified widebandcircular patch antenna tailored for 5G Sub-6GHz N77, N78, andN79 band applications. At first, a circular patch antenna with acomplete ground plane was devised, followed by incorporating and optimizing a circular slot, partial ground slots, and stubs to cover the desired frequency bands. The proposed antenna occupies a volume of $35 \times 25 \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$ and is mounted on an FR4 substrate with a permittivity of 4.4. The simulation findings show that the operational bandwidth extends from 3.04 GHz to 5.35 GHz. The use of partial ground contributes to the antenna’s wideband characteristics while introducing slots and stubs, which aids in achieving impedance matching and enhancing radiation characteristics. The wideband circular patch antenna showcases favorable performance, enabling effective operation across a wide frequency range, characterized by a high return loss of – 45 dB. The antenna achieves a maximum gain of 4.5 dBand a Radiation Efficiency of approximately 95%. Evaluation and optimization of the antenna’s performance parameters are conducted using the High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS).

articleTitle: Incremental Learning in Generative Adversarial Networks(GANs) using Pseudo Replay to overcome Catastrophic Forgetting
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The process of incremental learning in generative adversarial networks (GANs) presents an immense challenge in the form of catastrophic forgetting, which occurs when the network is trained on novel data and subsequently forgets previously acquired information. Diverse replay methods, which entail replaying previously generated data to the network during training, have been proposed as a solution to this problem. Different kinds of replay methods utilized in incremental learning for GANs are examined in this paper, including hybrid replay, generative replay, and discriminative replay. In addition, the difficulties of implementing pseudo-replay approaches in GANs are examined, along with the current state of the art in this domain. In conclusion, we conduct an exhaustive assessment of various replay techniques across multiple benchmark datasets, elucidating their respective merits and drawbacks. Based on our research outcomes, it appears that incremental learning in GANs can be substantially enhanced through the use of pseudo-replay methods. Furthermore, we find that hybrid replay methods, which integrate generative and discriminative replay, yield the most favourable results. Regarding the MNIST and SVHN datasets, our method has achieved an accuracy improvement of approximately $\mathbf{7 \%}$ and $20 \%$ compared to the current leading techniques for 5 -tasks. Similarly, for 10 tasks, our average accuracy is $10 \%$ and $19 \%$ higher than the state-of-the-art for the MNIST and SVHN datasets.

articleTitle: Geometric Feature-Based Classification of Anemia in Blood Smear Images using Decision Tree

articleTitle: Design of Square Microstrip Patch E-Slotted Antenna at 28 GHz for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The research presented herein provides a comprehensive analysis of a square patch antenna featuring an E slot design tailored specifically for 5G wireless communication applications. This study meticulously explores the utilization of bandwidth in facilitating effective communication within the 5G spectrum. The suggested antenna design showcases the implementation of the microstrip feeding technique, a pivotal aspect of its operational framework. Within the scope of this investigation, an array of performance parameters including antenna bandwidth, return loss, gain, voltage standing wave ratio, efficiency, and directivity are meticulously evaluated and documented. The proposed antenna configuration is characterized by a dielectric constant of 2.2, strategically chosen to optimize its performance within the intended frequency range. Operating at a frequency of 28 GHz, the antenna design is meticulously engineered utilizing an RT Duroid substrate 5880, distinguished by a height dimension of 1.5 mm. Noteworthy is the considerable bandwidth of 5.11 GHz exhibited by the proposed antenna, underscoring its efficiency in facilitating robust communication within the 5 G domain. Through comparative analysis, the study highlights the superior performance of the proposed square patch antenna when juxtaposed against prevailing methodologies. Simulation activities integral to this study are conducted utilizing CST software, ensuring a rigorous evaluation and validation of the proposed design’s effectiveness. The obtained parameters of the designed antenna are Gain 6.48 dBi, directivity 6.77 dB, bandwidth 5.19 GHz, return loss 27 dB and VSWR 1.09. By elucidating the comparative advantages and enhanced performance metrics of the proposed antenna configuration, this research endeavour contributes significantly to the advancement of 5G wireless communication technologies.

articleTitle: Intelligent Waste Management Systems Using Deep Belief Network in Smart Cities

articleTitle: Investigating the Potential of Sentimental Analysis Algorithms in E-Commerce

articleTitle: Comprehensive Review of Quantum Cellular Automata Based Nano Router Circuit Design for Nano Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Digital communication systems rely on several key components to transmit and receive data efficiently. Within these systems, encoders, decoders, parity generators, parity checkers, and routers play critical roles. Among them, the router stands out as a pivotal component, facilitating effective data communication and transfer. Notably, Nano routers, employing Quantum-dot Cellular Automata (QCA) technology, has evolved as game-changers in this domain. By harnessing QCA technology, Nano routers significantly enhance communication capabilities while simultaneously reducing area, delay, and power consumption. This article presents a comprehensive survey of research articles pertaining to the design and implementation of Nano routers and its design components using QCA technology. It delves into the innovative strides made in this field and unveils new and effective designs for Nano routers. The synergy of cutting-edge technology and novel design concepts promises to revolutionize digital communication, offering faster, more efficient, and power-conscious data transmission in an increasingly connected world.

articleTitle: Stochastic Event Detection and Quantization for Catastrophe Prevention
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Schools, stadiums, malls, and other locations that are frequented by large volumes of people can be described as Soft Targets and Crowded Places (ST-CPs). The relative lack of comprehensive security measures at these locations unfortunately results in ST-CPs being seen as prime targets for mass attacks that require little to no planning, including shootings, stabbings, and bombings. These attacks are significant security risks, as they are often difficult to detect and are carried out rapidly. To effectively prevent such attacks and minimize the damage caused, it is necessary to implement intelligent surveillance systems that are able to conduct risk assessments in real time and from a distance. When covering such large and dynamic areas as ST-CPs, it is important to use network control systems that consist of numerous individual sensors placed at various key locations. These sensors must communicate rapidly and reliably in order to ensure a swift response, meaning that data must be shared quickly and without degradation. Much of our research has been focused on Quantized Stabilization Stochastic Network Control Systems. Quantization errors are among the most common compression issues found in network communications. Our work is concerned with the most viable strategies for minimizing such errors, including methods such as feedback stabilization of Markov jump linear systems with time varying delay. Soft Target Engineering to Neutralize the Threat Reality (SENTRY) is committed to protecting against the threats to ST-CPs detailed above, particularly through the use of semiautonomous Virtual Sentries placed at critical points that process large amounts of information to facilitate real-time responses.

Author Keywords: Soft Target Engineering to Neutralize the Threat Reality-SENTRY

articleTitle: Lung tumor detection using modified EfficientNet-B1
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Lung cancer has the greatest death rate and is the foremost predominant sort of cancer. CT scans are utilized to diagnose lung cancer because it produces detailed pictures of tumors within the body and track their development. CT scans of the lungs were handled using Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) to identify any sign of harm. The tests are carried out on the “IQOTH/NCCD” dataset for persons with lung cancer who have been classified as benign, malignant, or normal depending on whether or not they have lung cancer. The EfficientNet-B1 network takes the input image of size $240 \times 240$ pixels. The data augmentation techniques were used to address the class imbalance issue. The input image is passed through the seven blocks of the Modified EfficientNet-B1 architecture that consists of Convolutional layers, Mobile Inverted Bottleneck layers, Global average pooling 2D, Dropout and Dense layer. The Global average pooling 2D is used instead of max pooling and average pooling. The purpose of the Global average pooling layer is to diminish the dimensionality of an image by compressing the pixel values. The addition of layers to the block and modification of the hyperparameters lead to the increased accuracy. The Modified EfficientNet-B1 model achieved an accuracy of 99.4%. The proposed modified EfficientNet-B1 is compared with other pre-trained CNN models like VGG19, EfficientNet-B0 and EfficientNet-B1. The Modified EfficientNet-B1 performs better than other CNNs in terms of accuracy. The suggested approach is employed for widespread clinical setting deployment because it is fast and requires less parameters than other CNN-based models.

articleTitle: Enhancing Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Sensor Precision with Adaptive Genetic Algorithm aided Kalman Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Accurate sensor data is crucial for the successful operation of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) in various underwater missions. However, achieving precision in sensor data pose significant challenges due to dynamic underwater environments and inherent sensor limitations. This paper investigates the utilization of the Kalman filter, a mathematical model, to enhance sensor data accuracy in AUV navigation. But the filter performance is highly dependent on accurate noise covariance matrices (process noise covariance Q and measurement noise covariance R). In dynamic environments, these noise characteristics can change rapidly and unpredictably, making it difficult to maintain optimal filter performance. Furthermore, it explores the integration of Genetic Algorithms (GAs) with the Kalman filter to optimize its performance in dynamic conditions. The proposed hybrid approach, termed Adaptive Genetic Algorithm based Kalman Filter (AGAKF), dynamically adjusts filter parameters using GAs, ensuring optimal performance in real-time. The study evaluates the efficacy of the AGAKF method through extensive simulations and comparisons with traditional Kalman filtering coupled with genetic algorithm in MATLAB. Results demonstrate that the AGAKF approach achieves superior noise reduction and preserves signal characteristics more effectively, offering promising potential for enhancing AUV navigation accuracy in diverse underwater environments.

articleTitle: Driving Change: Leveraging Predictive Modeling and Geospatial Insights to Strengthen Road Safety Measures in India and USA

articleTitle: Detection of Diseases in Cardamom Leaves by Using Digital Image Feature Selection Techniques

articleTitle: Real Time Fake Logo Prediction System Using K-Nearest Neighbors in Comparison With Recurrent Neural Network

abstract: The aim of this study is to improve the Fake logo prediction using Novel K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) in comparison with Recurrent Neural Network (RNN). A new approach has been developed for predicting the authenticity of logos, which involves implementing novel KNN and RNN models. By varying the training and testing splits, the system can produce accurate results for identifying fake logos. Compared to the Support Vector Machine (SVM) model, the RNN model is better at capturing sequential information in images, resulting in more precise predictions. Meanwhile, the SVM model is more adept at identifying logos based on their extracted attributes. Combining the results from both models leads to an improved ability to distinguish between authentic and counterfeit logos. The system is designed to be flexible, enabling it to work with various logos and quickly learn new ones. Overall, this approach aims to provide a dependable and efficient method for detecting fake logos, which is crucial for strengthening the credibility of marketing and advertising. The Gpower test used has a setting of parameters $\alpha=0.05$ and power $=0.85$, resulting in an accuracy level of approximately 85%. KNN has a higher rate of success (88.5950%) than RNN (80.7621%) by a margin of $p=0.002(\mathbf{p}{\lt}0.05)$. The independent sample test T found that alternative hypothesis was true. articleTitle: A Low-Cost Approach for Robot-to-Robot Cooperation

In the present paper, a low-cost approach is presented for cooperative working of two articulated robots in which an external IMU sensor provides the joint movements of the master robot to a generic controller which further controls the slave robot joint motors accordingly. Off the shelf available components were used for experimentation. The results validated the proposed hardware solution and algorithm for achieving cooperation between two robots having different types of controllers without any hardware/software interface.

articleTitle: Autonomous UAV Routing Protocols for Sustainable Telecommunication Networks

articleTitle: Automated Road Extraction from Aerial Images: A Generative Approach with W-FuseNet Model

Focused on applications in urban planning, disaster management, and logistics, the study employs convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and a conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) architecture. The Massachusetts Roads Dataset, comprising 1171 images, is subject to advanced preprocessing techniques, including resizing, concatenation, and normalization. The proposed model features a carefully crafted generator with an encoder-decoder architecture and a modified Pix2pix-based cGAN for semantic segmentation. Inspired by the PatchGAN concept, the discriminator assesses image patches to distinguish real from generated images. A literature survey evaluates methodologies, emphasizing the Road Structure Refined CNN (RSRCNN), generative learning approaches, and the fully convolutional network (FCN) for road extraction. Performance analysis demonstrates the model’s competitive IoU score compared to existing approaches along with accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score. articleTitle: Improved Squeeze and Excitation-Based YOLOv8-SE for Object Detection

abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning has made major advancements surveillance applications, yet detecting targets remains challenging due to size variations and environmental factors. In this paper, we integrated the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) module into various blocks of YOLOv8 to enhance feature discrimination and detection performance. The SE module, added to the backbone, neck, and head of YOLOv8, adaptively recalibrates channel-wise feature responses. This SE-enhanced YOLOv8 (YOLOv8-SE) model improves object detection on the challenging MS-COCO dataset, crucial for real-time surveillance across diverse day-night scenarios. Experimental results show that YOLOv8-SE attains high precision and recall, with a Mean Average Precision at 50 Intersection over Union (mAP50) of 0.5199 and mAP50-95 of 0.3647. Despite the increased number of parameters, the model maintains real-time inference speeds with reduced PyTorch inference time (in ms) and unchanged GFLOPs, establishing it as a reliable solution for real-time object detection tasks.

articleTitle: A System to Monitor Facial Expression Recognition using Support Vector Machine over Deep Belief Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The primary objective of this work is to investigate the real-time facial expression identification performance of Deep Belief Network algorithms and support vector machines. Methods of Research: The research makes use of both a special support vector machine technique and a deep belief network approach. A total of 3600 photos make up the dataset; 3360 of them were used for training, and 240 were used for testing. Combining an 85% G Power value with a 0.05% threshold and 95% confidence intervals yields a total of 10 samples for each group. Talk and Outcomes: The Novel Support Vector Machine Algorithm correctly predicts 89.81% of the facial expressions, compared to 88.80% for the Deep Belief Network Algorithm. Nevertheless, the independent source yielded no statistically significant result.

articleTitle: Suraksha: Advanced SOS Android App with Intelligent Spam Alert Management and Collaborative Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Safety is first and foremost in the current busy life, and smartphones give a helping hand in protecting. This paper has presented an Android app, Suraksha, which enhances personal safety during emergencies. This app ensures that assistance is sought immediately, whereas traditional ways require one to call a person or send the person a message or even unlock the phone, which may not happen when in distress. The nature of shrugs allows the app to differentiate a safe situation and a red alert. Through distress shrugs, the app sends the user’s location and the user’s defined message to the pre-registered ones. Suraksha app depends on humans to judge the alerts and all the information involved, which creates a bundle of evidence that will be sufficient. It is designed with a Machine Learning model, which studies the user’s learned things and the emergency type to understand its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Scanpath Prediction through Convolutional Neural Network and Feature-Based Clustering: A Bottom-Up Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the last few years, there has been a surge in researchers to investigate visual attention for various object-based applications. Visual attention requires a cognitive process to focus on specific regions of interest while ignoring others. Recent computational models emphasize on exogenous or reflexive attention that reveals the pixels with the high visual conspicuousness. A novel method is proposed for predicting the scanpath of the subject from the features extracted with Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and k-means clustering. Features like color, edges, orientation, objects, faces and corresponding fixations are trained using pretrained VGG net utilizing SALICON dataset. The visual path is predicted based on the visual conspicuousness of the pixels using the K means clustering. The model has got a high jaccard similarity match of 0.99 with grid size $2 \times 2$ and 0.92 with grid size $3 \times 3$ with the ground truth map.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Delight: Ice Cream Unboxing Redefined through Packaging Innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Ice cream product packaging is a critical element in the ice cream industry, serving as both a protective barrier and a means of communication with consumers. This review explores the evolution of ice cream packaging, from traditional materials to innovative designs, focusing on the key factors driving its development. Additionally, it investigates the growing importance of sustainability in ice cream packaging, analysing the adoption of eco-friendly materials and practices to reduce environmental impact. The review highlights the significance of visually appealing and practical packaging in attracting consumers and maintaining product quality. Furthermore, it emphasizes the role of advanced packaging technologies in preserving ice cream freshness and extending shelf life. By examining current trends and prospects, this review provides insights into the dynamic landscape of ice cream product packaging, emphasizing the increasing emphasis on sustainability and consumer-centric solutions.

articleTitle: A stress-based reliability prediction of 5G system design
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Reliability predictions early in the design process validate the architecture’s goals, identify critical components, and assess the impact of operating conditions on failure rates, guiding necessary maintenance renewals. Estimating reliability in increasingly complex PCB designs is challenging due to the mixed composition of digital, analog, RF, and mechanical components and a lack of simulation models for ICs and FPGAs. This complexity makes system-level exploration daunting and time-intensive, with the need to simulate numerous fault models quickly, stressing simulation capacity and performance at subsystem levels. This paper proposes a method to improve PCB reliability by dividing the design into simulatable sub-circuits to accurately assess absolute voltage, current, and power values and incorporating interconnect lifespan and electrical over stress(EOS) into the overall reliability assessment using reliability block diagram. This approach provides a comprehensive framework for enhancing PCB durability predictions.

articleTitle: Concealing Text Messages in Audio Using Steganography
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the current digital age, protecting sensitive data is crucial. Audio steganography is a technique that encrypts audio recordings to provide a secret means of communication. With the help of the Echo Hiding algorithm, this project offers a novel approach to audio steganography that offers a reliable and undetectable way to hide sensitive messages from listeners. In addition, the stego audio file is encrypted with the RSA technique to strengthen security and safeguard the concealed message even further. It is very difficult for unauthorized parties to find or decode the hidden information since Echo Hiding and RSA encryption work together to guarantee the confidentiality as well as the authenticity of the hidden data. This research offers a comprehensive solution for secure communication and data concealment in audio applications by showcasing the merging of cutting-edge cryptographic techniques with steganographic technologies.

articleTitle: A Face Re-triangularization Attack Robust 3D Watermarking Algorithm for Archaeological Data Security
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A Kirchhoff matrix-based 3D watermarking scheme that involves visual cryptography is proposed. It is shown that the proposed method is resilient enough to face a re-triangulation attack. Numerical experiments are performed to strengthen the underlying objectives. Various stages involved in the owner registration and identification phase, including 3D image processing, master and ownership share generation, attacked and restored host objects and watermarks, are depicted with the help of pictorial illustrations. Four objects namely Mushroom, Nefertiti, Pipe and Sphere are experimented. After the face-retriangularization attack, the watermarks are recovered. 96.5% of the original watermark is recovered for the sphere, which is the worst scenario as 37.1% faces are distorted. The resilience of the developed scheme to face re-triangulation attacks finds wide applications in cultural heritage and archaeological data security.

articleTitle: Next Generation Vehicle Electrical Distribution System (EDS) Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Traditional EDS architectures, primarily designed for internal combustion engine vehicles, are being reimagined to accommodate the distinctive characteristics of EVs, including high-voltage power distribution, energy storage systems, and complex power management requirements. The next generation of EDS for EVs and Non EVs prioritizes modularity, scalability, and efficiency to optimize the integration of various electrical components while ensuring robust performance and safety. The proposed work aims to create a statistical method to evaluate electrical distribution in automotive vehicles with the help of digital optimization (Process based) techniques. Key advancements in EDS architecture include the adoption of distributed power distribution strategies, such as multi-level power distribution units (PDUs) and intelligent load management systems, to enhance system flexibility and fault tolerance. For the work proposed three tests were simulated, fast blow fuse test where wiper motor had actual value of 0.097 Sec and the simulation results achieved was 0.030 Sec which is an acceptable value and is much less than the threshold of 0.050 sec, for Slow blow fuse the battery had actual value of 0.17 Sec and the simulation results achieved was 0.146 Sec which is an borderline value but is still acceptable as it is approximately equal to the threshold of 0.1 sec and for voltage drop test washer motor had load end voltage of 13.29 V and the simulation results achieved was 13.83 V which is an acceptable and in line with expected results. Work done provides an optimum platform for conduct-ing simulated tests for the vehicles and hence will help reduce physical proto development and electrical validation at the initial project level.

articleTitle: Secure Messaging in Post Quantum Cryptography using NTRUEncryption
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: QuantumChat is a real-time messaging application designed to address the emerging threat of quantum computing to traditional encryption. By utilizing post-quantum encryption methods, the software guarantees confidential and safe communication. Hybrid cryptography facilitates a smooth transition for consumers by enabling backward compatibility with traditional encryption techniques. Combining state-of-the-art security with intuitive features, QuantumChat provides a next-generation solution for safe communication in a rapidly changing digital environment. The hybrid cryptography approach strikes a compromise between compatibility and security by combining both classical and post-quantum encryption. This makes it possible for users to use QuantumChat without compromising their ability to safely interact with others using conventional cryptographic techniques. With regard to secure communications, the QuantumChat software is a major advancement that tackles the impending risks associated with quantum computing. In the rapidly changing world of digital security, QuantumChat seeks to provide consumers a private and secure communication platform by fusing cutting-edge encryption technology with an intuitive user interface.

articleTitle: Exploring Fuzzy Logic Multi-Agent Systems for Cloud-Based Data Center’s Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Fuzzy logic-based multi-agent structures for reinforcement learning in cloud-primarily based statistics centers can improve the system’s overall performance, scalability, and reliability. In this research, we discover how fuzzy good judgment and multi-agent structures may be used to develop intelligent reinforcement mastering algorithms. The bushy model of reinforcement mastering fashions could be trained and examined for the usage of cloud-primarily based information middle surroundings. The experiments are designed to evaluate fuzzy model performance with present rein-forcement mastering techniques. We will analyze and gift outcomes from our experiments to decide the effectiveness of the fuzzy version in exclusive factors of the gadget. They take a look at can even analyze how the bushy model is able to adapt to adjustments inside the environmental conditions of the information center. We count on beneficial insight into how fuzzy common sense and multi-agent systems can be used to effectively enhance the reinforcement getting-to-know method in cloud-based total data centers.

articleTitle: Investigating the Efficacy of Diverse Machine Learning Classifiers for Parkinson’s Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: To detect Parkinson’s disease, we compare the effectiveness of K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Random Forest (RF) algorithms. Utilizing a dataset with clinical and biomedical features, we preprocess the data to handle missing values and standardize the features. Subsequently, we train each algorithm with the preprocessed data and evaluate their performance using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Our results indicate that all four algorithms achieve excellent accuracy in diagnosing Parkinson’s disease, with KNN slightly outperforming the others. However, the selection of the algorithm may depend on specific needs such as interpretability and computational efficiency. Additionally, we conduct a feature importance analysis to identify the most relevant features for Parkinson’s disease identification, offering insights that can aid in early diagnosis and disease management.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Routing Protocols for FANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Routing protocols play an important role in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication networks. When transferring information in low-altitude environments, UAVs confront difficulties in ensuring efficient and reliable packet transmission between nodes. To address this scientific challenge, a routing protocol needs to be developed that can meet these requirements. In this paper, we have created a more realistic simulation environment based on NS-3 and conducted performance tests and comparisons on four classic routing protocols: Ad Hoc on-demand distance vector (AODV), Destination-Sequenced Distance-Vector Routing (DSDV), Dynamic Source routing (DSR) and optimized link state routing (OLSR). We have analyzed performance parameters such as packet delivery and throughput. Our findings demonstrate that alternative routing strategies may function effectively in several UAV communication network circumstances. These experiments generate quantitative data that determines the optimum pathways in every specific scenario. According to the data analysis, while utilized on networks of 50,100,200, and 250, the AODV protocol has an accuracy of 96%. The DSR protocol achieves 90% accuracy, the DSDV protocol 87% accuracy, and the OLSR protocol 80%. The results show that AODV outperforms other traditional approaches, resulting in a considerable improvement in network efficacy.

articleTitle: Data Mining Techniques to Enhance Customer Segmentation and Targeted Marketing Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The retail industry is facing an ever-increasing challenge of effectively identifying and targeting its customers. Using traditional segmentation techniques to fully capture the intricate and ever-changing character of customer behavior is difficult. This project will examine sales data from a general shop using an assortment of data mining technologies in order give insights into customer habits and purchasing trends. Retail sales records builds the dataset. K-means clustering, association rule mining, and regency, the frequency, and monetary (RFM) analysis will all be employed to look into the data. This study contributes to create something of focused marketing strategies and consumer segmentation by identifying high-value and atrisk clients. Association rule mining illuminates consumer taste and actions by identifying hidden patterns and correlations in large datasets. These discoveries extend the scope of our comprehension of consumer purchasing habits and offer data for more targeted advertising initiatives. Additionally, the K-means clustering algorithm divides customers according to their purchasing habits and behavior, allowing profound knowledge to enhance marketing and sales strategies. Findings from the research will give an extensive awareness of customer behavior and purchasing dynamics, which will improve the efficacy of the general store’s marketing and sales campaigns. The most effective technique for exploiting insights from sales data will be discovered by contrasting the outcomes of RFM analysis, K-means clustering, and association rule mining. This work promises to make substantial improvements to data mining and buyer behavior research algorithms, and it has the capacity to be implemented across an extensive selection of corporate restrictions intended to improve their sales strategies.

articleTitle: Identity Management Dapp using Ethereum Blockchain and IPFS
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of a verification and document management DApp into the core of the Ethereum blockchain and the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS). This way, the multi-signature wallets and intelligent contracts introduced help restore many traditional problems based on the secure handling of documents and ensure increased security, data integrity, and easily accessible documents. This DApp will allow such safe, transparent interaction that mandates consensus with multi-sig functionalities during document transactions to ensure the immutability and retrievability of those documents. This implies that the solution would scale using Ethereum and IPFS while offloading pressure off the blockchain to assure high data availability and reliability. Recent performance reviews indicate relevant improvements in the processes related to document management, and this improvement may even have broader implications for the filling implementation in essential sectors that need both a secure and efficient document-handling process.

articleTitle: Enhancing Object-Centric Process Model with Flattening Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Process mining is a data-driven technique that analyzes event logs to discover, visualize, and improve real-world business processes.
