Different approaches to process mining, like flattening and object-centric process mining (OCPM), offer contrasting techniques for analyzing event data. This study compares these techniques based on their effectiveness in process visualization, data volume handling, and their ability to capture object relationships within processes. We leverage the BPIC 2017 OCEL log, focusing on four key objects and their interactions with events. The analysis explores how flattening simplifies visualization but potentially obscures complex relationships. Conversely, OCPM offers a richer view of the process with object-centricity visualization but can lead to increased data volume and potentially intricate visualizations. By comparing the strengths and weaknesses of both techniques, this study aims to inform the choice of process mining approach based on the specific goals of the analysis, considering factors like data volume, desired level of detail, and the importance of object-centric insights.

articleTitle: Mental Health and Suicide Risk Among College Students: A Detailed Exploration of Contributing Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study aims to identify critical predictors of suicide and inform targeted interventions using data from 27,014 college students. It examines a comprehensive range of mental health indicators, including psychiatric symptoms, suicidal intentions, impulsivity, sleep disturbances, internet addiction, aggression, self-injury behaviors, and eating problems, alongside demographic and socioeconomic variables. Analytical techniques, including exploratory data analysis, cross-tabulation, and correlation analysis, uncover the complex interplay between these factors and suicide risk. The study evaluates several machine learning algorithms. The weighted Random Forest uses feature weighting based on point-biserial correlation coefficients to enhance prediction accuracy and prioritize relevant features. The findings reveal significant associations between higher scores in mental health indicators and increased suicidal behavior, emphasizing the need for comprehensive mental health support systems. By identifying key risk factors through machine learning models, the study provides actionable insights for developing targeted interventions aimed at reducing suicide risk among college students.

articleTitle: Distributed Arithmetic Based FIR Filter: FPGA Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this paper, a Distributed Arithmetic (DA) method for reconfigurable digital filters with finite impulse response (FIR) on FPGA is presented. The inherent parallelism of the DA architecture is used to optimize resource efficiency and performance. A conventional method with a comparable filter length is contrasted with the Distributed Arithmetic-based FIR filter design. It is found that, compared to normal FIR filters, DA filters require fewer LUTs and flip-flops, and no LUT RAM for memory storage or other implementation components. A useful tool for scientists and engineers involved in digital audio processing and communications is the suggested Verilog implementation.

articleTitle: Statistical Feature-based Cerebral Infarction Detection from Photoplethysmogram Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cerebral infarction is one of the leading reasons of death in the world which is also known as ischemic stroke. An early treatment can reduce its effect to a great extent. However, the popular ways of detecting this disease are magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) scan which are costly and time-consuming processes. Photoplethysmogram (PPG) is an optical signal that detects the changes in blood volume. Cerebral infarction causes disruption in normal blood flow, hence there is a potential to use PPG signal to detect this condition. So far only a few studies have used PPG signal to detect Cerebral infarction from PPG signal. Also, the use of statistical features for detecting the disease is yet to be explored. In this study, an equal amount of PPG segments from 30 healthy subjects and 20 cerebral infarction patients are chosen. Different feature importance tests are done to find out the best features among 9 statistical features. After that, several machine learning algorithms are applied to determine the most effective model. Among the various models tested, KNN performed the best providing 98.33% accuracy. This lightweight approach, marked by its high accuracy, may pave the way for a reliable point-of-care solution offering a potential breakthrough in enhancing patient care and treatment strategies within the realm of strokes.

articleTitle: Implementation of IoT and Fuzzy Logic Driven Real-Time Smart Storage Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Post-harvest losses of onion incurred during storage pose a significant global concern. To reduce post-harvest losses, this study explores the applications of fuzzy logic to predict the storage lifespan of onions. This study implemented an Internet of Things (IoT) based approach to monitor different parameters in onion storage and warehousing in real-time. Additionally, to enhance productivity, the system also offers a web-based interface and automated notifications (Email and SMS). Temperature, humidity and, presence of gases (Ammonia and CO2) are three major factors considered in the study. By utilizing these fuzzy variables, the fuzzy logic approach offers significant advantages over standard methods, effectively addressing the critical variabilities of these factors. When the environment conditions are maintained within the storage system, the predicted average shelf life of the onions is determined using fuzzy logic. This method ensures a more accurate and reliable estimate by taking into account the factors influencing the storage duration. The results of these experiments affirm that the suggested system assists stakeholders in taking necessary actions in case of any potential environmental fluctuations, thereby enhancing the quality and extending the shelf life of onions.

articleTitle: Internet of Things Enabled Precision Aquaculture Monitoring and Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The shrimp export industry in India, valued at over 23 thousand crores, faces challenges due to the high-risk, high-reward nature of shrimp farming and the demanding monitoring requirements it entails. Existing automation and IoT solutions often struggle to effectively monitor the diverse marine, brackish, and freshwater environments crucial for shrimp cultivation. This paper introduces the aqua buoy, a specialized monitoring system designed specifically for shrimp farming environments. Alongside detailing the aqua buoy’s functionality, the paper discusses its utility in monitoring various diseases that afflict shrimp cultivation. Furthermore, it explores how farmers are tackling these challenges through enhanced biosecurity measures, selective breeding programs, and sustainable practices. Offering insights into Litopenaeus vannamei shrimp farming, the article sheds light on the industry’s evolution, current hurdles, and promising prospects for aquaculture’s future. With its swift response times, continuous monitoring capabilities, and over $\mathbf{9 8 \%}$ accuracy rate in real-time environments, the aqua buoy leverages a machine learning-based approach for sensor calibration, ensuring optimal performance in shrimp farming operations.

articleTitle: Crop yield forecasting through novel machine learning dynamic ensemble selection techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Crop yield prediction is a crucial aspect of agricultural planning and decision-making. This study utilizes a Kaggle dataset featuring State, Year, Season, Crop, Area, Production, etc., employing extensive data preprocessing and one-hot encoding of categorical features to enhance predictive performance. Initially, ML regression methods including Multiple Linear Regression, Random Forest Regression, XGBoost, and Decision Tree Regression (DTR) were applied. Later, Stacking Regressor and Voting Regressor were employed. Subsequently, dynamic ensemble techniques, specifically Voting Regressor, integrated these models, dynamically selecting the best-performing ones for prediction. Remarkably, achieving an R-squared value of 99%, the dynamic ensemble significantly improved prediction performance. The study showcases the efficacy of dynamic ensemble techniques in crop yield prediction, offering valuable insights for agricultural decision-making and resource allocation strategies. Experimental results underscore the effectiveness of the approach, highlighting its potential for practical application in agricultural management and policy formulation.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Review of Machine Learning Approaches for Analysing EEG-Based Neurological Disorders
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Electroencephalography is a fast, inexpensive and non-invasive technology for analysing neurological disorders. Neurological disorders have a profound impact on the Autonomic Nervous System and the brain significantly influencing individual’s health and well-being. This review focuses on the analysis of EEG signals related to three significant neurological disorders: Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), and Epilepsy. The EEG parameters serve as potential markers for cognitive status in these disorders. Since the inspection of large amount of EEG by neurologist is time-consuming and inconsistent so the machine learning algorithms have made significant strides in identifying unique EEG patterns associated with each disorder which not only enables early diagnosis and timely preventive interventions but also helps to develop personalized treatment strategies. This review delves into the process of analysing EEG signals and integrating machine learning and deep learning algorithms for robust classification of neurological disorders. In addition, it intends to provide a comprehensive overview of the modern advancements in using EEG and ML for improved diagnosis and potential treatment monitoring of PD, AD, and epilepsy.

articleTitle: Implementation and Analysis of MAC Layer and Network Layer Protocols in 6LoWPAN Networks for Home Automation: A Comparative Study of Software and Hardware Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research paper addresses the problem of accurately evaluating energy consumption in ‘IPv6 Low Power Personal Area Networks” (6LoWPAN) used for home automation application, consisting of constrained devices with limited processing power, battery capacity, and memory. We implemented both MAC-layer protocols and the Network-layer protocol for the MRHOF-ETX objective function, comparing their performance using software and hardware approaches. Our 6LoWPAN network includes five nodes: one Border Gateway, one End Device, and three Routers. The End Device monitors parameters such as light intensity, temperature, and humidity, transmitting this data to the Border Gateway via the parent Router in the DODAG hierarchy. Our study reveals notable discrepancies between software simulations and hardware implementations. In the software approach, a single node consumed approximately 140 mW during communication, with an overall network consumption of 660 mW. The hardware approach, however, showed a single node consuming 110 mW and an overall network consumption of 520 mW, indicating a 22% reduction. These findings highlight the significant impact of MAC and Network-layer protocols on the power consumption of 6 LoWPAN networks. By exposing the gap between software simulations and real-world hardware results, our research emphasizes the need for hardware-based evaluations to develop accurate energy optimization strategies, providing valuable insights for the research community.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Controller of a New Single-Switch Non-isolated Converter with Low Order Ripples for Electric Vehicle Chargers
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This article introduces a new modified structure of a parallel connected single switch configuration which achieves higher efficiency compared with recently reported topologies. A novel single switch-single inductor-switched capacitor (SS-SL-SC) topology by employing an intelligent, robust controller (ANFIS) for better load voltage regulation and maintains ripple-free continuous load current at nominal duty cycle range which is commonly applicable to electric vehicles On-board chargers. Furthermore, design considerations, theoretical analysis, converter performance in CCM, and comparison with existing topologies have been incorporated. The converter simulation results are executed using MATLAB software to verify the system performance and a 150 W experimental prototype will be built and tested to validate the hardware results.

articleTitle: Understanding the Use of Block Ciphers in Applied Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Block ciphers are an important cryptographic asset used to guard touchy statistics from unauthorized get right of entry to or alteration. They are utilized in an expansion of programs, inclusive of in encrypting credit score card records, financial transactions, saved computer data, and communications to call some. This paper aims to offer an outline of block ciphers, their encryption and decryption algorithms, components of an ordinary block cipher design, and examples in their a hit packages. It’ll additionally discuss capability vulnerabilities of block ciphers and display how they may be mitigated. Sooner or later, it’ll offer a quick assessment of a number of the maximum famous and widely used block ciphers. Via inspecting these topics, this paper will help to provide a clear understanding of block ciphers and their use in implemented cryptography.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Thyroid Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive performance analysis of various machine learning algorithms for the prediction of thyroid disease, considering both binary and multi-class classification scenarios. We explore the effectiveness of Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, K-nearest neighbor, XGBoost, and Artificial Neural Network. By leveraging these algorithms and incorporating pertinent risk factors from the dataset, our findings demonstrate stable accuracies across multiple classifiers, with the highest accuracy of $\mathbf{9 5. 6 \%}$ achieved with the XGBoost in binary classification. However, further analysis reveals that performs poorly in terms of true identification. To address this, rigorous analysis and evaluation have been conducted, and it has been found that through Artificial Neural Network, an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 4. 9 2 \%}$ can be achieved in the multi-class classification. In the multi-class classification scenario, similar methodologies were applied, leading to insightful results. We have found that it yields a recall score of $\mathbf{9 0. 4 \%}$. Through visualization of training and testing accuracies, phenomena such as model overfitting and underfitting are investigated to understand the limitations of specific classifiers. The primary objective of this research is to identify optimal algorithms in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency for thyroid disease prediction, considering both binary and multi-class classification tasks.

articleTitle: Property Price Estimation Using Machine learning and implementing a website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Property price estimation uses various kinds of algorithms in Machine Learning like linear regression, lasso, and decision tree that best predict the house prices with the highest accuracy. In this paper, we use various machine learning algorithms to build a model that predicts the house prices based on the requirements like location, area, number of bedrooms, and no of bathrooms. A Huge set of data on housing prices is trained for various attributes to create an algorithmic model. To better understand the links between the several housing qualities and the selling prices, we will do exploratory data analysis (EDA), which entails visualizing the data and discovering patterns and trends that help to develop the prediction model. Data pre-processing and data cleaning is done before creating the model. We build a linear regression model, and we compare it with the other machine learning algorithms like lasso regression and classification and regression tree algorithms and use the one that yields high accuracy. The tested model is imported through a pickle file and a Flask server is used for developing the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Smart Healthcare - IoT and Artificial Neural Network(ANN)
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With the use of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), the growing accessibility of wearable devices, and the continual reduction in the cost of sensor-based technologies and green computing, internet-connected sensors allow users to track, analyze, and share welfare information employing a cloud-based platform. Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) find extensive use across various applications, including healthcare systems, drawing inspiration from the biological concept of neurons. This study explores the prediction of heart attack risks using a combination of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors and artificial neural networks (ANN). Through the integration of IoT sensors such as the pulse sensor and LM35 temperature sensor, essential physiological data related to heart rate and body temperature was collected. An ANN model was developed, focusing on predictive capabilities using the sigmoid function, feedforward and backpropagation techniques, and random weight initialization. The investigation further utilized Keras with TensorFlow and optimized model parameters using Adam Optimization and Later with One Hot Encoding plus a Genetic Algorithm (GA). Additionally, the study involved training neural networks on higher-quality UCI datasets to evaluate performance. Scatterplots were generated to visualize relationships between variables. Results demonstrated promising performance improvements, with the model achieving close to ${9 0 \%}$ accuracy on the testing dataset. Encoding techniques were employed to handle categorical variables effectively, contributing to the model’s robustness and generalization. Overall, this research offers valuable insights into leveraging IoT sensors and ANN for heart attack risk prediction.

articleTitle: Dual-Band THz Vivaldi Antenna with Circular shaped Resonator for Enhanced Gain in Next-Generation Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band vivaldi antenna with enhanced gain based on an array of circular shaped resonators for the next generation of wireless applications such as skin cancer spectroscopy, drug detection, and imaging systems. The suggested vivaldi antenna is made up of an equation-based curve and circular shaped resonators that increase the gain of the reference vivaldi antenna and allow it to operate in dual bands. The circular shaped resonators allow the antenna to increase gain along the end-fire direction, allowing it to operate at dual band frequencies. The suggested vivaldi structure operates within a frequency range of 0.74 to 0.90 THz and achieves a gain of $\mathbf{1 0. 3}$ dBi at 0.866 THz. To improve the behavior of the radiation properties, circular-shaped resonators are added to the normally manufactured framework. The integration of six rows of circular-shaped resonators resulted in a 12 dBi gain at 0.946 THz and a dual-band working frequency range of 0.646 to 0.75 THz with a bandwidth of 0.104 THz and 0.848 to 0.982 THz with a bandwidth of $0.134 \mathbf{T H z}$.

articleTitle: Collaborative Cognition of Humans and Machines for Anticipating Criminal Sentencing in the Judicial System
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Numerous research endeavors have been undertaken to create sophisticated Artificial Intelligence Systems that not only exhibit enhanced speed but also surpass human capabilities in prediction. However, a Humans possess certain inherent abilities that machines are incapable of acquiring, such as creativity, empathy, perception, and critical thinking. A revolutionary paradigm for the judicial system can be predicted by combining the best aspects of both. To achieve this objective, we compile a dataset by combining data from an online survey ($\mathbf{n}=103$) and interviews performed in Bangladesh on incidents about the ‘Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, of 2000’. We utilize multiple machine learning algorithms to develop a computer capable of predicting punishment with the same accuracy as a judge. We assess the test accuracy and predictive capacity of the models to determine which method performs superiorly and exhibits greater stability compared to the others. Humans can instruct machines in the process of determining whether someone is a delinquent.

articleTitle: Congestion Control Technique for VANETs Using Seagull Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) face significant challenges including packet transmission delays, high power consumption, and complex existing algorithms. These issues are exacerbated by the limited battery life of sensor nodes, which leads to energy wastage due to packet collisions and the need for retransmissions. Additionally, node failures occur when nodes with limited energy resources are used to transmit large packets. To address these challenges, this research introduces a multi-fitness function designed to monitor the arrival pattern of information from each vehicular sensor to the cluster head(CH) based master node, thereby optimizing data flow. The Seagull optimization technique (SOT) is utilized to manage congestion within the vehicular sensor network. Key parameters such as throughput, packet loss, queue size, message sending rate, delay, and congestion level are incorporated into the fitness function to enhance network performance. The proposed algorithm aims to minimize energy consumption and prevent node failures by efficiently managing the flow of data. By monitoring these critical parameters, the algorithm dynamically adjusts to ensure optimal performance and longevity of the network. The effectiveness of the designed algorithm is calculated using MATLAB 2022 and match up with existing algorithms including Adaptive Cuckoo Search (ACS), Particle Swarm algorithm - Gravitational Search optimization approach (PSOGSA), and Cuckoo Search (CS) optimized technique. In conclusion, the multi-fitness function combined with the Seagull Optimization Algorithm offers a robust solution to the challenges faced by VANETs, providing a more efficient and sustainable network operation. This research highlights the potential of advanced optimization techniques in enhancing the performance and reliability of vehicular networks.

articleTitle: Forecasting Coastal Changes: A Case Study on Florida’s Shorelines
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Predicting changes in coastline dynamics is crucial for coastal management and hazard mitigation. This work uses MATLAB’s Mapping Toolbox to develop a predictive model for coastline evolution along the Florida coast. Remotely sensed data and geographical information systems (GIS) are used to analyze coastline and geo-environmental data to forecast the shape of the coastline in the future. The method involves data pre-processing, feature extraction, model training, and validation. The outcomes of this research hold significant application for environmental awareness, coastal planning, risk assessment, and sustainable development in the Florida region. Additionally, the coastline changes of other regions can also be mapped using this model.

articleTitle: Sentiment Classification on Suicide Notes Using BERT, Bi-LSTM and CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the modern day, where sentiments and feelings are important in every element of our daily lives, from personal to professional, sentiment classification has become a crucial field of research. This entails learning what people think about different products and how they feel about a specific topic. Relevant research has demonstrated that several models and techniques have been applied to the sentiment classification of suicide notes, yet resulted in lower accuracie.In this area, we have to understand the sentiments of the people who are depressed and think about that. Suicide note analysis is an effective way to understand and reduce this problem because suicide notes present the mental state of suicide victims. We can understand the mental state of suicidal minds and then further avoid suicides. Tremendous work is happening in this area, but accuracy is critical in the analysis because of the sensitive topic. We analyzed the suicide note data set using a hybrid model containing BERT, Bi-LSTM, and Convolutional layers, achieving better results. The precision, recall, and F1 score produced by the model are 77%, 77%, 76%.

articleTitle: Novel Real-Time Monitoring and Diagnostic Battery Management System Integrated with Thermoelectric Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This project introduces an innovative Real-Time Monitoring and Diagnostic Battery Management System (BMS) integrated with thermoelectric technology to optimize battery performance and safety. Addressing the challenge of maintaining optimal battery temperature, the system uses an incandescent lamp for heat generation, monitored by an Arduino-controlled temperature sensor. When a set temperature point is reached, a Peltier module and cooling fan are activated by the Arduino for efficient temperature control. Current and voltage sensors, connected to a Node MCU through relays, interface with the Arduino IDE, enabling comprehensive monitoring of battery parameters. These parameters are then transmitted to a mobile app via the Internet of Things (IoT), providing real-time insights into the battery’s status. This integrated BMS leverages the synergy of thermoelectric technology, Arduino, and IoT, offering a sophisticated, adaptive, and user-friendly solution with broad applications in various fields requiring reliable battery management.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition in Images: CNN-based Classification of Happy and Sad States
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The difficulty of recognizing emotions from pictures is a real problem for mental health evaluation and human-computer interaction. In this study, it is suggested that the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) can help identify emotions in photographs focusing on classifying happy and sad states. The CNN architecture was trained using a dataset made up of images depicting people in various emotional states ranging from joy to sadness. After extensive testing and analysis, our model discerns between happiness and sadness. So, we investigate how the emotion recognition system performance could be maximized by trying out different CNN designs, data augmentation techniques as well as hyperparameters. Moreover, part of this chapter looks at the interpretability of the model’s decisions and also discusses implications and further research directions into emotion recognition with deep learning mechanisms. On the whole, our work advances emotion recognition technology and highlights how CNN-based techniques can aid in understanding human emotions through visual cues.

articleTitle: A CNN Approach to Detect The Anomalies In BGP Traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The stability and security of the Internet’s routing infrastructure, largely dependent on the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), are critical for ensuring reliable global connectivity. Anomalous routing behavior can disrupt this stability, making effective anomaly detection essential. Traditional methods face significant challenges due to the dynamic and complex nature of BGP networks. To address these challenges, we propose a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based approach for detecting BGP anomalies. CNNs are well-suited for capturing spatial dependencies and patterns within data, making them an ideal choice for this application. We evaluate the performance of our CNN model using the RIPE and BCNET datasets, demonstrating superior accuracy in anomaly detection compared to previous methods. Our results highlight the potential of CNNs to enhance the robustness of BGP anomaly detection systems.

articleTitle: IoT - Based Quality Monitoring and Control Automation in Dairy Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Milk is the essential basic product in day-to-day life which undergoes a series of essential processes from production to consumption. The industry faces a significant challenge in ensuring the freshness and quality of milk during storage and transportation. The primary objective of the proposed work is to develop an integrated system that enables dairy industries to remotely monitor and control parameters such as temperature, pH value and level of the milk in the tank using Internet of Things (IoT) technology. It incorporates components such as DS18B20 temperature sensor for accurate temperature monitoring, an ultrasonic sensor for precise level detection in the tank and a pH sensor for monitoring the pH value. These sensors are integrated with an Arduino UNO microcontroller, which serves as the central processing unit for data collection and control. When the temperature goes above the range of $5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ the controller activates the chiller thereby the temperature is maintained within the range of $4-5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The values of temperature, pH and the level of milk are monitored and displayed in the LCD. Additionally, IoT connectivity is facilitated through the ESP8266 module enabling remote access of the system via the Blynk App. Integration with the Blynk App offers a user-friendly interface for remote interaction, empowering dairy operators to monitor the chiller performance and the quality of the milk in the dairy sector.

articleTitle: Transforming the Travel with OmniCruise: Designing a fully Directional Autonomous Car with Smart obstacle Detection and Collision Evasion
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The development of autonomous cars has accelerated recently due to developments in artificial intelligence, processing capacity, and sensor technology. This paper is the implementation of an autonomous driving car which use an an array of sensors and Raspberry Pi microcontrollers. The main aim is to develop a scalable, low-cost prototype that can navigate predetermined routes with the least amount of human assistance. In daily life, driving consumes a significant portion of our time.The work carried out in this paper introduces a completely automated, or driverless vehicle that is intended to navigate and maintain road safety in order to address this problem. The creation of an autonomous car that can travel in all directionsforward, backward, left, and right-as well as stop on its own after path completion. A mechanism for automatically detecting obstacles and avoiding collisions is also included while travelling. Car prototype is capable of detecting traffic signals, traffic signs and take appropriate actions by itself. The Raspberry Pi 4, which manages the car’s autonomous functions, lies at the heart of this breakthrough. In a world where technology is growing, the car follows a predefined path and makes judgments on its own, making travel safer and more effective.

articleTitle: Comparison of Handover Latency Using Mobility Protocols for Wi-MAX Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Due to the growing call for for wireless facts offerings, handover latency should be minimized a good way to ensure consumer revel in. so as to reduce handover latency, one-of-a-kind mobility protocols are to be had for We-MAX networks, including fast Base Station Switching (FBSS), Dynamic pleasant of carrier (Duos), and greater dispensed Channel get admission to (EDCA). This paper offers a comparative study of handover latencies for these three mobility protocols. The research was carried out the usage of a Web-MAX network simulator to simulate numerous scenarios. results show that EDCA was discovered to be the first-class in phrases of handover latency, with an average latency of 1.18 ms, at the same time as fast Base Station Switching and Duos had a latency of 6.02 ms and 13.43 ms respectively. Additionally, the effects showed that EDCA decreased the handover latency by using 14.4%, as compared to FBSS and 39.2% in comparison to Duos. The look at additionally suggests that EDCA is extra suitable for handover in We-MAX networks, due to its low latency and high performance.

articleTitle: Implementing Linear Modulation Schemes with Field Programmable Analog Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study utilizes Modern Field Programmable Analog Arrays (FPAA) technology to showcase the application of various linear modulations, such as Single Sideband (SSB), Double Sideband (DSB), and Double Sideband with Suppressed Carrier (DSB-SC). By utilizing FPAA, many of the challenges associated with traditional DCS kits and discrete component circuit-based linear modulation approaches are circumvented. The FPAA circuits are developed using double sideband modulation techniques tailored to the requirements of analog RF transmission systems. With FPAA devices, which can be tailored based on electrical properties and signal shapes, this suggested solution makes it easier to reconstruct analog conditioning stages. Modulation of a sinusoidal carrier signal includes demodulation, DSB, DSB-SC, and SSB using a multiplier. These structures’ functional elements are built with customisable analog modules (CAMs) from Anadigm Designer 2, specifically AN231E04 and AN220E04 FPAA models. Simulations and experimental results align well with theoretical predictions, demonstrating the efficacy of the approach. Additionally, this paper introduces a new proposal that utilizes the structure of customizable analog blocks (CABs) and the Anadigm Designer2 software to implement DSB and DSB-SC technology. The AN231E04 board by Anadigm Inc. is utilized for system construction and verification. These modulation schemes offer potential for laboratory experimentation and the creation of virtual labs.

articleTitle: Ml-HCN: A Novel Healthcare System Architecture Based on Multi-layered Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a comprehensive multilayered Network designed to encapsulate the intricacies of the entire healthcare infrastructure. Our model leverages an evolutionary graph system, emphasizing discrete relationships among the fundamental entities that constitute the backbone of any healthcare system - Doctors, Departments, and Hospitals. By integrating these three pivotal elements into a cohesive framework, our approach aims to enhance the understanding of the complex interactions within the healthcare domain. Moreover, the multilayered Network model is crucial in healthcare systems where the interactions between different components are multifaceted. This approach has significant potential for improving healthcare system design and can enhance recommendation systems, providing personalized and reliable suggestions for patients using discrete healthcare entity relationships.

articleTitle: Utilizing Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI) for the Assessment of Ischemic Brain Injury
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) is an advanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) approach that has been lately carried out to assess and quantify ischemic mind damage. Its miles primarily based at the diffusion of water molecules inside an organic environment, and it gives an extra distinct insight in the effects of ischemia on abnormalities of tissue microstructure. DTI is able to presenting data, both in quantitative and qualitative form, approximately the altered microscopical shape inside sure tissues. By measuring the obvious diffusion coefficients (ADC) of water molecules alongside specific instructions, it could accurately represent the value, path and form of the diffusion of water inside regions tormented by ischemia. This precision has allowed DTI to be reliably used to hit upon and differentiate the severity of ischemic activities. Quantitative DTI makes a specialty of computed parameters derived from the derived ADC values, which include extent ratio, radial diffusivity, axial diffusivity, and mean diffusivity. Additionally, fractional anisotropy may be used to degree the impact of ischemic lesions in comparison with the everyday mind tissue. By means of developing maps for every one of these parameters, its miles feasible to actively monitor modifications in the area right now after ischemic activities along with stroke.

articleTitle: Staircase Patch With SRR DGS Antenna for S Band
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A small square in shape microstrip patch antenna with staircase slots is designed. Two split ring resonators of square shape are loaded on ground also circular split ring resonators are compared with square. CPW feed is used. Resonant frequencies obtained are $3.1 \mathrm{GHz}, 3.5 \mathrm{GHz}$ which enables multi frequency operation. The proposed structure is designed with a FR-4 substrate of $20 * 16 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. Parametric study of substrate material, feed width and feed thickness is done to finalize parameters. Aerial is applicable for radars, mobile phones, and wireless local area networks (WLANs)

articleTitle: Security: Cloud Data with Dynamic Protection Via Network Coding
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the age of cloud computing, cloud users with limited storage can outsource their data remote servers. These servers, in lieu of monetary benefits, offer retrieve ability of their clients’ data at any point of time. Secure cloud storage protocols enable a client to check integrity of outsourced data. In this work, we explore the possibility of constructing a secure cloud storage for dynamic data by leveraging the algorithms involved in secure network coding. We show that some of the secure network coding schemes can be used to construct efficient secure cloud storage (SCS) protocols for dynamic data, and we construct such a protocol (DSCS I) based on a secure network coding protocol. To the best of our knowledge, DSCS I is the first secure cloud storage protocol for dynamic data constructed using secure network coding techniques which is secure in the standard model. Although generic dynamic data support arbitrary insertions, deletions and modifications, append-only data find numerous applications in the real world. We construct another secure cloud storage protocol (DSCSII) specific to append-only data that overcomes some limitations of DSCS I.

articleTitle: Investigating Autonomous and Adaptive Communications Systems for Robotics Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growth in utilization of robotics applications all through more than one industry. Self-reliant and adaptive communication structures are crucial additives of gift robotics applications. Those structures permit controlled and efficient alternate of statistics most of the robotic and its surroundings. This paper offers a survey of research on self sufficient and adaptive communique structures for robotics programs. It examines the position of communique protocols, protocols used for robotics verbal exchange, additives of an adaptive communique device for robotics, and various annoying situations and programs associated with this era. Additionally, this paper introduces associated research topics and contemplates viable destiny commands for this region. In give up, this paper highlights the importance of unbiased and adaptive communication for modern and upcoming robotics applications.

articleTitle: Comparative Power Quality Analysis by PV D-STATCOM and EV D-STATCOM in Three-Phase Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations and solar photovoltaic (PV) in the distribution network produce the current harmonics in the grid. In this work, the voltage source converter of DSTATCOM system has been charged by EV charging stations and by PV system. In both the topology, the DSTATCOM has been controlled by the D-Q control. The D-Q control via PWM generator provides pulses for the switches of the DSTATCOM. The DC-DC converter of PV system has been controlled by Fuzzy based MPPT technique. It tracks changing conditions more rapidly than other MPPT techniques. Both DSTATCOM topology is connected to three-phase power system having non-linear load. The proposed topologies have been designed and executed in MATLAB/Simulink circumstances. The power quality improvement performance of the PV D-STATCOM and EV D-STATCOM topologies will be analysed and compared.

articleTitle: A Deepfake detection technique using Recurrent Neural Network and EfficientNet
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A deepfake is a computer-generated image or video that appears to be real but is a fabricated representation created to make an individual appear to be saying or doing something that did not occur. Deepfakes generate misleading or deceptive information by manipulating and superimposing faces onto pre-existing footage using artificial intelligence. This paper introduces a novel approach for deepfake detection through a combination of EfficientNet and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). This method enhances detection efficiency by leveraging the hierarchical features acquired by EfficientNet and employing RNNs, specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, to capture temporal dependencies. Application of this approach to the Celeb-DF dataset resulted in an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 9 8 \%}$.

articleTitle: A CNN Model For Plant Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The paper proposes a system that utilizes CNNs to accurately identify plant diseases with the help of images of leaves and provide remedies to prevent and mitigate the disease’s impact. The proposed system uses a grid-like topology with nineteen layers using VGG19 architecture. This architecture consists of sixteen convolutional layers and followed by three fully-connected layers. Where the captured image of a plant’s leaf acts as input to predict the plant’s condition, the proposed system can revolutionize how plant diseases are diagnosed and treated, offering a cost-effective solution for farmers to monitor and manage crop health. The system’s ability to accurately identify plant diseases can significantly reduce crop loss, and the remedies provided can be taken as a preventive measure to protect crops from getting affected by the disease. It is a valuable tool for farmers to protect their crops from disease and increase yield and quality. Here, we can get truthfully promising output with an optimum accuracy of 94.7%. Some remedies are provided through this system that can be taken as a cure. In this system, we used a data set collected from Kaggle containing 38 types of diseases with 3GB storage.

articleTitle: Instantaneous Envelope and Energy Features for LCL Activation based complementary 1D-CNN in EEG Stress classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The work proposes a stress classification scheme that uses instantaneous envelope and energy features from the electroencephalograph (EEG) signals. The approach uses linear-cosine-linear (LCL) activation function-based complementary kernel 1D-CNN for the classification of stress. Initially, the EEG brain signals are categorized into two components, where the first class corresponds to the components of the delta, theta, and alpha bands (DTA band), while the second class corresponds to the components of the beta band. The instantaneous energy feature is estimated from the DTA band, while the envelope feature is estimated from the B-band. These two features are used to differentiate the induced stress types namely the recognition task, arithmetic task, and color image recognition task each with intense levels of high, medium, and low. The EEG signals collected from the SAM-40 datasets with the measures namely accuracy, F1-score, recall, specificity, and precision are used for analysis. The proposed approach results in accuracy, F1-score, recall, specificity, and precision of $96.61 \%, 95.99 \%, 96.57 \%$, ${9 9. 5 7 \%}$, and 95.45% respectively which is higher than the traditional stress classification schemes.

articleTitle: Benchmarking Machine Learning Techniques for Attention Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Being attentive among the chaos of the current world is very important. It has applications in various fields such as education, safety, healthcare. Attention patterns can be very helpful in diagnosing mental health conditions such as ADHD, depression and can lead to early treatment. It is also very important in workplaces which involve high-risk tasks that need the full attention of the person who perform it to prevent any mishaps and prevent any damages. It is also important in driver monitoring systems and can play a pivotal role in preventing accidents and dangerous situations. This paper compares various machine learning models which include KNN, Naive Bayes, SVM and 2 tree based models which are RandomForest and XGBoost, by observing how accurately they can detect attentive and inattentive states. Each model has been trained on an extensive dataset containing over 4000 records and have been cross-validated for the best possible accuracy and fair comparison between models. The dataset contains various features obtained from video-feed that have undergone extensive pre-processing to obtain numerical values. The final dataset contains over 4000 records of data such as coordinates and confidence values in numerical format and categorical variables such as pose and label. The results of the comparison have been displayed using numerical statistics such as accuracy, precision, recall and also using graphical means such as ROC curves and confusion matrices.

articleTitle: A novel Blockchain based model for regulating non-OTC medicine sale
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The illicit sale of non-over-the-counter (OTC) medicines without a prescription poses significant risks to public health and safety. Traditional regulatory measures often struggle to effectively monitor and prevent such activities due to loopholes and inefficiencies in supply chain management. This paper proposes a blockchain-based solution to enhance the tracking and regulation of non-OTC medicine sales, focusing on the creation of a transparent and secure supply chain ecosystem. Utilizing blockchain technology offers several advantages in this con-text. This paper proposes a blockchain-based solution to monitor and prevent the illegal sale of non-OTC medicines without a prescription. Blockchain ensures transparency and security by recording every transaction in a tamper-proof ledger. Smart contracts automate regulatory compliance, allowing legitimate transactions while flagging illegal sales. Stakeholders collaborate within the blockchain network to share data and enforce regulations. Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in enhancing regulatory oversight and protecting public health. Challenges such as interoperability and privacy concerns require ongoing research for widespread implementation.

articleTitle: Understanding the Frequency Response Characteristics of Network Connections to Enhance Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The improvement of contemporary electronics has led to an increased dependence on networks. This paper studies the frequency reaction traits of community connections as a way to provide higher ranges of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). Outcomes are offered that illustrate the significance of the frequency reaction value and section, frequency selectivity, and amplitude shift over unique frequencies while connecting networks. Those effects are discussed in relation to an expansion of business networks and the 2 main EMC requirements, ANSI/IEEE and EN 61000. The most desirable combination of frequency reaction components to gain better stages of EMC is likewise diagnosed. Subsequently, guidelines are supplied on the layout and implementation of networks, considering the frequency response traits, if you want to make certain higher EMC compliance.

articleTitle: IoT Based Plant Monitoring System For Smart Irrigation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Using cutting edge technology, nations all around the world are working to improve agricultural sustainability. Achieving water-use efficiency and being in line with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially Goal 6 and Target 6.4, need improving irrigation systems. In order to accomplish these goals, this article emphasizes the need of SMART irrigation, using the Internet of Things (IoT) and sensing systems. The study highlights the vital role that automated irrigation systems play in preserving water resources through the use of secondary data and a qualitative methodology. Agricultural techniques become more efficient and successful when IoT and automation are included; this increases sustainability overall. Sensory systems lessen their negative effects on the environment, increase resource conservation, and help farmers understand their crops better. These technologies make it possible to monitor soil and weather conditions effectively, which facilitates appropriate water management. Irrigation system optimization is acknowledged, and ongoing research and development are encouraged to improve sustainability and lower expenses. Additionally, the study examines the drawbacks and advantages of sensory-based irrigation systems, providing scholars and farmers with important information to enhance irrigation methods and practices.

articleTitle: Sustainable Agriculture Using Machine Learning and IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to sustainable agriculture, integrating Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and the Internet of Things (IoT). It employs IoT devices with cameras for real-time monitoring of plant health, enabling early detection of diseases and pests. Through disease and pest detection machine learning models, the system provides farmers with timely alerts and tailored solutions via a user-friendly web application. Additionally, an IoT-based spraying mechanism delivers targeted treatments, reducing the overuse of pesticides and promoting sustainability. It provides precision agriculture, offering an efficient solution to enhance crop management and productivity while minimizing environmental impact.

articleTitle: Optimizing Task Load Distribution in Cloud Environments via Dynamic PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach to optimize task load distribution using the Dynamic Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is presented. The traditional PSO algorithm is enhanced by integrating dynamic mutation techniques, allowing for improved adaptability and efficiency in load balancing scenarios. The dynamic PSO algorithm is implemented on the MATLAB platform, where multiple iterations of selection and mutation are performed to refine the solution continuously. Significant improvements over the traditional PSO algorithm are demonstrated, particularly in terms of makespan and response time metrics. Better load balancing is achieved, overall execution time is reduced, and resource usage is minimized through effective task load distribution. This method is found to be particularly suitable for complex optimization problems in cloud computing environments, where efficient task scheduling and resource management are critical. Performance parameters are optimized, showcasing the potential of the proposed method as a robust solution for task load distribution challenges.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Real-time IoT Solution for Smart Meter Data Analysis in Microsoft Azure
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research presents an end-to-end IoT solution designed as a project, not a traditional lab setup. It simulates high-velocity data generation from smart meters and focuses on real-time data visualization within Azure’s cloud ecosystem. An integral part of this project is an AI-based spike and dip anomaly detection system. The project creates an IoT ecosystem that replicates smart meter telemetry data. It utilizes Microsoft Azure’s robust services to cover the entire IoT data lifecycle, from data ingestion to real-time visualization. Key project components involve Azure resource provisioning, IoT Hub setup, and the deployment of a Device Provisioning Service. The project implements a lambda architecture, filtering and processing a subset of telemetry data in real-time. This data undergoes immediate visualization, showcasing Azure’s agility in handling high-velocity streams. This paper is a valuable reference for interests in implementing IoT solutions with Microsoft Azure, particularly emphasizing real-time data processing and visualization within a lambda architecture while incorporating AI-based anomaly detection for spikes and dips.

articleTitle: Spatial attention enhanced deep learning model for Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease has a major challenge for neurologists due to the time-consuming and sometimes imprecise manual methods. Given Alzheimer’s substantial impact on the brain, employing an automatic diagnostic system using brain images could yield more precise outcomes. In this work, a spatial attention assisted improved deep network model is proposed for classifying Alzheimer’s disease with brain magnetic resonance images. Using ADNI2 dataset, the proposed model demonstrates commendable performance, achieving a accuracy rate of 86% (AD vs MCI vs CN), which is better than previous methods.

articleTitle: Utilizing Formal Methods for Power Optimization in Embedded Computer Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Formal techniques were used as a powerful device for verifying laptop systems and are increasingly more applied for optimizing embedded pc architectures. in particular, formal techniques are hired to optimize the electricity consumption of embedded structures with the aid of reading device fashions at various tiers of abstraction. through formal techniques, designers can select out and optimize positive low-level abilities, including reminiscence manage rules, useful resource allocation algorithms, and the layout of circuits within the gadget, which greatly impact power consumption. additionally, formal strategies can be used to research the strength consumption of complex interactions between couples of additives of an embedded gadget if you need to discover regions of improvement. moreover, formal strategies can also be used to affirm machine designs and power-saving measures taken by designers, ensuring that no unexpected issue effects rise. In sum, using formal strategies for electricity optimization in embedded computer architectures can lessen complexity and price while offering higher reliability and overall performance.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of Big Data Technologies on Network Performance of Smart Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Large facts technology have revolutionized the manner smart systems, along with the net of things (IoT) and gadget-to-device (M2M) verbal exchange networks, operate. The accelerated availability of massive datasets, blended with excessive-overall performance computing and facts storage talents, has enabled the development of many powerful programs and network overall performance-enhancing answers. This paper analyzes the impact of huge statistics technology at the performance of smart structures. We study the use of huge statistics technologies which includes Hadoop, Apache Spark, and Apache Flink within the context of numerous smart applications, inclusive of predictive analytics, actual-time analytics, and facts lake optimization. The paper argues that the adoption of huge statistics technologies can enhance the scalability and overall performance of smart systems drastically. Specifically, the usage of huge statistics technologies can enhance the scalability and safety of records lakes and permit actual-time analytics in smart systems.

articleTitle: zkSHIELD – A Web-Based Cross-Chain Zero Knowledge Asset Proof
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The global transition towards Web3 is giving rise to many blockchain networks, each with its native cryptocurrency. Ethereum is used for decentralized applications, Bitcoin is used for investment, and Polygon is used for scalability solutions. Furthermore, a few well-known blockchain platforms have implemented interoperability features, meaning users can now send wrapped tokens around different blockchains. User assets are then distributed across multiple blockchain networks and wallets. This means user assets are already distributed across multiple tokens on different blockchain networks. This work presents a web application that allows you to visualize your assets distributed across different blockchain networks and wallets. Notably, this work supports the straightforward integration of secondary wallets with user accounts. In addition, this work supports tracking the historical user asset transfer requests, including incoming and outgoing ones, and storing the metadata associated with each asset transfer, including its corresponding proof’s Content Identifier (CID) after zkSNARKs proof generation by hosting it on the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS).

articleTitle: Analyzing Intelligent Optimization Techniques for 6G Radio Resource Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This technical abstract discusses the software of shrewd optimization strategies for 6G Radio aid Allocation (RRA). Technological advances in 6G wireless structures require efficient radio aid control algorithms for proper network characteristics, particularly in phrases of spectrum allocation. The cutting-edge RRA solutions have relied mainly on conventional optimization methods, which include Particle Swarm Optimization, Differential Evolution algorithms, and Table seek. However, due to the extended complexity of 6G networks, more than conventional techniques are required. Consequently, this observation proposes to explore and analyse the modern-day clever optimization strategies, together with synthetic Bee Colony, Deep Reinforcement gaining knowledge of, and Swarm Intelligence, to broaden superior RRA answers. Simulations and actual international assessments will be applied to analysee and evaluate the performance of the distinctive sensible optimization techniques. It is expected that the proposed methods will provide higher RRA solutions with improved spectral efficiency, throughput, energy performance, and latency in 6G networks.

articleTitle: Energy Management in Microgrid using Linear programming Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Microgrids are low-voltage distribution network which comprise of controllable loads and distributed energy resources (DERs) that can be used in an isolated or grid-connected mode. The microgrid energy management system (EMS) is the hardware or software components used to efficiently operate microgrid energy resources by scheduling commitments for on-demand distributed generation units energy storage systems, energy imports and controllable loads to meet specific goals. Reliability, stability, and efficiency in microgrids are dependent upon effective energy management. The utilization of optimization techniques is crucial in accomplishing these goals. The optimization process present in the paper stores or sells energy battery system based on anticipated costs and load profile. The linear programming (LP) optimization approach minimize operating costs of microgrid for a sunny and cloudy day while maintaining the operational restrictions using MATLAB 2020. The results shows that on a cloudy day the cost of microgrid is 46.9% increased as compared to a sunny day.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition of Autistic Children from Facial Images Using Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Interpretation of an individual’s feelings can be done through analyzing their facial expressions and body movements. Emotion detection from facial expressions is a prominent research focus within the field of Artificial Intelligence. This approach is particularly significant in areas such as detecting autism in children, where precise diagnoses are important for personalized aid and support. However, it is challenging to predict the expression of kids with autism as one fails to read their feelings by seeing their reactions because they are unable to show reactions like normal human beings. Autism, sometimes known as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), encompasses a wide range of conditions characterized by challenges in communication, both verbal and nonverbal, repetitive behaviors, and social interaction skills. In this paper, we propose a new image dataset of autistic children named FERAC which has four classes (joy, anger, natural and fear) with the help of an existing dataset by Dr. Fatma M Talaat. In addition, we present a novel approach utilizing a hybrid model that integrates DenseNet121 and MobileNetV2 architectures to identify the emotions of autistic children from facial images. We developed and analyzed our hybrid models with four deep-learning models (CNN, VGG16, ResNet18, and IncerptionV3) and among them, our proposed hybrid model outperformed the other individual deep-learning models in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Autonomous and Adaptive Communications Systems in Automotive Applications

abstract: Autonomous and adaptive communications systems are increasingly being used in automotive programs to permit safer and extra-green navigation and driving. This communication allows the automobile to dynamically adjust its verbal exchange and navigation strategies in response to modifications in the environment, inclusive of visitors and weather. articleTitle: Enhanced PSO-Integrated Machine Learning for Launch Vehicle Engine Temperature and Pressure Monitoring for Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Maintaining the health of the launch vehicle engines is essential to the mission’s success, including safe ascent, payload deployment, and orbital insertion. Preemptive maintenance is made possible by early anomaly identification, which reduces mission risks and maximizes operational effectiveness. Engineers can prevent catastrophic failures by proactively mitigating possible difficulties by accurate forecasting before launch. During space exploration missions, timely maintenance and modifications protect personnel, spacecraft, and important payloads, further enhancing mission reliability. This Research work presents a pioneering approach to predict launch vehicle engine health, the study integrates Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with Enhanced PSO (EPSO) to precisely determine vehicle engine health. Employing real vibration data from rocket launches, and developing various machine learning models such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Naïve Bayes, and k-Nearest Neighbours(KNN) among the four models we chose KNN since it showed better accuracy. We integrated the EPSO to the KNN model to implement the accuracy for better prediction. This research contributes significantly to advancing health diagnostics and optimization for launch vehicles, ultimately bolstering the safety and dependability of aerospace systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Total Airborne Duration for a Quadcopter/ Hexacopter Using Tethered Power Cable/Mechanism

The sustenance time in the air achieved through these batteries is limited to 20 minutes to 60 minutes. However, if the quadcopters and hexacopters are required for relaying purposes or aerial surveys of a disaster-struck place, then the information gained is very little, as the sustenance time to perform such roles is very limited. articleTitle: Investigating Optimality Models for Spectrum Sharing in 6G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Spectrum sharing in 6G networks is an area of study that has currently been gaining attention due to the improved call for Wi-Fi offerings and the finite amount of to-be-had spectrum. This paper investigates optimality fashions for spectrum sharing in 6G networks with the intention of attaining maximum performance. In particular, the authors consciousness of the hassle of spectrum sharing among multiple users and suggest a stochastic optimization version primarily based on the Nash Bargaining answer (NBS). The proposed model is then evaluated for unique eventualities with the use of a 6G community simulator. The outcomes show that the proposed model can acquire vast gains in spectrum efficiency compared to existing tactics. Furthermore, the authors also explore the impact of the parameters of the version on the performance and provide insights on the way to optimize them. The findings of this study may be used to expand more green spectrum-sharing mechanisms for 6G networks.

articleTitle: Keyword spotting using convolutional neural network for speech recognition in Hindi
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this study, we investigate the application of keyword spotting (KWS) in the domain of Hindi speech recognition, utilizing a dataset comprising $\mathbf{4 0, 0 0 0}$ audio samples. With a sampling rate of 44 kHz and an average duration of 1.9 seconds per sample, we focus on developing an efficient on-device KWS system tailored for user-specific queries. Leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for classification, we employ feature engineering techniques to convert raw audio recordings into Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) as an input for our network. Our experiments encompass various CNN architectures, exploring their efficacy in identifying predefined keywords within the continuous speech stream. Our CNN-based approach achieves a commendable accuracy rate of $\mathbf{9 1. 7 9 \%}$ through rigorous evaluation, demonstrating promising performance while ensuring computational efficiency and user-specific customization in Hindi speech recognition.

articleTitle: Classification of Motor Imagery EEG Signals Using Divergence Based CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Motor imagery-based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have garnered significant attention in neuro engineering for their potential to enable communication and control in individuals with motor impairments. Electroencephalography (EEG) signals captured during motor imagery tasks offer valuable insights into the intention to execute specific movements. This study introduces a novel approach that utilizes a Divergence-based Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN) for classifying motor imagery EEG signals. The DCNN aims to augment the network’s discriminative power and enhance classification accuracy. The proposed approach incorporates three main components: Daubechies wavelet transform, Common Spatial Patterns (CSP), and CNN model. The Daubechies wavelet transform is employed to extract relevant features from the EEG signals. CSP is utilized to select discriminative features that capture the differences between motor imagery tasks, finally the CNN model is trained to classify the EEG signals into different motor imagery categories. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed DCNN surpasses baseline CNN models and achieves higher accuracy in classifying motor imagery EEG signals. Furthermore, the DCNN exhibits robustness to variations in EEG signal characteristics with accuracy of $85 \%$ while the existing methods classifies with accuracy of 79%. The findings suggest that the integration of divergence-based regularization within the DCNN architecture holds promise for enhancing the classification performance of motor imagery-based BCIs. The proposed approach has the potential to contribute to the development of more accurate and reliable BCIs, thereby facilitating improved communication and control for individuals with motor disabilities.

articleTitle: Redefining Disease Prediction with EnhancedMachine Learning Models

Previous studies have focused on machine learning models such as Random Forest, Decision Trees (DT), Support Vector Machines (SVM), k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Gaussian Naive Bayes, using symptoms as parameters for disease detection. Unlike previous methods, this model utilizes a Kaggle Disease Symptom Prediction dataset and enhances the information by weighting symptoms based on their rarity. The dataset is then trained using various machine learning techniques, including Random Forest, Decision Tree, Gaussian Naive Bayes, SVM, and KNN. Additionally, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are employed to analyze the patient’s historical data. The SVM algorithm is used to identify the most likely illness. The proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and reliability. Random Forest-98.15, Decision Tree classifier-94.64, KNN-90.46, SVM-81.14, Gaussian Naïve Bayes89.09

articleTitle: Sensor-Based Real-Time Monitoring System for Product Counting, Inspection and Production Analysis in Industrial Environment

abstract: This paper presents an innovative automated system for counting and inspecting plastic gunny bags in industrial settings, addressing the prevalent challenges of manual counting such as errors, inefficiencies, and delays. The system employs IR sensors and Node MCU technology to automatically count bags as they move along a printing machine, marking them as finished products and detecting any damage. Upon detecting damage, the system can halt the entire process to prevent further issues. An integrated Database Management System (DBMS) efficiently stores and manages the production data generated by the sensors. This automation not only eliminates human errors and improves counting accuracy but also enhances overall production efficiency. Furthermore, the system provides real-time data for comprehensive production analysis, enabling informed decision-making and optimization of production workflows. The proposed method offers a reliable and efficient solution for modernizing plastic gunny bag counting and inspection processes in industrial environments.

articleTitle: Advancements in Cricket Shot Detection: Integrating Human Pose Estimation and Deep Learning for Automated Analysis
