articleTitle: Enhancing Deployment and Performance Measurement of Serverless Cloud Microservices with Warm Start
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for deploying and evaluating the performance of applications in serverless cloud environments for microservices. It addresses challenges stemming from the distributed nature of microservices and the imperative to protect sensitive data. Key aspects covered include architectural design considerations, emphasizing decomposition into independent microservices with clear interfaces. Robust security mechanisms such as encryption, authentication, and authorization are discussed for safeguarding data shared between microservices. Deployment strategies on serverless cloud platforms like AWS Lambda are explored, highlighting benefits like automatic scaling and cost efficiency. The framework also integrates warm start techniques to mitigate cold start latency issues commonly associated with serverless computing. Techniques for monitoring and logging performance metrics such as responses times, error rate, and supply usage are discussed. Real-world case studies demonstrate the practical implementation and effectiveness of the framework in overcoming challenges associated with deploying an application in serverless cloud environments for microservices.

articleTitle: A Novel Chaotic Map with High Chaotic Dynamics for Image Encryption Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This article provides a novel chaotic map, termed a Sine $e \pi$ map, that deals with the problem of non-uniformity and lower Lyapunov exponents. In the Sine $e \pi$ map, transcendental functions are applied along with modulo operations, which physically represent discontinuous time-varying non-linearities. This results in extremely complex chaotic behaviour that is highly sensitive to initial conditions and control parameters, both of which are regarded as the keys to the cryptosystem. The Sine $e \pi$ map is examined through the phase diagram and Lyapunov exponent. Further, the Sine $e \pi$ map is used to develop an image encryption algorithm based on simultaneous confusion and diffusion. According to experiments and security simulations, the image encryption algorithm effectively encrypts images in less computational time while providing great protection against a variety of attacks such as brute-force, differential, statistical etc.

articleTitle: Developing Virtual Reality Applications in Medical Education for Osteotomy Knee Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising tool in medical education, offering immersive and interactive experiences for trainees to learn complex surgical procedures. This paper explores the development of VR applications specifically tailored for medical education in osteotomy knee surgery. By leveraging VR technology, medical students can engage in realistic simulations of the surgical procedure, enhancing their understanding of anatomy, surgical techniques, and decision-making processes in a controlled and risk-free environment. The VR applications for osteotomy knee surgery providing a comprehensive educational experience. Through a combination of realistic graphics, and interactive scenarios, VR facilitates experiential learning and skill acquisition, ultimately improving the competency. Moreover, the scalability and accessibility of VR platforms offer opportunities for widespread adoption in medical training programs, addressing the growing demand for innovative and effective educational tools in healthcare.

articleTitle: An Improved Multi-Camera Fusion Technique for Object Detection and Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper offers a multi-digicam fusion approach for item detection and tracking that appreciably outperforms conventional techniques. The machine consists of a fusion-based technique that combines photograph frames from more than one camera to section out item areas. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is then used to stumble on and classify objects within these areas. Publish-processing strategies are used to refine the outcomes for progressed accuracy. Finally, a Kalman clear-out is carried out to allow item tracking in real time. Experimental consequences demonstrate that the proposed method is capable of reaping better accuracy for each detection and tracking compared to the baseline methods. Moreover, for the same digicam setup, the system is able to detect and track objects in an environment stricken by big lighting variations and adjustments in the background. It focuses on the robustness of the proposed machine and its capacity for sensible programs.

articleTitle: An Area-Efficient VLSI Architecture with Ladner-Fischer PPA for High-Speed Pseudo-Random Bit Generation

abstract: Pseudorandom Bit Generation (PRBG) plays a crucial role in ensuring the security of cryptographic systems by generating random bit sequences using deterministic algorithms. The effectiveness of these systems hinges on the unpredictability of the cryptographic keys they generate. This study focuses on optimizing the efficiency of PRBG systems by addressing key factors such as speed, area utilization, and power consumption. Leveraging the parallel prefix adder (PPA) architecture, particularly the Laden-Fisher design, our proposed method aims to enhance the performance of PRBG implementations. We present a Verilog-based design implemented using Vivado 2023.1 targeting an Artix-7 FPGA platform. Through this approach, we achieve rapid and reliable bit generation while effectively managing FPGA resources, ultimately enhancing the overall efficiency of PRBG systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive Traffic Control Using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The adaptive traffic light control using edge computing project leverages AI-driven techniques to enhance the efficiency of traffic management at critical road junctions. By employing image processing methods, it captures real-time data on vehicular density and traffic patterns at the junction. These images enable the system to identify vehicle types and count their numbers in different lanes. This information feeds into a pre-trained machine learning model, which generates recommendations for optimal traffic signal durations. These recommendations are then communicated to the traffic light controller, which dynamically adjusts signal timings based on current conditions. The adaptive traffic control system continuously monitors and adapts to changing traffic patterns, leading to reduced congestion and minimized delays. This innovative approach ensures a more efficient use of road infrastructure and smoother traffic flow at important junctions.

articleTitle: DeepAge: A Convolutional Neural Network Approach for Accurate Age Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In a variety of applications, including human-computer interaction, targeted marketing, and a project offers a reliable method for precise age estimation based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Making use of an extensive dataset, the model applies sophisticated data augmentation methods to improve training robustness and diversity. The incorporation of regularization, techniques like dropout and L2 regularization, which greatly reduce overfitting and enhance generalization to new data, is one of the major advances. The outcomes show a significant improvement in the training and validation measures, with the mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE) for age prediction showing the most reductions. The model performs admirably despite a small amount of overfitting, demonstrating the effectiveness of the used methods. This work highlights CNNs’ promise in age estimation problems and provides a strong basis for further improvements, such as the addition of bigger datasets and more complex architectures. This thorough methodology guarantees that the model can be applied in real-world situations, which makes it a significant contribution to the subject.

articleTitle: Deepfake Video Detection using Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The rapid advancement of deepfake production technologies is threatening the reliability of media content. Deepfake videos have the potential to increasingly deceive and manipulate viewers by propagating false information, influential public opinion, and damaging reputations. The pseudo-realistic content produced by these methods is exceedingly difficult for conventional detection techniques to identify. Therefore, there is a need for effective deepfake detection and identification of such videos and images. This research employs neural networks, specifically, ResNet, EfficientNet, and InceptionNet, to distinguish between fraudulent and authentic videos and images. FF++ 2020, Deeper-Forensics, and DFDC datasets are used, and evaluated these models Our results demonstrate the potential of these neural networks in countering the growing threat posed by deepfake technology.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Piezoresistivity in Junctionless Gate-All-Around Nanosheet and Nanowire
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Piezoresistivity is the property of certain materials, including semiconductors, to demonstrate a shift in electrical resistivity in response to mechanical stress or strain. Gauge factor is used to measure the piezoresistive sensitivity. In this paper, we have designed Gate All Around Juntionless Nanosheet and evaluated the piezoresistivity specifically for low strain applications in comparison to the Gate All Around Junctionless Nanowire. The gauge factor of the nanosheet is greater than the gauge factor of the nanowire when the area of their cross-sections is equal. Strain of $360 \mu \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{m}$ is applied and than NW JLFET when operated in the subthreshold, threshold, and above threshold regimes, respectively. Because of the increased piezoresistive sensitivity in nanosheet, the GAA JL Nanosheet are excellent choices for applications requiring lower strain sensing.

articleTitle: Investigating the Challenges of 5G-Enabled Health Care Management Models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The 5G era is the modern-day development within the discipline of verbal exchange networks, and its emergence is anticipated to revolutionize contemporary digital offerings. Mainly, the 5G-enabled healthcare control models are anticipated to facilitate specialized and included solutions to deal with the organizational, operational, and regulatory challenges inside the healthcare area. This paper examines the capability-demanding situations posed via the adoption of 5Genabled fitness care management models. The paper outlines the ability blessings of 5 G -enabled models, such as enlarging access to fitness care offerings, green useful resource usage, advanced facts privacy, and real-time monitoring. However, the usage of 5 G technology also introduces challenges associated with the excessive fee of installation and adoption, the need for secure hardware and software program infrastructure, and the risk of era disruption. The authors also talk about the various risks posed via the integration of 5 G technology with current structures in fitness care, which includes malfunctioning of the devices and community. The paper concludes that there is a need for careful consideration in the use of 5G-enabled services for health care management.

articleTitle: SIGDI: Reviving Tradition for Urban Sustainability.
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Traditional cooking stoves serve an important role in households around the world, giving sustenance and cultural importance to communities with varied socioeconomic backgrounds. Among these, the SIGDI, a traditional Indian cooking stove, represents culinary history, simplicity, and efficiency. However, as urbanization accelerates and environmental concerns grow, there is an urgent need to rethink and alter conventional cooking processes to line with modern sustainability aims. In response, this study investigates the resuscitation and augmentation of the SIGDI using novel materials and manufacturing procedures. Using stainless steel and the deep drawing technique, they move away from traditional fabrication processes and toward a more efficient and scalable manufacturing strategy. The use of stainless steel, which is known for its durability and heat resistance, promises to extend the SIGDI’s life and performance while meeting the different cooking needs of both rural and urban areas. Furthermore, our examination of the SIGDI’s adaptability as a cooking stove and fireplace highlights its ability to reconcile traditional and modern lifestyles. This study aims to contribute to the ongoing discussion about sustainable cooking practices by combining materials science, manufacturing engineering, and cultural anthropology, fostering a deeper appreciation for traditional wisdom while also embracing the possibilities of contemporary innovation. Finally, by resurrecting classic cooking stoves like the SIGDI, they hope to pave the road for a more sustainable, resilient, and culturally rich culinary scene in the twenty-first century.

articleTitle: Deep Ensembling with Multimodal Image Fusion for Efficient Classification of Lung Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study focuses on the classification of cancerous and healthy slices from multimodal lung images. The data used in the research comprises Computed Tomography (CT) and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) images. The proposed strategy achieves the fusion of PET and CT images by utilizing Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and an Autoencoder. Subsequently, a new ensemble-based classifier developed, Deep Ensembled Multimodal Fusion (DEMF), employing majority voting to classify the sample images under examination. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) employed to visualize the classification accuracy of cancer-affected images. Given the limited sample size, a random image augmentation strategy employed during the training phase. The DEMF network helps mitigate the challenges of scarce data in computer-aided medical image analysis. The proposed network compared with state-of-the-art networks across three publicly available datasets. The network outperforms others based on the metrics - Accuracy, F1Score, Precision, and Recall. The investigation results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed network.

articleTitle: Development of Real-Time GPS Tracking and ETA on an Android Application using Esp32 and Ublox NEO6MV2 for E-Jeepney in Quezon City, Metro Manila
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: There is no denying that public transportation is and will continue to be a part of a commuter’s daily life as it serves as a quick and easy way to reach their destinations. However, it holds its own disadvantages, such as unpredictable arrival times, poor comfort and safety, and disorganized queues. Research shows that in Metro Manila, Jeepneys are the second most used public transportation, making up $19.1 \%$ of all journeys. Additionally, 7,000 out of 150,000 jeepneys are electric or contemporary models. To eliminate challenges faced by the current transportation system, this research paper was proposed to develop a real-time GPS tracking and ETA system, and an Android App to access data for E-Jeeps in Quezon City, Metro Manila. Tests were conducted and results show that the GPS tracking system generated a percentage error of $0.0017 \%$, making the system accurate and reliable. Whereas the ETA system resulted in an average delay of 1 minute and 35 seconds for all trials.

articleTitle: Cross Language Compiler Construction From Matlab To Python
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The domain of cross compiler development pertains to the process wherein code written in one programming language is translated to another so that it may be compatible with another environment and may take advantage of the benefits of the other platform. This work aims at constructing a cross-language compiler to convert code of MATLAB to Python. Therefore, higher performance language and a powerful matrix operation library NumPy and a robust visualization library matplotlib is used in this research. The system is named as Mat2py, and it works efficiently in translation. Difficulties are to resolve issues related to the syntactic and semantic differences in the languages, overcome numeric imprecisions, and ensure the coherence of data structures and libraries. These complications are responded in this work by using NumPy and matplotlib of Python to transplant all the functionality accessible in MATLAB. Mat2py, therefore, ensure a correct and optimal conversion process through an analysis of the MATLAB function to its equivalent Python version and testing individual functions.

articleTitle: Adaptive clustering strategies and channel allocation for a D2D communication system
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This technical abstract offers a novel adaptive clustering approach and channel allocation approach for a tool-to-device (D2D) communique gadget. An optimization method is proposed based on the graph concept and recreation concept to reduce the general interference of many of the D2D entities. Clustering techniques are utilized to segment the D2D users and decide the channel allocation. Similarly, D2D interference is prevented via allocating channels on an adaptive basis to make sure that the largest quantity of D2D entities can talk efficiently. The proposed optimization approach can be implemented in any wireless conversation device and is especially beneficial when the frequency aid is limited. Simulation consequences exhibit that the proposed strategy considerably improves the overall performance of the gadget by averting interference and improving the connectivity of the D2D cluster.

articleTitle: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence for Sentiment Analysis in Smart Citie
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Sentiment evaluation is a form of artificial intelligence (AI) that makes use of herbal language processing (NLP) to classify text in keeping with the emotional tone it conveys. This technology can provide valuable insights into the sentiments of residents living in smart cities. It could allow nearby governments to better track and deal with sentiment shifts in a fee-green manner while also supplying them with the possibility to decorate their urban planning by incorporating reactions to offerings and tasks. By means of utilizing AI-primarily based sentiment evaluation, nearby governments can become aware of developments and styles and gain a deeper knowledge of the general public sentiment about their city in real-time. They also can use the insights to sing the success of beyond guidelines and offerings while improving upon them within the destiny. In addition, it is able to enable neighborhood governments to react quickly to online newsfeed pastimes, permitting them to deal with issues swiftly and efficaciously permitting them to higher reply to the needs of their residents.

articleTitle: Improving Cancer Prediction in Recommender Systems through Gradient Boosting
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The analysis of various styles of most cancers is frequently reliant on accurate prediction models. Recommender systems are powerful equipment that allows the prediction of cancer development and recurrence based totally on information accumulated from affected person information. But, standard feed-forward neural networks (FFNNs) utilized in current cancer prediction fashions are limited via their potential to capture subtle nonlinear relationships among affected person variables. Gradient boosting is a device gaining knowledge of set of rules that makes use of an ensemble of weak selection bushes to produce an effective predictive version. This have a look at examines the capability for boosting algorithms to enhance the predictive ability of the FFNN fashions currently used in recommender structures for predicting most cancers progression and recurrence. The outcomes of our test reveal that boosting algorithms are able to boom model accuracy over FFNNs whilst additionally lowering training time. Moreover, nonlinear relationships between affected person variables are captured extra successfully by means of boosting than with FFNNs. those findings keep crucial implications for the development of powerful predictive models for cancer progression and recurrence.

articleTitle: Enhanced Gain Double - Output Boost/Buck DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research paper presents a comprehensive study on the mathematical modelling and control of a single input dual output (SIDO) step-up and step-down voltage converter. The focus of this study is on achieving optimal voltage gain while addressing challenges such as load variation and line variation. A detailed mathematical model of the SIDO converter is developed to understand its behaviour under varying operating conditions. The study emphasizes the analysis of voltage gain characteristics, the converter's performance in the presence of load variations and line variations. To enhance the converter control and stability, a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller method is employed. The PI controller is designed and optimized to achieve efficient regulation of the output voltages, ensuring stability and improved response to dynamic load and input voltage changes. MATLAB simulations of the proposed control strategy demonstrate enhanced voltage regulation, reduced output voltage ripples, and improved transient response. The findings contribute to advancing the understanding and application of SIDO converters in power electronics, offering a valuable approach for efficient power conversion in various systems.

articleTitle: Outage Analysis of Downlink Cooperative SWIPT -NOMA system with optimum energy harvesting and imperfect CSI
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cooperative communication is an important technique for 5G and future wireless communication to increase the quality of services in vast infrastructures. The power consumption of devices is becoming a significant concern in wireless networks composed of thousands of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors as we progress toward more advanced communication systems. To overcome this problem, there is a push for green communication technology such as radio frequency energy and simultaneous wireless power and data transfer (SWIPT) are introduced. In this work, a cooperative SWIPT- SWIPT-based non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) communication system has been analyzed which overcomes the aforementioned issues. Here, the quality of services in huge networks is improved with cooperative technique and the energy efficiency of wireless communication networks is improved with SWIPT. This can lead to increased network sustainability and lower energy costs. In this paper, we are considering imperfect CSI (channel state information) to obtain an accurate analysis of Cooperative SWIPT NOMA. We are considering two user NOMA where the user positions are near and far. Here, we have obtained the closed-form equation for outage probability (OP) with inaccurate CSI and simulated results are validated with analytical results.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: AI-Driven Dermatology: CNN-RF Hybrid Model for Skin Lesion’s Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The spectrum of skin diseases, based on their nature, poses significant barriers to health that affect individuals internationally. Thus, basic procedures such as accurate and early diagnosis are paramount to successful treatment. This paper presents a hybrid model called Convolutional Neural Network and Random Forest (CNNRF) for accurately diagnosing five different types of skin diseases: Melanoma, Benign nevus, Basal cell carcinomas 5CC, Dermatofibroma, vascular lesions. Resizing, normalization techniques, and data augmentation were applied to preprocess the dataset, including annotated photos of skin lesions. The CNN-RF method is based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) feature extraction and classification provided by Random Forests (RFs). Based on the results of the experiments, it was established that the proposed CNN-RF model achieved greater classification accuracy of 94% compared to the CNN model with $\mathbf{9 1 \%}$ and the RF model with $\mathbf{8 8 \%}$. Moreover, for the same experiment, the CNN-RF model established an accuracy of 93 per cent, recall of 94 per cent, and $\mathbf{F 1}$ score of 94 per cent. The model’s performance was demonstrated and analyzed using a confusion matrix and classification reports. The accuracy and recall rates were very high for this type of skin lesion, specifically up to 95% accuracy and 96% recall for Dermatofibroma and Vascular Lesions. Nonetheless, this research asserts the reliability of the proposed CNN-RF model as a feasible instrument for diagnosing skin diseases automatically, as well as with superior precision and stability. Thus, the findings hold significant implications for clinical practice alerts, as the model can assist dermatologists in providing timely identification to improve the quality of treatment for their clients. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and exploring other types of compound models to increase the accuracy of the diagnosis. This work contributes to the advancement of automated diagnostic-making systems in dermatology.

articleTitle: Weakly Supervised Temporal Attention Framework for Video Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Weakly supervised anomaly detection in surveillance videos is a formidable challenging task in visual understanding research community. A key factor contributing to the challenge of detecting abnormal events is the inability to effectively represent the temporal relationships between the snippets in videos. To address this challenge, our proposed approach incorporates a temporal attention module to model the temporal dependencies among video snippets. This module enables the network to focus on the more significant snippets by assigning attention scores to them. By multiplying the attention scores with the corresponding feature vectors, our method effectively detects anomaly events. Moreover, we explore the use of an inner-bag ranking loss function, which aids in learning discriminating representations and anomaly scores for efficient abnormal event detection. Experimental results obtained from the UCFC and LAD benchmark datasets validate the performance of the proposed method. It outperforms other existing methods, demonstrating superior performance in terms of anomaly detection accuracy and false alarm rate.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Currency Recognition and Value Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Accurate currency recognition and conversion are essential for smooth cross-border transactions in today’s globalized economy. Yet, the wide variety of cash denominations and variances, combined with the complexities of deep learning and image processing, make this work extremely difficult. A comparative comparison of deep learning models is helpful in addressing these issues by identifying the best method for value identification and currency recognition. The objective of this research is to examine how well ResNet50V2, VGG16, and MobileNet perform in terms of precisely identifying and valuing currencies. Utilizing a sample of Thai and Indian banknotes from IEEE data port that include notes with differences in orientation (rotated at 180-degree angles), lighting conditions, and other environmental factors., the study assesses how well each model handles the complexity of money data. The purpose of this study is to give practitioners in the banking and finance industries useful insights.

articleTitle: Code Confabulator: Harnessing LLMs to Compile Code for Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Code visualization tools play a core role for visualization of the code and helping novices in understanding, analyzing, and optimization of their programs. Tools such as Algorithm Visualizer and PythonTutor are developed to make algorithm visualization possible across different programming languages like Python, Java, C, and $\mathrm{C++}$. Despite their advantages, these tools suffer from unnecessary data collection, increased time complexity, and limitation in visualizing a few data structures. In our research, we want to introduce a more humanlike view of understanding and solve the shortcomings mentioned above by proposing a framework, which will make use of LLMs for extracting data from the code in Python, Java, C, or C++ to be visualized. In our framework, we have used LLMs instead of the traditional compiler for feasibility and adaptability. Our objective is the appropriateness evaluation of LLMs for this task, starting from freeform prompts. The LLM is asked to generate outputs in a given format; hence, these outputs are taken and converted into visualizations with a rule-based approach. The task will be done to enhance quality visualization and reduce time complexity while allowing the user to view the code at a human level view. We have also publicly released the framework so that people are able to provide further contributions and improvements.

articleTitle: Utilizing Generative AI for Text-to-Image Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With the rapid evolution of generative artificial intelligence (AI), this research project delves into the realm of Text to Image generation. Leveraging advanced neural network architectures, the study explores the synthesis of visual content from textual descriptions. The project not only investigates the technical intricacies of the generative models involved but also delves into the potential applications across various domains such as creative content creation, design, and multimedia enhancement. The methodology encompasses a comprehensive examination of state-of-the-art techniques in Text to Image generation, analyzing their strengths, weaknesses, and advancements. Natural language processing (NLP) plays a pivotal role in capturing the semantic nuances embedded in textual inputs, enabling the models to create visually compelling and contextually accurate images. The comparative analysis considers factors such as model performance metrics, scalability, and adaptability to diverse textual inputs. As the project unfolds, it addresses ethical considerations inherent in image synthesis, emphasizing the importance of responsible AI practices and the need for validation mechanisms to ensure the generated images align with the intended context. The paper concludes with a discussion on potential applications of Text to Image generation in fields like content creation, virtual environments, and educational materials, highlighting the transformative impact of generative AI in shaping the future of visual content creation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Virtual Machine Migration Technique for Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Virtual Machine (VM) migration in cloud environments is essential for maintaining high availability, load balancing, and efficient resource utilization. Pre-copy VM migration, a prevalent technique, often faces challenges like high data transfer volumes, extended migration times, and noticeable downtime. This study proposed a compression-based pre-copy VM migration technique that employs Characteristic-Based Compression (CBC) to address these challenges. Our approach significantly reduces data transferred by analyzing and compressing memory pages based on their characteristics, thereby decreasing total migration time and minimizing service disruption. Experimental results demonstrate that our technique outperforms traditional pre-copy methods by reducing data transfer by up to 69% and migration time by 33.33% while diminishing downtime by $\mathbf{4 2 \%}$.

articleTitle: An All-Inclusive Daily Task Tracker App for Enhancing College Student Productivity
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research proposes a comprehensive daily task tracker app designed to alleviate the challenges faced by college students in effectively managing their busy schedules. The app offers a user-friendly interface with intuitive features aimed at enhancing productivity and organization. Key components include task creation, allowing users to input and categorize assignments, deadlines, and activities. Customizable priority levels and reminders assist users in staying on track with their tasks. Flexibility is integrated to accommodate the dynamic nature of college schedules, enabling users to adjust and update tasks as needed. Seamless integration across multiple devices facilitates access from smartphones, tablets, and computers. Emphasizing the user experience, the app employs a visually appealing design and intuitive navigation for accessibility across all technical backgrounds. Continuous improvement and updates are prioritized through feedback collection and iterative refinement. Ultimately, the daily task tracker app aims to empower college students to efficiently manage their time, reduce stress, and achieve academic and personal goals effortlessly.

articleTitle: Automated Detection and Analysis of Minor Deformations in Flat Walls Due to Railway Vibrations Using LiDAR and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study introduces an advanced methodology for automatically identifying minor deformations in flat walls caused by vibrations from nearby railway tracks. It leverages high-density Terrestrial Laser Scanner (TLS) LiDAR surveys and $\mathrm{AI} / \mathrm{ML}$ techniques to collect and analyze data. The scan data is processed into a detailed point cloud, which is segmented to distinguish ground points, trees, buildings, and other objects. The analysis focuses on identifying sections along flat walls and estimating their deformations relative to the ground orientation. Findings from the study, conducted at the RGIPT campus, reveal significant deformations in walls close to the railway corridor, with the highest deformations ranging from 7 to $\mathbf{8 c m}$ and an average of 3 to 4 cm. In contrast, walls further from the corridor show negligible deformations. The developed automated process for feature extraction and deformation monitoring demonstrates potential for structural health monitoring. By integrating LiDAR data with machine learning, the methodology provides an efficient system for identifying and analyzing structural deformations, highlighting the importance of continuous monitoring for ensuring structural integrity and public safety in urban infrastructure. This approach represents a substantial advancement in automated feature extraction and deformation analysis, contributing to more effective management of urban infrastructure.

articleTitle: A Novel Accuracy Analysis of Credit Card Fraud Detection Using ResNet50 Over Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A novel accuracy identification of fraudulent activity on credit cards using ResNet50 over linear regression (LR). For the purpose of detecting credit card fraud in online transactions, data mining was crucial. In our research, we will be using ResNet50 as proposed, which will be compared with existing algorithms such as linear regression (LR). The data set needed for the detection of credit card fraud is accomplished by utilizing ResNet50 and Linear Regression (LR) algorithms. For two algorithms, there are two groups each with 15 dataset sample size values and G power values as 75% and 95% confidence intervals. The accuracy of ResNet50 is $\mathbf{9 5. 3 9 \%}$ and the loss is 4.61%, which outperforms linear regression (LR) at $\mathbf{9 0. 7 6 \%}$ and loss at 9.24%, respectively. a T-test with independent samples and obtained a p-value of 0.00 ($\mathbf{p}\lt0.05$), where the level of significance is lower than 0.05. This implies the results are statistically more significant. The result shows that ResNet50 is statistically more significant than the linear regression for novel accuracy analysis of credit card fraud regarding accuracy

articleTitle: Natural Language Interface for Data Visualization: Harnessing the Power of Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Democratizing data analysis is the need of the hour, empowering a wider range of users within corporations to engage with data and uncover valuable insights. Because of the inherent ambiguity of natural language and the frequent lack of quality and clarity in user queries, implementing functioning Natural Language Interfaces (NLIs) has proven to be a challenging task. These problems make it difficult for existing language models to understand user intent effectively. This study introduces a novel data visualization tool that leverages the power of Large Language Models (LLMs) to empower corporations and research institutions in extracting meaningful insights from vast datasets. LLMs interpret user input and generate goals, which LIDA, a library developed by Microsoft, uses to create a wide range of visualizations with libraries like matplotlib, seaborn, and plotly, based on these goals and user instructions. This system bridges the gap between Natural Language Interfaces(NLIs) and data visualization by enabling users to submit prompts in natural language. Users can formulate questions in natural language, eliminating the need for complex code or data manipulation expertise. This work compares and contrasts the performance of open source models Mistral 7B instruct-v3, LLaMa3 8B, and proprietary model, gpt 3.5-turbo across several case studies as the graphs generated are dependent completely on the interpretation power of LLMs.

articleTitle: Machine Vision Solutions for Automated Fatigue and Stress Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: System imaginative and prescient solutions for computerized fatigue and stress, trying to provide a scalable answer for an extensive variety of stress and fatigue checks. The solutions allow for the purchase of pics from multiple viewing angles, offering facts from multiple check specimens for analysis and reporting. These answers automate the assessment of specimen responses to fatigue and stress, such as pressure measurements, vibrational analysis, and cloth displacement. The collected facts are analyzed with the use of PC imaginative and prescient algorithms, and the consequences are offered in graphical and numerical formats for comparison and assessment towards predetermined reference or experimental values. These approaches can be automatic to lessen the time and effort to measure and realize the check effects, imparting a powerful device for testing and exceptional management. Furthermore, the accumulated data can be used for additional studies and development duties, consisting of new material or issue designs to expect performance behavior below simulated stress and fatigue.

articleTitle: Weighted Average Ensembled Probability Pipeline of Pre-trained CNN Models for Hand Gesture Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The automatic detection of sign language from hand gesture images is fundamental for effective human-computer interaction, especially for individuals with hearing and speech disorders. Achieving accurate detection and classification of sign language gestures is paramount. However, accurately recognizing these gestures frequently presents challenges due to dull backgrounds, variations in gesture orientation, and fluctuations in lighting conditions. Previous approaches tried to overcome these challenges but still the model performance lacks recognition accuracy and visual quality. To address this need for accuracy, we proposed a Weighted Average Ensembled Probability Pipeline composed of EfficientNetB7, ResNet-50, and Xception models. Leveraging the Extensive Hand Gesture Recognition Database (HGRD), comprising 20,000 images, our individual models achieved notable accuracies: 96.498 % for EfficientNetB7, 93.2 % for ResNet-50, and 90.175 % for Xception. Through ensemble learning, we integrate these models to attain an impressive overall accuracy of 98.95 %. This research contributes to robust gesture recognition system and underscores the significance of ensemble techniques in enhancing performance for Gesture recognition systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Mental Health with AWS Cloud Services for Mental Well Hub
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A unique online resource called Mental Well Hub was created to help those who are struggling with mental health conditions like stress, anxiety, and depression. This serverless web application uses an extensive suite of AWS services to offer a variety of features targeted at improving mental health, such as self assessment tests, educational resources, real-life user stories, targeted exercises, and expert consultation services. The deployment approach involves hosting the website on Amazon S3, with CloudFront providing quick and safe access to the content. The back end and front end are connected via the API Gateway, and dynamic data management is made possible by interacting with DynamoDB through AWS Lambda functions. This design offers a dependable and seamless user experience by guaranteeing scalability, low latency, and high availability. The paper describes the benefits, design, and implementation of Mental Well Hub and shows how cutting-edge cloud technologies may be used to solve serious mental health issues.

articleTitle: Real-Time Connectivity with the Industrial Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The economic net of things (Eliot) is an emerging era permitting the relationship and optimization of devices, machines, and belongings in industrial settings via statistics switch and exchange. Real-time connectivity with the Iota has revolutionized how business systems perform and has opened the door for full-size upgrades in productiveness, performance, and protection. With actual-time connectivity, commercial operations were capable of advantage near real-time perception into gadget performance, surroundings conditions, and the behavior of machines and property. It interprets into improved situational cognizance, higher decision-making main to optimized operational processes, and stepped forward usual operational visibility. Furthermore, actual-time connectivity with the Eliot is likewise allowing superior information analytics capabilities, taking into account the improvement of predictive analytics fashions, optimization of plant operations, and the gathering of critical information factors. All of those traits have improved the efficiency, scalability, and reliability of business operations and networks, permitting companies to higher-utilize their assets and become greater efficient.

articleTitle: Learning through Internet of Things (IoT): Does it impact youngesters’ social behaviour?
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Youngsters, nowadays, are obsessed and dependent on having their cell phones with them. This study is designed with objective to know whether smart phone usage among youngsters increases the smart phone dependency or not. Secondly, we also tried to examine the significant impact of smart phone dependency on youngsters’ social behavior, and mental well-being. We have used quantitative analysis to determine the dependency of technological interface among Youngsters and its impact on their behavior. Data was collected through set questionnaire which was previously designed by researchers in past studies. A total of 352 youngsters from private and public school of Delhi NCR participated in the study. Data was analyzed by using correlation regression technique. The outcomes of the study establish that there is a strong linkage between youngsters’ social behavior and smart phone usage.

abstract: Modern surveillance systems need to be able to count and track people in video streams accurately and in real time in order to support a variety of applications, from crowd control to security monitoring. This paper offers an integrated approach that makes use of the YOLOv4 and DeepSORT algorithms for accurate human detection and effective tracking, respectively, together with a method for forecasting the direction of individual movements. YOLOv4 is leveraged for its high detection accuracy and speed, ensuring that human figures are recognized rapidly in diverse environments. Subsequently, DeepSORT is used to track the identified persons between frames. This technique uses a Kalman filter in conjunction with appearance traits derived from deep learning to preserve identity consistency even in crowded settings. abstract: Malware poses a significant threat in the modern world as it can maliciously affect users’ data. To combat this menace various machine learning techniques have emerged as potent tools for detecting and mitigating malware attacks. In a bid to discern malware from benign software several machine learning and deep learning models were compared. The dataset sourced from GitHub comprised samples of both malware and non-malware instances. Through rigorous training and testing on this dataset the models’ accuracies were evaluated. Results revealed that the Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) model achieved the lowest accuracy clocking in at 93%. Conversely the ExtraTree Classifier model outperformed others boasting an impressive accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 5 4 \%}$. Other models tested included Random Forest with 98.38% accuracy, Decision Tree with $\mathbf{9 8. 8 \%}$, Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) with 96.4% Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with 96.6% and KNearest Neighbors (KNN) with $\mathbf{9 8. 8 2 \%}$ accuracy. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the ExtraTree classifier in accurately identifying malware.

articleTitle: Epilepsy Detection with CNN and Explanation with Layer-wise Relevance Propagation

abstract: Neurological disorder epilepsy causes seizure attack and it is diagnosed with the help of Electroencephalogram (EEG). Many epileptic seizure detection systems based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model exists which performed well in detecting epileptic seizure. But it is difficult for neurologists to trust their decisions as there is no way to understand why the system has arrived at specific decision, and small mistakes in prediction can be life threatening. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods provide explanation for the results generated by complex CNN models which are black boxes. This paper proposes automated method for detecting epileptic seizure which uses transfer learning approach and provide explanation for the decisions generated by the model. In this study, EEG signals are converted into images before giving to model. VGG16 network is used to classify EEG signal images. XAI method Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) is implemented in VGG16 network for explaining the results generated by the network. LRP method mark the pixels which have positive contribution in classifying the image either in epileptic seizure class or non-seizure class. These explanations are very much helpful for neurologists as they can understand why the signal is classified in seizure class or non-seizure class. This model achieved accuracy of 99.89% on Bonn University dataset. Transfer learning approach has many advantages including reduction in training time and reduction in required number of training samples. This model combined benefits of both, transfer learning approach and XAI method which is used to explain the results generated by model.

abstract: Road congestion is the main cause for slower speed, long waiting time for the emergency vehicles. The project proposes a Smart Traffic Management System for ambulances to reduce road congestion, improve response time, and reduce waiting times. The system uses Dijkstra’s shortest path algorithm to calculate optimal routes based on real-time traffic conditions, road closures, and congestion, ensuring the ambulance is always on the most efficient route. The Smart Traffic Management System uses the YOLO deep learning algorithm to detect and track ambulances in real-time, enabling rapid and accurate vehicle recognition in complex traffic scenarios. Once detected, the system controls traffic signals along the ambulance’s route, prioritizing green lights when approaching intersections. This intelligent traffic signal control balances the needs of the emergency vehicle with traffic flow, minimizing delays and improving response times. The system’s combination of YOLO-based vehicle detection, Dijkstra path optimization, and intelligent traffic signal control makes it a valuable tool for modern urban emergency services, reducing ambulance response times.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel reversible data hiding method that utilizes adaptive absolute moment block truncation coding (AMBTC) for large payload embedding. The approach begins by segmenting the image into blocks and classifying these blocks into saved and hiding blocks based on their complexity. The hiding blocks are then encoded using the AMBTC technique and further divided into multiple sub-categories based on the resulting quantization levels. The encoding of each hiding block is subsequently refined to minimize the discrepancy between the original and reconstructed images while preserving the compression ratio. Although this refined encoding produces bit-planes and quantization levels of varying sizes, it significantly expands the available space within the cover image, allowing for substantial payload embedding while ensuring complete recoverability of the original image. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses current state-of-the-art AMBTC-based data hiding techniques in both embedding capacity and image quality, while ensuring the original image contents’ privacy.

abstract: Prompt and precise identification of plant diseases is essential to guarantee agricultural output and food security. Conventional techniques that depend on visual examinations are inefficient, based on personal judgment, and frequently cannot be expanded to larger scales, emphasizing the necessity for automated alternatives. Recent advancements in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown promise in addressing these challenges, offering high accuracy in image classification tasks. However, existing CNN architectures often require extensive computational resources, limiting their real-time application and scalability. Ensemble methods, while improving accuracy, also increase model complexity and deployment difficulty. To address these issues, we propose a custom CNN architecture specifically designed for plant disease detection. Our model includes advanced features like depthwise separable convolutions, dilated convolutions, and an attention mechanism to improve the efficiency of feature extraction and focus on essential parts of the image. These enhancements ensure high classification performance without imposing excessive computational demands. Our experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the custom CNN, achieving a remarkable validation accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9 . 4 4 \%}$, precision of 0.98, recall of 0.97, and an $F 1$ score of 0.97. By the fifth epoch, the model’s training process shows a consistent decrease in loss, with the training loss dropping to 0.0245 and the validation loss to 0.0196. These results underscore the model’s ability to generalize effectively to unseen data while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for real-time applications. The proposed custom CNN significantly outperforms traditional CNN architectures and ensemble methods in plant disease detection.

This paper digs into an essential progress from customary encryption techniques, including AES, DES, RC6, and LSB steganography, towards the reconciliation of multi-party encryption for strengthened information security in cloud conditions. The shift means to address impediments in existing safety efforts, especially in working with secure document dividing between assorted clients. This study frames the strategy, underlining the precise course of carrying out multi-party encryption while featuring its expected effect on framework proficiency, security, and ease of use. Through exact examination and exhaustive assessment, this exploration attempts to feature the adequacy of the progress, at last upgrading information trustworthiness and access control in cloud-based document sharing practices.”

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling for Real-Time Customer Lifetime Value
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV or CLTV) is the measurement of the overall net revenue of a business that may be expected from a customer. Unlike the previous studies involving segmenting customers and forecasting CLV, the focus of this work is to predict the CLV of the new customer coming in. Further, this work has been performed on the data set of an online store of a gifting company. The proposed model is based on Probabilistic models viz BG/NBD, Pareto/NBD, and Regression models viz KNN regression, decision tree, linear regression, and random forest to predict the CLV. From the experimental results, it is demonstrated that this framework builds a more optimal CLV model compared to the previous model showing an improvement of approximately 10%.

articleTitle: Job Crafter - The One-Stop Placement Portal
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents Job Crafter, a novel initiative designed to disrupt the current placement paradigm within educational institutions. The project aims to address the pervasive issues of complexity, inefficiency, and outdated methodologies that plague traditional placement processes. Job Crafter seeks to achieve this by establishing a user-centric, streamlined, and technologically advanced platform. The core functionality of Job Crafter revolves around the automation of critical placement-related tasks. This is accomplished by leveraging the MERN stack (MongoDB, Express.js, React, Node.js), a robust technology suite that facilitates the development of a seamless web-based platform. Agile development methodologies are employed to ensure iterative development and rapid adaptation to user needs. Additionally, the platform incorporates robust data collection practices, fostering the generation of valuable insights for informed decision-making. The anticipated outcomes of Job Crafter are multifaceted. The platform has the potential to significantly reduce the time and effort expended on placement processes for both institutions and students. Furthermore, by optimizing student-opportunity matching through intelligent algorithms, Job Crafter fosters an environment that enhances placement success rates. Ultimately, Job Crafter aspires to serve as a cornerstone for the evolution of education management systems, emphasizing innovation and a user-centric design philosophy.

articleTitle: Smart Contract System with Blockchain Capability for Improved Supply Chain Management Traceability and Transparency
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study delves into the integration of blockchain technology, specifically smart contracts, to revolutionize supply chain management. By leveraging smart contracts, the flow of products from farmers to consumers is securely recorded and verified on an immutable ledger, bolstering transparency and trust throughout the supply chain. Furthermore, the research addresses blockchain scalability challenges by proposing an adaptive algorithm to adjust gas fees based on network congestion, optimizing block confirmation times and transaction processing efficiency. A robust software architecture is outlined, emphasizing scalability to effectively handle large-scale supply chain operations. Through this interdisciplinary approach, the thesis aims to advance supply chain management practices by harnessing blockchain’s transformative capabilities, laying the groundwork for resilient and efficient supply chain ecosystems in the digital age.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Model for Intelligent Resume Recommendation and Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The research aims to develop a system that is capable of suggesting the most suitable resumes based on the job requirements provided by recruiters through uploaded files. The proposed System approach utilizes the Bert Model to enhance the precision and relevance of job recommendations, and ensure a seamless alignment between skills and job requirements. Furthermore, that system offers constructive feedback to candidates whose skills may not match the specified job requirements, going beyond the traditional job recommendation process. This feedback mechanism gives valuable insights for personal and professional growth, and it is also promoting a transparent and constructive interaction between candidates and the hiring process. In addition to providing instant resume recommendations and feedback, our model will also anticipates upcoming future job opportunities based on the candidate’s skills set. This predictive feature is allowing candidate to strategically plan their career paths and stay ahead of evolving industry demands.

articleTitle: Correlations of Evaluation Metrics for Voice Conversion: An Experimental Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Voice conversion (VC) refers to the transformation of vocal features from one speaker to another speaker while keeping linguistic content unaltered. Recently, VC has seen rapid advancement with the development of deep learning techniques, becoming increasingly critical in applications such as voice assistive technologies, voice dubbing for movies, and privacy protection. A core challenge in VC research lies in the comprehensive evaluation of converted voice quality, speaker similarity, and intelligibility. This study presents an extensive experimental analysis aimed at investigating the correlations between objective and subjective evaluation metrics used in VC. A series of experiments using state-of-the-art (SOTA) VC models has been performed on several benchmark datasets. Objective metrics such as mel-cepstral distortion (MCD), modulation spectra distance (MSD), etc. are calculated, alongside subjective assessments including mean opinion score (MOS) for quality and similarity. This analysis reveals significant insights into the strengths and limitations of commonly used metrics, highlighting cases where different measures correlate well with each other and instances where they diverge. Our findings contribute to a better understanding of metric effectiveness in VC evaluation, offering guidelines for future research and development in the field.

articleTitle: Multi-Layered Security Framework for Intrusion Detection System in Software Defined Networking Environment Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In Software-Defined Networking (SDN), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) are crucial for enhancing network security. These systems analyze and detect network anomalies dynamically, making SDN environments more responsive to emerging threats. The BAT-MC model has demonstrated effectiveness in improving network traffic analysis within SDN. This model integrates bidirectional context understanding and attention mechanisms, combining Bi-directional Long ShortTerm Memory (BiLSTM) and Attention layer with multiple convolutional layers. The proposed system offers precise anomaly detection and improved traffic optimization within the SDN infrastructure. Traditional IDSs relying on the NSL-KDD dataset face accuracy and scalability constraints, even with machine learning techniques. Moreover, manual feature engineering complicates the challenge due to the increasing diversity and complexity of network traffic. To tackle these issues, BAT-MC employs advanced deep learning techniques by seamlessly integrating BiLSTM and attention mechanisms, eliminating the need for manual feature design and significantly improving intrusion detection capabilities. To address existing dataset limitations, the In-SDN dataset is used, aiming to enhance system performance in intrusion detection when combined with the BAT-MC model and ensemble methods. Through a comprehensive approach, the goal is to improve accuracy, scalability, and adaptability, achieving an impressive $\mathbf{8 6 \%}$ performance in safeguarding SDN environments from various potential threats.

articleTitle: Yoga Pose Recognition and Correction Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Yoga is an ancient practice that holds contemporary significance in promoting holistic well- being. This study focuses on yoga pose recognition via deep learning-based methodology, utilizing Media Pipe for pose estimation. Specifically, the study concentrates on estimating poses for beginners. The yoga pose images were manually categorized into three levels: Beginners, Intermediate, and Advanced. The estimated yoga pose data for beginners was used to train several types of deep learning models: an Advanced Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a hybrid model combining Convolutional Neural Network with Long Short-Term Memory, ResNet50, VGG16. All the models have demonstrated promising accuracy. The CNN model achieved a training accuracy of $\mathbf{9 8. 8 9 \%}$ and a validation accuracy of $83.33 \%$. In contrast, the CNN- LSTM model achieved a training accuracy of $94.06 \%$, resulting in a marginal increase in validation accuracy to $84.79 \%$. Furthermore, with an accuracy of $92 \%$, the VGG16 model showed excellent performance, while the ResNet50 model attained an astounding $\mathbf{9 3. 6 8 \%}$ accuracy. The primary objective is for the model to accurately identify beginners’ yoga poses and provide recommendations for adjusting alignment to achieve the perfect Yoga Pose.

articleTitle: Detection of Distributed Denial of Service in The Application Layer of IoT Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cybersecurity prevents harmful assaults on computers, networks, and mobile devices. Included in the category of cyber-attacks are threats like as malware, distributed denial of service assaults, phishing, spoofing, code injection, and supply chain attacks. Massive denial-of-service assaults are destructive. As part of a Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) assault, hackers bypass botnets and go straight for the server. In order to temporarily block or suspend a website, these botnets send a flood of requests to the server. The server typically takes requests and returns responses. There will be a brief outage if the server gets more requests than it can handle. While this attack makes the service inaccessible, it prevents data theft. A machine-learning approach is used to detect server-side DDoS assaults. The term “machine learning” refers to software that can learn new tasks and solve old ones without any input from a human. Learning Vector Quantization, Support Vector Machine, Naive Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbour, Random Forest, and Decision Tree are the six ML classification models used since these ML procedures enhance accuracy. The main goal of this research is to use the CIDAD dataset to find ways to protect the application layer of the Internet of Things (IoT) against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. The lower layers of the IoT network architecture are disregarded by this dataset, which comprises information at the COAP level.

articleTitle: Enhanced Crop Yield Prediction using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In modern agriculture, accurately anticipating crop yield estimation is critical aids of sustainable resource management, efficient decision-making, and food security. This is therefore a process that includes a breakdown of those systems containing data on temperature, rain, yield values, pesticide usage. This process commences with data preprocessing which consist of engineering the features, cleaning, normalization and fusing of discrete data sources. The prediction of agricultural output which is based on the machine learning approach and input interactions is an outcome of this machine learning approach. In the model developed uses several classifiers, that is SVM, Decision Tree, Random Forest, AdaBoost, XGBoost, Naïve Bayes, KNN, MLP, Logistic Regression, Linear Discriminant Analysis, Extra Trees, and Voting Classifiers. The model reported an accuracy of over 99%. This was achieved through the use of Extra Trees technique, which is an ensemble learning method. The reliability of these statistics helps farmers, agricultural policymakers, like the other stakeholders, to make good vital decisions, in turn increasing agricultural production and food security.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Crop Disease Detection using MCCNNs and Decorrelating Color Spaces
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The detection of crop diseases using computer-vision techniques has been widely studied. However, most existing research is based on lab images with controlled backgrounds, which limits the applicability of these methods. Moreover, most of the existing methods rely solely on $R G B$ images. However, $R G B$ components are highly correlated, and reflection from sunlight and illumination changes may induce intensity variations. This problem can be solved by decorating the $R G B$ channels using color transformations such as CIE $L * A B$ or $H S V$, which uses decorrelating transformations and provides a novel approach that uses multichannel convolutional neural networks (MCCNNs) to detect crop diseases using images in CIE $L * A B$ format, which separates achromatic and chromatic information. We experimented with different variations of the MCCNNs by varying the number of filters. This paper also provides MCCNNs, where the image is converted into $H S V$ and $R G B$ color space, and both formats of images are fed to their respective branches of MCCNNs. Here, as in the case of CIE $L * A B$, different variations of MCCNNs varying the number of filters are provided, and the results are compared with those of state-of-the-art transfer learning models, such as InceptionV3, ResNet50, and Xception. The results show that our proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. It should also be noted that our proposed MCCNN is less complex with fewer trainable parameters than other models.

articleTitle: VoIP QoS Refinement through Call Sequencing using Adaptive Jitter Buffer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: VoIP, or voice over internet protocol, has gained popularity as a real-time communication technology because it is flexible and reasonably priced. However, maintaining a good level of quality of service over a variety of dynamic network conditions is necessary to guarantee a satisfactory user experience for VoIP applications. To optimize voice traffic delivery and guarantee a reliable and excellent communication experience, adaptive QoS dynamically modifies network parameters. This paper introduces the concept of Adaptive QoS, a proactive strategy leveraging Call Sequencing, Machine Learning Regression Analysis, and two pivotal algorithms-Silence Suppression and Adaptive Jitter. The Silence Suppression Algorithm efficiently manages silent periods, optimizing network resources, while the Adaptive Jitter Algorithm mitigates jitter impact for smoother voice transmission. Through comprehensive assessments of latency, jitter, bandwidth, packet loss, and network stability, approach dynamically adjusts network parameters. Results indicate that the Adaptive Jitter Buffer has a latency of 0.02 milliseconds, while Silence Suppression (CNG) exhibits a significantly lower latency of 0.001 milliseconds. In terms of jitter, the Adaptive Jitter Buffer introduces a jitter value of 0.0639375 milliseconds, whereas Silence Suppression achieves a much lower jitter of 0.001 milliseconds. These findings demonstrate that Silence Suppression outperforms the Adaptive Jitter Buffer in both latency and jitter, contributing to a smoother and more reliable real-time communication experience.

articleTitle: Boomerang Packet Testing to Mitigate Wormhole Attack in MANET
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: MANET is an infrastructure-less wireless technology used in various critical infrastructure areas such as the military environment, disaster management, etc. MANET is also subject to various security breaches. One such attack is the wormhole attack. Wormhole attackers can unleash a great deal of damage like dropping data packets, manipulating data, disrupting routing, etc. In this paper, we have proposed a novel wormhole mitigation security framework. Our security framework utilizes the attack model to detect an active wormhole attack in MANET. The crux of our framework is that an admin node is chosen from a list of trustable nodes. The admin node periodically relays a boomerang packet across the network. The boomerang packet is the packet destined to return to the admin node itself. Based on the state of the boomerang packet, when it returns admin decides if the packet has been subject to a wormhole attack. If it is subject to a wormhole attack, preventive measures are taken to mitigate the attack. We conducted exhaustive experiments in the NS-3.26 simulator and compared the results with state-of-the-art solutions. Our strategy was able to detect the wormhole nodes at an accuracy of 97%. The packet loss rate was also less when compared to other state-of-the-art solutions during the wormhole attack. This was because of the early and accurate detection of the wormhole attack in MANET.

articleTitle: Enhanced Potato Leaf Disease Detection via Modified Swin Transformer Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Potatoes are a primary agricultural product in India, with stable production hinging on effective disease prevention. Detecting whether potato leaves are healthy or afflicted by diseases such as early or late blight is crucial. This study introduces a novel method based on the Swin Transformer for identifying these diseases. In the last few years, there have been notable developments in the use of advanced deep-learning algorithms to classify and detect diseases in potato leaves within the industrial sector. Based on transformer architecture, the Swin Transformer model has notably improved classification tasks, efficiency and accuracy. The research utilized a deep learning method with the Swin Transformer to detect diseases in potato leaves. The model’s performance was assessed using precision, recall, accuracy, and $F 1$ score. After training, the method achieved a notable accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 3 8 \%}$. These findings highlight the efficacy of the Swin Transformer model in identifying potato leaf diseases, offering exciting prospects for agricultural research.

articleTitle: GVMP: A Novel Internet of Things Application Module Placement Strategy for Heterogeneous Infrastructure using iFogSim
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The growing usage of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in smart city applications has resulted in a surge in data volume. However, a centralized cloud server for IoT applications is practically infeasible because of high latency and network congestion. Fog computing offers a solution by processing data near the network edge through distributed network devices. Nonetheless, selecting a fog device capable of placing, hosting and processing an application module is quite challenging and a nondeterministic polynomial (NP)-hard problem. Therefore, an efficient application module placement strategy is needed to minimize latency and network usage in an IoT-fog-cloudbased environment. This paper proposes the gateway validation module placement (GVMP) strategy for effectively deploying application modules in IoT-fog-cloud-based environments. The proposed strategy places modules on heterogeneous fog devices in the environments. The performance of the GVMP strategy is evaluated using the iFogSim tool and compared with the edgeward module placement (EWMP) strategy. The simulation results show that the GVMP strategy significantly reduces average application latency and network usage compared to the EWMP strategy.

articleTitle: Monitoring and detection of NEFT fraudulent requests: A comparative analysis of machine learning models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The world is going through a fast pace of “digital disruption” in business driven by “technology transformation.” Similar to the global trend, the Indian banking industry is experiencing a major digital explosion, especially in the post-demonetization era, and accelerated further with the COVID19 pandemic. Digital channel services create massive volumes of electronic transactions and are automatically processed from end to end. With the increasing use of digital banking and online payments, cyberattacks, money laundering, and other fraudulent activities are rising in frequency and intensity. Frauds are dynamic, show irregular patterns, and are difficult to identify accurately. Cyberattackers use innovative technologies to find the existing systems’ vulnerabilities and siphon millions of rupees. This means traditional fraud monitoring and detection methods are inadequate to meet the challenges that banks and financial institutions face today. This study aims to analyze the results of applying Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to digital payment transactions and measure the accuracy of segregating valid and abnormal transactions. The methods used are Logistic Regression (LR), k-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naïve Bayes (NB), and Decision Tree (DT). The datasets used are the National Electronic Fund Transfer (NEFT) N02 messages. We analyze five evaluation metrics - Precision, F-Score, Accuracy, Misclassification Error, and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC). The results propose the models in online payment systems for continuous monitoring and early detection of possible fraudulent transactions.

articleTitle: Wildlife Management System- Integrating Location Tracking, Healthcare Management, and QR-based Incident Reporting
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Internet of Things have the potential to greatly enhance wildife management practices. By providing real time data on wildife migrations, behavior and social habits these networks can be invaluable. GPS enabled sensors can help prevent the entry of wild animals in living areas and resolve property disputes, while health tracking devices can detect signs of disease or discomfort in animals. Moreover, QR codes can be utilized to enable others to scan and access the contact information of the forest officer in situations, like lost and found cases. This technology empowers ranchers, farmers and people to make alert calls to respective officers. Analyzing data have improved animal’s health, increased productivity and better resource allocation.

articleTitle: Installation of Multicellular 5G Campus Network ‘ for Remote Driving and Flying
