abstract: Dysarthria, a neuromuscular communications disorder presented with impaired pronunciation, is a daunting task to identify and quantify the level of dysfunction. Through this paper, a critical study of automated dysarthria severity classification using transformer-based deep learning methods will be discussed. Transfer learning is facilitated by employing three variations of Vision Transformer (ViT) models: ViT-L-16, ViT-L-32, and ViT-B-16, on UA-Speech Corpus and TORGO datasets, achieving remarkable results with 99.01% accuracy for the UA-Speech dataset and 99.39% accuracy for the TORGO database. The study evaluates the models’ performance focusing on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scores. Experimental results emphasise the potential for automated diagnostic units in neurology clinical practice and establish a baseline for leading work in dysarthria severity classification with the selection of an efficient ViT model.

articleTitle: Securing IoT Devices and Data: An Analysis of Blockchain Technology and Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Internet of Things, or IoT, has expanded substantially in recent years. Combining IoT and the Internet allows heterogeneous intelligent devices to process real-time data and conduct transactions. Thanks to the Internet of Things (IoT), almost everything and everything can be connected to the internet and covered. Smart housing, smart healthcare, smart irrigation, and many other uses for IoT are all common [2]. However, the IoT’s dependability in terms of privacy and security presents significant development challenges. Consensus mechanisms, decentralization, smart contracts, and data encryption are all blockchain elements that are well suited for building IoT systems since they assist designers in preventing potential attacks and lowering transaction costs. Blockchain serves as a decentralized and open database platform, which can improve the performance of IoT security. We must consider the security challenges and concerns that come with blockchain technology in addition to its ability to provide us with more dependable and useful services. Blockchain technology creates a decentralised, tamper-proof ledger that can securely record and confirm transactions, offering a viable solution for improving the security of IoT devices. Using an explanation of the underlying blockchain technology, a discussion of the security issues that IoT devices must deal with, and a description of the possible advantages of using blockchain for IoT security, we investigate the utilization of blockchain innovation for safeguarding IoT gadgets in this paper.

articleTitle: Financial Inclusion for Visually Impaired People using YOLOv7Bank+ based Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A key component of contemporary society is financial inclusion, which guarantees that everyone, regardless of ability, may access and successfully manage their resources. This proposed assistive aid, “Banking Assistance for the Blind,” aims to address the particular difficulties that people with visual impairments encounter when utilizing financial services at banks. The objective of this proposed assistive aid is to create an all-encompassing application that uses different deep learning algorithms such as You Only Look Once(YOLO),Residual Networks(ResNet), etc, to enable blind people to easily and independently access banking services. The system will incorporate assistive technology, such as speech recognition, and accessible mobile applications. In order to promote financial independence and inclusion for people with visual impairments, the proposed assistive aid aims to close the accessibility gap in the banking industry. This application helps to create a more equal and inclusive financial environment by ensuring that banking services are easily accessible and understandable to everybody, benefiting not only the blind population but society at large. This application has an accuracy of $92 \%$ with a minimal latency (almost instantaneous) which accounts for the reliability of the application.

articleTitle: PokkahScan - An Intelligent Drone for detection of Pokkah Boeng Disease in Sugarcane Using Transfer Learning and eXplainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Traditional systems for crop disease detection often rely on manual inspection methods, which are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and prone to human error. In this context, the necessity of using transfer learning becomes apparent as it allows for leveraging pre-existing knowledge from large datasets to improve the performance of models trained on smaller, domain-specific datasets. IoT has also played a significant role in our automation process. Transfer learning leveraging MobilenetV2 is particularly beneficial for this problem of detecting Pokkah Boeng disease in sugarcane crops, as it enables the adaptation of pretrained models, such as MobileNetV2, to accurately identify Pokkah Boeng disease even with limited set of data. LIME is employed to provide transparent explanations for the model’s predictions, enhancing its interpretability and facilitating informed decision-making in agricultural management. By combining transfer learning with xAI and aerial drone technology, having add-ons of IoT and facilitating a comprehensive comparative study, PokkahScan offers a comprehensive solution for timely disease detection and crop management in sugarcane farming.

articleTitle: Advanced Severity Analysis of Garlic Leaf Disease Using Federated Learning and CNN Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research paper discusses the novel integration of federated learning (FL) and Convolutional Neural Networks(CNN) used to diagnose garlic leaf disease severity in four classes. Using data on four disparate agricultural clients, the study shows how FL aggregates local learning to create a robust model applicable globally. It also involves assigning the disease in garlic leaf to one of four severity levels (mild, moderate, severe and critical) using a CNN model trained across clients for a few federated learning. The result analysis shows good diagnostic accuracy in local data, approximating global use through federated averaging. In particular, the mentioned research highlights impressive performance metrics such as Macro Average, Weighted Average and Micro Average, which are consistently above average among all clients. The Macro Average for client dq_1 was 97.83%, while the weighted average and micro averages are also at 97.83%. The client dq_ 2 showed a Macro Average of ${9 8. 8 4 \%}$, the Weighted Average was also equal to it, and the Micro average was the same, which means all three averages are the same, as observed in the table below. Likewise, the Client dq_3 scored at a Macro Average of ${9 8. 7 0 \%}$, Weighted Average of 98.69% and Micro. In summary, combining federated learning with CNN is a milestone in agricultural technology explicitly related to garlic leaf disease diagnosis. This study is a primer for future precision agriculture innovations, setting the tone towards scalable privacy-preserving and accurate disease detection methods.

articleTitle: Comparison of Model Adaptation Techniques with Machine Unlearning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With the use of data-driven learning processes, machine learning (ML) has become a disruptive technology that enables systems to gain insights and make wise judgments. But data settings are dynamic, which poses difficulties and calls for the creation of efficient machine unlearning methods. In this research, we examine how well-suited different machine unlearning techniques are to meet the changing needs of contemporary machine learning systems. We undertake a thorough comparison investigation of various unlearning approaches on MNIST dataset. These methodologies include naive retraining, influence function-based unlearning, a combination voting classifier with the SISA technique. We assess various performance parameters, to reveal subtle variations in performance as well as computing efficiency and flexibility in dynamic data contexts. Notably, naive retraining and the voting classifier demonstrate superior performance, achieving accuracy scores of 0.971 and 0.970 respectively, while influence function and SISA methods offer competitive alternatives with enhanced efficiency. Our findings underscore the importance of considering factors such as computational resources and data drift dynamics when selecting an appropriate unlearning approach. Additionally, we discuss future research directions, including dynamic ensemble learning and online learning strategies, to enhance model adaptability and efficiency in dynamic ML environments. By expanding our knowledge of machine unlearning techniques and their uses, this research helps to create more robust and morally sound machine learning systems.

articleTitle: Exploring the Synergistic Relationship Between Syntax and Semantics in Rule-Based Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This in-depth review explores the synergistic relationship between syntax and semantics in rule-based translation, emphasizing their interplay in producing accurate and contextually appropriate translations. The review highlights the significance of rule-based translation approaches, particularly in domains where linguistic and cultural nuances are paramount, despite the advancements in neural machine translation techniques. The review begins by defining syntax and semantics in language processing, followed by an examination of their distinct roles in rule-based translation. The review then delves into the synergistic relationship between syntax and semantics, demonstrating how they work together to produce high-quality translations. By synthesizing existing literature and practical insights, the review underscores the importance of contextual considerations in rule-based translation models, ultimately facilitating cross-linguistic communication and understanding. The implications extend to future research directions, including the development of hybrid translation approaches and the integration of advanced natural language processing techniques into rule-based translation models.

articleTitle: Enhanced Brain Tumor Segmentation using UNet3D: A Deep Learning Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Brain tumors pose huge challenges in diagnosis and treatment due to various reasons such as their aggressive nature, heterogeneity, and resistance to standard therapies. Accurate segmentation of brain tumors from multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans is crucial for treatment planning, disease progression tracking, and patient outcome prediction. This research proposes a novel U-Net-based deep learning method tailored for the BraTS 2020 challenge dataset and aims to improve brain tumor segmentation accuracy. The methodology integrates ensemble strategies, attention mechanisms, and residual connections to enhance the model’s learning capacity and durability. Leveraging complementary data from various MRI modalities (T1, T2, T1c, FLAIR) using a multi-input, multi-output approach, the proposed method aims to better define tumor sub-regions. The integration of deep learning with radiomic characteristics from segmented tumors had been explored in this research for predicting overall survival and differentiating true recurrence from pseudoprogression. The study offers reliable testing across diverse imaging protocols and scanner configurations. The proposed method emphasizes the importance of multimodal MRI analysis in improving brain tumor diagnosis accuracy and contributes to the advancement of precise and trustworthy brain tumor segmentation algorithms and enhances overall patient care and treatment outcomes.

articleTitle: CNNs for Optimal PDE Solvers
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to solving partial differential equations (PDEs) using machine learning techniques, specifically convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Traditional methods like the finite-difference method (FDM) discretize PDEs into systems of linear equations, which are then solved iteratively. Our method optimizes existing solvers by learning update rules using CNNs, ensuring convergence while enhancing performance. We focus on the Poisson equation and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on various problem instances. The results show significant performance improvements without sacrificing convergence, paving the way for more efficient numerical methods in solving PDEs.

articleTitle: Optimizing Prenatal Care with a Hybrid Model for Fetal Health
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Fetal health classification involves assessing the wellbeing of a developing fetus. It is vital for early detection of risks, prevention of complications, optimizing prenatal care, reducing mortality and also for research and development for advancing medical knowledge. Early diagnosis and treatment of any disease process is essential for the health and safety of mother and baby. In this study, we created a hybrid model that effectively uses Cardiotocography (CTG) data to classify the fetus’s health, achieving remarkable accuracy rates of 98%. The remarkable accuracy rates were achieved through rigorous model training and validation, indicating the effectiveness of our techniques. The Hybrid model combines Random Forest, Support Vector Machine and Gradient boost powered by Artificial Neural Networks. Three skilled obstetricians divided the 2126 records in the dataset—21 attributes taken from cardiotocography exams—into three classes: normal, suspicious, and pathological. A hybrid model in fetal health classification offers improved accuracy, robustness, and feature representation by combining SVM, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). It enhances generalization and adaptability, ensuring better prenatal care outcomes.

articleTitle: A Novel Blockchain-Based Encryption Model to Protect Fog Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Utilizing blockchain along with fog computing to improve secure data access control mechanisms within the realm of distributed data storage and authentication poses various challenges. One such hurdle is finding a balance between decentralization and scalability within blockchain technology. As the blockchain ledger grows, it may lead to increased latency and resource requirements. The goal of this research is to combine blockchain with fog computing, along with an algorithm for hybrid encryption, to improve the security and efficiency of data access control in distributed data storage as well as authentication. Authentication mechanisms leverage Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and Token-Based Authentication for heightened security. Token-Based Authentication employs dynamic codes generated by a physical or mobile token. Symmetric encryption ensures efficiency in data transmission, while asymmetric encryption provides secure key exchange Honey Encryption-based Hybrid Cryptographic Algorithm. The integration of the Zero Trust Security (ZTS) Model with Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) enhances the security of data access and storage in distributed fog environments. Zero Trust emphasizes the necessity for continuous verification of user and device trustworthiness, irrespective of their location, reinforcing the principles of SMPC. MATLAB experiments were implemented to evaluate the efficacy of proposed mechanisms under a range of scenarios. Leveraging the platform’s computational capabilities, simulations were conducted and analyzed to provide a comprehensive performance assessment of the proposed solutions, thereby informing the design and optimization of these mechanisms. The findings for encryption time and decryption time of these metrics reflect the durations needed to encode and decode data of varying sizes securely. The potential for the blockchain along with the fog computing model to ensure secure data access control in the future depends on further developing interoperability standards and improving consensus mechanisms to increase scalability.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach Using Graphical Neural Network for Network Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This investigation is centered on addressing the imperative for a System on Intrusion Detection capable of accurately discerning anomalies and attacks within a system. As the frequency and severity of network intrusion incidents continue to rise, the necessity for a robust IDS becomes increasingly pronounced. To contribute to this endeavor, we have devised a classification model specifically designed for network intrusion detection, leveraging advanced techniques.In today’s interconnected landscape, network security is of utmost importance. Network intrusion attacks pose formidable challenges for all computer networks and can incur substantial costs for manufacturers. Consequently, the significance of a robust and dependable Intrusion Detection System with the ability to identifying and attacks within the system is steadily increasing. In this research, we primarily focused on developing a multinomial classification model for network intrusion system. We trained our model on a dataset including various attack types, such as R2L, PROBE, DOS, and U2R, alongside typical attacks. To achieve it, we explored ML methods such as decision trees, k-nearest neighbors, and random forest classifiers. We measured each algorithm’s performance based on metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Notably, our research and numbers indicate that the GNN algorithm outperformed others, achieving an accuracy rate of $91 \%$.

articleTitle: Role of Drivers of Employee Service Innovative Behavior in the Hospitality and Tourism Sector Using Fuzzy AHP Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Employee Service Innovative Behaviour (ESIB) is a significant contributor to the economic growth of many developing countries in the hotel and tourism industry. Numerous antecedents influencing ESIB have been examined in hospitality and tourism-related research; nevertheless, there are still numerous domains where our knowledge of these antecedents is lacking. The evidence supporting the relationships between ESIB and its antecedents has been inconsistent among studies, leading to data inaccuracies and inconsistent findings for both academics and practitioners. The present study used the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to determine the drivers that foster innovative behavior among employees in developing nations in the hospitality and tourist sectors. The findings demonstrated that the most important sub-factor influencing the ESIB is Work Motivation and that the primary crucial factor affecting the ESIB is Individual Work Attitude.

articleTitle: An Improvised Genetic Algorithm Technique on Task Scheduling in Edge and Cloud Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In current years, part cloud computing systems have received huge adoption because of their capability to provide low latency and high bandwidth offerings to users. however, one of the primary challenges in these structures is green undertaking scheduling in the presence of dynamic and heterogeneous sources. To deal with this trouble, genetic set of rules (GA) optimization strategies were proposed as a potential solution. This approach utilizes genetic operators, which include mutation and crossover, to conform a populace of potential solutions and choose the best one. by way of considering various constraints and objectives, consisting of strength consumption and make span, the GA-primarily based project scheduling technique can efficaciously optimize useful resource allocation in area cloud computing structures, at the end improving their performance and resource utilization.

articleTitle: Adaptive Multi-Level Feedback Round-Robin
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Scheduling is vital in operating systems, controlling process resource access. Round Robin stands out among traditional algorithms due to its improved performance, unlike First Come First Serve (FCFS) or Shortest Job First (SJF). While the Priority-based scheduling algorithm executes processes depending on their priority, the proposed algorithm is particularly designed for time-sharing systems. The paper aims to improve system performance, reduce latency, and enhance overall responsiveness in multitasking environments. The time quantum assigned ensures fair allocation of CPU to all the processes getting executed. Based on their burst time and assigned priorities, different processes can be divided within multi-level queues. Multilevel queues adjust task priorities based on the time execution. The use of priority for each process enables prioritization of the important processes in each queue. Decrementing the priority based on the time taken to execute, is an efficient solution to reduce the starvation time of the other processes. It shows a reduction in turn-around time. The implementation will also include comprehensive performance evaluations and benchmarking against traditional scheduling algorithms, demonstrating the superiority and effectiveness of the proposed scheduler in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Deep Learning Approach for Emotion Monitoring System in Online Examinations
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Around the world, a large number of students experience difficult life situations that have an effect on their emotional and mental health and, ultimately, their academic performance in examinations (exams in short). Emotions have an effect on a student’s motivation, focus, and memory, and finally how they perform in exams. An Emotion Monitoring System could be really helpful for understanding how students are feeling during exams and how it affects their overall performance. The contribution of this paper involves in designing a novel facial emotion tracking system which can be used for analyzing facial expressions in real-time thus providing timely emotional support during exams. In this work, we utilized five pretrained deep learning models, namely: DenseNet-121, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, Inception-V3 and Xception - to classify emotions on processed Emoset dataset. Further, we developed an ensemble model by fusing aforementioned two top-performing deep learning models, thus harnessing the strengths of both models. From the results it can be inferred that ensemble model outperforms the individual pretrained models giving an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 8. 6 7 \%}$. The superior performance of the ensemble models makes it an ideal choice for implementing emotion recognition in real-time applications like Emotion Monitoring in exams.

articleTitle: Online Influence Maximization via an Explore-exploit Ensemble Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Online Influence Maximization (OIM) seeks to maximize influence spread by identifying the optimal individuals to expose information to, despite lacking prior knowledge of influence probabilities. Traditional OIM algorithms often receive limited feedback, as they only partially explore networks. To address this, we propose an explore-exploit ensemble approach based on the EXP4 algorithm, introducing two variants: EXP4-OIM and EXP4-OIM-Greedy. Tested on the NetHEPT (15,229 nodes, 62,752 edges) and PhysicianSN (181 nodes, 19,026 edges) datasets, both EXP4OIM and EXP4-OIM-Greedy outperformed existing benchmarks in influence spread. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of our ensemble approach in optimizing information dissemination in social networks.

articleTitle: ConGANomaly: A Contrastive Learning Approach Of Anomaly Detection Using Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Anomaly detection (AD) is essential for numerous machine learning applications across a wide range of fields. Semi-supervised AD involves identifying anomalies in data with limited labeled examples, using labeled and unlabeled data for training the model. This research endeavors to enhance the effectiveness of semi-supervised AD models, namely GANomaly and Skip-GANomaly, by adding novel changes to the model so as to incorporate contrastive learning into their architecture. In contrastive learning model learns to distinguish between positive and negative sample pairs to develop robust representations. The performances of the modified architecture were measured across-different datasets and yielded positive improvements in model performance.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fusion-Enhanced CNN Architectures for Advanced Image Classification in E-Commerce
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Image classification is a fundamental aspect of modern artificial intelligence, impacting various applications ranging from autonomous vehicles to medical diagnostics. With the development of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), traditional classification methods have been significantly enhanced, improving the accuracy of image analysis by capturing complex patterns within extensive datasets. Despite these advancements, a notable challenge remains in dynamically integrating multiple CNN architectures to fully utilize their collective strengths, especially in adapting efficiently to diverse image characteristics. To address this challenge, this study introduces a novel fusion model incorporating the unique features of three well-known CNNs: VGG16, ResNet50, and MobileNetV2. This model employs a dynamic concatenation strategy that effectively merges each network’s unique capabilities based on the input images’ specific characteristics, thereby improving the model’s adaptability and performance. Designed to leverage the depth and complexity of VGG16, the residual learning capabilities of ResNet50, and the efficiency of MobileNetV2, this robust system excels in accuracy and computational efficiency. Experimental results on the Fashion-MNIST dataset confirm the effectiveness of our fusion model, which achieves a training accuracy of 97.50% and a validation accuracy of 89.27%. This model markedly surpasses traditional single-model approaches, especially in distinguishing more nuanced categories, as shown by detailed evaluations including precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC curve analysis. This research effectively closes a significant gap in adaptive model fusion. It establishes a new benchmark for image classification tasks, presenting substantial implications for future applications that demand high accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Optimizing Crop Monitoring: A Data Warehouse Approach in Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Precision agriculture harnesses advanced technology and data analytics to enhance the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of agricultural production. This paper presents a comprehensive case study focused on optimizing crop monitoring through the implementation of a robust data warehouse framework. Our objective is to propose development of a system capable of seamlessly collecting, storing, and analyzing data from diverse sources, including drones, sensors, and farmer-contributed information, all integrated within a cohesive data warehouse architecture. In response to the dynamic needs of farmers, our primary aim is to facilitate the swift retrieval of crop-specific information at any developmental stage. To achieve this, we introduce a sophisticated multidimensional data model adept at managing intricate agricultural datasets. This model seamlessly integrates with modern technologies such as machine learning algorithms and decision-support systems, providing an enhanced decision-making ecosystem for farmers. In the context of this under explored subject, our proposed approach empowers farmers with precise information for informed decision-making in crop management. We anticipate that this strategy will not only enable farmers to increase yields and improve crop quality but also contribute to significant cost savings. Our research aims to pave the road for a more ecological and efficient agricultural industry by eliminating the current access gap to detailed crop life-cycle data.

articleTitle: Auto-Scaling Anomaly Detection in Cloud Computing Models using MAPE-K Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Computing paradigms are changing at a faster pace leading to highly complex and dynamic environments, thereby demanding resource management acumen. Pivoting in these paradigms, auto scaling ensures optimal resource allocation, sufficient to accommodate variable demands. However, the dynamic nature of such settings poses challenges in maintaining reliability and efficiency in auto-scaling methodologies. This paper proposal solves this challenge through a dependable anomaly detection system intended for auto-scaling in cloud computing frameworks. This work tries to design, develop, and validate the framework of anomaly detection for resource consumption and workload patterns using a MAPE-K loop. The envisioned framework is meant to use machine learning techniques and methodologies of data analysis to track in real time system parameters for the early identification of potential scalability issues. In terms of scores for all metrics, it has performed better with the MAPE-K loop, and the R2 score for all metrics came out to be 1.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Classifiers for Audio-Based Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In order to address the increasingly significant role played by the monitoring of health issues during the times of growing healthcare challenges, this research paper will discuss more about the use of audio signals for diagnosing respiratory diseases by the means of analyzing of cough sounds, breathing patterns, and other audio cues. However, the vision of this work comes from the desire to make a non-invasive and efficient diagnostic process to overcome the difficulty of the traditional invasive ways of imageries. Combining the machine learning techniques using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) for feature extraction we aimed to construct a powerful tool that can do health state labels using the audio signals with accuracy. In the end, our multi-classifier approach in conjunction with accuracy measurements reveal the promising applications of machine learning algorithms to accurately differentiate between various respiratory diseases, thereby opening the avenue for more robust health monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Progress on Graphene as a Multifunctional Nanomaterial for Cancer Therapy
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Graphene-based materials have demonstrated promising results in a variety of medical applications, including sensing/imaging, gene/drug delivery, tumour therapy/diagnosis, and cell engineering/regenerative medicine. Graphene oxides and Graphene-based (Nano) structures are highly drug loadable and have the potential to induce reactive oxygen species, making them attractive candidates for cancer therapy. The manufacturing of Graphene-based materials has made use of a wide range of processes, including liquid-phase exfoliation, chemical vapour deposition (CVD), Hummer’s method, power-driven cleavage of graphite, chemically reduced GO, arc exoneration of graphite, and thermal fusion. If we want to use G-based structures in more clinical and biomedical devices, we need to rigorously evaluate how they fare against essential criteria including biocompatibility, compatibility, and inflammatory reactions. In addition, the anticancer actions of these structures depend on factors such as concentration, detection methodologies, cell types, and surface features (such as surface structure, charge, lateral dimension, oxygen content and corona influence). In this article, we discuss the latest developments in cancer therapy employing Graphene and its oxides-based systems and the major problems and future perspectives.

articleTitle: Multimodal Lung Cancer Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper addresses the significant global impact of lung cancer, the primary cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide and the second leading cause of mortality following cardiovascular disease. The challenge lies in detecting lung cancer, often diagnosed at an advanced stage, complicating treatment efforts. The proposed model integrates CT (Computed Tomography) and PET (Positron-Emission Tomography) scans to enhance lung cancer prediction. CT scans offer detailed anatomical insights, while PET scans excel in identifying abnormal metabolic activity and precise tumour localization. This combined approach provides a comprehensive assessment, empowering healthcare professionals with improved diagnostic accuracy and better-informed treatment planning for lung cancer patients.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection of Service Disruption Attack for Industrial Electrical Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Industrial drive systems play a critical role in modern manufacturing processes, and their reliable operation is essential for productivity. These systems often consist of multiple interconnected control units that communicate through transmission control protocols. The security of these protocols remains vulnerable to attacks if the network is compromised. In this article, the security challenges faced by industrial electrical drive system is investigated and the strategies to enhance their resilience against cyber threats are proposed. The intended drive system is realized with a 2.2 kW squirrel cage induction motor and two-level voltage source inverter controlled using the F28379D microcontroller. The microcontroller is interfaced with the computer through USB for deploying the control program, as well as to monitor and tune the drive parameters. The focus lies on the computer, which provides speed commands to the microcontroller. By implementing these strategies, an effective intrusion detection system is tailored to the unique requirements of industrial electrical drive systems, safeguarding them against service disruption attacks.

articleTitle: Energy-efficiency Analysis of Different Scheduling Algorithms for Mobile Crowd Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Mobile crowd computing (MCC) has emerged as a promising paradigm to leverage the underutilised computational resources of smart mobile devices (SMDs). However, the energy constraints of these devices pose a significant challenge in efficiently executing computational tasks. This study analyses the energy efficiency of various scheduling algorithms for MCC environments. The study compares the performance of seven scheduling algorithms: PPIA, RAS, PSO, GA, MaxMin, MinMin, and MCT. These algorithms were evaluated in terms of their energy efficiency when executing different sets of tasks with varied instruction lengths. The experiment used a simulated MCC environment with real data from five SMDs. The results demonstrate that the PSO algorithm consistently outperformed the other scheduling schemes regarding energy efficiency across all task sets. The GA algorithm also showed promising results. The MinMin algorithm exhibited the lowest energy efficiency. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for designing and implementing energy-efficient task scheduling strategies in MCC systems. Analysing the different algorithms under varying task loads can help MCC service providers make informed decisions when selecting appropriate scheduling techniques to optimise the energy utilisation of SMDs.

articleTitle: A Ensemble Deep Learning approach on risk management in finance and marketing sector
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The ensemble deep getting to know technique is a powerful and innovative tool for danger control inside the finance and advertising quarter. It combines the strengths of more than one deep getting to know models to provide accurate and comprehensive risk tests. By using harnessing the electricity of artificial intelligence and device learning, this approach can efficiently analyze extensive amounts of facts and perceive capability risks in actual time. This enables monetary and advertising establishments to make informed and well timed selections to mitigate dangers and enhance their normal overall performance. With its potential to conform and learn from new data, the A Ensemble Deep getting to know method is reworking the way threat is controlled in those industries.

articleTitle: De-Modulation Techniques for Non-Coherent UWB Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Extremely Wideband (UWB) radio conversation systems provide the potential of high statistics fees and occasional strength intake from a small range of transceivers. The use of UWB for non-coherent packages is, in particular, attractive because of its low complexity and value. However, sign demodulation is a difficult challenge due to the presence of inter-symbol interference and the requirement of particular timing. Numerous demodulation strategies were proposed to address both the presence of inter-symbol interference and the want for precise timing. It includes time redundancy coding, frequency hopping, spreading, and linear codes. This paper critiques the one-of-a-kind demodulation techniques for Non-Coherent UWB Radio systems and goes over the key capabilities and blessings of each method. Time Redundancy Coding uses an encoding scheme that introduces temporal redundancy into the signal, allowing for premier demodulation at the receiver. Frequency Hopping employs a binary segment shift keying (BPSK) modulation for the UWB signal and utilizes unexpectedly converting carrier frequencies to randomize the interference in the channel. Spreading utilizes some form of spread-spectrum modulation for the UWB sign, which expands the bandwidth of the sign and enables the unfolding of the energy across an extensive frequency range.

articleTitle: Towards Autonomous Intrusion Detection: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The growth of cyber-attacks and records breaches, there is a growing want for effective and efficient intrusion detection structures (IDS). Conventional IDS are based heavily on human intervention and manual analysis, making them time-consuming and prone to human errors. The latest improvements in artificial intelligence (AI) have shown promising consequences in various domains, including cyber security. AI-based totally techniques, which include machine studying, deep learning, and herbal language processing, can automate the detection and prevention of intrusions in real time. In this paper, we propose a framework for building an independent intrusion detection gadget by leveraging AI techniques. The proposed framework will utilize machine-gaining knowledge of algorithms to analyze community traffic and discover any strange behavior or patterns that might indicate an intrusion. Furthermore, we are able to gain deep knowledge of fashions to research and adapt to new assault kinds and patterns constantly.

articleTitle: Ant Colony Optimization for Service Composition in Multi-cloud Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: the Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm is a famous metaheuristic technique that has been successfully applied in various optimization issues. It mimics the foraging conduct of ants to locate the shortest path among meals assets and their colony. Recently, ACO has been increasingly more applied for provider composition in multi-cloud environments. This involves the composition of offerings from different cloud carriers to satisfy the service necessities of a person. By way of using ACO, services can be correctly selected and composed from a couple of carriers, considering elements including cost, excellent, and availability. ACO has proven promising outcomes in enhancing the overall performance and reliability of carrier composition in multi-cloud environments, making it a precious technique in todays tremendously distributed computing landscape.

articleTitle: Pretrained DeIT for Brain Tumor Classification: A Fine-Tuning Approach with Label Smoothing
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research introduces a novel approach for brain tumor detection utilizing transformer-based deep learning architectures. Conventional methods and CNN-based techniques suffer significant scalability and performance issues, highlighting the necessity for more sophisticated solutions. By leveraging transformer architectures, our methodology integrates precise preprocessing techniques such as contour analysis, endpoint detection, channel-wise pixel value normalization, AdamW optimization, and the LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy criterion for improved model performance. We utilized SMOTE for class balancing, and our augmentation strategies further increased dataset diversity and generalization. The model is based on a pre-trained DeIT framework with a fine-tuned, redesigned head architecture and final layers, achieved an outstanding accuracy of 97.42% in brain tumor detection, along with notable average precision and recall metrics. These outcomes exceed those of existing models, promising enhanced treatment strategies, patient care, and early tumor detection capabilities in medical imaging, representing a significant advancement in the field.

articleTitle: Investigating the Role of Deep Learning in Data Science: Promises and Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Data science has revolutionized how we create products and offerings and solve problems. With access to vast shops of virtual statistics and the application of state-of-the-art system learning algorithms to this information, data scientists can spot styles, cluster facts, and make predictions leading to the method of actionable insights. Deep mastering, a subset of machine learning, has lately received significant interest in records science due to its capacity to address complicated issues. This technology allows computer systems to research underlying institutions and traits in datasets with minimum human intervention. Deep mastering has enabled the improvement of state-of-the-art stop-to-cease structures that routinely wear out duties that had been historically very difficult for computers due to the full-size complexity of parameters and datasets. In this article, we discover the guarantees and potentialities of deep gaining knowledge of in statistics technological know-how, how it is being used to attain groundbreaking effects, and what the destiny ability might be. We additionally speak about a number of the challenges that should be addressed to recognize this generation’s ability genuinely. ultimately, deep gaining knowledge can enormously increase the modern kingdom of facts and technological knowhow, provided that the proper equipment and techniques are used to extract its total price.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Natural Language Processing Techniques for Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In an era marked by the unprecedented proliferation of cybersecurity threats, conventional malware detection paradigms characterized by signature-based and heuristic methodologies are encountering limitations in their ability to address zero-day and polymorphic malware variants. This lacuna in the cybersecurity landscape necessitates the exploration of innovative, efficacious approaches. Natural Language Processing (NLP) has emerged as a formidable technique in this arena, exhibiting a marked capability for enhancing malware detection frameworks. The current manuscript offers an exhaustive review of NLP methodologies applied to the domain of malware detection, substantiated by a rigorous categorization of extant literature. Empirical evidence suggests that NLP-driven techniques have realized detection accuracy rates upwards of 98.7%, thereby outclassing traditional methods and underscoring the efficacy of linguistic analysis in cybersecurity applications. This review delineates the multitude of NLP techniques such as tokenization, Named Entity Recognition (NER), and sentiment analysis, whilst evaluating their operational practicability, computational efficiency, and scalability. Furthermore, the manuscript elucidates existing limitations and delineates future research vectors, notably emphasizing the requisite for real-time analytics and adaptability to a dynamically evolving threat landscape. Intended to serve as a seminal reference point, this review aims to synthesize current knowledge and foster interdisciplinary dialogue between the NLP and cybersecurity research communities.

articleTitle: A decentralized organ donation registry enabling transparency in medical field
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Recent advancements in technology have resulted in the creation of novel approaches for administering organ donation systems, with an objective of overcoming the restrictions of traditional centrally controlled systems. Blockchain technology is a potential replacement to the existing centralised methods for better transparency, security, and efficiency in organ donation. Previous research on organ donation systems mostly employed centralized database solutions, which have limited interoperability, a predefined set of protocols, and do not permit distributed control due to lack of security, transparency and accountability. A further significant component of the transplantation procedure is the matching of organ donor/recipient based on compatibility. Despite traditional centralised database solutions, blockchain promotes decentralized control, improving interoperability and accountability. Crucially, it facilitates the critical donor-recipient matching process, improving compatibility and possibly revolutionising transplantation operations.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Power of Text Mining for Information Understanding
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Text mining is an essential form of information mining used to extract actionable records from significant volumes of unstructured textual content. Text mining may extract means from the textual content, for instance, to categorize textual content into classes, extract events and relationships, uncover sentiment, help discover insights, identify styles and developments, and examine consumer remarks. Text mining uses sophisticated technology to automatically extract the underlying shape of text and facilitate meaningful analyses. It is far specifically beneficial for uncovering hidden know-how in textual content, including in regions inclusive of biomedical literature, patron reviews, and social media. With the usage of textual content mining gear, researchers can analyze and discover greater successfully the large quantity of text data generated by their studies. Textual content mining is likewise increasingly getting used to find hidden relationships and find out correlations within textual content datasets. It can facilitate understanding discovery and allow more accurate natural language processing structures. ultimately, leveraging the strength of textual content mining for statistics information will assist in making higher selections associated with facts evaluation and interpretation.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of VGG16, Inception V4, AlexNet, and ResNet 50 for Plant Disease Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The increasing incidence of leaf diseases in agricultural crops has necessitated the development of efficient and automated detection methods to safeguard crop health and maximize yield. In the field of artificial intelligence, deep learning has emerged as a major computing paradigm with immense potential for solving computer vision problems. CNN is a type of deep learning architecture that is designed to provide accurate results for tasks such as image recognition and object detection. This study utilizes state-of-the-art ResNet-50 model to identify and classify plant leaf diseases combined with transfer learning to enhance its accuracy and efficiency. The proposed methodology involves dataset curation, preprocessing, and finetuning of the ResNet-50 architecture. We have tested and assessed the performance of VGG16, Inception V4, AlexNet, and ResNet-50. Upon examining the results, ResNet50 has demonstrated good outcomes in the identification and categorization of leaf diseases and outperformed alternative architectures with an accuracy of 99.7%.

articleTitle: Leveraging a Custom Multi Modal OCR System for Marksheet Data Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the current educational landscape, the transition towards digitalization has become crucial. However, the manual entry of data from traditional physical marksheets into digital systems remains a significant bottleneck in the process. Educators often spend significant amount of time and effort entering data into electronic systems, which could be better utilized for more productive tasks.In this paper, we offer a solution to this problem. We propose an automated system that leverages Optical Character Recognition (OCR) Technology to streamline the extraction of essential information from marksheets. We discuss about the Dataset, preprocessing on the input image, Multi Modal OCR system Structure and other implementation details. We conclude the paper by a comparative study of our Multi Modal OCR system with other Commercially available OCRs like EasyOCR, PaddleOCR and PyTesseract.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Dynamic BPSO for Road Accident Severity Prediction using Twitter Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The traffic and medical authorities utilize accident severity prediction through social media postings for better administration and robust emergency response. Deep learning-based models can be used for accident severity prediction using social media data. However, most of the deep learning methods can only perform well when trained with an optimal set of hyper-parameters. This necessitates the use of meta-heuristics in conjunction with deep learning. Moreover, the increase in depth of the networks warrants partial training of the network to make the training process efficient. In this work, we propose a novel partial training-based hybrid deep neural network on convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM), which is partially trained, and the hyperparameters are optimized using a dynamic version of binary particle swarm optimization (DBPSO) known as accident tweet hybrid deep dynamic BPSO (AT-HDBPSO). Experiments show that the proposed AT-HDBPSO turns out to be efficient in training compared to traditional deep learning-based training. Finally, the proposed method outperforms other baseline and state-of-the-art techniques in prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Unveiling Natural Based Underwater Image Colour Enhancement: a Paradigm Shift in Underwater Image Processing and Colour Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In several fields, including marine research, environmental monitoring, and undersea exploration, underwater imaging is essential. Unfortunately, the complicated interactions between light and water molecules make it difficult to take high-quality underwater pictures, leading to problems including low contrast, colour distortion, and poor visibility. Even with improvements in imaging technology, these problems are frequently not adequately addressed by current enhancement methods, particularly in deeper water or under unfavorable circumstances. To address these shortcomings in existing enhancement strategies, this work presents the method of Natural-based Colour Enhancement of Underwater Images (NUCE). NUCE seeks to improve underwater photos’ authenticity, boost contrast, and reduce the colour cast. by using a four-step technique that includes colour cast neutralization, fusion of dual-intensity images using the mean and median as averages, mean equalization based on swarm intelligence, and unsharp masking. NUCE’s ability to enhance item visibility and detail in underwater scenes by restoring real colours, boosting contrast, and minimizing colour cast has been demonstrated empirically using the EUVP dataset.

articleTitle: Weather Image Classification Using Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Weather forecasting is a technique that uses science and technology to foretell the atmospheric conditions at a specific area and time. Since the 19th century, weather forecasting has been conducted formally after being carried out sporadically for thousands of years. Weather forecasts are made using quantitative information on the status of the atmosphere, land, and ocean, meteorology to predict the atmosphere changes in a specific area. Weather forecasts are crucial as they protect property and human lives. Forecasts can be used to schedule activities around these phenomena as well as to prepare ahead of heavy rain, snow, and wind speed. There are several techniques to forecast the weather, such as looking at historical data, current cloud conditions, etc. The usage of machine learning methods and deep learning techniques for weather forecasting is growing. In machine learning, the mean atmospheric pressure, mean humidity, maximum temperature, and minimum temperature are used to predict the weather. In deep learning, weather images are used to predict climatic conditions. However, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) learns only the necessary features from an image not the details of each pixel. The most advanced level of computer vision and widely used for a variety of image recognition applications. CNN now face a formidable rival in the form of Vision Transformer (ViT). This work proposes an efficient vision transformer model for weather image classification.

articleTitle: Forehand to Deep Learning: A CNN-LSTM Framework for Serve Shot Analytics in Table Tennis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: It introduces a novel method for detecting and recognizing the table tennis serve-shot motions based on the advanced convolutional and Long Short-Term Memory models. The model is designed to classify serve shots into five categories: side-spin, backspin, shots with no spin, slicing, and illegal service. It consists of CNNs for precision image classification and the LSTM network for considering the time movement of people through a sequence of shots. Experimental data proved the viability of a model, so the overall accuracy was achieved at ${9 0. 3 9 \%}$. The accuracy metrics for the varied classes can stretch from 84.6% to ${9 4. 2 2 \%.}$ Another key indicator is the high recall rates for Serve shots. This table has an astonishing rate of ${9 7. 0 3 \%}$ for class 3, demonstrating how the model can effectively recognize serve shots. The high F1 scores illustrate the balance between the Precision and the Recall, the values of which exceed 87% for all instances. The model’s performance is guaranteed as performance evaluations are based mainly on macro, weighted, and micro averages. We usually have 90-95 percent accuracy, recall, and F1-Score scores. The experiment proves that the classifier finds the answer to the issue, which is indeed a significant achievement considering the job’s toughness and numerous data. The CNN-LSTM model’s fantastic accuracy and dependability are a reference tool for coaches and athletes they can rely upon. While some argue that it can help trainers and give a macro view into the course, others cannot stop them for fear that this will create doubts about the authenticity of the competition.

articleTitle: Efficient Meeting Insights: NLP-Enhanced Summarization of Voice and Text
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In order to improve meeting efficiency in the ever-changing workplace, research has mostly focused on sophisticated text summarization techniques such as machine learning, hybrid, semantic, and graph-based methods. These approaches have shown efficient in extracting key information from lengthy talks, hence dramatically improving decision-making and knowledge retention. However, their potential has been somewhat limited by a major concentration on processing material in a single language, which ignores the complex, multilingual environment of modern global enterprises. Our most recent research project tries to overcome this gap by combining these various summarizing approaches into acomplete, language-neutral framework.Furthermore, to address the specific difficulty of long meetings, when extracting insights might be especially difficult for those who are not there, we propose using the Longformer encoder-decoder paradigm. This methodology excels at distilling lengthy talks into digestible summaries, regardless of the original language, ensuring that critical insights are easily accessible to anybody, hence increasing inclusion and comprehension across multinational teams.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Satellite Constellation Systems for Global Coverage and Capacity
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper explores the layout and analysis of satellite constellation systems for worldwide insurance and capacity, with unique cognizance on geostationary orbit (GEO) structures as well as low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO) constellations. It starts off evolved by way of describing the technical necessities of such networks, which include the quantity of satellites inside the constellation, the orbital parameters, the system architecture and the communications era in vicinity, and examines the advantages and challenges associated with every solution. The paper then presents a top level view of the related value, trade-offs, and affects associated with numerous nominal layout parameters which includes latency decision, latency, structural complexity, payload capacity, and electricity. an in depth analysis of optimization techniques used to reduce the value and maximize the performance of the constellation is also supplied, with unique dialogue on the role of community topology and the type of orbit choice. Subsequently, the paper gives some practical insights related to the implementation and operation of a constellation system, similarly summarizing the predicted blessings in phrases of progressed insurance, ability, and latency for global packages.

articleTitle: NewsNet: A Comprehensive Neural Network Hybrid Model for Efficient Bangla News Categorization
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Through the internet, Bangla news has grown enormously within the modern era of digital information. Every news outlet came up with its own categorizing system in order to handle such a huge quantity of content. The organization and categorization of online Bangla news articles, however, might not always correspond with the particular requirements of different users because of the heterogeneous nature of these platforms. Also, multiclass Bangla text classification has become increasingly important for Bangla newspaper platforms to enhance their recommendation system and reduce the manual labor required to classify their various article categories. To address the above limitation, we introduced NewsNet a text classification approach by combining the embedding layer, convolutional neural network(cnn), and recurrent neural network. In recurrent neural networks(rnn), we have employed two models including gated recurrent unit and bidirectional-LSTM (biLSTM) respectively. We have also used several preprocessing techniques such as Label encoder and tokenization correspondingly. We have experimented with our model on a Kaggle dataset called “Bangla Newspaper Dataset”.NewsNet achieved a good accuracy of 94.57%, 94.51% precision, 94.32% recall, and 94.43% f1 score respectively. NewsNet has demonstrated superior performance compared to other approaches on this Kaggle dataset.

articleTitle: A Visual Analysis of Ultrasound Breast Cancer Scans with Segmentation, Classification and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The amount of people who are suffering from breast cancer has increased over the years. The people affected by breast cancer have an impact on their physical and emotional health. Detecting breast cancer at an initial stage is very important to prevent the affected ones but doing it at an early stage is a hectic task for healthcare systems as they have to perform comprehensive screening, diagnosis treatment, and support services. Regular screening mammograms and clinical breast examinations improve the chance of survival. Worldwide detection of breast cancer in women remains difficult even though there are advancements in the technology of diagnosis and treatment. To tackle the issue, this study performs multiple segmentation models on Ultrasound scans that predict cancer at an initial stage. The proposed model’s workflow is segmentation models, developing the ML models, and then followed by explanation using Explainable AI libraries.

articleTitle: Cross-Linguistic Hate Speech Detection with Transformer Architectures: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The proliferation of online platforms has led to an increase in user-generated content containing offensive language, including hate speech. Previous research on hate speech detection has primarily focused on monolingual datasets and traditional machine learning approaches. With the advent of transformer models, significant advancements have been made in natural language processing (NLP), enabling more effective multilingual hate speech detection. To mitigate this issue and foster positive online communities, detecting hate speech is crucial. This paper focuses on multilingual hate speech detection using a dataset comprising French, English, and Hindi languages. The dataset used in this study was carefully curated to include a balanced representation of these languages. The paper utilizes advanced transformer models such as BERT, RoBERTa, DistilBERT, and XLNet to identify instances of hate speech. Our experimental results indicate that transformer models achieve impressive performance in hate speech detection, with XLNet showing the best results: an accuracy of $93.46 \%$, F1 score of $93.12 \%$, sensitivity of $91.56 \%$, negative predicted value (NPV) of $92.34 \%$, and precision of $94.74 \%$. We hope this study will aid researchers in the field of hate speech detection by highlighting the most effective transformer models.

articleTitle: Enhancing Underwater Networks Performance Through Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Underwater networks face a variety of challenges, together with confined bandwidth, long propagation delays, and excessive blunders charges. Those demanding situations can have an enormous impact at the overall performance of underwater networks, making it hard to gain dependable facts transmission and efficient useful resource allocation. In order to conquer these challenges, there has been a developing interest in the usage of fuzzy common sense techniques to beautify the performance of underwater networks. Fuzzy common sense is a mathematical technique that allows for the processing of vague or uncertain facts, making it especially nicely-appropriate for managing the noisy and unpredictable nature of underwater environments. thru the usage of fuzzy good judgment, choice-making processes can be made more adaptive and conscious of changing environmental situations, leading to progressed network overall performance. One key software of fuzzy common sense in underwater networks is in enhancing routing protocols. Traditional routing protocols may battle to adapt to the continuously converting topology of an underwater network, main to inefficient routing decisions and ability network screw ups. By incorporating fuzzy common sense, routing choices may be made based totally on a mixture of traditional metrics (including distance or hyperlink quality) and environmental elements (including water depth or salinity). This allows for greater strong and adaptable routing choices, leading to accelerated network performance. Some other vicinity wherein fuzzy common sense can enhance underwater community overall performance is in resource allocation. In an underwater network

articleTitle: Interpretable Deep Learning for Skin Cancer Detection: Exploring LIME and SHAP
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: An effective treatment for skin cancer necessitates early detection, a global problem. This work introduces a unique deep learning technique that extracts important characteristics from skin lesion photos by using CNNs, Resnet50, VGGNet, and DenseNet. The integration of LIME and SHAP approaches improves interpretability by emphasising significant portions of the picture. According to the model’s competitive performance criteria (specificity, sensitivity, and accuracy), dermatologists may be able to depend on it to assist in the early identification of skin cancer. The research also examines the possible advantages and drawbacks of deep learning for the diagnosis of skin cancer, emphasising the technology’s potential to advance healthcare by strengthening diagnostic abilities.

articleTitle: Advancements in Intrusion Detection Systems: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and AI Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: To improve the effectiveness of intrusion detection system (IDS), this article explores the use of machine learning and AI based technology. The study encompasses the application of various approaches in the category of classification, clustering, and neural networks, across diverse datasets. The primary focus is on evaluating the accuracy and efficiency of each method for consolidated analysis and detailed insightful comparison. The outcomes of this detailed study are then compared and scrutinized to extract insights into the merits and demerits of each technique. After analyzing the various techniques, it is observed that in the classification category K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) is outperforming by showing the highest accuracy among all the classification techniques studied in this work. Moreover in clustering category Balanced Iterative Reducing and Clustering using Hierarchies (BRICH) clustering technique has shown highest accuracy. Further in the AI category all the models those are studied in this work has shown the accuracy of 91% and above. Among these AI models the Convolution Neural Network (CNN) has recorded the highest accuracy of 96% on an average across the various datasets. The overarching objective is to elevate the overall effectiveness of IDS in identifying and countering cyber threats. The findings from this study make a substantial contribution to current initiatives focused on strengthening network security and defending against the continuously evolving landscape of cyber threats.

articleTitle: Class of Service based Bandwidth Optimisation using AI in MPLS Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the ever-changing world of network technologies, Multi Protocol Label Switching (MPLS) serves as a robust and adaptable solution for optimizing data packet routing. With its ability to efficiently manage traffic and enhance network performance, MPLS networks have become essential in modern communication infrastructures. Nonetheless, effective bandwidth management is crucial to fully leverage the potential of MPLS. These networks play a critical role in managing various types of traffic and ensuring Quality of Service (QoS). However, current bandwidth allocation strategies during admission control at ingress routers often result in inefficiencies. This paper outlines strategies for overcoming these challenges by using forecasting analytics to optimize bandwidth utilization based on service classes. The dataset has been synthesised for the purpose of research using Python Code. The research examines three machine learning algorithms: RNN (Recurring Neural Network), LSTM (Long Short Term Memory), MLP (Multi Layer Perceptron), and Bi-LSTM (Bi-directional Long Short Term Memory) to forecast future bandwidth consumption. The Bi-LSTM surpasses the balance models with an average Mean Square Error of $\mathbf{0. 0 5 3 4}$.

articleTitle: The Graph Neural Network with Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network for botnet detection in smart city IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: One of the main risks to the security and stability of Internet of Things (IoT) networks in smart cities is botnet assaults. The identification of complex and emerging botnet attacks has not been entirely contained by traditional methods of botnet detection. In this study, we present a new hybrid approach, called GNN-WGAN, to efficiently detect bots in IoT-based smart city networks by integrating Graph Neural Network and Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network. The suggested method, which ultimately aims to improve the precision and robustness against botnet detection in dynamic IoT networks, effectively uses WGANs to generate synthetic botnet traffic patterns to add more training data and GNNs to capture dependencies between and interactions across network topology. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the GNN-WGAN technique in accurately recognizing botnet activities, which enhances the security and resilience of IoT networks in smart cities.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-Based Emotion Recognition Using Augmented Speech Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Ongoing developments in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) through speech signals signify a shift towards seamless, natural communication, enabling accessibility and efficiency in technology utilization. This evolution promises to bridge the gap between users and machines, enhancing user experience and simplifying complex tasks. This study proposes an effective speech emotion recognition method, an essential component in HCI. The proposed approach is evaluated using the RAVDESS and EmoDB emotion databases, employing augmented audio data to enhance generalizability. Mel spectrograms extracted from the augmented data serve as feature representations, feeding into VGG19 for emotion classification. Results demonstrate that VGG19 achieved promising metrics, setting benchmark accuracies of $\mathbf{97.71 \%}$ on RAVDESS and $\mathbf{9 8. 7 9 \%}$ on EmoDB, outperforming state-of-theart methods. This study serves as a valuable benchmark in the task of speech emotion recognition, and the achieved results contribute to the persistent efforts in HCI to create more natural, intuitive, and accessible interfaces.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Performance of Adaptive Error Control Coding Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Adaptive blunders management coding strategies have become increasingly essential to ensure reliable communique in wireless systems. This paper presents an evaluation of the overall performance of adaptive error control coding strategies in noisy channels. Specifically, the authors offer a theoretical and numerical analysis of the error probability, throughput, and channel ability of adaptive error management codes over Rayleigh, Rican, and Z-diversity channels. The theoretical evaluation is based on the discrete-time finite-country Markov chains and the belief in perfect channel country records. The final results of the theoretical analysis famous that the error opportunity decreases while the channel fading is slower and that the error performance may be notably improved by the usage of more than one diversity technique. The numerical analysis is based totally on Monte-Carlo simulations of adaptive error control coding systems with frequency-hopping spread spectrum modulation. The consequences of the numerical evaluation show that the adaptive error management coding systems can efficiently enhance the overall mistake performance in Rayleigh and Rican fading channels. Moreover, the authors conclude that the Z-variety coding device substantially improves the channel capacity and throughput in comparison to other coding strategies.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity in Healthcare: IOT Security for Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving Internet of Things (IoT) era, the healthcare sector’s fast embrace of digital technology and connected medical devices has revealed hitherto unknown prospects for improved patient care and operational efficiency. However, the digital revolution has resulted in an increase in cybersecurity vulnerabilities unique to the healthcare business. To maintain the safety of patient data and medical equipment, this study proposal, Cybersecurity in Healthcare: Securing Patient Data and Medical Devices, explores the primary cybersecurity challenges threatening patient data integrity. This study suggests a number of methods focused on protecting personal health information and preventing unauthorized access to connected medical devices. These include in-depth security assessments of medical equipment, secure communication protocols, the development of privacy-preserving data handling policies, and proactive steps to prevent insider threats and phishing schemes. This study intends to protect patient privacy, reinforce medical infrastructure, and eventually improve the quality and security of healthcare services by improving cybersecurity in healthcare.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Collective Decision-Making Systems and the Future Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth survey of the current state and future trends of artificial intelligence (AI) in augmenting collective decision-making processes. At the intersection of AI and group dynamics, this research explores how advanced AI technologies such as machine learning, reinforcement learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics, and swarm intelligence, revolutionize the way collective decisions are made in various sectors, including business, healthcare, governance, and finance. We delve into the theoretical foundations of collective decision-making, highlighting the pivotal role of AI in enhancing human judgment, overcoming cognitive limitations, and facilitating consensus in group settings. The paper examines the application of specific AI methodologies like decision trees, ensemble methods, Bayesian approaches, optimization algorithms, and simulation models in diverse decision-making scenarios. Real-world case studies are presented to illustrate the practical implications and transformative impact of AI in fields such as business strategy, healthcare decision support, financial market predictions, and public policy formulation.
