We address the challenges and limitations inherent in AI-driven decision systems, such as data quality, ethical concerns, biases, transparency, and integration with human processes. The abstract concludes by discussing emerging trends and future directions in AI collective decision-making, including advancements in explainable AI, ethical AI governance, integration of quantum computing, democratisation of decision-making, continuous learning in AI systems, and cross-disciplinary applications, underscoring the potential of AI to significantly enhance the efficacy and equity of collective decision-making across various domains.

articleTitle: Multi Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning approach for Traffic Signal Control
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In response to the growing challenges posed by traffic congestion in urban areas, Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) have emerged as indispensable tools for optimizing traffic flow. Amongst the pivotal components of ITS, Traffic Signal Control (TSC) holds particular significance in alleviating congestion at intersections. Recent efforts have witnessed a surge in research endeavors leveraging Deep Learning (DL) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) techniques to enhance TSC efficiency. However, existing frameworks also pose challenges in some areas and open the scope for a lot of research, for example, reward formulation. In this paper, we propose a novel methodology aimed at refining the definition of state and reward functions to enhance the performance of traffic signal controller agents. By advocating for a more intuitive and consistent design approach, we anticipate improved training stability and expedited convergence towards optimal policies. Our approach integrates the Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) architecture with the redefined state and reward to further enhance learning efficiency. Through extensive simulations conducted in the Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) environment, our results demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed methodology compared to other approaches in state and reward design.

articleTitle: Improving Public Safety with Advanced CNN-SVM Gun Detection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study uses a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network-Support Vector Machine (CNN-SVM) model to classify weapons into five unique categories: revolvers, machine guns, shotguns, submachine guns, rifles, and assault rifles. An information collection of 2500 photos demonstrating the model’s high effectiveness and durability in classifying firearms shows that The model reached 92. on average precision macro. 69%, Recall of 92. Achieving a novel accuracy score of 88% and F1Score of 92%. 72%, showcasing a performance class able to train and pass every test. The Weighted Average gives rise to numeric parameters such as a Precision of 92, which is more precise than a computed Compound. 77%, Recall of 92. With an F1-Score of 92 and Accuracy of 69%, it saved the model with the best results. In doing so, the model scores 66% points, indicating its ability to tackle the class imbalance successfully. The conclusion model’s performance is adequate as the Micro Average Precision, Recall, and F1-score, all 92 offer no issues. Regarding the validation and verification of the model’s reliability and accuracy, the test results in 69% of cases confirm the general reliability and accuracy. The results of the ROC curve prove that every class has a high Area Under the Curve (AUC) value, which is a sign of the high diagnostic capacity of the current model. The confusion matrix allows us to inspect the degree of reality of various classifications through a complete analysis.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Multiclass Classification of Viral, Bacterial, Pneumonia and Healthy Lungs from Chest Radiographs
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has increased interest in computer-aided diagnosis (CAD),particularly the use of X ray images to diagnose and classify lung diseases. The overlap between pneumonia and COVID-19 demonstrates the importance of CAD during the epidemic. The purpose of this study is to assess how well-suited individual models and model combinations are for the classification of lung illnesses. The results showed that InceptionResNet_V2 achieved an F1 result of 93.52 % when used alone. In addition, the F1 score of the combined model is at a high level of 94.84 %, which is better than the single model. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of joint systems in improving lung disease accuracy and thus the potential of CADsystems.

articleTitle: IoT - Driven Allergy Management & Modelling
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This work delves into the transformative potential of the Internet of Things (IoT) in reshaping healthcare services, environmental monitoring, and home automation processes. The emphasis is on tackling prevalent allergic conditions such as allergic rhinitis and asthma in India. Recognizing the significant health implications of snoring during sleep and its potential to mitigate a multitude of health issues, this study aspires to address this concern as well. By harnessing IoT technologies, the aim is to redefine human interactions with living spaces, health metrics, and the environment, offering a seamless fusion of convenience, well-being, and sustainability. The application seeks to distinguish itself by providing an innovative solution that aims to enhance respiratory health, enhance indoor air quality, and alleviate the impact of allergens on allergy-prone individuals by bridging existing research gaps. The proposed system utilizes sensors to detect indoor contaminants, activating a humidifier to adjust room humidity when allergen levels exceed a preset threshold, while also intelligently coordinating with room temperature to avoid interference with the air conditioner.

articleTitle: MazeSolver: Exploring Algorithmic Solutions for Maze Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The initiative examines the efficiency of various maze-solving algorithms, including breadth-first search (BFS), depth-first search (DFS), A* search, Markov decision processes with policy iteration (MDP PI), value iteration (MDP VI), and an enhanced wall-follower algorithm. The study seeks to discover the best algorithm for the autonomy of navigation in harsh and non-obvious environments, which is a crucial step for robotics applications in logistics, exploration, and rescue operations. In a comparative analysis within a controlled maze environment, each algorithm’s performance is evaluated based on path length, execution time, and memory usage. The study highlights the benefits of sophisticated decision-making and optimized pathfinding, particularly in MDP implementations and heuristic-based A* searches, addressing traditional limitations such as high computational costs and susceptibility to specific maze configurations. Results from this study are anticipated to enhance autonomous navigation systems, provide valuable educational insights, and improve operational efficiencies in critical applications.

articleTitle: Utilizing EHR in Machine Learning-Based Systems for Early Heart Disease Prediction in Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Machine learning methods have become instrumental in the prediction of heart diseases, offering a potent means of early detection and personalized risk assessment. By harnessing various algorithms and techniques, these models analyze extensive datasets encompassing patient demographics, medical histories, and clinical measurements. The interpretability of machine learning models remains a pertinent issue, as the complex algorithms often lack transparency, hindering clinicians’ understanding of the underlying decision-making process. Furthermore, model bias and generalization issues can arise, particularly when datasets are not representative of diverse populations or when algorithms are trained on data from specific healthcare settings. Addressing these challenges requires a concerted effort to improve data collection practices, enhance model interpretability, mitigate bias, and ensure equitable access to healthcare technologies. This paper proposed the Entropy Hidden Markov Model (EHMM) for heart disease prediction. The proposed EHMM model uses the estimation of entropy with consideration of local and global features for the estimation of modalities in the heart. With the estimated entropy Hidden Markov Model (HMM) is employed for disease detection and prevention. With the proposed EHMM the feature points are computed for the heart diseases. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed EHMM model achieves a higher prediction rate of 0.98 with minimal loss than the conventional ML with the classifiers SVM and RF.

articleTitle: Interpretable Machine Learning Algorithms for Interpretation of Clinical Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Interpretable machine learning (IML) algorithms use mathematical principles of machine learning to assist know-how, perception, and manipulation of scientific facts. Those algorithms aim to bridge the gap between clinicians’ knowledge of the facts and the output of traditional predictive analytics. IML algorithms have proved suitable for diverse obligations related to records analysis and interpretation of scientific facts, inclusive of predicting medical responses to remedy, exploring medical pathways, predicting future medical outcomes, and clustering affected person populations. Numerous techniques may be employed while using IML algorithms, which include linear fashions, choice tree models, help vector machines, neural networks, and Bayesian networks. Those fashions are mixed with specific parameters, including feature selection and weighting that can be used to evaluate the importance of every characteristic in predictive models. Moreover, those models can be implemented for non-linear facts by using regularization techniques. One essential advantage of IML over traditional devices in getting to know algorithms is the capacity to interpret the version outputs. Through using interpretable facts visualizations consisting of bar plots, scatter plots, and heat maps, clinicians can take advantage of insights into the relationships among features and goal variables.

articleTitle: Fashion Recommendation System for E-Commerce using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the increasingly competitive outlook of ecommerce, personalized recommendation systems have emerged as pivotal tools to enhance user experience and drive sales. This paper proposes a novel Fashion Recommendation System (FRS) leveraging deep learning techniques to offer personalized fashion suggestions to users. The system utilizes a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image feature extraction. Through a comprehensive analysis of user interactions and preferences, the FRS generates tailored recommendations that align with individual style preferences and current trends. The work proposes a novel approach that utilizes the ResNet50 algorithm to analyze images of fashion items, extracting meaningful features that capture the essence of style, color, and texture. By training the ResNet50 model on vast datasets of fashion images, thereby enhancing its ability to make accurate recommendations. Through the integration of user preferences and historical data, this system can generate personalized fashion recommendations tailored to each user’s unique style and preferences, thus enhancing user satisfaction and engagement. By harnessing the power of deep learning and the ResNet50 algorithm, fashion retailers can offer personalized shopping experiences, increase customer retention, and drive sales.

articleTitle: Augmented Prediction of Employee Anxiety and Depression: an Ensemble Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Mental health is integral to overall well-being, significantly affecting quality of life and productivity. Anxiety and depression are prevalent in the workplace, leading to reduced performance and increased absenteeism. Addressing mental health concerns proactively not only benefits individuals but also cultivates a more inclusive and thriving work culture, underscoring its significance in contemporary organizational contexts. This study leverages machine learning to predict employee anxiety and depression, utilizing K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree, Random Forest and Logistic Regression, in conjunction with ensemble techniques such as ExtraTreeClassifier, BaggingClassifier, AdaBoostClassifier, and StackingClassifier. Analyzing a dataset comprising demographic, occupational, and psychological characteristics, we assess model performance using accuracy, precision, and AUC score metrics. Random Forest improves accuracy and mitigates overfitting through ensemble learning, while KNN evaluates the impact of proximate data points, Decision Tree provides interpretable decision rules, and Logistic Regression establishes baseline predictions and identifies key predictors. The findings of this article demonstrate that the Random Forest model outperforms other approaches, enhancing the accuracy and reliability of workplace mental health assessments. These results offer valuable insights for developing robust predictive tools to promote employee well-being and inform future research in mental health prediction.

articleTitle: Optimizing Automatic Test Case Generation Using Singular Value Decomposition Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Test case generation is a complex problem when dealing with multiple objectives, which hinders search efficiency with algorithms like DynaMOSA in the EvoSuite framework. To address this issue, we propose SVD-DynaMOSA, utilizing Singular Value Decomposition for dimensionality reduction. This approach aims to optimize the test case generation process, leading to improved efficiency. Experimentation with 49 projects and 110 classes from the SF110 dataset, selected for their complexity and number of objectives, demonstrates SVD-DynaMOSA’s superiority over DynaMOSA. It achieves higher or comparable coverage in multiple metrics, enhancing test case generation performance significantly. SVD-DynaMOSA shows promise in producing comprehensive test suites in practical time frames, overcoming the limitations of current methods.

articleTitle: Optimizing Energy Efficiency in Video Multicasting Over 5G Networks Through D2D Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The exponential increase in video data demands over the wireless network has created the interest among the researchers to come up with a potential solution to efficiently distribute the video content over 5G and beyond networks. Therefore, in this paper, an energy-efficient scheme for video content dissemination by utilizing the device-to-device (D2D) communication has been proposed. The work aims to address the twin issues of energy efficiency and distortion minimization simultaneously. In the current cellular networks, every user downloads the video independently which often leads to low quality as the distance between the base station (BS) and mobile device increases. In the proposed scheme, proximate mobile nodes are grouped into clusters and among them a cluster head is chosen which forwards the data to cluster members using D2D communication. To make the system more spectral efficient, performance of the proposed scheme is evaluated in underlay mode where D2D links are sharing the channels with the primary cellular users. To show the efficacy of the proposed scheme, numerical analysis is conducted, and results show that significant energy saving can be achieved with the proposed scheme as compared to the conventional multicasting scheme, and it also provides improved video quality with lesser distortion and delay.

articleTitle: Analyzing The Benefits and Challenges of Behavioral Economics in Consumer Behavioral Modeling in E-commerce
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Behavioral economics is a rising interdisciplinary area that integrates financial and mental concepts to give an explanation for and predict consumer choice behavior. It has been carried out for client behavior modeling in e-commerce, with the purpose of improving decision-making and targeting for online stores. This paper provides a scientific review of existing literature on the benefits and demanding situations of the usage of behavioral economics for consumer behavioral modeling in e-commerce. We discover that, at the same time as behavioral economics can assist online outlets to benefit from deeper information on customer behavior with implications for better choice-making; there also are a number of challenges related to using this method. These challenges include confined admission to facts, the want for superior technical expertise, and an accelerated price stratification manner. Regardless of those demanding situations, the potential advantages of the use of behavioral economics for client behavioral modeling in e-commerce are extensive. In conclusion, the usage of behavioral economics is suggested for e-trade organizations with objectives to make knowledgeable decisions and optimize performance.

articleTitle: Integrating IoT, Edge, and Cloud Computing for Early Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes: A Machine Learning-Driven Smart Healthcare Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: As diabetes continues to be one of the most prevalent chronic illnesses worldwide, affecting approximately 537 million individuals according to the IDF Diabetes Atlas 2021 report, there is a critical need for enhanced awareness and prediction capabilities. Leveraging the Internet of Things (IoT) and edge computing offers a promising approach for early disease detection through real-time analysis. This study introduces “HealthEdge,” a comprehensive smart healthcare system that integrates machine learning with IoT and edge computing to detect Type 2 Diabetes. “HealthEdge” employs machine learning models at both edge and cloud levels to identify early signs of Type 2 Diabetes using real-time patient health data collected from IoT sensors. By prioritizing real-time processing at the edge to minimize latency and utilizing cloud resources for comprehensive data analysis and model training, “HealthEdge” addresses privacy concerns through robust encryption, demonstrating promising results in early diabetes diagnosis while emphasizing scalability, efficiency, and accessibility. Moreover, the proposed solution has been implemented and validated on real-world patient health data, showcasing impressive accuracy of 98% using the random forest algorithm on the original diabetes dataset. This solution can be deployed on various intelligent edge devices, paving the way for improved diabetes management and healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: Predicting NIRF Ranking via Novel K-Star Ensembles
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) was established by the Indian Ministry of Education (MoE), which ranks higher education institutions across the country. The institutions being ranked may benefit if their rankings or performance could be predicted given their parameters, thereby, improving their Institute’s attributes. However, less attention has been given to the problem of predicting rank from the parameters collected for the rankings. The main objective of this research is to forecast the ranking of the Institutions using a four-year dataset of NIRF collected for 16 Indian Institute of Technologies (IITs). The change in parameter data was collected across 16 parameters to predict the change in ranks using two consecutive years. A novel K-Star 2 -stage ensemble algorithm was developed. In the first stage, a number of lazy learning algorithms, K-Star, Instance-Based Learner (IBk) and Locally Weighted Learning (LWL), were trained using 10 -fold crossvalidation. The predictions of these algorithms from stage 1 were taken into stage 2, where the K-Star predicted the change in rank. The results revealed that the K-Star Ensemble had an RMSE of 0.009 compared to other algorithms including IBk (RMSE: 5.76), K-Star (RMSE: 5.85), and LWL (RMSE: 5.91). We highlight the main implications of our work for rank prediction in the real world.

articleTitle: Paddy Leaf Disease Detection Using Fine-tuned EfficientNetB4 Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Agriculture remains the backbone of many countries since it acts as the main source of income and food. In this regard, different food crops are significant in the global economy, where rice occupies a very central position as one of the most important staple foods in many Asian countries. However, rice cultivation encounters various diseases at the different stage affecting either the quality or the rate of growth in the crop. Diagnosis of these diseases can be tiresome by applying traditional methods and use of naked eyes because symptoms of most diseases are often related. Therefore, the use of automated systems and the integration of such systems adds more realization to disease detection, hence informing the farmer to take appropriate measures on time to minimize crop or plant losses in order to yield quality produce. In the last several years different approaches utilizing image processing, machine learning, and deep learning algorithms have been investigated by researchers to create effective automatic systems. Therefore, this paper aims at optimizing several of the existing highly accurate deep learning-based state-of-art Convolutional neural networks for the early detection of different rice crop diseases, also known as paddy leaf diseases. This work also pointed out a comparative assessment of the utilized techniques through precision, accuracy, recall, and F1-score metrics with a fine-tuned EfficientNetB4 model with an optimum F1-score of approximately 99.7%.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Framework For Satire Vs. Sarcasm Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Sarcasm and satire are common ways to communicate complicated ideas with humor and irony, both expressing criticism or mockery. Detecting sarcasm vs. satire in real life can foster better communication by understanding intent, preventing misunderstandings, and promoting critical thinking and empathy. We introduce an innovative dataset for detecting Multi-modal Satire vs. Sarcasm, leveraging the MUStARD dataset for its construction. This dataset includes visual utterances annotated with sarcasm and satire labels, enriching its potential for studying multimodal satire and sarcasm detection. This enriched dataset serves as a robust foundation for training and evaluating machine learning and deep learning architectures that combine textual and visual cues to identify satire and sarcasm in multimedia content. By incorporating this enhanced dataset, the research aims to advance the field of multimodal satire and sarcasm detection and contribute to a deeper understanding of humor and irony in online communication. We carry out experimentation with various architectures like LSTM, GPT2, BERT, SVM, and Logistic Regression. The proposed architecture achieves an F1 score of $\mathbf{0. 9 5 6}$, outperforming other baselines.

articleTitle: Bottle Cleanliness Detection Device with Electronic Nose using PCA-KNN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact Bottle Cleanliness Detection Device that uses the PCA-KNN algorithm and an Electronic Nose system to expedite bottle inspection procedures. This is especially important in areas like the Philippines, where bottle reuse is prevalent. Using machine learning-processed sensor data, the device uses smell analysis to distinguish between “clean” and “unclean” bottles. The investigation confirms the device’s reliability with a high accuracy rate of 94.67% and an F1 score of 94.52%. This research provides small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) with a portable, affordable quality assurance solution supporting consumer safety.

articleTitle: News Article Summarization using PEGASUS model for Efficient Information Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Text summarization is a crucial task in natural language processing aimed at condensing large volumes of text into concise and informative summaries. Traditional methods of summarization, primarily extractive techniques, have limitations in capturing the essence of the original text and producing human-like summaries. In response to these challenges, advanced abstractive summarization models like PEGASUS have emerged, leveraging transformer-based encoder-decoder architectures and innovative pre-training strategies. Unlike extractive methods, which simply select and rearrange existing text segments, abstractive models generate summaries by synthesizing new sentences that capture the key information from the original text. While extractive summarization can suffer from redundancy and lack of coherence, abstractive models like PEGASUS excel in producing contextually rich and coherent summaries. However, abstractive summarization also presents challenges, such as maintaining factual accuracy and preserving the intended meaning of the text. Despite these challenges, PEGASUS has demonstrated remarkable performance in text summarization tasks, showcasing its ability to generate human-like summaries and distill pertinent information effectively. By incorporating advanced features like attention mechanisms and self-attention layers, PEGASUS enhances its ability to capture and summarize key information while maintaining coherence and readability. Moreover, PEGASUS offers additional features like highlighting entities of interest and customizing user output, allowing users to tailor summaries to their specific needs and preferences. Overall, PEGASUS represents a significant advancement in text summarization technology, offering a promising solution to the limitations of traditional summarization methods and paving the way for improved understanding and synthesis of complex textual information.

articleTitle: Assessing the Robustness of Machine Learning Algorithms against Emerging Privacy and Security Threats in Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Using gadgets to realize algorithms in medical packages can provide new insights and talents, including new approaches to diagnose illnesses or reveal treatments. Rising privacy and security threats pose potential dangers to those structures that can restrict their efficacy and average performance. To make sure tool mastering algorithms are resilient to those threats, it is critical to assess their robustness. This summary offers an assessment of techniques to evaluate the robustness of tool-getting-to-know algorithms against emerging privacy and protection threats in medical programs. First, we check the kinds of threats and discuss how they’ll affect the general performance of machine studying algorithms. Secondly, we compare a selection of strategies for measuring the robustness of gadgets and gaining knowledge of algorithms, which include static, dynamic, and adverse check strategies. Ultimately, we speak about techniques for mitigating threats in scientific packages, which provides for incorporating relaxed layout thoughts in tool studying structures and utilizing smoke assessments and strain tests. Through this assessment, we aim to provide more facts on the techniques for assessing the robustness of gadget-studying algorithms against rising privacy and security threats in scientific programs.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security and Privacy of Machine Learning Algorithms in Agricultural Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper specializes in enhancing the safety and privacy of machine-mastering algorithms in agricultural automation. With the emergence of digital generation in agricultural production, system mastering algorithms have emerged as essential to offer precision control in farm control operations. However, their security and privacy may be compromised due to assault vectors inclusive of opposed inputs, facts leakage assaults, and facts poisoning attacks. Several ability solutions are studied, which include the introduction of statistics anonymization strategies, getting the right of entry to manage mechanisms, cryptographic strategies, and software program and hardware protection tactics. This paper analyses the one-of-a-kind security and privacy enhancement techniques and affords a comprehensive discussion of their effectiveness. Sooner or later, the authors advise a complete solution that encompasses all the security and privacy enhancement approaches to shield the gadget studying algorithms in agricultural automation effectively.

articleTitle: Automatically Generate Impression From Findings In Radiology Report Using BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The vital work of summarizing medical reports so that the general public can easily access them can be considerably aided by the recent developments in deep learning and large language models (LLM). One medical specialty that can make use of it is radiology, where it's essential to summarize the most crucial information from the “findings” part into the “impression” part of a report to help radiologists and referring physicians communicate more easily. To automate the development of the “impression” part in radiology reports, we propose a unique architecture for summarization. The workload for radiologists is greatly reduced by this method. Because of the specialized vocabulary employed in radiology, existing models and approaches for abstractive summarization-such as those that utilize recent advances in the field of natural language processing (NLP), such as BERT and its derivatives, are not immediately relevant. As such, our system is specially designed to tackle the particular difficulties presented by radiology reports. We create a pre-trained language model in radiology to address the issue of automatically summarizing reports on radiography. More specifically, In this research BERT Encoder is pre-trained on the MIMIC-CXR dataset. Next, an abstractive summarization model is built by combining a Transformer decoder and a pretrained BERT. In conclusion, for the abstractive summarization task, the model will be improved utilizing reports from chest X-rays. Furthermore, the publically available OPEN-I datasets is used for evaluation.

articleTitle: Fortifying the Academic Perimeter: A Study on Network Sniffers in University Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study presents a specialised Java-based network sniffer designed for department-level monitoring of commercial computer systems on university networks. The sniffer is a powerful, platform-independent tool for real-time traffic analysis and intrusion detection. The research looks into the operational complexities of educational environments and compares them to alternative technologies. The paper emphasises its application by detailing the sniffer’s smooth integration with university computer systems, overcoming scaling problems. For detecting the presence of packet sniffers, advanced detection approaches like as Address Resolution Protocol(ARP) detection, Round Trip Time (RTT) analysis, and Simple Network Management Protocol(SNMP) monitoring are examined. The outcomes provide a full performance review, recognising issues and suggesting technological remedies. Potential upgrades and collaborative opportunities are among the future work considerations. The abstract emphasises the research’s unique application in departmental-level monitoring. The abstract underscores the research’s specific application in departmental-level monitoring, emphasizing its contributions to efficient and secure network practices within university environments.

articleTitle: Quality of Service Analysis of Network Coding Algorithms in Cooperative Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Network coding algorithms have been proposed as a unique technique to improve the best carrier (quality of service) of cooperative Wi-Fi networks. Those algorithms leverage community coding strategies to increase the network throughput, eliminate troubles related to traditional routing protocols, and improve transmission reliability. The quality of service performance of network coding algorithms in cooperative wireless networks is impacted by the diffusion of things such as the topology, channel traits, and the coding method hired. This article comprehensively reviews the latest advances in analyzing satisfaction providers of network coding algorithms in cooperative wireless networks. In particular, we discuss various metrics used to degree the quality of service, packet transmission latency, throughput, channel capacity, hyperlink reliability, and energy efficiency. We additionally present an outline of how network coding algorithms can enhance these performance metrics and provide an in-depth evaluation of the quality of service evaluation techniques used in the literature. Ultimately, we also provide an attitude at the challenges and possibilities of similar research for quality of service analysis in community coding algorithms for cooperative Wi-Fi networks.

articleTitle: Content Delivery Models for Distributed and Cooperative Media Algorithms in Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Content transport fashions for allotted and Cooperative Media Algorithms in cellular Networks (DC-MAMR) is a unique technique to providing multimedia content material in mobile networks, the use of disbursed and cooperative media algorithms. DC-MA-MR leverages an aggregate of content material request-based networking models, distributed and cooperative media algorithms to permit green dependable content material delivery. Particularly, DC-MA-MR takes benefit of the subscriber’s ability to select preferred content for extraordinary services, while allowing for disbursed and cooperative media algorithms to be recognized prior to content request time. The ensuing model may be used to discover consumer-precise resources for content shipping, accordingly permitting them to receive content over more than one channels. Moreover, DC-MA-MR permits strategies for instant content material distribution, with an emphasis on robustness of the delivery mechanisms in the presence of various user requests and environmental conditions. Further, DC-MA-MR entails mechanisms for deciding on most effective media resources on the basis of know-how of user mobility, network situations, content recognition, and different issues. Eventually, DC-MA-MR is likewise designed for scalability and sustainability by way of leveraging more than one additives of current networks, along with coding, caching, clustering, and dispensed computing.

articleTitle: Leveraging Pre-Trained Text-To-Text Transfer Transformer Language Model for Accurate Prediction of Drug-Target Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The success of modern drug development relies on identifying potential drug-target interactions. However, predicting these interactions is challenging due to the limitations of traditional approaches. Thus, the application of artificial intelligence is crucial for discovering new drug candidates. This research explores the deep learning method of employing the Text-to-Text Transfer Transformers (T5) model, which facilitates the construction of representations using a dataset of protein sequences and drug Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) to improve drug-target interaction (DTI) predictions. This study adopts the pre-trained Prot T5 model and Chem T5 for protein sequences and drug compounds data for extraction of knowledge embeddings to address DTI prediction. The resulting embeddings are concatenated and fed into various machine learning techniques, such as logistic regression, naive bayesian, XGBoost, random forest, K-nearest neighbor, support vector machine, and adaBoost for classification. Reported results highlight the model’s effectiveness, surpassing state-of-the-art models in predicting interactions between drugs and targets.

articleTitle: Texture Recognition Using InceptionNeXt-based Texture Perception Network
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Recognizing textures remains challenging in images due to variations in fundamental elements (primates) and characteristics (attributes) caused by spatial context. Existing Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) approaches typically use detailed local descriptions with unordered aggregation for spatial layout inconsistency. However, these methods overlook the inherent structure relationships between primates and the semantic meanings conveyed by attributes, which are crucial for texture. This paper suggests a newfangled approach for texture cognition using Inception NeXt, a deep learning architecture known for its long-range modelling capabilities. Inception NeXt uses large-kernel convolutions to capture broader contextual information within textures. We address the computational efficiency boundaries associated with large kernels by incorporating an Inception-inspired decomposition strategy. This approach decomposes the large kernels into smaller, parallel branches, enhancing efficiency while maintaining performance. Our model extracts features by analyzing the relationships between these primates and attributes within the spatial context of the texture. The Inception NeXt architecture facilitates the capture of long-range dependencies between texture elements, leading to more robust feature representations. Experiments on two challenging texture databases demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving superior performance in terms of accuracy, robustness, and efficiency compared to traditional CNN-based methods.

articleTitle: A Review of the Automated Techniques for Brain Tumor Detection Using MR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the field of medical diagnostics, identifying brain tumors through imaging is a tough task for radiologists. Sorting out the complexities of finding brain tumors in MRI pictures includes many steps. One important part is segmentation, which helps classify and understand the images. Manually segmenting brain MR images is no easy task and demands a lot of time from experts. The lack of repeatability in this process highlights the need for an automated approach to efficiently segment White Matter (WM), Gray Matter (GM), and Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) in the brain more quickly. Accurate segmentation is vital, as misidentifying diseases can have serious consequences. To tackle these challenges this research aims to explore and evaluate the strengths and limitations of existing segmentation techniques discussed in literature. This article enriches the readers with a comprehensive view of the subject, shedding light on innovative aspects of employing various machine learning and image segmentation techniques required for the detection of brain tumors. However, it is important to note that the introduction of a novel technique falls outside the scope of this study as we will not develop any new method but evaluate and review existing techniques.

articleTitle: PolySegResUNet: Polyp Segmentation Residual Unet based Model for Colonoscopy Images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In clinical area, a colonoscopy is still the highest standard screening for cancer of the colon. However, computer-aided technologies to reduce the chances of specialists overlooking polyps, particularly in cases with numerous tiny adenomas where there’s a significant risk of miss rates. Moreover, The key challenge is the wide variety of infected polyp features inside the colon and the lack of distinction between healthy and diseased regions. To solve these issues, the proposed novel Customized Polyp Segmentation Residual Unet (PolypSegResUNet)-based model for segmenting polyps from colonoscopy images. The customized Residual network feature is extracted from polyp colonoscopy images. Furthermore, Unet model is applied in an upsampling layer to enhance feature selection maps and manage scale variance during training. Additionally, the Gateaux Derivatives (GD) approach is used to segment boundary boxes of polyp regions. The proposed method has been evaluated on four datasets, namely the Kvasir-SEG, ETIS-PolypLaribDB, CVC-ClinicDB, CVC-T, and CVCColonDB datasets, for segmenting and detecting polyps. The validation results have been examined by simulation metrics, namely accuracy, Intersection-Over-Union (IOU), mean IOU, precision, recall, Mean Process Time per Frame (MPTF), F1score, and mean Dice Similarity Coefficient (meanDSC) for proper validation. The proposed scheme outperforms the existing model on the polyp datasets.

articleTitle: Explainable Machine Learning Models for Clinical Decision Support Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Explainable Machine Learning (ML) models are an essential component of Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS), since they provide the transparency and interpretability that are essential for efficient decision-making in the healthcare industry. With a particular emphasis on their capacity to provide comprehensible explanations in case of clinical predictions along with recommendations, this study investigates the development along with deployment of explainable ML models in (CDSS). We analyze a variety of strategies and methodologies that are used to improve interpretability of ML models in healthcare settings. This is accomplished by doing a substantial study of the relevant literature and case studies. Feature significance analysis, attention mechanisms, rule-based systems, and model-agnostic explanation approaches are some of the techniques that fall under this category. We also examine the difficulties and possibilities that arise when implementing explainable machine learning models in clinical settings that are based on the real world. These include issues around data privacy, compliance with legal requirements, and integration with preexisting processes in the healthcare industry. The purpose of this paper is to educate healthcare professionals, researchers, and policymakers about the potential of transparent and interpretable artificial intelligence models to improve patient outcomes, reduce medical errors, and enhance trust in AI-driven healthcare systems. This will be accomplished by elucidating the benefits and limitations of explainable ML in CDSS.

articleTitle: Early Prediction and Risk Identification of Chronic Kidney Disease Using Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this research, we explore the efficacy of advanced learning models for classifying images by utilizing the ResNet50, MobileNet, and InceptionV3 frameworks. Through our investigation, we have gained fascinating insights into their performance when dealing with diverse data types. The ResNet50 model exhibited exceptional precision, attaining an astonishing 98% accuracy in image classification. This showcases its proficiency in extracting deep features and categorizing images. On the other hand, MobileNet and Inception V3 achieved impressive accuracy rates of 92% and 94%, respectively. These findings underscore their suitability for specific applications while also emphasizing the trade-off between model complexity and performance. Additionally, our research underscores the significance of data enhancement, maintaining optimal learning rates, and implementing early termination as crucial elements in successful model training. By delving into these aspects, our study contributes to the ongoing discourse surrounding the selection of the most suitable algorithm for image classification tasks. Furthermore, it sheds light on understanding the nuanced characteristics of each sample and the pivotal role of hyperparameter optimization in achieving accurate classifications.

articleTitle: Leveraging IoT and Blockchain Technologies for Wetland Monitoring and Community Engagement
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Wetlands are vital ecological systems that face growing risks due to human activities and climatic changes. This study introduces a method for monitoring wetlands, utilising the Internet of Things (IoT) and blockchain technology. Our approach involves using an Internet of Things (IoT) sensor system to monitor and assess the state of wetlands. Additionally, we actively involve local communities by leveraging blockchain technology. The IoT sensors monitor vital environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, $\mathbf{p H}$, dissolved oxygen, turbidity, and conductivity, allowing for immediate data gathering, transmission, and secure storage in the cloud. The integration of blockchain technology enables the facilitation of crowdsourcing, which incentivises users to give useful data regarding wetland conditions. This strategy promotes active participation from the community in environmental preservation, empowering individuals as “citizen sensors.” This paper explains the proposed architecture, consisting of an Internet of Things (IoT) sensor network and an Ethereum blockchain platform. Furthermore, we developed an Ethereum smart contract that evaluates the user data and decides the incentives. We also benchmarked the smart contract, and the test results show that the smart contract is efficient.

articleTitle: Home Interior Design Suggestion System using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research investigates the transformative potential of deep learning in revolutionizing home interior design through the development of a web application with three core functionalities: object replacement within an existing interior design image, object removal from the interior design image, and text-to-image design generation based on user inputs. Leveraging deep learning models like ControlNet, DeepFill, and stable diffusion, as well as YOLOv8 for object detection and image classification (home interior/non-home interior), the proposed system is an innovative approach to democratizing design knowledge and expediting interior design procedures. This research advances interior design practices and shapes the future of personalized and effective home interior design solutions by offering effective design modifications and design suggestions.

articleTitle: Hydrothermal Scheduling by Hybrid Computing Technique in RE Rich Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Hydrothermal scheduling with the integration of renewable energy is a critical factor in the shift to sustainable power generation. Maximizing the efficiency and undependability of these conventional systems is essential to attaining energy sustainability objectives. This article presents a novel approach for scheduling of hydrothermal and renewable energy systems on the IEEE 30 bus system utilizing an enhanced hybrid computational technique by combining the evolutionary programming (EP) technique with genetic algorithm (GA). The method combines the benefits of genetic algorithms with powerful optimization mechanisms to successfully control the equality and inequality constraints in the systems. The suggested technique optimizes scheduling by considering various parameters such as energy consumption, resource availability, and environmental restrictions to improve system performance, decrease costs, and reduce the ecological effects. Simulations and case studies on the IEEE 30 bus system illustrate the EP-GA technique’s efficacy and resilience, highlighting its potential for practical deployment in real-world energy management settings.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Archaeological Discoveries: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Site Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) utilization during the study of archaeological sites is a sea change in archaeology. The resulting possibilities of unlocking new features without the limits of traditional methods and improving the efficiency, precision, and breadth of archaeological research are at hand. The research follows this up with a look at how artificial intelligence (AI) and especially machine learning (ML) technology could detect and analyze archaeological sites and artefacts. It uses sophisticated algorithms such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), LIDAR, & Ground-Penetrating Radar (GPR). We implement these cutting-edge technologies in remote scanning, scene modelling, and artefact classification. The second-best result in accuracy by the Artifact Classifier based on the CNN classifier was around $92 \%$. It demonstrated a precision rate of 88 % and an F1-score of $89 \%$, pointing out the high degree to which the device identified the artefacts. These models demonstrated astonishing $87 \%$ and $90 \%$ accuracy utilizing LIDAR detection and GPR analysis. These results showed again that these models are of great use when locating the site and analyzing the subsurface. As well as acknowledging the success achieved, the report highlights challenges when implementing new technologies in traditional archaeology procedures. Other barriers are ethical problems created by the protection of personal data, the possibility of bias, and the technological and cultural factors that prevent the rapid dissemination of biotechnology. The success of the AI and ML systems has demonstrated great potential for these technologies to transform the archaeological field. Nevertheless, applying these technologies should be done carefully and with the purpose of their improvement, discussing how to mitigate the risks and make them more beneficial. This research improves the subject with focused discussions on AI’s key consequences. It sets realistic challenges for AI in archaeology to offer an unbiased point of view on AI’s future use and development.

articleTitle: Optimization of BERT Algorithms for Deep Contextual Analysis and Automation in Legal Document Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Legal document processing is one of the main areas where technology has advanced significantly, thanks to the introduction of deep contextual analysis and automation. The goal of this work is to improve the performance of Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERTs) algorithms in deep contextual analysis, with a particular focus on legal document processing. The effort aims to increase the accuracy and efficiency of BERT-based models in capturing complex legal situations, enabling automation in the reading and analysis of documents. By means of meticulous tuning, attention mechanism modifications, and investigation of ideal hyperparameters, our refined BERT algorithms demonstrate exceptional contextual comprehension and document processing skills. The acquired results show considerable improvements over the baseline BERT models in terms of speed and accuracy. In legal document analysis tasks, the enhanced algorithms produce a significant decrease in processing time while retaining or exceeding the high accuracy and recall of the original model. The study suggests optimizing BERT algorithms for improved efficiency in legal document processing, leading to increased productivity and automated contextual analysis in the legal sector The Python implementation of the BERT-based legal document processing system achieves an accuracy of 92%.

articleTitle: From Theory to Practice: Analyzing the Feasibility of Augmenting Human Intelligence with AI Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: this abstract summarizes a research paper inspecting the feasibility of augmenting human intelligence with synthetic intelligence (AI) technologies. The paper starts by means of exploring the theoretical underpinnings of augmenting human intelligence with AI, especially, the function of human cognition and the natural boundaries of AI era. In comparison to other existing attempts to use AI as a way of augmenting human intelligence, the paper indicates that AI technologies must be deployed in an adaptive manner that might enjoy the collective intelligence of all of the individuals of a given network, both human as well as AI-based. So as to research this theoretical approach in addition, the paper then proposes various simulations and empirical research to evaluate the feasibility of augmenting human intelligence the use of AI technologies. In the end, the paper describes potential effect of such an endeavor at the economy, society, and the scientific community, in addition to offering a variety of sensible implications for groups, coverage makers, and designers. In the long run, the paper gives a comprehensive analysis of the practical feasibility of augmenting human intelligence with AI technology.

articleTitle: Text Mining for Automated Data Analysis and Information Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Textual content Mining is the method of automatically analyzing vast amounts of natural language documents so that you can discover latent topics, extract vital understanding, and summarize relevant statistics. It consists of techniques. It presents critical insights into the content of information articles, emails, books, and other files, allowing us to gain insight into trends and styles that otherwise wouldn’t be seen. It can also stumble on sentiment, discover underlying entity relationships, extract key terms, and convey summaries. Textual content Mining is, for this reason, turning into an effective device for automatic information evaluation and records retrieval.

articleTitle: Beyond the Black Box: Explainable AI for Glaucoma Detection and Future Improvements
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Timely and precise identification of glaucoma is essential to avert irreversible vision loss. Automating glaucoma detection is essential whilst the disease worsens over time and manual screening methods possess limitations. It facilitates early identification and treatment in order to prevent the vision impairment. Machine learning and deep learning algorithms are efficient, nevertheless, they suffer from a lack of interpretability and require a substantial amount of data and computational resources. Transfer learning proves efficient by improving scarcity of data with enhanced performance. This study seeks to examine the operational characteristics of transfer learning approaches and employ XAI (eXplainable Artificial Intelligence) method LIME to achieve clear interpretability of the features obtained by the model for prediction, so as to address the challenges related to interpretability. This study has used a combined dataset consisting of RIMONE, PAPILA, CHAKSU, and AKSHI (a dataset created by the authors) to develop ResNet-50, ResNet50-V2, VGG-16, VGG-19, and EfficientNet-V2S models. Among the developed five models, ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-V2S provide better accuracy as demonstrated in this study with an analysis using metrics and feature visualization. Both models attain a maximum test accuracy of ${91.78\%}$ and the minimum test loss of, with ResNet-50 at 0.24 and EfficientNet-V2S at 0.23. In addition, these models demonstrate superior precision, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score, all around 92. Further, feature maps and class activation maps for ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-V2S show distinct and concentrated zones of activation, indicating accurate interpretation. Thus, in this comparative study, ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-V2S are choosen as the best models for this classification task owing to their high accuracy and reliable interpretability via visual activation patterns. Consequently, the mobile app ANSAN has been integrated with the ideal clinical decision-making model.

articleTitle: A Roadmap of Byte-Sized Morality in Traversing With Ethical Landscape of Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Potential enabling artificial intelligence (AI) to fundamentally transform both businesses along with civilizations has made AI a revolutionary force. AI has many beneficial applications, but there are also many moral dilemmas that come with its development. With the increasing integration of AI systems into every aspect of lives, there is an increased possibility of unforeseen effects and ethical conflicts.The lack of information’s gathering, sharing, as well as readability; the inability to demonstrate the internal decision-making process; and the disregard for ethical considerations in the creation of AI frameworks are some possible impediments to the ordinary application of AI. In artificial intelligence, “byte-sized morality” corresponds to the moral precepts and considerations that are ingrained in AI systems including are frequently constrained by information in digital format, algorithms, and analytical procedures. In this paper aims to contribute to ongoing ethical AI discussion, By examining these advancing understanding of legal obligations that accompany the advancement developing artificial intelligence in the technologically advanced society.

Author Keywords: Bias in AI Algorithms Privacy Concerns in AI Development

articleTitle: Detection of Specific Language Impairment Using XGBoost Model
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Specific Language Impairment (SLI) in children, a neurodevelopmental disorder presenting significant hurdles in language acquisition. Motivated by the prevalence and complexity of SLI diagnosis, this article introduces an methodology using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and chroma features combined with the XGBoost algorithm for classification. By analyzing a diverse dataset encompassing both SLI-diagnosed and non SLI children, the proposed model achieves efficiency of $\mathbf{9 9. 3 \%}$ accuracy on unseen data. Notably, the model’s strategic feature selection and utilization of XGBoost demonstrate superior performance compared to existing methods, highlighting its importance in SLI diagnosis and intervention planning. This work significantly advances machine learning-based diagnostic tools and holds promise for improving the quality of life for individuals impacted by SLI.

articleTitle: Resource Optimization and Forecasting of Mobile Ad-hoc Network using Particle Swarm Optimization along with Ensemble ML Modeling in 6G
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the evolution towards 6G networks, Mobile ad-hoc networks (MANETs) emerge as vital components, offering adaptability in dynamic environments. However, efficient resource management remains a challenge. This study delves into resource optimization and forecasting techniques within 6G MANETs, particularly focusing on bandwidth and congestion parameters. We utilize innovative machine learning models, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and ensemble methods, to enhance resource utilization effectively. Moreover, we employ Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (AN-FIS) to forecast temporal variations in network conditions. Leveraging historical network data, our models generate accurate and precise forecasts. By integrating optimization and forecasting techniques, this research contributes to enhancing network scalability and performance, thus directly aligning with the objectives of UN Sustainable Development Goal 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure.

articleTitle: Exploring Extended Reality Adoption in Moroccan Sports Institutes: A UTAUT Perspective for FIFA World Cup 2030
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: As anticipation builds for the FIFA 2030 Moroccan World Cup, the Sports Science Institute is pioneering the integration of emerging technologies, notably extended reality (XR), into sports education. XR technology holds promise for transforming learning and training methodologies in sports. However, its successful adoption relies on understanding acceptance and usage patterns among Moroccan sports students. This study investigates the acceptance of XR among Moroccan sports students, focusing on 162 participants and utilizing the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) model. Results indicate that Effort Expectancy (EE) and Hedonic Motivation (HM) significantly influence students’ behavioral intention (BI) to use XR in sports. These findings provide insights for technical developers and educational institutions, facilitating a deeper understanding of factors influencing XR technology utilization in sports education. Such insights can inform the development of tailored strategies and policies to optimize XR usage in sports training and learning environments.

articleTitle: Survey of Vulnerabilities and Architectural Flaws in Existing Collaborative DDoS Mitigation Systems for Autonomous Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the era of modern internet infrastructure, DDoS attacks create a severe threat to cyberspace. So, it is essential to mitigate these attacks by strategizing a collaborative defense mechanism that combines resources collected from various sources like ASes, ISPs, and CDNs. This paper focuses on the security aspects of Collaborative DDoS Mitigation Systems. We begin by discussing the components of Collaborative DDoS Mitigation Systems for AS in two ways: Centralized and Decentralized. Based on the centralized and decentralized approaches, the paper discusses the Vulnerable points or attack points and architectural flaws in the existing frameworks. Apart from discussing the components and vulnerabilities, the paper also conducts a deep examination of the framework to evaluate and identify the vulnerabilities and flaws linked to security, scalability, and protocols used for communications, resource management, and decision-making processes. By understanding the challenges and vulnerabilities discussed, the paper aims to contribute towards the development of more resilient as well as robust collaborative DDoS mitigation approaches for affirming the availability and integrity of critical online services.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Learning Paradigm for Efficient Stock Market Predictions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Predicting stock market movements is essential for investors to mitigate risks and capitalize on opportunities for wealth growth and portfolio diversification. Traditionally, stock market predictions have relied on statistical models, fundamental analysis, and technical indicators. However, recent advances in machine learning (ML), particularly ensemble learning, have shown promise in improving prediction accuracy and robustness. In that direction, ensemble learning combines multiple base models to make predictions, leveraging the strengths of each model to improve overall performance. In this work, we focus on predicting stock market data intelligently using an ensemble learning approach. Random sampling is employed to create subsets for training different machine learning models, introducing variability in the learning process. Our ensemble model consists of five base models, including Support Vector Regressor (SVR), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Random Forest Regressor (RF), Bayesian Ridge Regressor (BR), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), combined through a stacking regressor using a Gradient Boosting Regressor as the final estimator. Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Coefficient of Determination ($\mathbf{R}^{2}$) are used to evaluate the performance of the proposed ensemble model. From the results, it is observed that our model provides better performances than the baseline works.

articleTitle: Optimizing Electric Vehicle Charging Station Deployment: A Predictive Modeling and Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Owing to extensive environmental advantages, energy optimized processes, and amazing technological innovations, Electric Vehicles (EVs) have become an important domain for research and development. EVs utilize stored electricity power from rechargeable batteries rather than conventional ICE vehicles, which run on gasoline or diesel fuel to power their engines. increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has placed a strain on the current infrastructure for charging, leading to the need for efficient deployment of EV charging stations. Work done is an effort to identify the areas with the greatest potential for installing EV charging points and suggest the fastest and most affordable charging options. It evaluates current $E V$ adoption trends and utilizes curve-fitting to predict future demand suited for EV charging facilities. It then leverages the Gurobi optimization solver to address cost minimization by allocating demand to charging stations strategically. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in optimizing EV charging station deployment, achieving an accuracy of over $93 \%$. Notably, Scenario 1 achieved an optimal solution with a cost of INR 3,978,066/-, highlighting the potential cost savings this method offers. Optimizing the deployment of EV charging stations is essential to ensure a smooth shift to ecofriendly transportation and satisfy the rising demand for it.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Self-Recharging Electric Bicycle
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research paper aims to design and develop a self-recharging electric bicycle which is convenient for the users. The main idea of this project is to enable the bicycle to recharge its own battery by utilizing the its speed and human effort. With that in mind, the goal can be broken down into several objectives. The first objective is to design and develop a dynamo that is able to generate electricity using the bicycle’s front fork. The electricity generated will then be stored in a small portable storage device. The second objective is to integrate a battery unit that is use to power motor. Both the dynamo and battery will act as the main supplementary power sources. This will in turn increase the practicality and convenience of a regular electric bicycle because the users will no longer have to worry about finding a power outlet to recharge the battery.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Agent Based Optimal Scheduling & Congestion Free Routing Scheme to Enhance QoS of NFV Enabled Heterogeneous Wireless Sensor Network Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In wireless sensor network (WSN), congestion is regarded as an unavoidable issue as of today’s scenario at which the data traffic is increased to their aggregated channel capacity. This results in the consequence of buffer overflowing which leads to packets drop thereby reducing packet delivery ratio and degrades network throughput. Also, routing is the most favored approaches for the minimization of nodes energy consumption and the enhancement of Heterogeneous WSNs throughput. Since, the problem of routing has been proved to be an NP-hard, it has been realized that optimization-based technique offers better performance. For solving these issues, this paper proposes a congestion free optimal routing scheme based on Genetic algorithm-based distance aware-Low Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy (GADA-LEACH) protocol to predict intelligent agent path. The major intention of this work is to enhance the efficiency of energy and QoS (throughput and delay) in edge-cloud based IoT environment of data transmission. Initially, the system model is initialized and the graph construction is made for the process of clustering using Spectral graph theory (SGT) at which the cluster head (CH) selection is made. Then, the scheduling process is carried by means of Packet weighted based ensemble optimization scheduling (PW-EOS) scheme. The NFV enabled optimal edge node is selected using Reconfigured Cuckoo Search optimizer (RCSO) after which the intelligent agent moving path in the Heterogeneous Network (HetNet) are predicted by GADA-LEACH technique. From this, an effective routing path is determined among CH and an optimized Edge node. Eventually, the performance assessment is carried in terms of throughput, energy consumption, survival rate, PDR, End-to-End delay and the outcomes conquered are compared with existing methods to attest the proficiency of proposed scheme.

Author Keywords: Packet weighted based ensemble optimization scheduling

articleTitle: Image Processing and Deep Learning Based Road Object Detection System for Safe Transportation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Road object detection, a pivotal task in computer vision and artificial intelligence, is dedicated to the identification and precise localization of a diverse array of elements on roadways, including vehicles, pedestrians, road signs, traffic lights, and potential obstacles. The essence of this task lies in its ability to provide real-time and precise object detection, ultimately serving as a crucial safeguard to prevent accidents and ensure the safety of drivers, passengers, and pedestrians. It also lays the foundation for advanced warning systems and aids in collision avoidance. Several popular models were implemented, encompassing YOLOv7, YOLOv7-Modified, YOLOv7-Tiny, YOLOv7-E6E, Faster R-CNN, and SSD. Among these, YOLOv7 achieved an impressive mean average precision (mAP) of 83.6%, with an inference speed of 15.1 ms, while YOLOv7E6E achieved the highest mAP of 86.2%, but with the cost of a slower inference speed of 30.3 ms. The modified version of YOLOv7 has produced 2.2% higher average precision accuracy (89.1%) than the main version of YOLOv7 due to its double RepVGG layers, skip connection and concatenation layers in the head architecture. To make this research accessible to a wider audience, a user-friendly web application is developed with an intuitive interface.

articleTitle: Hyper Parameter Optimization in Machine Learning For Enhancing Loan Sanction Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The main activity of banks is loan lending. A bank’s earnings are mostly made up of profits. These days, loans are the most important necessity in society. Only a small percentage of the total profits go to banks. It is beneficial for people to buy luxury goods of any kind, such a house or car, and for students to budget for living and learning costs. Individuals are submitting loan applications, and banks are profiting more from lending. Assessing each applicant’s information by hand is more time-consuming and subject to human mistake. To determine if a borrower will be approved for a loan, machine learning techniques and algorithms including Random Forest, Naive Bayes, KNN (KNearest Neighbor), Logistic Regression, SVM (Support Vector Machine), and Logistic Regression are employed. Grid Search is a machine learning technique for hyperparameter optimization that finds the best set of hyperparameters for a model. Grid Search automates hyperparameter modifications, which boosts productivity and lowers personnel costs. The assessment’s goal is to identify the set of hyperparameters that, while accounting for accuracy, yields the highest model performance. In order to find qualified applicants, we consequently create an automated machine learning loan prediction technique. With an accuracy of 98.48%, we discovered that the Random Forest method yielded the best results based on the validation set. This model outperformed other techniques, making it the most reliable for predicting loan eligibility. The implementation of this automated loan prediction system offers substantial benefits for banks and applicants by streamlining the loan approval process, enhancing accuracy, and reducing human error. Consequently, this system significantly improves efficiency and customer satisfaction in the banking sector.

articleTitle: Integrating Real-Time Automation and Big Data Analytics in the Oil and Gas Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The oil and gas industry is arguably one of the most important industries in this modern world because some say it supports civilization as we know it. With the changing dynamics and increased competition, this sector is growing in demand for convenient solutions to improve operations with higher profits. Implementing real-time automation and big data analytics has become vital for the oil and gas industry. Real-time automation refers to using a control system, sensors, and an IT solution to monitor or control operations in real-time. It leads to faster decision-making and efficiency in drilling, production, and distribution processes. At the same time, big data analytics is about storing and analyzing massive amounts of data from different sources—these are sensor data production processes for the oil and gas industry market trends. Big data analytics can intelligently detect patterns & trends with the help of sophisticated algorithms along with machine learning, based on which necessary insights are drawn that lead to better operations and decision-making. Why these technologies will transform the oil and gas sector: Individually, both powerful new technologies provide many benefits, but integrated, they can potentially change the game in this industry. When combined with real-time automation (robots and material handling equipment), it can lead to actionable insights as things are happening, helping the business get control of its operations and reduce cost, ultimately leading to increased profitability.

articleTitle: Text Summarization using Textrank, Lexrank and Bart model
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In natural language processing, text summarization is crucial for applications like information retrieval, content generation, resource optimization, and legal and academic research. It creates a concise version of the original text without omitting crucial information, thereby facilitating the efficient understanding and processing of large data volumes. Researchers are increasingly focusing on developing more effective summarization techniques. This paper reviews existing text summarization methods, including the Textrank algorithm, fuzzy logic, Latent Semantic Analysis, and deep learning techniques. We have implemented Textrank, LexRank, and the BART model on the news summary dataset. For evaluation, we utilized ROUGE1, ROUGE2, and ROUGEL metrics, considering precision, recall, and F-measure.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Robust Multicast Trees for Lossy Wireless Ad-Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper affords a layout and implementation of a sturdy multicast tree technique for loss wireless advert-hoc networks. The proposed technique seeks to provide dependable delivery of statistics in dynamic environments where hyperlinks revel in excessive degrees of packet loss. This method is based on a mixture of spanning tree clustering, hyperlink-country routing, and acknowledgements-primarily based recuperation mechanisms, using re-transmissions and adaptive retransmission periods to catch up on packet loss.
