Our experiments demonstrate that ML-driven computerized network Anomaly Detection can provide accurate and well-timed detection of network anomalies with little supervision and parameter tuning attempts. The outcomes of our experiments display that Random Forests and Support Vector Machines (SVMs) carry out first-rate some of the model’s grid searches, demonstrating aggressive accuracy and precision ratings from an anomaly detection perspective. We also intensely evaluate the consequences and provide insightful discussion on the possibilities and challenges surrounding using ML for automatic community Anomaly Detection.

articleTitle: Unmasking Deception: Leveraging advanced Transformer model for detecting Fake images on the Web
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Significant issues arise from the spread of hate speech and fraudulent data on the internet, especially during times of social and political unrest. To solve these problems, this study suggests a transformer-driven method for identifying bogus data, with an emphasis on how it relates to hate speech. We utilize the Swin Transformer model, which is well-known for its effectiveness in managing vast amounts of image data, to accurately identify and discriminate between authentic and counterfeit information. Our experimental results reveal that our approach is resilient in detecting bogus data, especially when it comes to hate speech, with an accuracy of up to 97.76%. Further evaluation metrics demonstrate our model’s strength: sensitivity at 0.9916, specificity at 0.9615, precision at 0.9672, and an F1 Score of 0.9793. This study makes a substantial advancement in deep learning.

articleTitle: Adapting Optimal Solutions to Travelling Salesman Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A comparative analysis of algorithms for the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) is proposed that evaluates four distinct approaches: Nearest neighbor (NN), 2-opt algorithm, Genetic Algorithm (GA), Simulated Annealing (SA) and a hybrid method of NN and 2-opt to determine its minimum distance achieved with minimum execution time. These algorithms are evaluated by their capability to find the shortest route and the total distance travelled in the given dataset. The evaluation process consists of execution time and route rendering. The results claim that the hybrid approach outsmarts all the other methods in terms of their execution time as it takes as low as 0.308 seconds as compared to other methods on the given dataset. This hybrid approach has the potential to improve the shortest distance in an iterative manner which balances the time versus distance objective criteria in a scalable manner.

articleTitle: Athletic PathFinder: Motion Dynamics and Trajectory Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: It is not outside the scope of this to say that the new paper was a pioneer work that revolutionizes our understanding of the rules of routine production. The new approach put forward by our research manages to quantify ball possession time out of each game for both teams. This helps us understand better how games actually develop. The study employs the latest tool: VAEP (Valuing Actions by Estimating Probabilities) framework, and also maps the field in a 2D plane. With this new method, it becomes feasible to measure quantitatively the actions of all players, thus enabling a purely objective appraisal of each individual’s performance. Analytical powers are further boosted by the study by incorporating a leaderboard that rates players according to their performance indicators. This all-around approach not only makes the game strategies of teams open to view in a whole new way, but also singles out indeed decisive players who have a substantial effect on events. The Pioneer Athletic PathFinder is a breakthrough for sports analytics, providing a powerful means for coaches, players, and analysts to study and improve their game strategies. Four baseline classifiers were trained, achieving the following accuracies: XGBoost (${9 9 \%}$), Random Forest (${9 7 \%}$), Polynomial (${9 2 \%}$), and Bagging (${9 2 \%}$).

articleTitle: An Approach for Multimodal Biometric Authentication using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Multimodal biometric authentication is a robust security mechanism designed to enhance user authentication systems’ reliability and security. It includes two or more biometric traits to design a more reliable and secure identification system. The enhanced accuracy and robust security make multimodal biometric authentication an excellent choice for improving the security and performance of user authentication systems. This paper proposes a multimodal authentication approach fusing fingerprint, ear, and face biometrics. Further, a dynamic weightage is assigned to each of the matching systems, calculated with experimental analysis using a Genetic algorithm. The genetic algorithm has shown excellent results in the proposed approach owing to its ability to work with noisy data and explores the search space to give effective results. The publicly available face data ORL, Yale, IITD Ear data, and custom datasets are utilized. The approach is evaluated on the above datasets and achieved an accuracy of $97 \%$.

articleTitle: Exploring the Versatility of QAOA: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is the notable advancement in quantum computing, which allows us to solve optimization problems differently. In this paper, we provide a detailed investigation of the possible applications of QAOA accompanied by an overview of previous implementations. This is where QAOA shines and can spin out solutions where ordinary methods takes millennia to converge with acceptable results for NP-hard optimization problems that involve transfer of $\mathbf{n}$ qubits between a quantum state. We present a comprehensive literature review in this paper, and potential areas of application where QAOA could be successfully used such as logistics, finance and Artificial Intelligence.

articleTitle: An InDepth Analysis of AI Techniques for Predicting Genetic Disorders
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with predictive methods and a deeper understanding of genetic diseases has the potential to greatly simplify and expedite the diagnosis of rare genetic diseases. Estimates indicate that over 5 million babies are born with genetic diseases annually in India, imposing a significant burden on the economic and social fabric of society. The identification of rare genetic disorders requires advanced genetic testing and specialized expertise due to their intricate nature. In this study, various machine-learning models were employed to analyze datasets related to genetic disorders and their subclasses. The first step in the analysis involved preprocessing the dataset by checking for any missing values. Subsequently, these absent data points were visually depicted within various categories like genetic disorders, subclasses of genetic disorders, samples of symptoms, inherited genes from both parents, birth defects, and others, with the aim of recognizing any discernible patterns or trends. After preprocessing, standardized features were selected and used as input for the machine learning models. The models used in this study included Deep Learning-Powered Advanced Genome Disorder Prediction Model, Random Forest, XG Boost, Baseline Gradient Boosting Classifier, Gradient Boosting with Hyperparameter Tuning and Cross Validation, Ensemble Learning with hyperparameter Tuning and Cross Validation. The predicted classes are compared against the true classes to categorize the outcomes into four groups using confusion matrix. The results of the analysis showed that Deep Learning-Powered Advanced Genome Disorder Prediction Model and XG Boost achieved the highest accuracy of 91% for genetic disorders. However random forest and Gradient Boosting Classifier achieved accuracy of 88% for genetic disorder subclasses.

articleTitle: Cloud Computing in Industry 4.0: Enabling Real-Time Data Processing for Smart Factories
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With Industry 4.0 leading the charge, cloud computing has revolutionized how industries work today. The cloud computing feature added in Industry 4.0 paved the way for real-time data processing that seeped right through intelligent factories and reflected the most significant improvements in efficiency, production, and cost reduction, all playing an important role today. It is a predictive maintenance technology that contributes to the concept of IoT in manufacturing, with proper machine-to-machine and system communication channels for data exchange. Cloud computing provides a scalable and adaptable data storage/analysis environment for large amounts of information to be maintained in predictive maintenance mode with optimization processes based on real-time applications. A data layer standing in between, rendering relevant information when needed to oversee the remote operation of plants can facilitate smart manufacturing over time. The cloud also allows collaboration and visibility at every point in your supply chain, significantly boosting overall SCM to Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Recent Trends in Elliptic Curve Cryptography for Authentication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) is a powerful cryptographic technique that permits the comfortable transmission of personal statistics and the authentication of identities over the net. It is miles becoming increasingly famous as a modern protection era because of its many security benefits, such as shorter key lengths and multiplied resistance to cryptanalysis. Because the elliptic curve algorithms have advanced, more than a few recent traits have emerged. Those solutions are designed to make ECC even greater efficient and more relaxed to be used in authentication systems. Those traits consist of the usage of massive high fields, the software of best regular bases, advanced point representations, the adoption of new curves, and the growing reliance on super singular curves. As a result, ECC is becoming even more at ease and can provide an excellent higher degree of authentication than earlier.

articleTitle: Towards Realistic Image Synthesis An Analysis of GAN-based Method
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Generative antagonistic networks (GANs) are a form of the generative version that is becoming increasingly famous in the field of photograph synthesis. GANs paintings via schooling neural networks, a generator, and a discriminator in an adverse setting. The generator is skilled in generating compelling snapshots that the discriminator has a problem discriminating between actual and fake pictures. In contrast, the discriminator is educated to differentiate between real and faux photos. This paper gives an evaluation of GAN-primarily based methods for practical picture synthesis. A comprehensive overview of GAN-primarily based strategies is supplied, including the principle, structure, programs, and evaluation metrics. Furthermore, challenges that limit the success of GANs are mentioned, consisting of mode crumble, vanishing gradients, and distribution mismatch. In the end, several techniques for improving the performance of GANs are proposed, inclusive of regularization and facts augmentation. Those strategies provide a road for future research into GAN-primarily based techniques for realistic image synthesis.

articleTitle: Investigation on Smart Agriculture Monitoring System Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This article serves as a starting point for conveying and merging information, which is the artifact of IoT data collection network, to describe and perform great smart agriculture tasks. IoT (Internet of Things) is an automation combination technology that helps to process the feedback data from large sensors in a controlled environment. IoT plays an important role in agriculture. The rational way of using IoT can increase efficiency and benefits for farmers. In today’s world, climate change has become one of the major challenging problems. IoT-based smart cultivation of agricultural fields is going to become the inevitable method for farmers. This paper aims to reap the benefits of IoT in the field of agriculture to provide more benefits to small-scale farmers. We implement a smart agriculture system that gathers data in all stages related to cloud plants, weather information from data fusion servers, and analyzes the processing to predict crop growth and determine accuracy for future predictions. To facilitate research and practices in deploying agriculture, we develop our test-based model and consider multiple parameters including humidity, temperature, and soil moisture, as well as security data features of normal and abnormal camera images. To allocate smart agriculture to sustainable land use, we also describe obstacles and difficulties before the sustainable model has come into effect.

articleTitle: Crowd Counting and Analysis using YOLOv7 and Closed Circuit Televisions (CCTVs)
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper introduces a Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) system integrated with the YOLOv7 algorithm for crowd-counting applications. The system leverages the advanced object detection capabilities of YOLOv7 for accurate crowd counting with only 10% error, showing great potential for practical applications such as crowd management, public safety, and event planning. However, the system is not without limitations as it faces challenges in low-light conditions and produces false positive results. Despite that, it still shows capabilities of accurately counting up to 250 people. The research demonstrates the system’s reliability and effectiveness, offering a valuable tool for various applications such as event management and public safety.

articleTitle: Enhancing Energy Efficiency in Wireless Sensor Networks via Adaptive Sparse Bayesian Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this research study, we offer an energy-efficient technique to reduce energy consumption in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). In addition to using the Bayesian model in conjunction with adaptive compressive sensing (A-CS), our methodology presents a novel approach to minimise the number of sensors needed for successful target detection. During the initial stage, a small number of sensors are chosen at random. Depending on our procedure approach, the base station (BS) calls the sensors’ measurements that obtain the highest values in the Error bars. This methodology not only improves resource utilization and enhances overall network performance, but it also increases the energy efficiency of WSNs. Our research results show how successful and efficient this approach is at resolving the energy consumption issue that arises in WSNs where the energy consumed in the proposed approach is substantially lower than that consumed by other approaches especially when there were few targets. Our approach solves the energy consumption issue in WSNs by reducing the number of sensors used and preserving exemplary target detection levels, which will further wireless sensor technology.

articleTitle: Word Based Tic-Tac-Toe Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach in playing Tic Tac Toe by replacing traditional Xs and Os with synonyms sourced from a lexical database, WordNet. Leveraging Reinforcement Learning (RL), our agent learns optimal strategies based on the meanings of these words, enhancing gameplay with language understanding. Through the integration of Natural Language ToolKit (NLTK) to download WordNet, and Gensim for importing Word2Vec model, coupled with Q-learning algorithm, our system dynamically adapts its gameplay to the semantic context of the words occupying the game board. This abstracts the game into a domain where linguistic comprehension influences strategic decision-making, presenting an innovative fusion of language and gaming.

articleTitle: Pattern Recognition in Lung Disease Classification: Leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks that Employs Local Phase Quantization Features
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Lung diseases are wide group of diseases related to the respiratory system, and is ranging from acute infections to chronic disorders with multifactorial causes. Recognition of the lung disease is very crucial in the proper diagnosis, forecasting through prognosis, and remedies. Hence proposed lung disease classification with feature extraction technique. The proposed work carried out feature extraction with Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) and Local Phase Quantization (LPQ) combined with Convolutional Neural Network(CNN). The goal is to create a model that reduces diagnostic errors, ensuring more precise early detection and classification of pulmonary disorders. This initiative facilitates the advancement of pulmonary medicine by promoting accurate radiologic imaging, while future directions emphasize integrating medical workflows to enable personalized and timely diagnosis and treatment. Additionally, the ResNet model demonstrates superior performance in hernia detection, achieving a test accuracy of 89.43% for GLCM based feature extraction and Pneumonia detection with 79.20% test accuracy for LPQ based feature extraction.

articleTitle: IBRF: An Ensemble Model for Power Change Prediction in Electric Bicycles
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: E-bikes, or electric bicycles, are becoming more and more well-liked as a green form of transportation. However, riders may find it distracting to have to exert manual effort to operate the motorized propulsion system, particularly when they have to modify their hand placements. The objective of this study is to resolve this problem by automating the e-bikes power-change procedure. The Hero Lectro electric bicycle, a well-liked e-bike in India, was used in this study to gather cycling data, which were then analyzed to forecast changes in power mode. Data on heart rate and caloric intake were also taken into consideration as analysis inputs. Instance-Based Random Forest (IBRF), a novel ensemble model, was created and evaluated against a number of alternative machine learning strategies, such as instance-based learner-k, random forest, and decision tree. With an accuracy of 98% and F-measures of 0.980, the results showed that the IBRF ensemble model offered the best match to the observed data. These results demonstrate how well the IBRF ensemble model predicts changes in the power mode of e-bikes. Novice riders can experience a smoother and less turbulent ride, improving their overall safety and enjoyment, by having power changes automatically.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cloud Security through a Blend of Symmetric and Asymmetric Cryptography Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the cloud services business, ensuring cloud computing security of key concern. Protecting data a shared cloud environment and offering dependable and secure services necessitate a strong encryption solution with little performance effect. This research presents an efficient cryptographic strategy to improving cloud security while reducing performance effects. Com-plex encryption methods do not lend themselves to the cloud’s emphasis on processing speed. As a consequence, for encryption and key security, this approach combines an upgraded Blow-fish technique with an elliptic curve-based method, resulting in greater security and efficien-cy. For data integrity, a digital signature mechanism is also utilized. The evaluation shows that factors such as throughput, execution time, and memory use have improved.

articleTitle: Enhanced deep learning model using transfer learning to segment and detect brain tumors
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A brain tumor is characterized by an abnormal growth of nerve cells within the brain, which disrupts its normal function. This condition has resulted in the loss of numerous lives. Timely detection and appropriate treatment are imperative to mitigate the impact of this disease. Nevertheless, the process of identifying cells affected by tumors within the brain of human is labour-intensive and a process that consumes significant time. The challenge of accurately and swiftly detecting brain tumors remains significant in the field of image processing. The three primary classifications of brain tumors include pituitary gland tumors, meningiomas, and gliomas. In this study, we present an Enhanced Deep Learning approach designed to diagnose these tumors. Our objective is to facilitate earlystage tumor detection with a high degree of accuracy, thereby aiding physicians in clinical practice. Our proposed model utilizes fine-grained segmentation using the watershed algorithm. By accurately delineating the tumor region, the segmented area can be quantified and used as a crucial feature for stage prediction. Typically, features such as tumor size, shape, and location are extracted from the segmented area, and the proposed system predicts the stage of the tumor. The proposed deep learning model is characterized by its lightweight design, comprising a smaller number of layers compared to previous models, making it highly suitable for real-time applications. The promising results, including a significant increase in accuracy to 98% for multi-class classification, demonstrate the superior performance of our new framework model. This study highlights that our proposed deep learning model outperforms other Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) when attempting to identify tumors in the brain. Furthermore, this study introduces a web application capable of classifying whether a patient has a brain tumor or not based on uploaded MRI images.

articleTitle: Enhancing Home Appliance Service by Improving Appliance Control Unit Diagnostics Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to increase the field service ability of home appliances by integrating advanced diagnostic capabilities into the Appliance Control Unit (ACU). Traditional maintenance practices often face challenges like complexity of appliance system, unable to identify exact root cause, access to components individually and simply identifying and rectifying faults in home appliances, leading to increased prolonged downtime and increased service cost and customer dissatisfaction. To address these issues, this paper proposes the integration of current sensing and voltage sensing circuit within the feedback loop of the ACU, enabling real- time monitoring of electrical parameters during operation. So that it will make it easier for service engineers to identify the correct component of malfunctioning and their data. ACU interprets these sensor circuit data to diagnose various operational irregularities, including motor strain, pump blockages, and voltage fluctuations, short circuit, and open circuit. The data obtained from the current and voltage sensing circuit is fed into the microcontroller. Subsequently, establishing a connection with the service module through the wire port connector, a connection with phone through bluetooth, facilitating seamless communication between devices. The validity of the proposed method was verified by analyzing the simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: LW-ALDDNet: A Novel Lightweight CNN Model for Automated Detection of Apple Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Plant diseases cause substantial losses in crop production, which exerts a major impact on the economic development of agriculture. Early detection of these diseases is inevitable to prevent significant production losses. However, accurate identification is challenging due to similarities in diseases, characteristics. Therefore proper recognition of these diseases has become a challenging task for farmers. But with the help of artificial intelligence and deep learning models in IoT devices, anyone can now take advantage of correctly recognizing diseases of various crops. As the Apple is the most consumed fruit in the world, a novel lightweight CNN model is introduced in this study to accurately identify apple leaf disease from the images of apple tree leaves. Our proposed model is evaluated alongside various popular deep CNN models, including MobileNetV2, InceptionV3, ResNet50v2, AlexNet, SqueezeNet, etc. on two public datasets of five and nine categories of apple leaf diseases with healthy leaves. The evaluation results revealed that our proposed model achieved 91.65%, and 97.53% accuracies on datasets of nine and five classes, respectively, which exceeded the accuracies of six deep CNN models implied on those datasets. Moreover, being a lightweight CNN model, our designed model has the least number of parameters, proving that it can detect apple leaf diseases with better accuracy and with less storage, less computational resources, and shorter detection time requirements.

articleTitle: Fine-tuning Llama-2-7b Model for Conversation Summarization
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this research paper, we explore the optimization for conversation summarization of the Llama 2.7 b model by quantization-aware fine-tuning, specifically exploiting QLORA quantization techniques. In natural language processing (NLP), large language models (LLMs) have become powerful tools for various text-processing tasks including dialogue summarization in a rapidly evolving landscape. Still, the computational needs of these model’s present obstacles to their practical implementation in conversational interfaces and live applications. Quantization observance fine-tuning is an optimistic way of compressing model parameters while still enhancing performance. This analysis demonstrates through rigorous experimentation that the QLORA quantization is effective on fine tuning the Llama 2.7b model for conversation summarization. Fine-tuning the model on a well-rounded dataset with conversational data derived from different sources such as social media, chat logs, and customer interactions makes it more adaptable to any sort of dialog that takes place. The incorporation of QLORA quantization’s also improves the attention mechanism of the model enabling it to obtain relevant information such as generating concise summaries. The latest version of Llama is 2.7. It is called Llama 2.7b and provides several practical advantages for summarizing dialogues such as improved computational efficiency, better user experience in conversational interfaces, and capturing key insights from long conversations. Its outputs are in line with the current research on LLM-based conversation summarization and exhibit the viability of optimization techniques like quantization-aware fine-tuning to maximize the performance of large language models for particular natural language processing tasks (NLP).

articleTitle: Harnessing the Power of CNN and SVM for Robust Cattle Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The study article offers a comprehensive investigation of bovine health status identification powered by a CNN-SVM hybrid technique to elevate diagnostic technical abilities in veterinary medicine. The disease areas are five significant illnesses of the cattle, and the models’ performance is assessed using a comprehensive data set that trains the models for these events. We tried the CNN-SVM system with high precision, recall, and $\mathbf{F 1}$ scores across all disease categories in the testing phase. The prediction model showed % accuracy rates of $\mathbf{9 4. 1 3 \%}$ for class $\mathbf{1, ~} \mathbf{9 5. 4 3 \%}$ for class $2, \mathbf{9 5. 5 1 \%}$ for class $3,96.24 \%$ for class 4, and 96.63% for class 5 in the study. The recall rates were as follows: Class 1-100%, Class 2-98.74%, Class 3-98.74%, Class 4-96.38%, and Class 5-100. The F1Scores were as follows: $\mathbf{2 3. 6 8 \%}$ for the Class $\mathbf{1, 4 3. 3 1 \%}$ for the Class 2, 44.14% for the Class 3, 36.31% for the Class 4, and 38.91% for the Class 5. The achieved model is 95.61% accurate on average for all classes, hence speaking for its high quality and considerable dependability. Measurement of models thereby necessitates calculating such other types of averages, e.g. macro, micro and weighted. The macro average accuracy was 97.66%, the recall was 97.65%, and $F 1$-Score was 97.64%. The weighted average, paying attention to the proportion of samples, provided an accuracy degree of 95.62%, a recall level of 95.61%, and an F1-Score of 95.60%. The micro average that sums all the class’s contributions of 95.61% steadiness is steady in accuracy, recall, and F1-Score. The averages are the Pillars of the R-type model Success in all categories.

articleTitle: Comparing a Novel Multilayer Perceptron’s Performance Analysis with an Extreme Gradient Boosting Algorithm for Financial Fraud Transaction Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Aim: This study is aimed at pinpointing instances of financial fraud through comprehensive computations, ultimately devising a system capable of effectively flagging online fraud and implementing XGBoosting to mitigate its occurrence. The escalating prevalence of fraudulent transactions has evolved into a pressing global concern. In this research, we introduce an innovative approach founded on the Novel Multilayer Perceptron for fraud detection. The implementation and model delineations of rival models are also illustrated, highlighting the substantial superiority of our proposed model. Methods and Materials:The study employed sample files specific to fraudulent transactions for a more accurate assessment of accuracy. Each of the two datasets comprises 130 participants, and the sample size determination utilized a G-power pretest score of 70%, a significance threshold of 0.05%, and a confidence interval of 94%. Result: The sample T-test indicated that there was no statistically significant difference between the performance of the Novel Multilayer Perceptron and the XGBoosting models, with a p-value of 0.000 (p>0.05). This suggests that both models performed similarly. The XGBoosting model demonstrated a slightly higher accuracy of 97.539% compared to the Novel Multilayer Perceptron’s accuracy of $\mathbf{9 7. 1 8 8 \%}$. Therefore, the difference in performance between these two algorithms is not statistically significant. Conclusion: The study’s findings indicate that the Novel Multilayer Perceptron model outperforms in the analysis of fraud transaction detection performance.

articleTitle: Integrating Deep Learning and Data Science: Challenges, Opportunities and Implications

articleTitle: A Support Vector Machine-Based Power Control Scheme for Maximizing Aggregate Capacity in D2D Communication with Limited Channel Information
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A D2D pair comprises two D2D users (DUEs), encompassing a sender and a receiver. To optimize spectral efficiency, our underlying assumption posits that D2D pairs use a singular communication channel. The efficient management of power becomes indispensable for minimizing interference between D2D pairs while maximizing the network’s capacity. In scenarios where the information is solely about typical cellular channel gains between base stations and DUEs, and channel gains amongst DUEs remain entirely obscured, there is a challenge of D2D power regulation. For each distinct D2D pair, a support vector machine (SVM) is employed to improve transmission power levels. From the results, it is shown that the traditional power level capacity is $230 \mathrm{bps} / \mathrm{Hz}$, while the output of the proposed model is close to $340 \mathrm{bps} / \mathrm{Hz}$. The proposed method harnesses the cellular channel gains existing between D2D users and proximate base stations to compute the transmission power for each D2D pair. The distinguishing feature of this work is that it relies solely on the readily available knowledge of cellular channel gains, which are routinely reported for various conventional communication and handover processes.

articleTitle: Enhancing CNN Performance Across Diverse Domains: Exploring the Efficacy of Domain Adversarial Neural Network with the Use of CNN for Improved Generalization in Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are foundational tools for image classification in deep learning, with models like InceptionNet, ResNet, MobileNet, and DenseNet excelling in feature extraction and validation. However, their performance can suffer in domains with high variability. Domain Adversarial Neural Networks (DANN) address this issue by reducing domain shift through finding domain-invariant representations. DANNs, by training adversaries, enable CNNs to generalize better across different environments, thus enhancing overall performance. This study explores the efficacy of DANN in boosting CNN performance across varied environments. Initially, we detail each base model, focusing on their architecture and feature extraction capabilities. We then introduce DANN as a domain optimization method, showcasing its ability to learn domain-invariant representations. Extensive testing and comparative analysis reveal that integrating DANN with CNN models significantly outperforms using CNNs alone. The findings confirm DANN’s improved generalizability, effectiveness in mitigating domain shift, and potential for advancing deep learning-based image classification tasks.

articleTitle: Triple Stack Deep Variational Autoencoder For Improved Hand Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for hand gesture recognition using a triple-stack deep variational autoencoder. By employing a VAE framework, we facilitate both efficient representation learning and the generation of meaningful latent spaces for gesture recognition and classification. This is an extension of the traditional VAE architecture that incorporates three layers of encoding and decoding with a spatial deep neural network. In a regular VAE, there is typically only one layer for both the encoder and decoder. By stacking three layers in both the encoder and decoder, a triple-stack deep VAE can learn more complex hierarchical representations of the input data. Each layer in the encoder extracts increasingly abstract features from the input, while each layer in the decoder reconstructs the input from these abstract representations. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score on six benchmark datasets: ASL Static, Massey University Dataset (MUGD), ASL Digit, NUS-2, Bengali Sign Language (BSL), and Hagrid-14 (HG-14) datasets. The results of the experiment show that the proposed 3S-DVE achieves an accuracy of ${7 6 \%}$ (MUGD Set 1), ${8 0 \%}$ (MUGD Set 2), ${9 7 \%}$ (MUGD Set 3), 96% (MUGD Set 4), 86% (MUGD Set 5), ${9 7 \%}$ (ASL Digit), ${6 2 \%}$ (ASL Static), ${7 4 \%}$ (NUS-II Dataset), ${6 6 \%}$ (BSL), 76% (MUGD Set 1), 80% (MUGD Set 2), 97% (MUGD Set 3), 96% (MUGD Set 4), 86% (MUGD Set 5), 97% (ASL Digit), 62% (ASL Static), ${7 4 \%}$ (NUS-II Dataset), ${6 6 \%}$ (BSL), and 79% (HG-14), respectively, which is better compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Exploring Machine Learning Algorithms for Job Recommendation: A Focus on Career Development
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The education system plays a pivotal role in shaping individuals’ careers. In addressing the challenge of recommending suitable jobs for students who are nearing the graduation, our research focuses on developing a job recommendation system leveraging machine learning (ML) algorithms. This study assesses the effectiveness of ML algorithms in categorizing jobs into sectors such as “IT Sector”, “Teaching Sector”, “Bank Sector” and “Business Sector”. Various parameters, including SSLC marks, PUC marks, communication skills, aptitude, and proficiency in subjects like networks, DBMS, data structures, operating systems, and programming skills, are considered. By conducting correlation analysis and employing dimensionality reduction techniques, we identify the most relevant attributes for job prediction. Three ML algorithms—Cat (categorical) Boost, Ada Boost (adaptive Boost), and XG (extra gradient) Boost—are compared for their predictive performance. A 70-30 training-testing model was employed to evaluate the performance of each model. Evaluation metrics such as accuracy, F1-score, precision, and recall were used to determine the best-performing model. Cross-validation techniques are applied to detect underfitting or overfitting. Among the three ML algorithms examined, Cat Boost emerges as the most effective, achieving a 94.7% accuracy rate in predicting job sectors. Consequently, Cat Boost is selected to build the predictive model.

articleTitle: An Optimized Intrusion Detection Model Using ML and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the maintenance of network security, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are very crucial in identifying unauthorized access and malicious activities. This research assesses how well different machine learning algorithms enhance IDS functionality, highlighting model interpretability through explainable AI techniques. Eight machine learning algorithms were assessed using a dataset from Kaggle that reflects a military network environment with 41 features and 22,544 records. Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) was used to analyze the top five models for their decision-making procedures. In several metrics, Random Forest algorithm appeared as the best performing among them all. LIME application provided useful insights into the main features that impact on the predictions being made by the model. The outcomes demonstrate the effectiveness of Random Forest for IDS and indicate how vital explainable AI methods such as LIME are in ensuring that IDS deployment can achieve transparency and reliability concerning its predictions for this model’s purpose.

articleTitle: Comprehensive ECG Signal Analysis for Heart Disease Classification: Integrating Neural Networks with Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The heart’s function in circulating blood to our organs is vital, making the early detection of heart disease imperative to prevent severe health outcomes. Electrocardio-graphy (ECG) is a primary diagnostic tool for identifying heart conditions. This study leverages the PTB-XL database to explore the integration of Ensemble Learning and Deep Learning techniques for automated ECG signal analysis. We implement a hybrid model that combines Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layers to effectively capture the temporal dynamics and complex patterns in ECG signals. To further enhance the robustness and generalizability of our model, we integrate Random Forest (RF) ensemble classifiers. Our comprehensive evaluation of the PTB-XL dataset indicates that this integrated approach successfully distinguishes between heart disease and normal signals, surpassing the performance of existing single-model methods. Additionally, we conduct extensive comparative analysis to ensure the reliability and validity of our findings. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of our method for ECG signal classification, offering significant potential for clinical application in improving the early detection and diagnosis of heart diseases. This research highlights the promising role of hybrid ensemble learning and deep learning models in medical diagnostics, paving the way for more accurate and automated cardiovascular disease screening.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Node with Concurrent Transmission in WSN
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: : Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) play a crucial role in enabling various applications ranging from environmental monitoring to smart infrastructure. One of the key challenges faced in WSNs is the limited energy resources of individual sensor nodes. To address this challenge, the design of energy-efficient nodes has become a focal point of research. This research paper focuses on exploring the design of energy-efficient nodes with concurrent transmission capabilities in WSNs. The first section delves into the key components of an energy-efficient node, optimization strategies for minimal energy consumption, and the trade-offs involved in designing such nodes. Concurrent transmission, another critical aspect of WSNs, is then examined in detail, highlighting its potential to improve network performance and the challenges associated with its implementation. Subsequently, existing energy efficiency techniques in WSNs are reviewed, along with their application to enhance overall network performance and the limitations they face. Node synchronization is also discussed, emphasizing its importance, synchronization methods, and its impact on energy consumption in WSNs. Lastly, the paper investigates the performance evaluation of energy efficient nodes with concurrent transmission, focusing on evaluation methodologies, performance metrics, and key findings from the study. By addressing these aspects comprehensively, this research paper aims to contribute to the advancement of energy-efficient node design and concurrent transmission techniques in WSNs, ultimately enhancing the overall efficiency and performance of wireless sensor networks.

articleTitle: Addressing Security and Privacy Concerns in Cloud-Based Deep Learning Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The proliferation of contemporary, deep, modern-day technology has brought about its increasing adoption in various industries, from healthcare to finance. With the developing quantity of information to be processed, many corporations have turned to cloud computing to handle the computational and storage needs of the present day deep today. However, this has raised issues about the safety and privacy of cutting-edge sensitive facts saved and processed inside the cloud. One of the most important security worries in cloud-based deep modern-day systems is the vulnerability to cyber assaults and fact breaches. As those structures trendy involve the sharing of ultra-modern assets and information, there may be an increased chance of modern-day unauthorized get entry to or manipulation of present-day facts. Additionally, the use of $1 / 3$-party cloud offerings might also introduce new protection dangers. Protecting the privacy of brand-new touchy records, including private or clinical information, is a crucial challenge in cloud-primarily based deep latest systems. The risk of today’s unauthorized access to these statistics can lead to excessive effects for individuals and businesses, such as loss of trust and felony ramifications.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation for Image Understanding
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Semantic segmentation is a way of photo knowhow that entails labeling the objects in a picture on the pixel degree and assigning every pixel within the photograph a category label. This method is utilized in PC imaginative and prescient programs to construct a representation of a scene from digital photographs. It may be used to correctly phase discrete items consisting of vehicles, pedestrians, and timber, as well as more summary standards, which include shadows and reflections. On the way to achieve success, semantic segmentation algorithms require a large amount of designated labeling and accurate pixel-degree statistical analysis. Latest advances in deep mastering strategies have allowed for the improvement of more sophisticated algorithms that could achieve incredible effects on hard-picture segmentation datasets. Those strategies have progressed the accuracy and efficiency of the photograph know-how algorithms, allowing them to carry out duties that include scene understanding, item identification, scene type, and pixel-stage segmentation.

articleTitle: Secure Access Control Schemes for Cloud-Based Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This abstract provides a state-of-the-art review of secure access control schemes for cloud networks. The rise of cloud computing and the security of the cloud have increased the need for robust access control for securing data and resources. In this paper, role-based, attribute-based, multi-factor authentication access control methods and their strengths and weaknesses are addressed. It goes further to tackle some of the challenges of using these schemes in a cloud environment and offers solutions for the same. Following that, it will focus on what the research means for future directions in this field, in terms of the security of cloud networks & beyond.

articleTitle: Comprehensive investigation on Deep learning models: Applications, Advantages, and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have been completely transformed by deep learning (DL), which provides unmatched power in handling massive, unstructured information from a variety of fields. CNNs, neural networks with recurrent connections (RNNs), generative models, (DRL), and deep learning via transfer are the main deep learning models that are covered in detail in this article. The structure, uses, advantages, and drawbacks of each model are thoroughly investigated. In this work, we use the Fruit-360 dataset, a benchmark picture classification dataset, for an empirical investigation. Six well-known deep learning architectures are compared and evaluated: Bidirectional LSTM, CNN, Simple RNN, (LSTM), (GRU), and Bidirectional GRU. Analysis is done on performance parameters including accuracy, precision, recall, and computing efficiency to have a better understanding of how well they work on various tasks. The purpose of this survey is to give scholars, professionals, and enthusiasts a thorough grasp of the various uses and capacities of deep learning models. The study provides insights that help progress the discipline and direct the selection of suitable models for certain real-world problems.

articleTitle: Vehicular Network Security: Threats, Vulnerabilities and Countermeasures
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Vehicular community protection (VNS) covers a diffusion of security measures to ensure the secure, cozy, and dependable operation of motors on the street. VNS is an essential software of the Internet of Things, and its safety features are critical in the prevention of injuries, intrusion, and malicious interference. Most of the prevailing VNS solutions depend on verbal exchange protocols, consisting of 802.11p and DSRC, with the purpose of shielding the integrity, privacy, and protection of the records transmitted in the network. However, there needs to be more comprehensive studies on the threats, vulnerabilities, and countermeasures associated with VNS. The primary threats to VNS encompass guy-in-the-middle assaults, spoofing, and denial-of-provider assaults. These attacks take advantage of vulnerabilities in the protection mechanisms that defend vehicular network verbal exchange and may lead to privacy breaches, lack of statistics, or maybe hijacking of the car. Capacity vulnerabilities include insufficient encryption and authentication of the information transmitted inside the vehicular community, lax authentication processes, vulnerable memory control, and inadequate access control. Furthermore, the multiplied connectivity of cars to the internet and the global Wi-Fi will increase the hazard from malware and other malicious code.

articleTitle: Dynamic Spectrum Access in Cognitive Radio Networks: A Game-Theoretic Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cognitive radio networks (CRNs) are a promising technology which could offer better spectrum efficiency and utilization via permitting dynamic spectrum get right of entry to (DSA). Game idea has been an increasing number of hired as a tool for analyzing and addressing optimization problems in CRNs. This abstract discusses the utility of sport theory to the evaluation and optimization of DSA in CRNs. the main consciousness is to broaden a widespread recreation-theoretic approach for DSA that can model numerous styles of interactions among cognitive customers. Specifically, we speak 8 exceptional styles of games that may be used to model the DSA problem, including static, dynamic, and multi-attribute games. Using game principle for DSA in CRNs can assist to enhance the performance of CRNs in terms of throughput, fairness, energy efficiency, and security.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning based Model for Prediction of Lung’s Infection using X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Lung’s infection is a crucial clinical challenge, caused due to germs and virus. Recently, COVID caused havoc across the globe. The deep infection may cause pneumonia, leading to hospitalization. Therefore, prediction is an essential process to mitigate this. In the diagnosis process, visualization of chest X-ray (CXR) images takes an important place. Learning based techniques are widely reported for diagnosing the medical images. In this work, a transfer learning (TL) based model is proposed for the prediction of Lung’s infection. The proposed method is implemented in four steps. In the first step, data collection and pre-training is performed. In the second step, a pre-processing stage is introduced, which involves the augmentation, enhancement, and normalization of CXR images. The feature extraction is accomplished using TL mechanism in the third step. Finally, the classification is performed using an improved ResNet50 model. The TL approach of feature extraction is intended to deal with the overfitting problem of a limited sample dataset and improvising the training process. The suggested model is examined using two widely recognized benchmark datasets. The findings demonstrate the superiority of the suggested approach over cutting-edge methods.

articleTitle: An ECC-Isogeny Cipher Shield for Navy Inverter Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the realm of naval operations, the imperative to secure inverter systems underscores the gravity of this research. The ECC-Isogeny Cipher Shield, a novel integration of Elliptic Curve Cryptography and Isogeny, is introduced as a paramount solution for elevating security standards in maritime environments. Our comprehensive study meticulously analyzes naval inverter systems, identifying and addressing potential vulnerabilities. The ECC-Isogeny Cipher Shield emerges as a stalwart guardian, fortifying data integrity and significantly enhancing overall security protocols. This innovative shield, uniquely crafted for the intricacies of naval operations, promises unprecedented resilience. Its adaptive nature positions it as a formidable defense against the evolving landscape of cyber threats at sea, blending mathematical elegance with cryptographic strength. In delivering a distinctive perspective on naval security, this research provides a tangible and innovative solution intricately aligned with the complexities of inverter systems. The ECCIsogeny Cipher Shield stands as an emblem of cryptographic excellence, safeguarding the integrity and confidentiality of pivotal maritime data. With an unwavering commitment to originality, this research ensures a plagiarism-free contribution to the ongoing discourse on enhancing naval cybersecurity.

articleTitle: FTASD - A Fine Tuning Approach for Stable Diffusion Models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Image generation is one of the critical tasks performed in today’s world for the expansion of research domains like computer vision and Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI). Therefore, there is an ultimate need for 2-D image synthesis models, which are already introduced by the researchers in the form of stable diffusion models. Recently, various companies like OpenAI and Google AI introduced such models in the computer vision industry. The fundamental approach is to generate target images through a diffusion process. The various applications of stable diffusion include text-to-image generation, image restoration, image-to-image generation, video generation, and facial restoration. In recent years, multiple development plans have been incorporated for improving the image generation models. The improvements have been done in the form of improving the loss function, architecture designs and optimization method. In this paper, we propose a fine-tuning method for improving the performance of various image generation models using Stable Diffusion (SD). Our major focus is on various stable diffusion models which involve text (prompt) to image generation methodology for generating various synthetic images. In our fine tuning process, we leveraged the KerasCV and trained the pre-trained Stable Diffusion Model on a diversified POKEMON (BLIP caption generated) dataset fetched from the Hugging Face database. Our model outperformed the existing KerasCV stable diffusion model which is responsible for text to image generation. We also fine-tuned the model using our self collected Keji National Forest dataset and it produced outstanding application specific results.

articleTitle: Fake Currency Detection Using Convolutional Neural Network and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The increased use of modern printing and scanning technologies has led to a significant rise in counterfeit currency production, posing a serious threat to global economies. To tackle this growing issue, our project, titled “Fake currency detection using Convolutional Neural Networks and Image Processing,” introduces an innovative solution that utilizes artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning for efficient counterfeit detection. Financial institutions, banks, and businesses are facing heightened vulnerability to counterfeit currency, resulting in considerable financial losses and a decrease in the value of genuine money. Current currency detection systems often rely on time-consuming traditional methods and manual inspection, which are prone to human error. Even the counterfeit detection machines in use have limitations when it comes to identifying sophisticated counterfeit notes. Our project addresses these challenges by proposing an advanced system that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and image processing techniques. Given the advancements in printing and scanning technologies, counterfeiting has evolved into a more sophisticated and widespread problem. Traditional currency detection methods, rooted in hardware and image processing, have proven to be inefficient and time-consuming. Hence, there is a critical need for a more robust and rapid solution to detect counterfeit currency. Our proposed approach employs a transfer-learned CNN, a deep learning model trained on a dataset comprising real and fake currency images. The CNN learns the intricate features of both genuine and counterfeit banknotes, allowing it to accurately identify fake currency in real-time. The transfer learning process enables the CNN to leverage knowledge gained from a diverse dataset, improving its ability to recognize subtle patterns associated with counterfeit notes. The primary components of our project include a diverse dataset with images of real and fake currency notes. This dataset is divided into training, validation, and test sets, totaling 575 images and covering various denominations and currencies. The CNN architecture is crafted to extract relevant features from these images, facilitating precise classification. Implemented as a web-based application for enhanced accessibility, our system allows users to upload images of banknotes through a user-friendly interface. The underlying AI model processes and analyzes these images, providing real-time feedback to indicate whether the currency note is genuine or fake. This user-friendly approach ensures easy integration into existing processes in financial institutions and businesses. Our project tackles the urgent issue of counterfeit currency detection through the integration of advanced AI and machine learning techniques. By combining CNNs and image processing, we aim to offer financial institutions and businesses a reliable and efficient tool to combat the growing threat of fake-currency, contributing to the protection of economies and financial systems.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability Assessment in Smart Electric Grid Under False Data Injection Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The energy sector of today is becoming more and more digital and this brought new security challenges for the modern smart grid infrastructure. Integration of cyber space (information sensing, processing, and control) with physical space (traditional power sector) termed as cyber physical system. Energy transfer and utilization become more efficient due to rapid digitalization. A novel kind of cyber attack known as False Data Injection (FDI) attack can manipulate measurement data available across communication channel to target the power system state estimation. In the smart grid FDI is an usual data integrity attack. The proposed assessment takes into consideration how FDI intrusion alters the system voltage stability and the real power injection. DC state estimation has been utilized to generate FDI attack vector and Voltage Sensitivity Equation (VSE) is used to detect voltage change whereas system voltage stability is assessed using L index parameter. The proposed mechanism has been implemented using the MATLAB tool on standard IEEE test systems, including the IEEE 9-Bus, IEEE 14-Bus, IEEE 30Bus, and IEEE 118-Bus systems.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Feamework for Modeling and Analyzing Complex Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Complex networks, characterised by intricate structures arising from the relationships and interactions among their constituent elements, play a pivotal role in various domains such as social networks, biological systems, and technological infrastructures. The evolution and dynamics of complex networks are analysed for various applications such as link prediction, information diffusion, and recommendation systems. Recent research has focused on the study of structural motifs and the probabilistic analysis of motifs to capture the dynamics of the network. The motifs, considered building blocks of the larger network structure, are recurrent patterns in the network. This study focuses on the different probabilistic models built on triads, which are sets of three interconnected nodes. We investigate six different probability distributions, including Poisson, Gamma, Exponential, Power Law, Gaussian, Lorentzian, and Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) that can be applied in the complex network to capture the insight of the connectivity pattern. The applications of this research extend to refining network models, improving simulations, and enhancing our understanding of the likelihood of observing distinct patterns within complex social networks.

articleTitle: The performance analysis of image resolution model using deep residual algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Deep residual algorithms succeeded wildly in different computer vision problems (e.g., Image Super resolution). Deep neuraenablersraredesign and residual learning are great enablers that define how these architectures overcome limitations in traditional image resolution models. This article implements a deep residual algorithm representing the image resolution model performance research. This paper aims to synthesize HR images from their low-resolution (LR) counterparts by training the proposed model using large-scale image pairs across different resolutions. The model is tested using multiple evaluation criteria and compared with classical resolution models. Experimental results show that the deep residual model performs better in peak signal-to-noise ratio(PSNR), structural similarity index(SSIM), and visual quality metrics. It examines the influence of various network architectures, training strategies, and datasets on how well this algorithm can recognize dialog acts. Experiments demonstrate the superiority of the proposed model with a deep residual algorithm in terms of improving Resolution compared to traditional models.

articleTitle: Improved GAN for Efficient Cyber Forensics
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The society is now deeply connected with digital exchanges running on cyber-physical systems for their daily operations. This gives rise to cyber crime and creates a need for cyber forensics. This paper presents an innovative approach based on improved Generative Adversarial Networks(GAN) for efficient cyber forensics. The proposed system uses the existing GAN networks of SRGAN and DCGAN to generate high quality images from low quality images. We experiment with different activation functions, number of layers, nodes and network architectures to improve the accuracy achieved in super resolution of images. The system has been tested for use in cyber forensics to super resolve the images of accused in a video frame and for better detection of car number plate images taken from cameras on traffic lights and CCTV cameras. The experimental results show that our proposed system outperforms existing GAN networks in terms of PSNR value by ~2.24% and the SSIM method by ~3.59%.

articleTitle: Techno–economic Evaluation Optimization Framework for Grid independent IRESs with Biogas and Wind power systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Economic Load Dispatch (ELD) is the primary problem of operating grid-connected or island micro-grids. ELD focuses on reducing the fuel expenses associated with traditional generators. To meet the load demand, adhere to generator constraints, and minimize fuel costs, ELD distributes the output power of the operating generating sources. Therefore, a variety of optimization techniques are applied to difficult and convex ELD issues. These techniques, although simple, converge to the solution very slowly. The development of novel power management techniques is essential for making micro-grids a desirable replacement for traditional power systems. The main objective of utility operators is to lower the price of generating power and the amount of pollutants released into the atmosphere. Creating a new hybrid optimization technique for the ELD solution in a micro-grid with thermal and wind power units is the primary objective of the suggested technique. The objectives of this study are also taken into consideration, including the cost function of fitness, the overall cost of biomass units, and the wind power generation cost. The hybrid optimization model known as Particle Oriented Cat Swarm Optimization (POCSO) maximizes the power production of thermal power plants by combining the concepts of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Cat Swarm Optimization (CSO) within the maximal and minimal limits. The optimal selection of turbines and biogas quantity is made using the hybrid optimization model. In terms of cost function, the suggested method’s performance is compared with the traditional approaches.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Effect of Spatial Correlation on Performance of Multi-User Multiple Access Techniques

articleTitle: Ambient Intelligent System for Appointment Management
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In today’s fast-paced world, efficient management of appointments is crucial for both service providers and consumers. Efficient appointment management is essential in the modern service industry to enhance both operational efficacy and client satisfaction. This project report presents the development of an Ambient Intelligent System (AIS) for Appointment Management designed to optimize the handling of appointments in dynamic environments. Utilizing Bluetooth technology, the AIS efficiently manages both scheduled and ad-hoc appointments by detecting user presence via ESP32 micro-controllers. This system dynamically adapts to changing conditions, prioritizing appointments based on real-time data to minimize wait times and enhance user experience. The comprehensive architecture includes mobile applications for users and administrative staff, backend services, and a robust database system to ensure real-time synchronization and responsiveness. This study evaluates the AIS’s performance in streamlining appointment processes, demonstrating significant improvements over traditional methods in both efficiency and user satisfaction.

articleTitle: Exploring the Relationship between Artificial Intelligence and Data Science
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This technical abstract search for a court between synthetic Intelligence (AI) and statistics technology (DS). We analyze and survey the regions wherein the two fields overlap. We also look into the ethical implications of such technologies and how AI can help enhance DS studies. Subsequently, we speak of viable software situations in a selection of domain names.

articleTitle: Detection of Pneumonia in Chest X-ray using Deep Learning Enabled Adaptive and Altruistic PSO-based Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Children die from pneumonia in many underprivileged areas around the world. The diagnosis of pneumonia in developing countries is still a difficult task, even with simple instruments available and medications available to treat it. Pneumonia can be identified in these nations using computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) technologies. We apply the ideas of deep learning and meta-heuristic algorithms to our pneumonia detection CAD system. In the first stage, we extracted the deep features by using the ResNet models. We performed feature extraction using various ResNet modelsResNet50, ResNet101, and ResNet152-to identify which model is better at extracting the features, and it can then be fine-tuned based on a target pneumonia dataset. After performing the feature selection procedure by particle swarm optimization, we modify the parameter using involvement of memory in adaptation and enrich it by developing agents that exhibit altruistic behavior We also consider adaptive and altruistic particle swarm optimization (AAPSO) for efficient feature selection and remove the non-informative features extracted by the ResNet model to improve the ability to detect pneumonia. In addition to ResNet models for feature extraction and AAPSO for feature selection, we applied the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm for classification, as SVM is widely used for better classification and regression purposes.

articleTitle: A Model Employing Interpretable Deep Learning Techniques to Forecast Dental Caries Through the Analysis of Panoramic Radiograph Images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Dental caries represents a common dental health condition that significantly impairs people’s quality of life by causing excruciating pain and infections. Despite concerns about the interpretability of machine learning models for dental caries detection, we propose an accessible deep learning model to facilitate early diagnosis. This approach aims to address the concerns of medical professionals by offering a clear and understandable solution. We assessed the suitability of three widely known models, namely ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, and EfficientNet-B0, to identify the best-performing model for caries detection. These algorithms use panoramic images as input and produce a binary classification of caries or non-caries along with a heat map that highlights the tooth’s regions of interest. To assess model performance, we conducted a performance evaluation using panoramic images. Remarkably, all three models performed comparably well. ResNet-50, however, fared somewhat better than DenseNet-121 and EfficientNet-B0, with an F1-score of 91.61%, sensitivity of 87.33%, and accuracy of 92.00%. The precise site of caries was established by visual evaluation of the heat maps produced by ResNet-50. When diagnosing dental cavities, our suggested understandable deep learning model showed remarkable accuracy and dependability. It leverages heat maps to highlight specific regions of the teeth, enabling an intuitive interpretation of the model’s output. This feature can help medical professionals confirm the classification results and lower misclassification errors by mitigating the interpretability problems that many machine learning models have.

articleTitle: Explainable AI in NLP: Interpretable Models for Transparent Decision Making
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the realm of Natural Language Processing NLP, the (XAI) initiative aims to build interpretable models that provide light on decision-making procedures. A challenge in this field is the development of models that not only perform admirably but also explain their reasoning behind certain forecasts or assessments. The problem arises from the fact that top-notch models are required. s for this kind of study often include topics like feature visualisation, attention processes, and model-agnostic techniques like LIME. Many believe that these approaches will make NLP models easier to understand and work with. Users may have trust in and understanding of the outcomes thanks to XAI in natural language processing, which explains how these models function. This facilitates the incorporation of these models into real-world applications that prioritise openness and interpretability, while also promoting accountability. The study compares the accuracy and error rates of traditional and proposed treatments. The proposed model reduces processing time and time taken for training, while the previous approach was prolonged by unfiltered data. The study also compares the time taken for the proposed approach and the time taken for the conventional approach. The results show that the proposed approach is more efficient and time-efficient than traditional treatments, resulting in better results.

articleTitle: Weather Forecasting Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Weather forecasting has become increasingly difficult due to the increasing consequences of climate change. Many industries depend on accurate weather forecasts. Accurate forecasts for the near future are quite valuable. The unpredictable nature of climate change often makes adhering to traditional protocols difficult. To increase the accuracy of weather forecasts, this paper designs a technique to predict the weather using machine learning. The technique uses Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, a kind of artificial neural network. The goal of the model was to predict both favourable and adverse weather. The technique uses various meteorological parameters, such as temperature, pressure, humidity, wind speed, and precipitation. The performance of the model is evaluated using a range of metrics and visualizations from the training and validation sets. This technique achieved greater results in Huber loss, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency. The results indicate that proposed LSTM-based neural networks outperforms state-of-the-art forecasting systems like Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) in terms of accuracy, MAE and MSE in predicting weather.

articleTitle: Residual VGGNet for Unveiling Optimal Process Parameters of Oil Rig Welding Through Mathematical Modeling and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The optimization of welding techniques for oil rig components is crucial to upholding the structural integrity and safety of offshore drilling activities. In this study, we utilize a residual VGGNet architecture, which is a modified version of the well-known VGGNet, for the purpose of extracting crucial information from images of welding processes. The methodology employed in this study involves the collection of a complete dataset comprising welding process images obtained from diverse oil rig welding activities. The provided images are accompanied by annotations that provide the associated welding parameters, including current, voltage, and welding speed. The residual VGGNet is subsequently trained to acquire knowledge about the complex associations between picture features and welding parameters. In order to develop a reliable mathematical model, regression techniques are utilized to precisely establish the relationship between the extracted features and welding parameters. The performance of the model is evaluated using cross-validation and compared to traditional regression models to emphasize its greater ability to capture intricate patterns within the data.

articleTitle: Hybrid Optimized A* Algorithm for Dynamic Rerouting in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research presents a new approach to adaptive control in autonomous vehicles by optimizing the Hybrid A star algorithm. This algorithm is designed to ensure reliable and efficient operation in complex environments. Leveraging the hybrid A star algorithm, this plan will improve the ability of autonomous vehicles to navigate difficult situations such as crowded cities or residential areas. Optimization of algorithms enables vehicles to plan routes quickly and accurately, increasing travel time and overall transportation efficiency. Additionally, the method further increases reliability by integrating real-time information to update the change process. Numerous simulations prove the superior performance of this algorithm compared to traditional routing technology. Autonomous vehicles, Dynamic routing, Blockchain, Hybrid A star algorithm, Data verification.

articleTitle: A High-Performance FPGA Based on Convolutional Neural Network for QRS Complex Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Mortality rates from cardiovascular issues have risen, especially among younger people. ECG signals, particularly the QRS complex, are vital for monitoring heart activity and detecting arrhythmias. A high-performance, low-power system is essential for diagnosing heart diseases. We present a hardware accelerator using a deep neural network to detect QRS complexes, enhancing energy efficiency. Our algorithm adjusts the number of parallel multipliers, reducing latency without extra hardware. We also developed a new method for the softmax layer that maintains accuracy with less hardware. Our design achieves a sensitivity (Se) of 0.99797 and a positive predictive value (+P) of 0.99936, comparable to the state-of-the-art on the MIT-BIH database. It operates at a maximum frequency of 320 MHz, consuming only 0.11 W, and reduces latency by 50% compared to conventional pipelines. Additionally, it outperforms CPU and GPU solutions in speed.

articleTitle: Comparative study of Machine Learning Approaches for Loan Approval Prediction in financial sector
