publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The surge in loan demand in India highlights the necessity for banks to refine their assessment methodologies to ensure accurate evaluation of applicants’ creditworthiness. As financial institutions address this demand, leveraging data analytics presents an opportunity to enhance loan approval processes. This paper aims to address this need by exploring various data analysis techniques tailored to comprehensively assess applicant backgrounds and contextual factors. To optimize loan approval processes, a comparative analysis of five prominent machine learning models - Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, K Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Random Forest Classifier, and Gaussian Naive Bayes is conducted. Through a detailed examination of the models’ performance, the study seeks to determine the most efficient method for accurately predicting loan approval outcomes. The findings unveil the exceptional performance of both Decision Tree and Random Forest models, with an impressive accuracy rate of 100%. Integrating these models into current bank loan approval systems can lead to significant improvements in efficiency and reliability. Specifically, these models can make the decision-making process more efficient, reduce human errors, and speed up loan processing. These enhancements benefit both financial institutions and applicants by improving the accuracy of loan approvals, increasing customer satisfaction, and ensuring more efficient and reliable lending decisions.

articleTitle: Homomorphic Secret Sharing for IoT: An Empirical Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Homomorphic secret sharing (HSS) is a cryptographic technique that combines the principles of secret sharing and homomorphic encryption (HE). It offers a powerful way to securely distribute sensitive data among multiple parties while enabling computations to be performed on the shared data without revealing the individual inputs. The process of HSS entails significant computational load. Due to the inherent involvement of complex computations, characterized by extensive random number exponentiation for each member’s input share, considerable energy and resources are imperative. This work explores the realm of HSS, a novel cryptographic paradigm that leverages Internet of Things (IoT) devices to incorporate the strengths of HE and the concepts of secret sharing. HSS employs a constellation of servers to execute computations on secret input shares. In this paper, we embark on a comprehensive exploration of HSS, wielding experimental methodologies to validate its practicality and potential. Our study delves into critical aspects such as power consumption, memory utilization, and overall execution time. We observe around $70 \%$ increase in the power consumption rate when the HSS procedure is implemented on IoT devices. The memory utilization is observed to be consistent over an average of 15 MB, while execution time averages around 0.13 seconds. By conducting thorough experimentation, we discover insights into the complex relationship between cryptographic security and computational efficiency. This sheds light on the potential benefits of HSS, revealing a promising landscape for further exploration.

articleTitle: Weather and Emission Data Analysis and Prediction using Machine Learning on a Big Data Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Weather data analysis examines large volumes of weather-related information to derive meaningful insights and patterns. It involves collecting, processing, and analyzing various meteorological data, to gain a deeper understanding of weather patterns, trends, and anomalies. This study integrates temperature data with emissions records to explore the impacts of human activities on climate trends in India. Hadoop MapReduce and Pig Latin were used for preprocessing, while machine learning models including linear regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, and ARIMA, forecasted temperature changes and identified significant climate drivers. Statistical tests like Mann-Kendall were performed to validate the trends observed in the data, adding robustness to the findings. Key contributions include identifying major emissions sectors, improving prediction accuracy, and revealing correlations between emissions, socioeconomic factors, and temperature changes. The ARIMA model, evaluated against recent temperature data from 2021 to 2023, achieved a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of $\mathbf{0. 2 3 1 \%}$, demonstrating its reliability. Additionally, strong correlations were found between temperature variations and emissions from CO 2, methane, and nitrous oxide. Industrial emissions from manufacturing, construction, and transportation, as well as agricultural activities, were found to play critical roles in climate change, highlighting the need for focused climate policies.

articleTitle: Enhancing Skin Disease Diagnosis with a Dual Vision Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: An increasing number of people are experiencing skin problems, and it is never easy for a clinician to make a correct diagnosis. One potential solution to these problems is the use of deep learning for skin disease diagnosis. In this paper, a new kind of neural network is proposed for diagnosing skin diseases. We provide a new dual Vision Transformer (ViT) model that has two patches for image embedding and transformer encoding, as well as two multi-level permutation (MLP) heads to combine the two models, in light of the fact that the research datasets are images of skin diseases. To get deep characteristics from images, the proposed framework employs a ViT model that is both appropriate and effective. As a first step in pre-processing, images are first divided into uniformly sized patches, and then compressed into a string of tokens. The second step is to process the flattened patches using two transformer encoders that are connected in parallel. For the transformer encoder, there are $N_{i}, N_{j}$ layers, where each layer has two sublayers. The first component is a self-attention unit with multiple heads, while the second component is a feedforward network with all connections enabled. After normalizing the inputs to each of the two sublayers, we evaluate the strength of the residual connections between them. The implementation of a classification block follows the concatenation of MLP heads. The block is made up of two layers: one that is flattened and one that is dense and optimized for batch processing. The experimental results of the method show classification accuracies of 88% (ISIC2016), 90% (ISIC2017), 91% (HAM10000), and 88% (Skin_disease_v1). The proposed model represents an advancement over state-of-the-art methods and signifies progress in identifying skin diseases.

articleTitle: Block chain and Deep Learning Based Secure Communication using SAE-LSTM &Salp Swarm Optimizer for Multivariate Industrial IoT-oriented Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The rapid development of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) imposes the needs for digitization of industrial procedures so as to enhance the efficiency of the network. Cyber-Physical System (CPS) has important role in applications of industries and infrastructure towards IoT. There are several challenges in IIoT environment such as centralization, scalability, privacy, security and communication latency. To overcome these issues, Deep learning based Sparse Autoencoder-Long Short-Term Memory (SAE-LSTM) with Salp swarm optimizer SSA based IoT-oriented infrastructure is used to detect the attacks. The major objective of this work is to propose a deep learning and blockchain based smart contract technique for a secure communication in smart city using Salp Swarm Optimizer algorithm for determining data privacy and security for the IIoT’s application service. Blockchain & data aggregation with Proof-of-Work (PoW) generates a distributed network for communication phase of CPS. The protocols to forward the data in the network is established by Software-Defined Networking (SDN). Smart contract is employed to execute the transaction. The suggested technique is implemented and the performance is carried out by estimating Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1 Score.

Author Keywords: Blockchain and data aggregation with Proof-of-Work (PoW)

articleTitle: Yoga Pose Detection with Deep Learning and Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: An approach to do real-time monitoring of Yoga Asanas using Deep Learning and Computer Vision approaches. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) are combined to create a hybrid deep learning model. Human pose recognition can be used to create a selfinstruction exercise system that enables people to learn and perform exercises appropriately on their own as these resources are not always readily available. This project discusses several machine learning and deep learning algorithms to precisely identify yoga positions on pre-recorded films as well as in realtime, laying the groundwork for developing such a system. These kinds of applications are useful during times of lockdown, such as the lockdown we experienced in 2020 due to the coronavirus epidemic, when people’s freedom of movement is severely constrained and they may use such programmers’ quite easily from home.

articleTitle: What Matters While Rating a Hotel by a User? An Indian Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the internet era, almost every business entity is trying to have its digital footprint in digital media and other social media platforms. For these entities, word of mouse is also very important. Particularly, this is quite crucial for the hospitality sector dealing with hotels, restaurants etc. Consumers do read other consumers’ reviews before making final decisions. This is where it becomes very important to understand which aspects are affecting most in the minds of the consumers while giving their ratings. The current study focuses on the consumer reviews of Indian hotels to extract aspects important for final ratings. The study involves gathering data using web scraping methods, analyzing the texts using Latent Dirichlet Allocation for topic extraction and sentiment analysis for aspect-specific sentiment mapping. Finally, it incorporates Xgboost to understand the importance of the aspects in predicting the final rating of a user.

articleTitle: Prediction of Kitty Moods using their Phonics in Convolutional Neural Networks(CNNs)
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Even though FeliusCatus(Cat) is one of the domestic pet animals, the cat human relationship has not gained significance compared to dog-human relationship. The cat involves relationship with human and with same species. The vocalization of cat expressed in isolation is considered as most negative and the vocalization expressed in brushing are considering as most positive. The studies shows that the perception of emotions of cat are very limited in number.The aim of this work is to analyze the extent of human recognizing vocalization of cat namely meow sound which is generated in various context such as isolation, brushing and waiting for food. In this work, cat sounds are converted into MFCC graphs and these graphs are trained to a Convolutional Neural Network to predict the cat emotions.

articleTitle: Integrated Robotics System for Ripeness Detection, Tomato Harvesting and Leaf Disease Identification using CNN and YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In contemporary agriculture, the need for innovative solutions to enhance efficiency and reduce costs are ever-growing. This project introduces a pioneering Integrated Robotics System designed to revolutionize the monitoring and harvesting processes for short-lifecycle crops, with a primary focus on tomato plants. This project uses an improved YOLOv8 based algorithm for real-time detection of plant leaf condition in improving the precision farming. The system integrates advanced technology to detect crop diseases, suggest suitable pesticides, and autonomously harvest ripe fruits by the usage of robotic system. In essence, the project envisions a paradigm shift in agriculture, optimizing resource utilization, reducing labour dependency, and promoting sustainability. The Integrated Robotics System seamlessly amalgamates technological prowess with agricultural needs. The integration of CNN for disease classification and YOLOv8 for object detection highlights a commitment to cutting-edge solutions, promising a more efficient and productive future for farmers and farming processes, effectively tackling the challenges of modern agriculture follow. To optimize the harvesting process, a precision robotic arm is employed, capable of identifying and plucking ripe fruits at the opportune moment. This not only ensures minimal wastage but also addresses the labour intensive nature of traditional harvesting methods.

articleTitle: Innovative Emotion Recognition with CNN-SVM: Bridging Deep Learning and Statistical Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: An attempt is made to classify the following five emotions using a CNN-SVM hybrid model designed for emotion recognition: the faces of fear, surprise, rage, happiness, and sorrow. Using convolutional layers, max-pooling layers, dropout layers, and fully-connected layers within the model’s architecture enables the extraction and classification of facial features via an efficient process. The model gives impressive results, as evidenced by the accuracy, precision, II, F value, and efficiency all over the spectrum, all exceeding for all classes. Mainly, Breaking class 3 shows the highest performance because it achieves exactness of $\mathbf{98 \%}$ concerning excellence at $\mathbf{92 \% 92 \%}$, recall of 97. The RNN network’s output reaches up to $\mathbf{58 \%}$, with precision levels the same as the F1 score of 95. 19%. This involves adding up macro, weighted and micro precision, recall and $\mathbf{F}$-Score metrics that equal $\mathbf{92 \%}$, which is the collective macro, weighted and micro averages-high AUC sleeves in the surroundings up to 1. Other incidents occurred at zero for all classes, leading to more evidence that the model is discriminatory. The model’s performance was not affected by differences between training and validation data as it scored $\mathbf{95 \%}$ and $\mathbf{93 \%}$ for the two categories, respectively, exhibiting high robustness and generalizability. By highlighting the superior performance of the CNN-SVM model in the emotion recognition domain, this study denotes a reliable remedy for real-life implementations.

articleTitle: Lane Detection with U-Net Optimization through Hyperparameter Tuning and Cross Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The implementation of secure technology in intelligent vehicles is essential, particularly with lane detection playing a crucial role in autonomous driving systems for enhanced navigation and traffic management efficiency. This paper presents a methodology for optimizing a UNet-based model for lane detection. The UNet architecture is utilized for image segmentation tasks, with an extensive evaluation of model performance conducted using various metrics. The training of the model involves fine-tuning hyperparameters within a specified search space that includes learning rates, batch sizes, and dropout rates. By iteratively adjusting these parameters based on validation loss, we aim to identify the most effective hyperparameters that will enhance the model’s performance. Additionally, a five-fold cross-validation is conducted to ensure the model’s robustness and ability to generalize to different datasets. The final model is constructed based on the best hyperparameters obtained from the tuning process. Throughout the training process, the model demonstrates a high level of accuracy, achieving a training accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 9 3 \%}$ and a corresponding loss of $\mathbf{0. 0 0 3 1}$. Furthermore, the validation accuracy stands at an impressive 99.81% with a validation loss of 0.01. The model achieves a high accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 7 8 \%}$ on the test set, with an IoU score of 0.8861 and an F1 score of 0.9396. These metrics suggest that the model effectively learns and generalizes proficiently to new, unseen data.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection in Network Traffic Using LSTM and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Network Intrusion Detection system (NIDS) helps in detecting the traffic and avoids any potential harm to the system. LSTM is a deep learning model architecture that uses recurrent neural networks (RNN) for handling sequential data. Unlike traditional IDS that depend on fixed signatures, LSTMs can interpret network traffic patterns and detect anomalies that indicate new attack methods. This flexibility makes it more effective against evolving cyber threats. While traditional IDS may only detect malicious activity, LSTMs can predict the specific type of attack by analyzing traffic sequences. This improved accuracy enables quicker and more targeted response strategies to prevent cyber threats. LSTMs have the capability to analyze network traffic data in real-time, allowing for immediate threat identification. The obtained accuracy and F1 score of the model are ${9 2. 8 3 \%}$ and ${9 4. 2 5 \%}$ respectively. This real-time analysis enables faster response times and classification of cyberattacks, reducing the potential impact of any security breaches.

articleTitle: SGridNet: An Efficient and Optimize Bagging Deep Learning for Intrusion Detection in Smart Grid Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: We have developed a framework called SGridNet, a Bagging Neural Network model, for enhancing security in smart grid networks by detecting intrusions and classifying threats. This framework focuses on analyzing time-series TCP/IP packets to identify anomalies. SGridNet employs Bagging to aggregate predictions from multiple models trained on different subsets of the data, enhancing overall model robustness. This approach helps in effectively identifying new attack features and accurately classifying threats. Initial experiments demonstrate promising outcomes, with SGridNet significantly reducing model size. While this does not inherently lead to faster inference times due to the nature of bagging, it does improve computational efficiency and resource usage. Evaluation on NSL-KDD datasets using KNN, SVM, and Ensemble learning algorithms for binary and multiclass classification tasks shows competitive performance using metrics like Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F-Measure. While KNN and SVM perform reasonably well across categories, Ensemble learning excels in specific tasks. Comparison with a baseline model indicates SGridNet’s superiority in terms of model size, computational efficiency, and marginal accuracy improvement.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Automated Attendance Monitoring: Harnessing Ambient Sensitivity and RSSI-based Proximity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Automated attendance monitoring is essential across various fields, offering efficient and precise alternatives to traditional manual methods. This paper presents an innovative approach to attendance tracking by utilizing a Raspberry Pi, microphone, audio input, and machine learning techniques. The system integrates LSTM-based ambient sensitivity and RSSI-based proximity analysis to achieve heightened accuracy in attendance monitoring. The Raspberry Pi acts as the central component, capturing ambient audio with a microphone and collecting RSSI data via a $\mathrm{Wi}-\mathrm{Fi}$ module. MFCC is employed for audio preprocessing to extract relevant features for training an LSTM model, capable of classifying diverse audio inputs. Simultaneously, RSSI data undergoes preprocessing and analysis to estimate device proximity accurately using machine learning algorithms. This paper presents a particular combination of current methods (RSSI, LSTM, and Raspberry Pi) for dual-audio attendance monitoring. With two distinct audio inputs for the teacher and pupils, it may be possible to analyse the presence of the teacher differently and to discern ambient noise based on location. By comparing audio inputs quantitatively, this method gives the attendance monitoring system an extra degree of accuracy. The proposed system’s student module records attendance by analyzing ambient sound and RSSI data processed by LSTM with MFCC. This comprehensive approach reduces manual efforts, enhances accuracy, and delivers real-time attendance information to the teacher module, facilitating efficient attendance management in educational environments.

articleTitle: Characterizing neural activity from EEG signals during game interaction using persistent homology
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Understanding the complex neural activity patterns in the developing brain remains a pivotal challenge in neuro-science. Characterizing neural activity during game interaction offers a unique opportunity to explore brain dynamics in a naturalistic and engaging context. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive method to capture neural signals with high temporal resolution, making it well-suited for studying real-time brain activity during dynamic tasks like gaming. Such signals are non-stationary and exhibit a non-linear manifold nature, which makes it difficult in classifying into different states during interaction. Topological data learning (TDL) framework can help in this context. However, there has been limited study conducted on the application of TDL framework for the purpose of characterizing and classifying EEG data. Therefore, this work utilizes topological attributes like Betti numbers and persistent homology of dimension 0 and 1 extracted from EEG signals to study the neural activity of an individual. Random forest classifier is used to classify the EEG signals during game interaction with accuracy $84.49 \%$. Results show that the performance is at par with deep learning approaches even when less number of topological features are used. The proposed framework shows the efficacy of persistent homology features in EEG signal classification. The robustness of the proposed framework is assessed with publicly available EEG-based Mobile brain-body imaging (MoBI) data of children.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Diagnostics of Air Handling Unit in Hospital Building Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Fault Detection and Diagnostics (FDD) in Air Handling Units (AHUs) are vital for ensuring optimal indoor air quality and operational efficiency in hospital buildings. AHUs play a critical role in regulating temperature and humidity, which directly impacts patient care and staff comfort. Effective FDD can prevent system malfunctions that lead to increased energy consumption, higher operational costs, and potential health risks due to poor air quality. This study explores the application of machine learning techniques for FDD in hospital HVAC systems. Utilizing comprehensive datasets from the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL), we focused on various classifiers, including Random Forest and K-Nearest Neighbors, which achieved accuracies of $99.85 \%$ and $99.77 \%$, respectively, in fault identification. These models demonstrated exceptional precision, highlighting their suitability for complex environments where accurate diagnostics are essential. Our findings emphasize the importance of integrating machine learning into building management systems. By enabling early fault detection, these advanced models significantly reduce operational costs and enhance system reliability. This approach not only improves indoor air quality but also supports sustainable healthcare environments by minimizing energy waste. The research contributes to the development of smarter, more efficient building management solutions, paving the way for real-world applications of data-driven FDD methods. The insights gained provide a strong foundation for future implementations, promoting safer and more sustainable healthcare facilities through enhanced HVAC system performance and fault management. This study underscores the potential of machine learning in revolutionizing building management and improving the overall hospital environment.

articleTitle: Quantum-Safe Authentication Protocol leveraging qPUF for Industrial Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Although there has been a substantial boost in automation due to the rapid growth of IoT devices, there has also been an increase in cyberattack vulnerability. Existing quantum-proof methods are inadequate for IoT devices with limited resources, and traditional cryptographic algorithms lack quantum safety. In response, we propose a lightweight, quantum-safe authentication system that utilizes Quantum-PUF to ensure secure communication, employing Xor Encryption and one-way hash functions without storing keys in non-volatile memory. We conduct formal verification using Scyther and implement it on NodeMCU, demonstrating the efficiency of our protocol and its suitability for Industrial Internet of Things applications.

articleTitle: Intervention Analysis for Predicting Stock Market using Deep Learning Algorithms and Time Series Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Stock market being intricate and volatile pose challenges for classical Time Series Analysis techniques in terms of generalization and computation on real-world data. In order to improve prediction capacities, new methods like intervention analysis and Deep Learning (DL) are required. The research seeks to unravel the complexities of stock price prediction modelling by comparing Time Series Analysis with Deep Learning augmented by intervention analysis. Upon evaluation on different datasets, the Deep Learning models, specifically the Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) performed better than the other models considered. RNN outperformed other models on Mean Squared Error (MSE) for Tesla and IBM data, with values 3.874 before intervention and 3.593 after intervention and 46.52 before intervention and 42.97 after intervention respectively, thus highlighting the advantages of Deep Learning models for predictions. The goal of investigating intervention analysis methods incorporated into predictive models is to create processes that can predict overall market trends and efficiently identify and address sudden deviations.

articleTitle: DUNE: Decoding Unified Naive Bayes Explainability through Gaussian methods for a Heart Disease Diagnostic
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Heart disease is still a prominent cause of illness and fatal death worldwide. In this work, we examine whether the existence of heart disease can be predicted using the Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB) algorithm from a tabular dataset that includes several clinical, lifestyle, and demographic factors. We did a substantial amount of feature engineering on the dataset to manage missing values and standardize features before training the GNB classifier to diagnose heart illness. We evaluate the supervised model using widely-used metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to show thst it distinguishes between people with and without heart disease. Using two state-of-the-art Explainable AI (XAI) techniques, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Modelagnostic Explanations), we shed light on the underlying mechanisms of the predictions made by the GNB model. The authors offer significant new insights into the prognostic potential of the GNB algorithm for heart disease. Our findings demonstrate the value of the dependability and transparency of machine learning models for significant healthcare applications

articleTitle: AI and Big Data: Achieving Optimal Data Retrieval Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Huge records and AI generation have the capacity to revolutionize the way records is retrieved and used, enabling greater green and powerful retrieval approaches. AI algorithms are increasingly getting used to optimize the retrieval of information from large databases, enabling extra correct decisions and quicker seek effects. AI algorithms can be hired to use filters, visualize information, and cluster information into extraordinary corporations, thereby improving get entry to applicable facts. Additionally, AI algorithms can be used to pick out patterns within the information that permit for better forecasting and prediction. Huge information analytics similarly empower AI algorithms to effectively analyze massive datasets and develop insights and correlations in an automated way. These insights and correlations may be used to higher apprehend and utilize statistics in a greater powerful way.

articleTitle: Investigating the Implications of Operations Technology in Cyber Crimes
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study examines how robots, Internet of Things (IoT), and industrial control systems (ICS) interact with critical infrastructure and how it affects forensic investigations. It is critical to comprehend the consequences of these technologies for digital forensics and criminal investigation as they become more and more integrated. In order to promote forensic science and cybersecurity in critical infrastructure protection, this research attempts to examine the prospects, risks, and best practices in doing forensic investigations using ICS, IoT, and robots. Forensic investigations face both potential and problems as a result of the integration of robots, Internet of Things (IoT), and industrial control systems (ICS) in critical infrastructure. This study looks at how these technologies affect forensic procedures in industries including manufacturing, transportation, and energy. This research intends to give insights into the difficulties of investigating cyber events and physical security breaches in industrial contexts by examining current literature, analyzing case studies, and identifying major issues. The results highlight how crucial it is to improve forensic preparedness and cybersecurity resilience via multidisciplinary cooperation, specialized training, and adherence to regulatory norms. With suggestions for reducing risks and enhancing investigation techniques in the face of changing threats, this study advances forensic science and cybersecurity in the protection of vital infrastructure. The revolution in critical infrastructure systems has been brought about by the confluence of Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT). However, these systems are now vulnerable to cyberattacks as a result of this integration. In the present work, we examine cybercrimes that target industrial robots in critical infrastructure. We specifically concentrate on the interactions that occur in IT/OT contexts between Industrial Internet of Things (IoT), Industrial Control Systems (ICS), Distributed Control Systems (DCS), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), and Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC). The goal of our study is to improve knowledge of cyberthreats, vulnerabilities, and defenses in this intricate ecosystem.

articleTitle: Fruit Damage Detection using Custom CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Fruit quality inspection is a critical aspect of the agricultural industry, impacting both production efficiency and consumer satisfaction. This study optimizes the VGG-16 architecture for fruit damage detection by strategically reducing layers, ensuring computational efficiency without compromising performance. The custom CNN architecture is meticulously crafted to balance model complexity and computational resources. Through systematic experimentation, an optimal configuration is identified, achieving a harmonious balance between accuracy and efficiency. By omitting specific VGG-16 layers and employing Batch Normalization (BN) for feature extraction, enhanced efficiency is achieved. The streamlined custom CNN rivals traditional architectures like ResNet50 and Inception V3, demonstrating potential for real-world automated fruit quality assessment systems with 99.3% efficiency. The reduced model complexity accelerates training and inference, making it suitable for resource-constrained environments. This study contributes to fruit quality inspection by presenting an alternative CNN architecture design, offering a pragmatic solution for fruit damage detection without relying on the GAP layer and incorporating two fully connected layers. It provides valuable insights into deep learning model optimization for precision agriculture and automated quality control systems.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of AI-Generated Text
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The advent of Large Language Models (LLMs), has largely transformed global interactions with artificial intelligence. These models, though useful in tasks ranging from translation to text generation, have now permeated everyday life, thereby raising concerns about their potential misuse, particularly in educational institutions. Despite measures like access restrictions implemented by educational institutions, AI based plagiarism has continued to grow, with existing plagiarism detection tools exhibiting limited efficacy in curbing the problem. This paper addresses the need for better AI detection algorithms, focusing on the detection of subtler forms of plagiarism facilitated by LLMs. Leveraging insights from existing studies, the research explores the efficacy of various boosting based machine learning models and dimensionality reduction techniques in improving the accuracy of detecting AI-augmented essays.

articleTitle: IIoT-based Realtime Environmental Monitoring System for an Underground Coal Mines
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Underground coal mines are harsh in the working environment, which leads to more causality. Therefore, modern mines are using sensor networks to monitor the mines regularly to minimize mine accidents. Hence, very limited real-time monitoring systems are developed using a Real-time operating system (RTOS). Contiki-NG is a popular embedded application development framework for Wireless sensor networks and the internet of things (IoT). This paper provides a detailed roadmap to design a real-time monitoring system for underground coal using Contiki-NG. The System design comprises designing sensor node with modified RPL protocol and border router using TI CC2650 launchpad and raspberry pi 3. The Node-RED middleware collects data from the application environment using a sensor node. Store the data into the MongoDB database and visualizes sensed data in a web browser in the monitoring center.

articleTitle: Using AI and IoT to Promote Intra-Party Democracy for Indian Electoral Reforms: Emerging Issues
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) opens transformative opportunities for the furtherance of intra-party democracy and electoral reforms in India. This paper delves into the developing problems and issues that are experienced with such convergence. The paper discusses the potential of ICT tools in bringing transparency and accountability into the electoral system as a mitigating way of issues like criminal and money politics. Core issues of the Indian electoral system that very much need to be given serious attention relate to problems like muscle power, money power, criminalization, misuse of government machinery, and casteism. It needs to address these prime importances in reforming the electoral landscape to ensure free and fair elections. It also underscores how electoral reforms can bring changes to the criminal, corrupt, and monetary influence on politics for strengthening democratic values in India. These will involve a critical examination of the electoral system and make the election process more inclusive for representative democracy of the diverse Indian populace.

articleTitle: Smart Contracts and the Law: A Computer Engineering Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Smart Contracts are designed to facilitate the alternative of digital goods and offerings with minimum transaction charges, counting on self-executing code to ensure that each contractual term is followed. This era has enormous potential to revolutionize business relationships. However, it has yet to benefit from regulatory popularity in many jurisdictions. To ensure that intelligent Contracts can function in a compliant way, comprehensive legal frameworks should be advanced and included to define liabilities, establish enforcement procedures, and defend the parties’ rights. A sizable task in this manner is that clever Contracts aren’t necessarily sure by the prison framework of a specific jurisdiction and may be concerned with exclusive legal guidelines relying on the parties’ agreement and the geographic places of the events. As such, felony frameworks should be transportable throughout jurisdictions to ensure a steady and harmonized regulatory panorama. In addition, studies are needed to explore how current felony fashions and agreement law can be adapted to govern clever Contracts and to perceive how the monetary transformation delivered by using this technology may enhance social value and create equitable consequences for all stakeholders.

articleTitle: RetrORAM: Oblivious Random Access Machines in Retrospect
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Encryption is considered as a best practice for preserving privacy of user data. With the progress of time and advancements in data breach techniques, it is no longer sufficient to just hide data via encryption. Given the setting of a trusted client who stores their encrypted data on an untrusted server, the access pattern of the client gets leaked despite encrypted data. The problem is quite relevant in this age of cloud computing. The prevention of access pattern leakage has become a necessity. To realize this mitigation, the idea of Oblivious Random Access Machine (ORAM) came into picture. A lot of research has gone into optimizing different existing ORAM techniques. However, very minimal work has gone into finding a suitable application for ORAM. This work aims to provide a comprehensive survey of existing ORAM techniques, and finding a pertinent application for the same. PathORAM, one of the most practicable ORAM technique, has been implemented in Python and its indistinguishability is verified by graphically analyzing the memory accesses.

articleTitle: A Detailed Analysis of Machine Learning Models to Predict Water Potability
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Water is one of the most indispensable things in our life. However, getting clean drinking water has become more difficult for a lot of people lately. This research paper uses machine learning techniques to tackle the crucial problem of predicting the potability of water. Reliability in water potability assessment is critical, as concerns about water quality and its effects on public health are becoming more widespread worldwide. We present a novel predictive model to assess the potability of water sources by utilizing an extensive dataset that includes various water quality parameters. In order to examine intricate relationships within the dataset, the study uses a cutting-edge machine learning framework that integrates algorithms like Random Forest, KNN, SVM, Decision tree, and Gradient boosting. To extract pertinent information, feature engineering is used, and model performance is rigorously tuned using hyper parameters. To determine the best method for predicting water potability, a comparative analysis of several models is carried out. The proposed model is validated on different datasets, which guarantees its robustness and generalizability in a range of environmental conditions. The outcomes show that the predictions of water potability have a high degree of sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy.

articleTitle: Feline Image Analytics:Predicting Breed,Age,Gender,Stamina and Emotion
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Understanding various aspects of cats, such as breed, emotion, age, gender, and stamina level, holds significance for humans in several ways. Firstly, it aids in establishing a deeper connection and bond between humans and their feline companions, fostering empathy and understanding. Secondly, it enables pet owners to provide tailored care that meets the specific needs of their cats, promoting their health and well-being. Additionally, recognizing these aspects helps in early detection of health issues and behavioral problems, allowing for prompt intervention and treatment. Moreover, understanding cat behavior and needs can contribute to a more harmonious coexistence between humans and cats, enhancing the overall quality of life for both parties. Traditional methods of obtaining advice on cat care, such as consulting veterinarians or purchasing specialized books, can indeed be costly for some individuals. Furthermore, access to reliable forums or online communities where pet owners can seek guidance may be limited in certain regions or communities. This lack of accessible resources can pose challenges for individuals seeking information on how to properly care for their cats, potentially leading to misinformation or inadequate care practices. A completely working web application that can predict cat breed,age,gender,emotion,stamina level using Convolutional Neural Network {CNN) based transfer learning models,specifically EfficientNet-b0 is suggested. System will take the essential characteristics from images of the cat to predict the aforementioned attributes. The collected findings indicate that the cat attribute prediction ranges from 48.05% to 100% when tested against four CNN-based models.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Mental Health Insights from Social Media: Taxonomies, Computational Methods, and Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Social media platforms such as Facebook Reddit, Instagram etc. have changed our world a lot. Nowadays, people are more connected than before and they show a kind of digital version of themselves online. More and more people are using the internet to share their thoughts and beliefs. This makes it possible for researchers who study online communication of users to better understand and ratify connections between what they post on social media and their mental health status. Researchers are looking at data from different times and over longer periods to emphasize the need for AI systems that can analyze mental health issues in the world community in real-time. To help classify where research is heading in the field of social studies and to keep track of improvements in techniques related to machine learning(ML) and deep learning(DL), using contents available on social media this paper propose conducting an inclusive survey on assessing mental health issues. We create a classification system for mental health care and point out current efforts to analyze people’s well-being based on the content they write, text they post and images they share on their social media account or platform. We outline all the potential research directions for mental health care and explore how to handle online social media data to recognize signs of various mental health related issues majorly stress, depression, and even potential cases of suicide. This paper attempted to put together this information to help young academician, students and researchers working in the area of mental health, to know how computers along with the latest ML and DL models can be used to analyze mental health available on social media platforms. This document summarize the results of many studies and take a close look at more than fifty research papers. In comparison of traditional approaches and ML models, DL models especially CNN and BiGRU along with attention, are really good at interpreting what posts on the internet mean, even when they have some words, emojis, and other symbols or the combinations of them. At the same time the combinations of two or more different models together provide the even better results than when they work on their own.

articleTitle: Automated Bengali Sign Language Character Classification with Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Recognition of Bengali sign language characters is crucial for facilitating communication for the deaf and hard-of-hearing population in Bengali-speaking regions, which encompass approximately 430 million people worldwide. Despite the significant number of individuals requiring this support, research on Bengali sign language character recognition remains underdeveloped. This article presents a novel approach to categorize Bengali sign language characters using the Ishara-Lipi dataset, based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and pretrained models. We evaluated our approach using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrices. Our findings indicate that the CNN model achieved the highest performance with an accuracy of 98%, followed by VGG19 with $\mathbf{94\%}$ and ResNet variants achieving around $\mathbf{88\%}$. The proposed model demonstrates robust and efficient classification capabilities, significantly bridging the gap in existing literature. This study holds substantial promise for enhancing assistive technology, thereby improving social inclusion and quality of life for Bengalispeaking deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals.

articleTitle: Designing A Llama 2-Powered Chatbot for Enhanced College Website Support
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Most of the Colleges and universities are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve website support and user experience in the fast-paced digital landscape of higher education. This research investigates a Natural Language Processing (NLP) based chatbot for college website support. In higher education’s digital landscape, AI-driven chatbots, particularly using the Large Language Model Meta AI Version 2 (LLaMA 2) model, are enhancing website support and user experience by addressing inquiries on admissions, courses, resources, and campus life. Another subset of research component is mainly focusing on predicting the cut-off marks for students for joining the institutions. Focusing on student/institutional cut-off mark prediction, the chatbot employs four different regression models to consider factors like joining year, quotas, previous marks, department preferences, exam difficulty, and job market demand. Evaluation metrics such as MSE, RMSE, and R-squared gauge predictive accuracy. By analyzing historical data and emphasizing academic performance, the study determines which regression models best predict student cut-off marks, ensuring a data-driven approach to decision-making. This AI-powered chatbot enhances user experience by providing comprehensive answers and accurately forecasting students’ academic performance.

articleTitle: Cutting-Edge Steel Damage Classification Powered by Cloud Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this era of rapid technological advancement, the detection of metal damage has become increasingly crucial across various industries. The proposed work “Cutting-Edge Steel Damage Classification Powered by Cloud Technology” aims to build an advanced system for real-time steel damage classification utilizing AWS services includes Rekognition, Lambda, and API Gateway that enables users to upload multiple images simultaneously for damage detection and classification, which will be an innovative approach to industrial defects detection which leads to their prevention. Such benefits of fast, accurate and scalable defect detection make it a critical asset for businesses expecting for exact and real-time solutions in every aspect. This study uses F1 score, precision, recall, and assumed threshold are as evaluation parameters. The use of AWS services is not just helping with model training and deployment, but it also provides failover mechanism and scaling capabilities to accommodate the varying workload demands. The model has the advantage of having rapid training time: 1.005 hours this shows the cloud infrastructure scalability and computational efficiency in dealing with the tasks requiring machine learning of complex nature.

articleTitle: Computational Approaches for Drug Discovery: A Review of Artificial Intelligence Techniques for ADME/T Prediction and Virtual Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Drug discovery, traditionally reliant on extensive experimental work and significant financial investments, often faces high failure rates and prolonged timelines. Recent advancements in computational methods and machine learning techniques aim to streamline this process. This study introduces VISMAI, a tool designed for virtual screening with modules for descriptor calculation, fingerprint generation, and drug-likeness prediction. Using SMILES strings and a GCNN-based model, VISMAI accurately assesses drug-likeness.

articleTitle: Selectivity Estimation of Spatial Query Types to Preserve Location Privacy using Innovative User-based Anonymity and Area-based Anonymity over K-Anonymity
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research activity is aimed to perform selectivity estimation of novel query processing types on spatial data in geographic information systems for the preservation of location privacy of the users using location-based services for retrieving nearest point of interests (POI) using innovative properties like User based anonymity & Area based anonymity over k-anonymity. The proposed anonymity model is tested and trained using a product ratings dataset made up of 100836 results of various items with 8 attributes that were taken as samples from the GroupLens website. It is considered as two batches such as innovative User based anonymity & Area based Anonymity over K-Anonymity where $\mathbf{N}=\mathbf{1 0}$ sample iterations to test the accuracy of the model for preserving location privacy while querying spatial data. For calculating the sample size and performing the t -test analysis G-power is considered as $\mathbf{8 0 \%}$. The results of the obtained accuracy for innovative User based anonymity & Area based Anonymity model has potential up to (79.83%) and the K-Anonymity indexing model has an accuracy of (61.90%). There is an existing statistical significance difference with ($\mathbf{p} \lt \mathbf{0. 0 5}$) between the User & Area based Anonymity and K-Anonymity. $\mathbf{p}=\mathbf{0. 0 0 1}$ is the obtained study’s significance value. The results obtained for selectivity estimation of spatial query processing types to preserve location privacy shows that using innovative User based anonymity & Area based Anonymity has better accuracy ($\mathbf{7 9. 8 3 \%}$), performance and significance than K-Anonymity with accuracy of (61.90%).

articleTitle: Balancing And Risks: Managing Machine Learning In Mental Health Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Evaluation Technique, which uses AI, has the potential to completely change the way mental health services are provided. An overview of artificially intelligent technology (AI) and its most recent developments in the medical industry is provided in this article. It also reviews current research on mental health, emphasizing how AI may help with diagnosis and therapy while taking into account its present drawbacks, unexplored territory, and ethical ramifications. New Developments: We have taken a look at psychological wellbeing analyses and evaluations that classify or split psychological problems like discomfort, extreme personality disorder, and various mental illnesses, such suicide ideas and attempts, into different categories. These evaluations make use of medical records, scales for measuring mood, neuroimaging data, cutting-edge monitoring systems, and information from social media sites. The promise of statistical machine learning to treat issues with mental health is shown by these study findings, but it is crucial to identify the methods that provide the greatest outcomes. Together, these investigations add to the expanding corpus of research that shows how AI may be used in psychiatric treatments. As AI methods develop, they hold the potential to help mental health professionals define psychotic symptoms accurately, recognize chronic illnesses at an earlier, asymptomatic stage when measures can be more effective, and customize treatment plans based on unique patient characteristics. However, care must be taken to avoid extrapolating too soon from preliminary results. To close the gap between clinical therapy and behavioral health research, further study is necessary.

articleTitle: Global Strategies in Addressing Cybersecurity Threats: Navigating the Intersection of Foreign Policy and Digital Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research marks a novel exploration into the potential connections between Foreign Policy and Cyber Attacks. In the contemporary landscape, there has been a notable surge in cyber-attacks from non-state and state actors. Nations are actively engaged in fortifying their cyber domains to protect their Data sovereignty. Concurrently, countries are enhancing their capacities for both offensive and defensive cyber warfare. This study investigates the alignment between a state’s strategic vision and its utilization of Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) groups to achieve its objectives in the realm of cybersecurity. The authors have tried to explore the intricacies of Foreign Policy objectives being achieved through cyber-warfare. A subtle tool which can bring nation to it’s knees is now becoming a force to reckon with. In this study, we have taken up certain countries and how they are achieving their goals by using cyber-warfare.

articleTitle: Does Human-Robot Collaboration Yield Better Search Performance? An Investigation Via Proximal Policy Optimization in Complex Search Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Prior research has been conducted on various supervised and unsupervised techniques for search tasks. However, these studies have primarily focused on assessing model accuracy and performance without evaluating how these models coordinate with humans during a task. The primary objective of this study was to assess the performance of a simulated robot running on a Proximal Pol icy Optimization (PPO) algorithm in coordination with a human player, combining the strengths of both a robot and a human for the search-and-retrieve task. In this study, 30 human participants were recruited to perform a search-and-retrieve task with a 5-minute training phase followed by a 5-minute testing phase. The environment, built in Unity3D, contained 56 distractors (e.g., walls, tables, and chairs) with negative points and 112 targets (e.g., pistol, laptop, and armor) with positive points during the training and testing phases. Humans were asked to search within an environment for targets with a robot player, where the robot was trained using the PPO algorithm. The results demonstrated that the inclusion of a human player along with the PPO robot led to superior performance of the human-robot team in the search-and-retrieve task. The human player outperformed the PPO robot when both players performed individually in the search-and-retrieve task. The PPO robots demonstrated comparatively poorer performance when performing alone in a task without human players. Our findings highlight the importance of human-driven search with a robot in simulated environments.

articleTitle: PSO-Based Optimization for Intelligent Grids: An Approach to Islanding Prevention and Detection in Hybrid Generation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper reviews the use of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), an application that can be used to improve islanding detection and prevention in hybrid networks with renewable energy sources. The research case involves a 4 kW PV station and a 10 kW wind power system within a hybrid generation scheme while this article investigates the efficiency of PSO for grid integration optimization, with stability being retained. Therefore, by using PSO as a parameter optimization technique for DC-AC inverters, seamless synchronization is ensured with the output grid thereby enabling hindrance of the islanding process. It is promising towards advanced grid technology development through AI-driven optimization techniques essential to improving resilience and efficiency in grids under dynamic energy demand and supply conditions. Consequently, it becomes clear that PSO effectively enhances reliability and stability within those hybrids, making modern power systems management a very important tool.

articleTitle: Enhancing Credit Card Fraud Detection with Deep Learning and Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Financial fraud poses a major threat to financial service institutions and clients, facilitating anomaly detection capabilities. This paper dives into deep learning models which can be implemented to detect and distinguish fraudulent transactions from normal transactions and flag anomalies. Further, conversion of tabular data to graphs have been implemented for keen understanding and improved pattern analysis of fraudulent transactions, challenges include evolving attack strategies, class imbalance and model interpretability. The proposed methods utilize a synergistic combination of ensemble learning techniques and unsupervised deep neural networks, like Auto-Encoders and Recurrent Neural Networks. In the graphical representation, this study focuses on implementing Louvain Modularity, Girvan-Newman and Label Propagation Algorithm for effectiveness in community detection. The outcomes exhibit consistently reliable results on credit card transaction datasets. A comprehensive comparative analysis follows to compare the proposed approach to traditional fraud detection methods, demonstrating its superiority in accurately identifying fraudulent transactions, adapting to emerging threats, handling high-dimensional data, and mitigating class imbalances with respect to data privacy and security.

articleTitle: Unveiling Diversity: CNN-LSTM Model for Indian Asparagus Types UC 157, Mary Washington and Jersey Giant
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study is about making a strong model to tell the difference between three popular asparagus types in India. They are called UC 157, Mary Washington, and Jersey Giant. It will be checked if it works well with Indian farming practices. The new model, made from Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks mixed, works well to correctly put asparagus types into different groups based on their unique looks. Using a very carefully picked set of $\mathbf{12,000}$ pictures, the computer does well with an overall correct rate of 96.7%. Accuracy measures like precision, recall and $\mathbf{F 1}$-score show that the model is very good at telling different types apart. The rates of getting things right are over $\mathbf{90\%}$. Looking at the mix-up table gives in-depth information about how well or badly the model is doing. It shows both good parts and where it could be improved better. Though the result is good, more work needs to be done. This will help make the model better at different times and places. This study shows how the developed model can be an important tool for farmers and others to accurately find out which asparagus types they have. This helps them improve their farm practices, making it easier to grow more in India’s agricultural areas.

articleTitle: Design of 32 Bit RISC V Processor
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a RISC-V processor core with a single-stage architecture, focusing on the execution of the base 32I instruction set. The processor core features a 32-bit address and data architecture, with 32 general-purpose registers for data manipulation. The design adheres strictly to the RISC-V ISA specifications, ensuring compatibility with existing software and toolchains. Key components of the processor core include a fetch unit, decode unit, ALU unit, register file, memory control unit, and instruction memory unit. Through rigorous design and simulation, the processor core achieves single-clock-cycle execution, enabling efficient processing of instructions at an operating frequency of 2.2 KHz. The instruction memory unit facilitates the retrieval of instructions from a 4.5 KB memory array, while simultaneous read and write capabilities are supported for both registers and data memory. Additionally, 13 pseudo-instructions have been incorporated to enhance programming ease and readability. Performance evaluation of the processor core demonstrates its effectiveness in executing a variety of computational tasks, showcasing its reliability and efficiency within the specified operational parameters. The design serves as a foundation for future enhancements, including the integration of pipeline architecture, branch prediction mechanisms, and frequency optimization.

articleTitle: Developing an AI-Driven Personalization Engine for Real-Time Content Marketing in E-commerce Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of e-commerce, the need for advanced personalization strategies has become paramount. This research endeavors to develop a cutting-edge Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-driven personalization engine explicitly tailored for real-time content marketing in ecommerce platforms. The proposed system goes beyond traditional methods by dynamically analyzing user behavior in real-time, utilizing CNN’s capabilities to interpret and respond to visual elements within the e-commerce platform. The methodology involves the integration of CNN algorithms into the personalization engine architecture, coupled with extensive data collection from various sources, including user interactions, preferences, and historical data. The CNN-driven engine aims to provide instantaneous and personalized content recommendations, enhancing user experience and engagement. Evaluation metrics encompass user interaction patterns, clickthrough rates, and conversion rates. This research contributes a novel perspective to the field of e-commerce personalization by leveraging CNN technology, promising not only enhanced accuracy in content recommendations but also the ability to adapt in real-time to the ever-changing preferences of users. With an accuracy rate of $\mathbf{9 8 \%}$, the engine demonstrates a high level of correctness in its recommendations, capturing both relevant and non-relevant items with precision. The findings hold significant implications for the future of real-time content marketing in the competitive e-commerce landscape.

articleTitle: Optimizing Content Delivery Networks for Enhanced Performance and Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) are fundamental to modern Internet content distribution, enabling high-speed delivery of web pages, videos, and other online resources. Optimizing caching strategies within CDNs is crucial for improving network efficiency and ensuring a seamless user experience. This research explores the efficacy of traditional caching algorithms such as LFU, LRU, RAND, and FIFO, in comparison to machine learning algorithms including Linear Regression (LR), Gradient Boosting (GB), K-Nearest Neighbours (kNN), Decision Tree (DT), AdaBoost, Random Forest (RF), LightGBM, and XGBoost. The findings demonstrate that machine learning techniques can significantly enhance CDN performance by identifying optimal caching locations and adapting to traffic patterns. Notably, the XGBoost model achieved a cache hit rate of Hyperparameters used for different 76.31 %, a latency of 0.98 seconds, and a throughput of $18,796.16$ requests per second, surpassing traditional methods in hit rate and overall efficiency. The study underscores the need for predictive and adaptive caching approaches in modern traffic management, highlighting the benefits of improved caching on user experience, operational costs, and environmental impact.

articleTitle: Ensem-EnsemHAR: Human Activity Recognition using Ensemble of Ensemble Methods and Smartphone Sensor Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Recognizing human activity has many applications in real life such as in biometrics, military, security, medical care applications, etc. In this paper, we proposed a new activity recognition method using the voting fusion of various ensemble methods. The data are subject-wise split into training and test sets to accomplish a person-independent recognition model. As base ensemble methods we have used random forest, extra-trees, AdaBoost, Histogram-based Gradient Boost, and XGBoost classifier. The hyper-parameters of base ensemble methods are fine-tuned using four different methods: RandomizedSearchCV, HalvingRandomSearchCV, GridSearchCV, and HalvingGridSearchCV. The recognition accuracies of each base ensemble for various parameter tuning techniques as well as for scikit-learn default values of the parameters are compared and we selected those values of hyper-parameters for which we obtained the highest recognition accuracy. Then the base ensembles are used in a voting ensemble which provides the final recognition result. The prediction results show the robustness of the proposed method to many similar existing methods, especially for unbalanced datasets.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Image-to-Audio Encryption with Data Hiding
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The proposed framework addresses the critical need for secure multimedia data sharing by integrating image-to-audio encryption with advanced AI-based data-hiding techniques. The core concept involves transforming static visual content into dynamic auditory experiences, injecting semantic depth and artistic creativity into the resulting audio output. Unlike conventional methods, this approach goes beyond translating pixels into sound waves. It holds promise in multimedia communication, artistic expression, and data protection. To enhance security, this framework introduces AIenhanced data-hiding techniques, leveraging adversarial training and reinforcement learning. This extra layer ensures resistance to unauthorized access and tampering. In summary, this approach fuses image-to-audio encryption and AI-enhanced data hiding, aiming to revolutionize multimedia, thus offering a robust solution, transcending boundaries by safeguarding visual data through the immersive medium of audio.

Author Keywords: Image to audio encryption and decryption

articleTitle: Leveraging Transfer Learning for Efficient Classification of Coffee Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Coffee leaf diseases pose a significant threat to the quality and yield of coffee crops, necessitating early and precise identification for effective disease management. This study introduces a robust approach leveraging transfer learning to classify seven prevalent coffee leaf diseases. By employing a ResNet50v2 model, the research aims to enhance classification accuracy while mitigating bias. The proposed methodology integrates data preparation, preprocessing, data augmentation, partial layer freezing, feature fusion, and fully connected layers to develop a reliable disease classifier. The ResNet50v2 model initially distinguishes healthy from unhealthy leaves, achieving an impressive test accuracy of ${96.99\%}$. In subsequent stages, the model classifies unhealthy leaves into sooty molds, brown spots, and rust leaf diseases with ${94.40\%}$ accuracy, and further identifies red spider mite, leaf miner, phoma, and cercospora diseases with ${92.66\%}$ accuracy. Overall, the model demonstrates a classification accuracy of ${94.20\%}$ across the entire dataset, underscoring its efficacy in detecting and classifying multiple coffee leaf diseases.

articleTitle: Geolocated Event Detection using Graph Mining Approach on Real-Time Multimodal Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Geolocated Event Detection is one of the most prevalent and novel research topic in social media event detection but presently very few researchers have addressed this problem. Thus, the aim of this research is to tackle the problem of natural disaster event detection with the help of real-time social media data in order to successfully incorporate the sentiments of the affected people so that the developed model must be able to train better with the aid of real-life scenarios. Currently, the focused natural disasters for this work are, earthquakes, floods and cyclones keeping the Indian Geography in mind, as Indian subcontinent is mostly affected by these calamities. Due to this, the real-time data required for training of the model was sufficiently available. Therefore, the prime aim of this work is to detect these events by mining real-time twitter data in the form of user tweets and images. Thus, these collected data is then linked to form graphs by finding patterns or relationships among them. This research is basically considering two different modalities of data i.e., text and image data in order to attain realistic results. This study will help in detecting natural disasters, such as earthquakes, floods etc. along with their location coordinates with the help of real-time user tweets and alerting the users in close proximity to the deducted location. This will benefit not only the people but also alert the concerned authorities so that help and other necessities can be provided well in time to the affected people and evacuations can be made before being too late, and thus the damages thus involved in any such event are kept to minimum.

articleTitle: TEXT-IT: A Secure Web Chat Application
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper introduces a secure web chat application that leverages steganography, a technique for concealing messages within images, to ensure secure and covert communication. The application integrates the MERN stack (MongoDB, Express.js, React.js, and Node.js) for robust development and employs the Least Significant Bit (LSB) algorithm for steganography. The paper delves into the intricate details of the application’s architecture, encompassing modular design, user authentication, real-time chat functionality, steganography integration, user interface, back-end server operations, database management, and security considerations. Additionally, it explores potential future enhancements, including video chat, group chat, and more sophisticated steganographic methods. This research offers a comprehensive overview of a web chat application that prioritizes user privacy and data security through steganographic integration.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enabled Smart Contracts: An Evolutionary Algorithm Approach for Automated Financial Agreement
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Blockchain technology has revolutionized various industries by introducing decentralized and secure systems. Smart contracts, self-executing contracts with the terms of the agreement directly written into code, represent a significant advancement in automating and enhancing the efficiency of financial agreements. This paper proposes an evolutionary algorithm approach to further optimize the implementation of smart contracts on the blockchain for automated financial agreements. The evolutionary algorithm, inspired by the principles of natural selection and genetic algorithms, aims to enhance the adaptability and performance of smart contracts over time. Through a continuous process of selection, crossover, and mutation, the algorithm evolves the codebase of smart contracts to better suit the dynamic and evolving nature of financial markets. This approach not only improves the efficiency of automated financial agreements but also enables smart contracts to adapt to changing market conditions, regulatory requirements, and user preferences. Furthermore, the security implications and challenges associated with the evolutionary algorithm are examined, along with potential strategies for mitigating risks. In conclusion, the integration of evolutionary algorithms with blockchain-enabled smart contracts represents a promising avenue for advancing the automation of financial agreements. This approach not only addresses the challenges of adaptability and optimization but also contributes to the ongoing evolution of blockchain technology in the realm of decentralized finance. The findings of this research have implications for financial institutions, regulators, and developers seeking to leverage the full potential of smart contracts in an ever-changing financial landscape.

articleTitle: Bridging the Gap with AI-Based Semantic Search Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Bridging the space with synthetic Intelligence (AI)-based semantic seek strategies gives you practical techniques for navigating the ever-growing virtual facts space. With AI-pushed semantic search, users can query for valuable expertise in several databases, raising statistics discovery to a new degree of speed and efficiency. AI-pushed semantic search can identify valuable data in complicated record sets, bringing practical insights into sharper awareness while brushing off redundant content material from densely populated facts collections. With AI-pushed semantic seek, fact discovery is faster, more profound, informed, and more valuable. Lay users can enjoy the more advantageous manipulation of personal facts while expert workers receive the essential records to make more knowledgeable selections.

articleTitle: An Innovative Method for Identifying Deepfake Videos Through Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The detection of deepfake videos is essential due to the significant potential harm posed by manipulated media. Various deep learning techniques, including customized convolutional neural networks (CNNs), MobileNet, and DenseNet, have demonstrated promise in this domain. This study introduces a system for detecting deepfake videos by leveraging tooth and mouth movements, which are notably difficult to replicate accurately. The proposed methodology utilizes multiple transfer learning algorithms such as InceptionV3, MobileNet, VGG16, VGG19, Xception, and DenseNet121 to enhance the algorithm’s capability to detect and classify deepfake videos based on biological signal attributes derived from jaw and tooth frames. The study specifically targets the identification of deepfake videos by extracting and cropping frames from the input video to emphasize the mouth and nose regions. These preprocessed frames are subsequently fed into a customized CNN trained to classify videos as real or fake, achieving an accuracy of $91.7 \%$.
