Additionally, pre-trained CNN models DenseNet121 and MobileNetV2 further improve accuracy, attaining $88.4 \%$ and $90.9 \%$, respectively. An ensemble approach that combines the predictions of these models results in an overall accuracy of $93.2\%$.

articleTitle: SPFaaS: Service Provisioning and Request Scheduling in a Hierarchical Edge-Cloud System under Function-as-a-Service Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The geographical distance between the data centers and users brings an obstacle to the centralized cloud system in serving the demands of the latency-sensitive applications of today’s era. As a result, the edge-cloud system evolves as a promising computing platform where a set of edge servers are deployed near the users. As these servers are also resource-constrained compared to the cloud, it is challenging to utilize their resources efficiently. To support the user applications, these edge nodes need to keep running various services. This paper considers hierarchically organized edge nodes and aims to effectively provision the services so that more requests can be served within the deadline. We conduct a wide range of experiments with both synthesized and real datasets and observe that the proposed strategy outperforms the state-of-the-art approach with a 41% increase in the number of requests served. In the case of the real dataset, the proposed approach beat the state-of-art and decentralized approaches by 17% and 67%, respectively. We further observe that the performance of the proposed strategy is close to that of the optimal centralized strategy.

articleTitle: Pioneering Pediatric Health - Machine Learning Ensembles for Appendicitis Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Children’s appendicitis is often diagnosed using outdated techniques that may not be as quick or accurate as they need to be. The present investigation employs sophisticated machine learning (ML) methodologies to mitigate these constraints and enhance the diagnostic results. We investigated the effectiveness of many ensemble machine learning (ML) models, such as Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), CatBoost, LightGBM, AdaBoost, and Decision Trees, using a proprietary dataset that contains a diverse range of pediatric appendicitis cases. After extensive training and validation, these models showed amazing accuracy and precision rates—the best models reaching up to 99% accuracy. In addition to outlining each model’s effectiveness, our comparison study clarifies which models are applicable in clinical contexts. This research work addresses how these models might improve clinical processes, lower diagnostic mistake rates, and speed up and improve the accuracy of clinical decisionmaking. The findings of this study demonstrate the revolutionary potential of machine learning to improve pediatric healthcare by offering reliable instruments for intricate medical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Guardian Eye: Hoslitic Parental Control Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In today’s world of technology, accessing the web requires just a few clicks. Anyone with a decent internet connection can easily browse the web and access any type of content. In such scenarios, it is important to safeguard the online activities of the children. As children can access any content very easily, which can be good or bad, monitoring the online behavior of the children helps parents make sure that their children are watching the appropriate content and are not having any negative effects on their mental state. As article [12] [13] [14] shows that kids having excessive mobile phones and social media usage may face mental issues and other sever health issues. Only monitoring might not be able to solve this issue completely. There is a need for active content blocking, through which children will not have access to inappropriate content in the first place, and limiting the time spent on the internet is important from a parent’s point of view. To solve this issue, we have come up with Guardian Eye. Guardian Eye is a holistic parental control system. With the help of Guardian Eye, parents can not only keep track of their children’s online activity but also dig deep into the online behavior of the children. Guardian Eye provides parents with in-depth monitoring of children’s online activities across the internet. Content filtering and blocking is also one of the main features where parents can block or filter any type of content that they think might not be appropriate for their children. Parents can also manage the time spent by children on the internet by limiting it. Parents will be provided with a dashboard where they will have access to detailed reports of children’s Internet usage and behavioral analysis of the children. Guarding Eye is a network-based solution based on a proxy server, so all the requests from children’s devices will go through the proxy server, and based on the type of request and rules created by the parent, appropriate action will be taken. Guardian Eye consists of three main systems: the first is a proxy server for intercepting the request; the second is the parent dashboard for reporting; and the third is a mobile application to redirect all the outgoing requests to the proxy server. Overall, Guardian Eye offers a comprehensive solution to parents to ensure safe and clean access for their children.

articleTitle: Text Mining for Knowledge Discovery and Information Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: textual content mining for know-how Discovery and facts analysis is an especially new subject of research that analyses unstructured data together with textual files. It’s far an interdisciplinary technique that consists of herbal language processing, system studying, facts mining, and statistics retrieval. Its intention is to broaden wise systems that can interpret and extract significant and useful records from text. Textual content Mining may be used for numerous know-how discovery and information evaluation responsibilities, which includes sentiment analysis, summarization, clustering, class, entity extraction, relation extraction, and key-word seek. The goals of textual content mining are to discover useful relationships and patterns between objects in unstructured records and to enhance the effectiveness of packages. Textual content Mining can be applied to many domain names to resolve knowledge discovery and facts extraction troubles and can be used to guide selection-making in businesses.

articleTitle: Speaker Diarization in Multispeaker and Multilingual Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Speaker diarization is a process in automatic speech processing that involves segmenting and labeling an audio recording based on distinct speakers. The goal is to identify and differentiate speakers within the audio. A comprehensive approach to multilingual speaker diarization, crucial for understanding and processing speech across diverse languages, was implemented. The Pyannote library has been utilized to develop a custom speaker diarization model and finetune it for the in-house multi lingual conversation dataset. Using PyanNet segmentation model, segmentation of audio recordings was done to identify speech regions. Speaker embeddings are extracted using the ECAPA-TDNN architecture, pretrained on Vox-Celeb data and fine-tuned on a unique multilingual dataset featuring six languages and 100 audio samples, split into training, development and testing sets for rigorous evaluation. Agglomerative clustering was employed and compared the system’s output with manually generated Rich Transcription Time Marked (RTTM) with ground truth speaker segments and labels, alongside ECAPA-TDNN, X-vector MFCC and X-Vector SincNet embedding models. This study advances the understanding of multilingual speaker diarization, offering insights into its potential applications in transcription, voice biometrics, and multilingual voice assistants.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Precise Brain Hemorrhage Detection from CT scans: A Web - Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Advancements in medical imaging has greatly improved the diagnosis and treatment of neurological disorders. Prompt identification of brain hemorrhage is essential for enhancing patient outcomes. This research introduces an innovative deep learning approach to automate the detection of brain hemorrhage in CT scans. It involves thorough data preprocessing, including synthetic data generation, and utilizes advanced convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with recurrent layers and ResNet models. The models are trained with dynamic augmentation techniques using an image generator to improve generalization. Evaluation methods include traditional metrics and a web application that loads a pre-trained model, providing heatmaps of Region of Interest (ROI) indicating hemorrhage or normal conditions. This tool aids in interpreting the model’s predictions, potentially improving the accuracy of brain hemorrhage detection in medical practice. By integrating deep learning with visualization techniques, this methodology aims to streamline diagnosis, enabling radiologists to make more informed decisions efficiently. Ultimately, it could lead to better patient care through early detection and intervention for brain hemorrhages.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning based Depression Detection via Questionnaires and Video
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study aims to detect depression by integrating machine learning with facial analysis. It features two main components: a ten-question multiple-choice questionnaire (MCQ) to assess depression aspects, and a video analysis module that records participants’ facial and verbal responses. Speech-to-text conversion and attention mechanisms analyze verbal responses, while facial expressions are examined for depressive symptoms. Machine learning techniques such as neural networks, decision trees, and regression analyze data from both segments to identify depression symptoms. Validation against established diagnostic standards and a focus on consent and data confidentiality underscore the system’s promise for early intervention and support.

articleTitle: Intelligent Street Light Management and Monitoring System with IoT Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has transformed several urban infrastructure systems, including street lighting. Traditional street lighting systems waste a lot of electricity, highlighting the necessity for energy conservation. The rising cost of electricity, caused by energy inefficiencies, needs more effective power-saving techniques. To resolve this issue, a completely automated street light monitoring system has been developed to improve the efficiency of street light operations. The proposed method uses modern technology, including IoT and sensor technology, to autonomously manage street light switching operations based on real-time situations, such as the presence of pedestrians or automobiles. Using server-based technology, each street light is continuously monitored and managed, leading to effective supervision and significant energy savings. The system makes use of light-emitting diodes (LEDs), which don’t require much electricity. As directional light sources, LEDs may emit light in particular directions, enhancing the performance of streetlamps. Light-dependent resistors (LDRs) can be employed with LED lights to modulate their intensity. The infrared (IR)sensors situated on a single side of the road assess the volume of traffic and provide signals to the LEDs to illuminate the next portion of the road. Furthermore, the sensors identify failures in the streetlights and notify the appropriate electrical board officer via email or message. The proposed solution performed better than existing systems in terms of energy efficiency and operational effectiveness.

articleTitle: Neural Scriptology: Delineating Handwritten Script Recognition Through CNN-LSTM Modeling

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis using YouTube Comments
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The “AI-Enhanced Product Recommendation System using YouTube Comments Analysis” leverages advanced deep learning models, specifically the Complex Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (CLSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (CGRU). This system harnesses the rich and diverse user-generated content on YouTube, employing CGRU and CLSTM to analyze and extract valuable sentiments from comments associated with product videos. The CGRU model excels at capturing intricate sequential dependencies, while the CLSTM model excels at recognizing complex linguistic patterns. The synergy between these models enables the system to effectively decipher the subtle nuances and sentiments expressed in online discussions. The process involves collecting and preprocessing YouTube comments, training the models on sentiment analysis tasks, and utilizing the learned representations to enhance product recommendations. The system addresses the challenges posed by the informal and varied nature of user-generated content on YouTube, incorporating robust natural language processing techniques. The implementation of these advanced models contributes to the creation of a sophisticated recommendation system, offering insights derived from user interactions, ultimately empowering content creators, marketers, and platform moderators to make informed decisions in the dynamic digital landscape.

articleTitle: Quantum Kernel based Support Vector Machine with Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm Embedding for improved Lung Cancer Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The integration of classical machine learning with quantum computing has sparked a remarkable revolution, opening avenues to tackle previously insurmountable challenges in diverse fields, particularly in clinical applications. One such challenging task is to predict lung cancer with minimal clinical samples and features. The prominent objective of this proposed research is to introduce a novel Quantum Kernel Support Vector Machine (QKSVM) constructed with the Quantum Kernel Circuit (QKC) enriched with Quantum Approximation Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) embedding circuit to classify highly complex lung cancer using a minimal number of samples and minimal feature dimensions. In this context, to compare the classification performance of the transformative potential of the proposed QAOA embedding QKSVM classifier model, we implemented two other variants of the QKC leveraging Angle embedding (Angle Embedding QKSVM) and Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial embedding (IQP Embedding QKSVM). We also compared their performance with that of a classical SVM classifier. In this study, we delve into the transformative potential classification performance of the proposed QAOA Embedding-based QKSVM classifier, which is contrasted particularly in scenarios with limited sample size and feature dimensions. Our investigation reveals the quantum kernel’s superiority, even when operating with smaller datasets. This remarkable performance is attributed to the quantum models’ robustness in extracting intricate diagnosing features, enabling it to extract more pertinent insights from fewer data points. Notably, the QKSVM model trained with a significantly selected feature vector of 4-Dimensions (4D) with Principal Component Analysis (PCA) emerges as the frontrunner in lung cancer predictions, achieving an outstanding test accuracy of 94.64% and the highest area under curve (AUC) metric of 82.33%.

articleTitle: Generative AI-based Health Monitoring and Prediction of Electrical Submersible Pumps
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Algorithms, Analytics, Modeling, and Knowledge-Based Techniques are used to propose an innovative solution in this research paper to enhance the prognostic health monitoring (PHM) of electrical submersible pumps (ESPs) by incorporating Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods. The method under consideration creates artifacts that mimic various conditions of ESP failure and degradation by training deep learning models such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Thanks to the use of synthetic data for constructing machine learning models, it becomes possible to predict the conditions in which the ESP function will start degrading and could potentially find the root cause before it becomes an issue. The data gathered from this experiment affirm that this method is most efficient in enhancing maintenance plans and reducing downtime to achieve optimum dependability and effectiveness of ESP operations. The proposed architecture of PHM involves the incorporation of Generative AI for enhancing the time of operation of the ESPs in industrial applications and presents significant opportunities for preventive maintenance.

articleTitle: An improved Vision Systems for modern computer applications using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)

This project aims to expand an advanced vision system for modern-day laptop applications by leveraging the energy of today’s Deep modern-day. Our proposed device will comprise deep ultra-modern algorithms to enhance the accuracy and velocity of state-of-the-art photo popularity and interpretation. Furthermore, we can design and train our system on massive and various datasets to improve its potential in dealing with specific trendy images and environments.

articleTitle: Bert-Ner: A Transformer-Based Approach For Named Entity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The NER (“Named Entity Recognition”) technique picks up on named entities including people, places, companies etc., that are in the unstructured data in a new language processing technique. But, it arises a fundamental issue of the lack of localization that cannot be feasible. In spite of the achieved top performance of supervised NER methods in resource-rich domains, they usually too slow and not so accurate in domains with little labeled data. Here, the work present a new model known as BERT-NER which is an exceptionally deep learning approach built on the BERT (“Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers”) architecture as its pre-trained language model. BERT-NER introduces the BERT installation to the NER mission making the context extraction be on the dot. BERT-NER fuses the BERT encoder and token classification layers together, optimized using cross-entropy loss. The experiment on the CoNLL-2003 dataset showed that BERT-NER could be an attention grabber as the scores were $\mathbf{9 3. 1 2 \%}$ precision, $\mathbf{9 4. 4 6 \%}$ recall, $\mathbf{9 3. 7 9 \%}$ F1 score, and 98.51% accuracy marking it as one of the field’s top results. The qualitative evaluation on the other hand, shows brilliance in systemic solutions across multiple domains. This project not only is about named entity recognition but focuses on creating broader domain in order to enhance the flexibility of the process. Through benefiting from transfer learning and initialized language models, BERT-NER increases the capability of the BERT model, in this manner extending a list of its applications in NER.

articleTitle: Exploring the Challenges of Optimizing the Efficiency of Ad-Hoc Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Ad-hoc Wi-Fi networks provide a Wi-Fi conversation platform without a hard and fast infrastructure. By leveraging consumer devices that have adopted the advert-hoc community protocol, they enable short and effective verbal exchanges. Effective usage of this sort of community can be difficult, however, as optimizing their performance calls for addressing certain technological and operational demanding situations. This abstract considers the challenges related to optimizing the performance of an ad-hoc Wi-Fi network. The maximum giant demanding situations related to optimizing the performance of an ad-hoc wireless network are associated with interference. Interference occurs when indicators from a couple of nodes overlap and intrude with every other, resulting in decreased community performance. To reduce this the most, one needs to decide and eliminate strange interference sources while ensuring appropriate transmitting power levels on nodes. Requirements are necessary that will allow you to control and coordinate efficiently to reduce interfering’s. Just like the challenges due to interference, these access types are also familiar for ad-hoc networks. There is a definite way to gain admission to those networks instead of usual Wi-Fi networks because a node has not established careers or one-way verbal exchange links. Subsequently, community directors are searching for a method to get into the controller for the network with its operator’s transport channels, thereby exercising equal tactile manipulation over visitors’ packets. Ultimately, even the role of optimizing an ad-hoc Wi-Fi network has a constrained coverage range that challenges their efficiency. This loss of distance results in performance inefficiencies because nodes must be spread thinly along the path to form an extensive, efficient network. Thus, the final submission can improve in combating interferences, enforcing admission manipulation, and promoting a better coverage range in multi-channels or bandwidth aggregation. There is no disputing the ability - given appropriate technical and operational measures - to further boost network performance.

articleTitle: Securing Smart Grid: A Cloud-Assisted Approach with Multi-Authority Attribute-Based Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With the evolution of smart grid technologies, the integration of cloud computing introduces new security challenges. Attribute-based encryption $(A B E)$ has emerged as a promising solution, leveraging its attribute matching mechanism. Recognizing the heightened demands posed by smart meters, we present a novel approach called Multi-Authority CP-ABE (MA-CP-ABE). Our scheme employs Linear Secret-Sharing Schemes (LSSS) access structures for robust access control. Additionally, it leverages private cloud infrastructure for managing user authorization lists and authentication. Smart meters encrypt data using the MA-CP-ABE scheme before transmitting it to the cloud for storage and processing. When authorized users, such as utility providers or grid operators, request access to smart grid data, the cloud evaluates their roles and attributes against the access policies defined by the MA-CP-ABE. Access is granted only if the user’s role or attributes match the access requirements, ensuring data confidentiality and integrity. Furthermore, extensive security analysis and performance evaluations are conducted to validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the MA-CP-ABE within smart grid environments.

articleTitle: Interpreting Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Medical Diagnosis Using Perceptual Encoding and Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The robust performance of deep neural networks (DNNs) in many areas, including medical diagnosis, is not accessible from the problem of interpretability. Even though DNNs have high accuracy, they tend to operate as black boxes, usually without any explanation of which basis their predictions are made. This interpretability issue has become important, especially for high-stakes applications, such as medical image analysis and disease diagnosis, in which people’s lives are at risk. The study was structured to raise novel approaches for DNNs, internal representation translation and provide visualizations to assist medical diagnosis tasks and ensure reliable and transparent decision-making procedures. Such techniques have been developed to improve the interpretability of DNN without sacrificing the performance. The models for proposed models succeeded in the clinical tasks of medical diagnosis. They reached competitive accuracy with the best model, obtaining an accuracy of 95.7% and an F1-score of 0.914 on lung abnormality detection from chest X-rays. AUC-ROC high sensitivity and specificity of 0.963 were observed when diagnosing brain tumors based on MRI scans. These models also provided improved faithfulness perceived through saliency maps, which had an average score of 0.82, and concept activation vectors, with a consistency of 0.77 from the evaluation done by medical experts. The suggested methods offer a chance for a better patient outcome via high-precision and safe diagnostics and treatment options with an expected change in misdiagnosis rate of 10-15%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cyclone Center Identification in Radar Images through Deep Learning and Match Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research focuses on improving the identification of cyclone centers using deep learning and match recognition applied to radar images. Accurately pinpointing the cyclone’s center is vital for predicting its intensity and trajectory. However, challenges persist in automatically locating the center due to the diverse nature of cyclone morphology and structure. To address this, the deep convolutional network’s capability is leveraged to capture various structural features in images by proposing two-step approach for cyclone center localization. Initially, a pre-trained EfficientDet model is employed using transfer learning to obtain weights. Subsequently, these weights, along with the data, are utilized in a deep learning model to provide precise coordinates of the cyclone center in the respective image. The effectiveness of existing deep learning and machine learning models show that the cyclone prediction systems have an accuracy ranging from $86 \%$ to $92 \%$ or better, and cyclone eye detection accuracy surpassing 87%. Experiment outcomes indicate that the proposed methodology outperforms conventional methods and existing works, showcasing its potential for enhancing cyclone monitoring and forecasting.

articleTitle: Multimodal Neuro-Fuzzy Approach for Emergency Healthcare Virtual Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Multimodal Neuro-Fuzzy Approach (MNFA) is a novel approach to providing healthcare services through virtual infrastructure. This method combines Artificial Intelligence (artificial neural networks) techniques with fuzzy logic, to provide a robust and reliable virtual healthcare infrastructure in cases of emergency. The MNFA approach enables healthcare professionals to have access to up-to-date medical information and treatment guidelines quickly and accurately even in remote or rural areas. Therefore, this approach has the potential for providing efficient and effective healthcare services in remote locations which otherwise would not be accessible due to geographical constraints. Additionally, with the help of MNFA approach, healthcare organizations can save time and money by reducing manual labor costs associated with responding to emergencies. This allows for better automation of clinical decisions in emergency situations. The MNF model is already trained with help azure of Microsoft and gets accuracies in matlab (ANFIS). It enables faster and more accurate diagnosis, improved patient care coordination, and a better understanding of the dynamics between health care providers and patients. This approach can also be used to design intelligent systems that are capable of accurately predicting patient outcomes based on past data. As created a framework with Django and MySQL which is deploy on cloud platform to easy access of framework and collect more data on which will store in cloud database and present in cloud public domain. As such, it provides an invaluable tool for improving healthcare services in times of crisis. Healthcare professionals to effectively monitor, analyze, and take necessary action in an emergency situation. In this framework use cloud platform to fast and easy access of virtual healthcare. This experimental investigation demonstrates that, when used to solve real-world problems, our suggested approach outperforms alternative methods.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on Developing Stacking Ensemble Model for Bangla Sports Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Bangladeshi people have a strong connection with sports, evident in the multitude of comments made before and after games regarding their favorite teams. Sports sentiment analysis is conducted to understand public sentiments in the realm of sports. In this work, we proposed a new sports based sentiment dataset extracted from YouTube comments covering football, cricket, traditional local games and others, totaling 82,612 instances which is publicly available in the repository https://github.com/cseku170202/Bangla-Sports-Sentiment-Analysis. Our empirical study considered the use of various trendy machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methods. Specifically, we utilized Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Transformer Neural Network (TNN) as deep learning methods and Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB), Random Forest (RF), and KNearest Neighbors (KNN) as machine learning techniques. Furthermore, we examined 48 different stacking ensemble models by combining these machine learning and deep learning algorithms. Subsequently, our proposed stacking model achieved the highest accuracy of 81%, demonstrating its capability to identify sports sentiments with remarkable F1-score of 0.82. To explain model’s interpretability, we utilized several Explainable AI techniques to better understand the impact of the base model in the stacking model output.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Explainable AI Applications in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a pivotal solution to address the opacity of conventional AI models, particularly in high-stakes applications like healthcare, finance, and security. While machine learning and deep learning excel at predictive tasks, their black box nature hinders interpretability and accountability. XAI aims to rectify this by enabling AI systems to provide understandable explanations for their decisions, fostering trust and transparency between humans and machines. This paper delves into the foundational principles and applications of XAI, emphasizing its role in enhancing collaboration and mitigating risks in AI deployment. Through techniques such as model-agnostic methods and interactive visualization, XAI empowers users to interrogate AI models and uncover biases or errors. Moreover, by enlightening decision-making processes, XAI facilitates comprehension and evaluation, vital for ensuring responsible and ethical AI usage. We examined recently published articles detailing the development and utilization of XAI in the healthcare sector. Our investigation involved searching scholarly databases including Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed for relevant publications spanning from 2018 to 2022. This review not only contributes to the existing body of literature on XAI but also serves as a roadmap for guiding future research endeavors in this burgeoning field.This comprehensive analysis emphasizes the critical role of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in improving trust, transparency, and accountability in healthcare AI applications, establishing the path for further breakthroughs and wider implementation.

articleTitle: Feature Selection for Heart Failure Prediction: A Comparative Analysis of Ranking Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study investigates the worldwide predicament presented by cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), which are the primary contributor to mortality, accounting for around 17.9 million deaths each year and 31% of total global mortality. By applying machine learning (ML) to the analysis of healthcare data, this paper examines the predictive effectiveness of ML models in predicting the risk of heart failure. The datasets utilised in the evaluation comprise features varying in number from 12 to 8. To forecast cardiac failure, it integrates a wide variety of algorithms, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naive Bayes, Decision Tree (DT), and K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN). Furthermore, the research investigates the effectiveness of various feature ranking algorithms-minimum redundancy maximum relevance (MRMR), chisquare (Chi2), ReliefF, ANOVA, and Kruskal-Wallis-in order to enhance the performance of the models. Through a comprehensive analysis of the efficacy of these algorithms in discerning pivotal predictors of heart failure, this article makes a valuable contribution to the advancement of machine learning methodologies utilised in the early detection of heart failure risk. The overarching objective is to mitigate the worldwide burden of cardiovascular disease.

articleTitle: Building a Deep Neural Network for Automated Essay Scoring in English Language Teaching
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Automated Essay Scoring (AES) represents a dynamic frontier in the realm of educational technology, leveraging advancements in deep learning and explainable artificial intelligence to transform assessment practices. This study undertakes a comprehensive exploration of AES, focusing on the rubric level and uncovering decision-making processes for holistic score predictions. The study also introduces faster SHAP implementations, demonstrating their efficiency in enhancing model interpretability. The approach uses linguistic indicators to quantify text cohesiveness, lexical variation, and complex syntactic structures.. The study evaluates the effect of deep learning using the most recent advances in feature selection, model-agnostic methodologies, and natural language processing. It finds that the addition of hidden layers to a neural network’s architecture increases descriptive accuracy by 10%. The novelty of this study lies in its systematic approach to AES, unraveling the AES black box and providing transparency through explanation models. By addressing the limited exploration of AES at the rubric level, the research contributes to the interpretability of scoring decisions, essential for trust in automated grading systems. Leveraging diverse models, including Deep Neural Networks and ensemble techniques, the research achieves notable accuracy rates, with the ensemble model showcasing an impressive 92.5% accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Knee Osteoarthritis Detection and Severity Grading Using Deep Learning and DenseNet169
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research project enhances knee osteoarthritis (KOA) detection using DenseNet169, a deep convolutional neural network. We introduce a novel adaptive early-stopping technique combined with gradual cross-entropy loss estimation to optimize training epochs and mitigate overfitting risks. Evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall demonstrate the model’s superiority over existing methods. DenseNet169, empowered by these adaptive techniques, achieves an exceptional 95% accuracy, surpassing previous models and underscoring its effectiveness in OA diagnosis. The study highlights the importance of accurate diagnostic tools in improving outcomes for KOA patients. Our versatile dataset supports both knee joint detection and OA severity grading in X-ray images, significantly impacting medical imaging and health informatics. Detailed sections on methodology, experimental design, findings, and commentary provide comprehensive insights into the research’s contributions and implications for advancing OA diagnosis and treatment.

articleTitle: Enhancing Industrial IoT Intrusion Detection with Hyperparameter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has changed the way of industrial processes, bringing a new era of connectivity and automation. But as these systems are becoming more interconnected, they are also becoming bigger targets for cyberattacks which is why Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are so important, to spot and react to these threats. However, for IDS to be truly effective in a useful sense, they need to keep pace with the constantly changing nature of cyber attackers. In this study, we explore how hyperparameter optimization can improve IDS performance in IIoT settings. Our study finetunes various parameters to enhance IDS detection of both known and unknown (zero-day) attacks. We tested a variety of hyperparameter optimization methods to see which ones could boost the accuracy, efficiency, and the robustness of the IDS. For the known attacks, we focused on improving classification accuracy, while for unknown attacks, we used k-means clustering to find unusual patterns which may indicate a threat. By fine-tuning these parameters, we aim to create IDS that is more resilient and adaptable to the ever-evolving landscape of cyber threats. We compared our approach to existing methods to evaluate its effectiveness in terms of detection rates and false positives and our results show that hyperparameter optimization can make a clear significant difference in performance of our IDS. This finding could be a game-changer for security in IIoT environments, offering a more robust way to guard against cyberattacks. The insights from this study could also guide future research on optimizing machine learning-based IDS for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Improving Quality of Service in Mobile Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Mobile satellite networks (MSNs) have ended up vital for supplying conversation offerings for a diffusion of functions in challenging areas. MSNs are normally used to offer communication services for faraway regions, supplying connectivity and offerings in regions wherein no other physical infrastructure exists. But, great of provider (QoS) is still a chief situation for MSN operators, specifically for real-time offerings consisting of voice and video streaming. This paper investigates potential solutions for improving the QoS of real-time offerings in MSNs. We first introduce a framework to pick out the key additives of QoS in MSNs, after which have a look at the capacity benefits of integrating technologies, which include gadget studying and software-defined networks computing (SDN-C), and progressive strategies, together with adaptive modulation coding (AMC) and small-shape factor antennas, into the network structure. Next, we endorse an idea for community-level optimization by using combining AMC and SDN-C. We then evaluate the capability of the proposed concept in phrases of decreasing quit-to-end put off and packet loss. Finally, we provide a comprehensive review of present day and future studies guidelines for optimizing and improving the QoS of MSNs.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of a Bioelectric Cell Biosensor Dataset Employing Machine Learning Classifiers for Reliable Listeria Monocytogenes Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Biosensors and machine learning (ML) work well together, particularly in biotechnology, environmental monitoring, and healthcare. Biosensors are instruments that identify particular biological substances or organisms and produce signals that must be deciphered. To analyze these signals and extract useful information, machine learning (ML) is essential. The dataset used in this study was taken from Kaggle and consists of data from the Bioelectric Recognition Assay (BERA) based cell-based biosensor technology and the portable B.EL.D (Bio Electric Diagnostics) instrument created by EMBIO Diagnostics. The study focuses on comparing different machine-learning algorithms applied to the given dataset to improve the accuracy of biosensors in identifying certain biomolecules or pathogens. The machine learning techniques used in this study are binary classifiers, and the most suitable one is selected based on its performance and characteristics. The results show that Decision Tree, KNN, and Support Vector Machine applied with 5-fold cross-validation for the evaluation of the predictive model which can identify listeria in milk samples with an accuracy rate of about 99%. Reaching 99% accuracy with 5-fold cross-validation is a noteworthy accomplishment, particularly when comparing different algorithms. This thorough validation process guarantees the novel combination of robustness and generalizability in the obtained results. ROC curves were plotted for various classifiers to evaluate the model’s performance at the classification threshold. Explainable AI has been used to check the contribution of each feature to the output of the model.

articleTitle: BERT in Cognition for Learner
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Profound subject knowledge is necessary for education to spark creative or formative projects and boost individual’s dynamism. Acquiring a magnificent education is crucial because it permits us to live completely, make wise decisions, and overcome obstacles in life. A learner’s academic journey is continued in early education, which also permits them to become more adept at discriminating between inequity and fairness and equips them for a broader spectrum of activities in higher education. Alongside superficial constraints like threats or financial crises, learners must compose a plethora of delightful and demanding activities in addition to their studies. Therefore, learners can experience moments of cognitive disorientation and progressively acquire cognitive ailments such as stress or depression, to name a couple. Thus, this research suggests a novel Bi-directional Encoder Representations from Transformer (BERT) method for ascertaining learners’ cognitive declines. This research utilizes the BERT-Base architecture, and the hyper-tuning of the hyperparameters is carried out by the innovative Tweaked Shuffled Frog Leaping Algorithm technique. Although there is a high need for language models these days, there are currently no specific language models that can reliably specify a learner’s cognitive deficits according to psychological inqueries. Thus, this work offers a novel strategy known as CogniBERT in response to this. Our approach confounds some of the weaknesses of the BERT methodology by choosing the right scaling factors during training. In terms of training, validation, and testing accuracies, the experimental result surpasses the other approaches, obtaining $\mathbf{9 9. 5 6 \%}, 98.97 \%$, and $99.29 \%$, respectively, when the suggested method is contrasted with a few state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: FPGA based real-time hand gesture recognition system
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Hand gesture recognition is a technology that enables computers to interpret and understand human hand movements, typically through machine learning and image processing algorithms. The proposed system employs contour detection for real-time conversion of input images into binary images, facilitating accurate identification of fingers and thumbs. Rather than relying on other methods, it computes features from detected contours, such as length, convexity defects, and aspect ratio, to categorize 5 different hand gestures. These features serve as valuable inputs for machine learning algorithms, allowing the system to categorize a diverse range of hand gestures effectively. This enables seamless human-machine communication. The system’s unique capability to recognize hand gestures in real time enhances its adaptability across various applications. This approach not only enhances accuracy up to 84.7 percent but also ensures real-world applicability without encountering performance issues like lag or delays. proposed system is compact easy to use and efficient in real time as it reduces the processing time as compared to existing systems.

articleTitle: Multi-user OTFS with Multi-antenna Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: We present a multiple access (MA) scheme with multi-antenna transmission for the recently proposed orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS), orthogonal time sequency multiplexing (OTSM), and the conventional single carrier for block-based transmissions (block SC). In this scheme, users send data streams using upsampled and circularly shifted inverse discrete Fourier transform (IDFT) spread quadrature amplitude modulated (QAM) symbols for OTFS, Walsh-Hadamard (WH) spread QAM symbols for OTSM, and direct QAM symbols for block SC from each transmit antenna in the uplink. These signals pass through different wireless channels and are received at the base station (BS), equipped with multiple antennas. We demonstrate that by stacking the received signals from each antenna at the BS, an equivalent single-user multiple input multiple output (MIMO) received signal is formed for the corresponding scheme (OTFS, OTSM, or Block SC). We also develop a successive interference cancellation (SIC) based receiver for uplink reception. Results show that the SIC receiver improves coded error performance with the order of spatial multiplexing in both single user and multi-user scenarios. We also examine the SIC receiver’s performance for single antenna transmission and multi-antenna reception.

articleTitle: An Efficient Residual Energy Based Routing Strategy for Mobile Nodes in MANETs using the CDROA-OSPF Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This Paper proposes CDROA OSPF and ABO-MDR (Minimum Drain Rate) techniques to reduce the amount of power required by units in a clustered network while transmitting. The CDROA OSPF protocol selects the best path based on each node’s energy usage. The CDROA OSPF protocol has been suggested for determining the best route according to each node’s energy consumption and transferring information from origin to destination. The proposed algorithm will be utilized to determine the best energy-efficient and power-saving approach. Eventually, the communication will be sent between the point of origin and the destination while using less energy. The NS-2 simulation is employed to evaluate the suggested protocol, and the results are compared to those of existing routing strategies. As a consequence, the obtained findings beat conventional methods in terms of many network metrics. The proposed algorithm generates effective results. The best path may be altered using ABO MDR. The power of each node varies depending on its location and motion. Given that nodes can change their paths rapidly because of their substantial mobility, some solution guaranteeing efficient pathways is required. As the nodes displacement is the following explanation: In terms of energy usage (0.1J), packet transmission ratio (0.81), throughput (1.2Mbps), routing burden (0.02), and delay (70 ms), the recommended ABO MDR clearly delivers better outcomes, according to the results. The CDROA OSPF algorithm was designed to determine the best path based on the energy consumption of each node. The CDROA OSPF method is suggested for finding the best path based on every node’s energy consumption and conveying information from source to destination. Then, since the node has shifted, the ABO MDR issued to rearrange the best path. Each node’s energy changes depending on its movement and position.

articleTitle: A Review of Soybean Crop Classification and Disease Identification Using AI Learning and IoT-Based Model
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A review of understanding crop disease identification and classification using artificial intelligence and IOT-based models for driving learning approaches. AI-based unsupervised algorithms, Convolution Neural Networks (CNN), and image processing methods facilitate and are used in soybean plants for validations of germination and health. Further, various techniques exist to identify different diseases and help pre-alarm the farmers to reduce agriculture waste and resources. The AI methods are appropriate for improving the production cycle and yielding high-quality-based production. The technologies are focused on the stepwise farming of soybean crops. This review suggested enhancement ideology for soybean crop germination and prevention of diseases. Specifically, reviews concentrate on integrating the deep learning algorithm, Residual Convolution Neural Network (ResCNN), to monitor plant condition and growth from leaf to root. This review suggested various developments and uses of IOT-based robotic sensors for image classification of Soybean crops and proposed the best method for disease identification. The review facilitates the deployment of an AI learning called ResCNN for segmenting the images where the classification predicts the plant health, and plant root conditions with suggestions for the prevention steps for the growth of plants.

articleTitle: Gastrointestinal Ulcer Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Stomach ulcers, also known as gastric ulcers, are sores that develop on the lining of the stomach. They are prevalent gastrointestinal disorders with significant morbidity and healthcare costs. Early prediction of ulcer development is crucial for timely intervention and prevention of complications. The primary cause of stomach ulcers is often attributed to the infection with bacteria. Other contributing factors may include the prolonged use of aspirin and ibuprofen, as well as excessive alcohol consumption, smoking, and stress. It is essential to seek medical attention if you suspect you have a stomach ulcer or are experiencing persistent abdominal pain and discomfort. Diagnosis typically involves tests like endoscopy, where a flexible tube with a camera is inserted through the mouth to examine the stomach lining. These ulcers have become very common nowadays and many people are suffering from ulcer and for finding the occurrence the existing algorithms have less accuracy. Utilizing MobileNetV3 as a pretrained base model in transfer learning offers a powerful and efficient approach for medical image classification tasks, especially when faced with limited labelled data. It combines the advantages of pre-trained feature extraction, fine-tuning, and data augmentation for improved model performance. MobileNetV3 is a classical convolutional neural network architecture which is based on an analysis of how to increase the depth of such networks.

articleTitle: The smart optimization model for Predictive Analysis of Supply Chain using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The integration of predictive analytics and IoT alludes to the combination of advanced analytics and data collected from connected devices, or the so-called Internet of Things (IoT). This integration provides businesses with the opportunity to optimize their supply chain by leveraging accurate insights on demand fluctuations and asset performance. Two areas are of particular importance in applying predictive analytics and IoT on the optimization of a supply chain. The first area pertains to the collection of data from IoT sensors. This involves the implementation of a proper data acquisition architecture, including both an effective network of protocol-enabled connected elements and a commensurate software platform for centralizing and analyzing the collected data. The second area involves leveraging predictive models and other advanced analytics techniques in order to generate forecasts of future processes and conditions, allowing for techniques such as dynamic demand forecasting or predictive maintenance approaches to be used for supply chain optimization.

articleTitle: Automatic Creation of Ontologies and Rules from ML Models for Access Control in IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Ontologies have been increasingly used in designing access control policies in Internet of Things (IoT) systems. Machine Learning (ML) has been extensively used to identify patterns from existing data. Trained ML models can be used on end devices for applying access control for resources and users. However it is unreasonable to deploy ML models into the low-powered and mostly hand-held IoT devices. This paper demonstrates an attempt to exploit the power of ML for generating access control rules. We propose algorithms for generating Ontologies and policy rules from trained ML models. Motivated by their simple design, low or almost no requirement for data preprocessing, no requirement for scaling/normalization of data, simple, intuitive design, and most essentially an inherent ability to optimize, by handling irrelevant features through pruning, we use Decision Trees (DT) for the classification in the proposed approach. For smart home dataset, we show in this paper, automatic creation of Ontologies and policy rules from trained DT models. The resulting Ontologies and Semantic Web Rule Language (SWRL) rules are then deployed into an Ontological framework (Protege) and tested for consistency using a Reasoner. Our approach demonstrates a significant improvement in the efficiency of rule generation and offers a promising direction towards designing automated access control systems. In Protege, we achieve 100% consistency in deployment and testing of the generated access control policies by firing queries. We obtain exactly the same accuracy from Protege queries as we get from ML model. We also propose pruning on DT as a fall-back method for IoT devices with limited computing and memory resources that can handle only limited number of policy rules. The proposed method creates a deployable access control system in a few minutes without any human intervention. Our experiment shows a turnaround time of $\mathbf{5}$ minutes for the Smart Home dataset.

articleTitle: Counterfeit Pharmaceutical Product Detection Using Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Counterfeit medicines rank among the most dangerous threats to world health, with an additional menace to global economic stability. This paper delves into the use of blockchain technology as an intervention strategy to curb this vice within the pharmaceutical industry. Blockchain, with its essential characteristics of decentralization, transparency, and immutability, seems to be an optimal solution for creating a highly secured and verifiable pharmaceutical supply chain. A blockchain-based system for pharmaceutical products, which would ensure integrity and authenticity while going from production to the point of delivery to the final user, has been suggested. Our assessment, through a detailed case study and comprehensive literature review, reveals significant enhancements in drug traceability, transparency, and regulatory compliance. It aims to increase consumer confidence by improving drug traceability and reducing the incidence of counterfeit products. Initial results are promising, pointing to a reduction of counterfeiting activities and an increase in regulatory compliance. This paper focuses on the ways blockchain could change the pharmaceutical supply chain. It specifically points out the fact that blockchain has a huge possibility to become a critical tool in protecting public health and economic interests from the pervasive threat of counterfeit drugs.

articleTitle: Online Food Order Management System With Recommendation Integrated ASP.Net and Microsoft SQL Server
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Online food ordering management system with recommendation is a full-fledged software model based on the Database Management, SQL and ASP.Net to minimize the manual work for the workers of the hotel. This helps to even customers to order their food easily in this evolving software world. This model has many features like Ordering food, Menu and Category updating by the Admin, Customers order history, Total payment done in a day, selling report of the hotel from a date to date, Login and mainly the recommendation for the customer. The software and hardware requirements for this software model are easily available and easy to work with. This helps us to keep track of all the data for long years. As the KNN classifier recommends the user. This software is completely based on the administration level as the DB admin can manage. The total workflow of the project and the work of DB admin explained in the methodology section.

articleTitle: A Novel Ensemble Technique for Diabetes Detection using LS-SVM Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Millions of people worldwide suffer from diabetes, a chronic illness for which early detection is essential to successful treatment. Here, we present a novel diabetes classification model that achieves improved accuracy and reliability by utilizing a variety of machine learning models and ensemble methodologies. In particular, we investigate the efficacy of an ensemble voting classifier, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gradient Boosting, and Logistic Regression. Through rigorous experimentation, we observed that the ensemble of these models outperforms individual classifiers. Our approach yields an impressive classification accuracy of $\mathbf{9 7. 1 \%}$ on the Pima Indian dataset [12], surpassing the performance of existing models.

Author Keywords: Adaptive Boosting with Support Vector Machine (AdaBoost+SVM)

articleTitle: Enhancing Rumor Detection of Twitter Tweets Using a Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Information spreads swiftly via social media in response to breaking news, modifying several aspects of the data. Nevertheless, it’s crucial to understand that early modifications can have been brought about by hearsay or unconfirmed information. Unverified data can be labeled to stop potentially false information from spreading. Rumor detection provides more data to a rumor-tracking system that evaluates the veracity of the rumors. In recent research, predictive models such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Conditional Random Fields (CRF), and Random Forests have been employed to detect rumors. Twitter, a popular medium for exchanging information, rebranded itself as $\mathbf{X}$ in response to recent changes in social networking sites. This shift might affect the dynamics of information sharing and represents a major turning point in social media history. We were able to employ the Deep Neural Network (DNN), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models to detect rumors in recent narratives by investigating the sequential differences in reporting when news breaks on social media platforms. LSTM obtained $88.55 \%$ test accuracy, DNN achieved $85.44 \%$ test accuracy, and GRU achieved $\mathbf{8 9. 6 2 \%}$ test accuracy based on the test data.

articleTitle: Advancements in Enhancing Solar Photovoltaic System Efficiency: A Comprehensive Literature Review of Applications and Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The transition to sustainable energy solutions necessitates a deep understanding of advancements in solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies. This analysis delves into recent advancements and creative strategies aimed at enhancing the effectiveness of Solar Photovoltaic Systems. This review focuses on six interconnected technologies in solar power generation: thin-film cells, Crystalline cells, Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSCs), Quantum Dot-Sensitized Solar Cells (QDSCs), Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) and Perovskite Solar Cells (PSCs). It explores their characteristics, mechanisms, historical development, fundamental properties, operational principles, and commercialization challenges. By synthesizing insights drawn from these technologies, the review conducts a comprehensive analysis of the current state and future prospects of solar photovoltaic (PV) research and development. Its goal is to enlighten researchers, engineers, policymakers and stakeholders, enabling informed decision-making and expediting the global uptake of sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Harnessing NLP to align Candidate Profile with Position Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: To showcase one’s talents and experience, using a resume is generally one of the more used and accepted approaches. It is usually written in several file formats (pdf, txt, doc, etc.) and in a variety of inconsistent styles with distinct personalized approaches. Job ads in the current digital era draw a flood of applications in a short amount of time. Hiring organizations incur cost challenges in addition to time-consuming delays when sorting through resumes manually. Selecting a candidate for a job solely on the basis of whether their resume matches a list of qualifications is usually a difficult, demanding, time-consuming, and effort-intensive process. Furthermore, the conventional screening procedure frequently lacks impartiality, which causes potentially qualified applicants to be passed over or unfit individuals to be chosen. Leveraging Natural Language Processing (NLP), in order to classify resumes into predetermined job categories, this study investigates the use of three machine learning algorithms: Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM), Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). To convert textual data into numerical form, a large dataset of resumes annotated with job categories is first pre-processed and vectorized using TF-IDF. Next, the efficacy of KNN, MNB, and Bi-LSTM models in classifying resumes according to their content is trained and assessed. After the classification phase, the cosine similarity score between the resume and job description vectors is computed using the trained models to match resumes with job descriptions. This two-step method seeks to improve the accuracy of matching candidates with appropriate job roles and streamline the hiring process by automating resume classification.

articleTitle: Economic Dispatch for multi agent Power Systems using Peer to Peer Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical control technique for AC microgrid inverters, utilizing a sparse communication network to reduce communication overhead. The controller focuses on average voltage regulation, network frequency restoration, and real-time economic dispatch, combining economic dispatch and frequency restoration at the secondary level. Reactive power and voltage controllers ensure network average voltage regulation and proportionate sharing, keeping output voltages near nominal levels and enabling individual inverters to fulfill reactive power demands, with convergence determined using Lyapunov stability criteria. The proposed controller, validated through simulation results and experimental validation, offers a decentralized method for managing multiple inverters in an AC microgrid, ensuring stability and reliability in changing conditions. It can withstand load fluctuations and communication failures, proving its robustness and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Exploring K-Means Meta-Heuristic Techniques For Prediction of Anomalies In IoT-Enabled Industrial Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Due to the broad implementation of the Internet of Things (IoT) in industrial systems, the introduction of Industry 4.0 resulted in a significant increase in operational efficiency. However, it also resulted in the introduction of new challenges when it came to identifying abnormalities. This paper presents a new method for boosting the flexibility and precision of anomaly detection models by integrating the best aspects of K-Means clustering with meta-heuristic approaches. The utilisation of K-Means meta-heuristic techniques is the driving force behind this research, which is being driven by the growing demand for reliable anomaly prediction in industrial systems that are enabled by the IoT. Aiming to discover methods that can improve the reliability of anomaly detection algorithms is the objective of this research. K-Means clustering is systematically integrated with metaheuristic techniques in this study, which allows for the optimisation of the clustering algorithm for the purpose of detecting abnormalities in industrial data that is enabled by the IoT. We use real-world datasets from a wide range of businesses in order to measure the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in comparison to more traditional ways. The results demonstrate that the K-Means meta-heuristic strategy greatly enhances the accuracy of anomaly detection in comparison to the approaches that are considered conventional. Recall, false positive rates, and precision are all areas in which it excels beyond its capabilities. The results indicate that this unique approach has the potential to be useful when applied to the challenges of anomaly detection in industrial systems that are enabled by the IoT.

articleTitle: Accurate Anomia Severity Detection in Post-Stroke Aphasia Patients using MobileNetV2
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for the detection of anomia severity, which is one of the symptoms of poststroke aphasia patients. Anomia is an inability to recall or name words that characterizes aphasia which is often the result of strokes or traumatic brain injury. In the proposed method, we train the melspectrograms taken from the audio recordings of the aphasia patients’ using MobileNetV2. The proposed method has been evaluated on APROCSA dataset with level of severity classified as light, moderate, and marked. Performance comparison results show that the proposed MobileNetV2 approach exhibited highest accuracy of $\mathbf{99.59\%}$, outperforming the other models; CNN, GoogleNet, and SqueezeNet. The study thus presents a promising tool for automated and precise estimation of the severity of anomia, which helps physicians track patients’ recovery and optimize rehabilitation treatments.

articleTitle: A MultiModal Neural Network Architecture for Document Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Document classification is a crucial domain in natural language processing that involves classifying text documents into predefined categories. However, in multiple cases, the documents are heterogeneous with different modalities such as images and flow diagrams, giving rise to the need for handling multiple modalities. Thus, multimodal document classification enables a more comprehensive understanding of document content by incorporating multiple modalities such as text and images. This enhances information extraction and enables more accurate categorization of documents, benefiting various applications such as content organization, search, recommendation systems, and information retrieval. This work proposes a deep learning approach that leverages both textual and image information for improved classification of multimodal documents. Our multimodal deep neural network architecture utilizes two different channels in processing the multimodal features: text and document images. The textual model leverages BERT to generate embeddings of the text, while the image feature extraction channel employs a hybrid architecture consisting of the pre-trained convolutional neural network model VGG-19 as the backbone followed by a vision transformer. The two different channels are incorporated into a unified framework that performs the final classification. The training and testing of the proposed framework were conducted on the benchmark TOBACCO-3482 dataset, demonstrating the effectiveness and potential of our proposed multimodal classification approach. The TOBACCO-3482 dataset is a widely used benchmark dataset for document image analysis and classification. The effectiveness in performing the classification of the proposed framework is evaluated on the grounds of performance metrics such as confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

articleTitle: AI-powered Prediction of 19 Personality Traits
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Graphology or handwriting analysis is the most powerful science of understanding the strengths and weaknesses of a person, it reflects one’s personality. It shows how the writer thinks, feels, and acts, what personality traits one possesses, and what one lacks. The personality in terms of various attributes like anger, self-esteem, pessimism, fear, honesty, work habits, social skills, etc. can be profiled using Graphology. The personality traits are based on various handwriting features like line spacing, margins, slant, letter size, text density, baseline inclination, etc. The proposed method utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to extract eleven distinct features from the letter ‘t’. Additionally, a support vector machine (SVM) integrated with the OpenCV library is employed to extract seven handwriting-independent features. These features are normalized and assigned labels based on experimentally determined thresholds. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves a minimum classification accuracy of $95 \%$ when tested against various handwritten documents.

articleTitle: Investigating the Performance of Deep Learning Algorithms for Hyper Spectral Time Series Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Deep learning algorithms are swiftly becoming one of the maximum famous strategies for analyzing and modeling hyper spectral time series data. Given the mathematical complexity of hyper spectral facts, deep learning can play an essential role in effectively capturing the underlying tendencies inside the information. In this paper, we investigate the performance of deep getting to know algorithms for hyper spectral time collection modeling. In specially, we awareness on convolutional neural community (CNN) architectures, namely, Inception-ResNetV2 and the Temporal Convolution community (TCN). To research the overall performance of those architectures, we evaluate the accuracies and training instances of numerous datasets. We additionally consist of a comparative overall performance take a look at of each network on the equal datasets. Our consequences show that the Inception-ResNetV2 achieves better accuracy than the TCN underneath various settings. Additionally, the InceptionResNetV2 also drastically outperforms the TCN in terms of education time. Based totally on our effects, we recommend that the Inception-ResNetV2 must be the algorithm of desire for hyper spectral time series modeling.

articleTitle: Leveraging Advanced Machine Learning Algorithms for Loan Repayment Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Accurately predicting loan repayment behavior is a critical challenge for financial institutions, which often face high default rates and financial instability due to inaccurate credit assessments. In order to address these problems, this study looks into the application of sophisticated machine learning methods such Random Forests, Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines, and Stacking Classifiers. The models, trained on diverse client variables, significantly outperform traditional credit scoring methods. The findings suggest that integrating these sophisticated models can enhance financial performance, reduce default risks, and enable more informed lending decisions. The study also examines potential avenues for future research, including the application of increasingly sophisticated machine learning techniques and the integration of new data sources to enhance models. This study advances the field of machine learning in finance by providing business and academics with insightful information that could result in stronger and more secure financial systems.

articleTitle: Personalized Travel Itinerary Recommender System using Tkinter and SQLite
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of travel planning, the ‘Trip Planner” application is highly recommended. Using Python, Tkinter, and SQLite managed through pandas, this tool enhances user interaction with technology, offering a user-friendly platform for selecting hotels, generating itineraries, and preserving travel plans. articleTitle: AyurChat: Empowering Health through AI-Driven Ayurvedic Guidance
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: AyurChat is a project aiming to transform healthcare discussions by blending intelligence (AI) with the wisdom of Ayurveda. The innovative chatbot system, known as AyurChat acts as a health companion offering personalized advice, for medical queries. The main goal of AyurChat is to empower individuals to manage their health through natural solutions rooted in Ayurvedic principles. By utilizing cutting edge language processing and machine learning techniques, AyurChat engages in conversations with users understanding their health concerns and providing tailored guidance based on Ayurveda. This system aims to improve access to healthcare by bridging the gap between technology and traditional healing practices. With a ranging knowledge base covering Ayurvedic remedies AyurChat ensures thorough and precise responses to user’s health inquiries. Through AI driven algorithms evolves over time, enhancing its grasp of user needs and refining its recommendations continuously. AyurChat stands as an endeavor that uses AI to make Ayurvedic healthcare knowledge more accessible. Offering discussions and personalized advice it provides users with treatments from the realm of Ayurveda rather than conventional Western medicine along with web links for alternative medicines, like Siddha and Unani.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Secure Shell (SSH) as a Wireless Network Security Tool
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Comfy Shell is an open-source protocol used for many years to comfy community logins and communication over the net. It is primarily based on public key cryptography and is well known for being one of the maximum cozy strategies of authentication and communication. It is now being explored as a Wi-Fi network security device for defensive information transmitted over WiFi networks, including those typically determined in cafes, airports, and other public locations. Its safety capabilities, which include robust authentication and encryption, make it an excellent desire to securely access assets, shift information, and connect to far-off structures. Moreover, it can be used as a digital private network (VPN) to safely establish connections between two or extra computers in a public community. At the same time as SSH is properly-appropriate for relaxed far-off connections, it can be configured to provide additional ranges of authentication and encryption to ensure the WiFi network’s safety from malicious assaults. This paper will explore the capability of SSH as a Wi-Fi network safety tool, discuss diverse implementations, and focus on the particular components of using SSH as a security device for WiFi networks.

articleTitle: The Impact of Automated Systems on HRM Algorithms in Multinational Companies
