Additionally, some interpretability methods employed here such as Shapley additive explanations SHAP analysis or line analysis give us insights into decision making by these models. The paper provides a complete approach towards securing networks effectively thus filling up this missing link between deep learning in research on cybersecurity implementation.

articleTitle: Automated Classification of Medical Images Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Medical imagery has been increasingly used in diagnosing and treating various diseases, leading to advances in healthcare. While humans usually lead the qualitative interpretation of visual features, Automated Classification of Medical Images Using Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) has gained traction for accurate image classification. CNNs are a type of deep learning algorithm that attempts to mimic the structure of the human brain and are ideal for image classification due to their convolution layers that can detect patterns within the image. These convolution layers enable the networks to learn the characteristics of the data through a series of convolution and pooling operations. Additionally, they can rapidly identify relationships and patterns within the dataset and extract features from the input image, thus allowing a more accurate classification. With the increasing availability of medical imaging data, advancements in the field of ML/AI has enabled the use of CNNs for automated medical image classification, helping clinicians to diagnose diseases accurately with less time and effort.

articleTitle: A Visual Approach to Understand Parsing Algorithms through Python and Manim
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Even with the growth of computer science and availability of new areas of specialization, the problem of building compilers continues to be a core subject and offered at many universities around the world. This area is not easy to teach and explore due to the number and specificity of the algorithms and ideas offered. The educational software systems are a critical component in the engineering education, as they enhance learning processes, since theoretical concepts and ideas are presented in a tangible form. So in this work a simple tool is developed, in Python that demonstrates the parsing processes of LL(1), LR(0),,LR(1), and LALR As the tool needs to generate a large and high quality visualizations such as syntax trees and step-by-step parsing animations, it is based on the Manim animation engine. The use of this tool for different grammars and input strings aids in learning the parsing algorithms while debugging and developing grammars can be made easier with the help of visualizations.

articleTitle: Predicting Protein-Protein Interactions Using Self-Attention-Based Deep Neural Networks and FastText Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Predicting Protein-protein interactions are central to understanding the intricate mechanisms governing cellular functions, as proteins seldom act in isolation. While current machine learning and deep learning models focus on encoding protein sequences based on residue composition or physicochemical properties, they often overlook the complex relationships between amino acid segments within lengthy sequences. To address these limitations, we propose a novel hybrid model that combines a self-attention to enhance Deep neural network feature extraction with an with FastText Protein embeddings for predicting PPI. Utilizing transfer learning via the unsupervised FastText embedding technique to derive statistical representations of protein sequences, offers advantages over traditional protein encoding techniques in the context of analysing k-Mer sequences. Our model’s performance is assessed through $\mathbf{5 - f o l d}$ cross-validation on datasets of S.Cerevisiae and Human-Bacillus Anthracis protein interactions, resulting in accuracies of $\mathbf{9 2. 2 8 \%}$ and $\mathbf{9 4. 0 8 \%}$, respectively. Compared to existing machine learning models, our model demonstrates superior performance on both datasets.

articleTitle: Auditory aid for understanding images for Visually Impaired Students using CNN and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The world is leading towards an equal experience in learning in all educational environments, it is also a world where visual content dominates the digital landscape. Hence it is our collective responsibility to ensure that no one is left in the shadows of the information age. By utilizing the power of image captioning, we are championing the cause of inclusion, enabling people with visual impairments to navigate the digital world with confidence and ease. This assistive technology is proposed to promote accessibility and inclusion in literature, allowing people with visual impairments to engage with a wide range of written works. We performed various evaluations to demonstrate the effectiveness of this proposed model, demonstrating its potential to improve the reading experience of blind people, thereby promoting independence and accessibility. Through this paper, we propose an innovative approach that aims to develop adaptive assistive technology to enable visually impaired people to access written and visual content. Ways to design a method of creating descriptive text descriptions of images and making it easier for blind people to understand visual content were explored. This research can be applied in promoting social inclusion of blind people in various fields and can be extended from the idea of blind students understanding images in textbooks to the blind public to have accessible E-learning in digital learning platforms to enrich their reading experience, in archives to understand historic artifacts such as images in historic documents, in Public Transportation to blind travelers to access important information in Transportation apps and digital displays, in social media platforms for blind users to understand shared images, in blind users being able to comprehend visual elements in their health reports and diagnostic images and overall empowering visually challenged individuals to traverse the digital world with ease and confidence.

articleTitle: Enhanced Underwater Object Detection Using Deep Neural networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The identification of marine animals has become a significant area of data processing and analysis due to the growing volume of underwater visual data and deep sea exploration. The imperative nature of safeguarding the environment underscores the significance of this undertaking; nonetheless, challenges persist due to factors such as intricate underwater scenery, subpar image and video clarity, and the diverse range of motions shown by marine organisms. To solve these challenges, this study used deep learning algorithms to recognize certain marine species and indicate their presence in submitted photos and videos using bounding boxes. The primary objective is to provide practical techniques for identifying marine species, so offering essential support for more research in this field. The study made considerable advancements in detection speed and mean average precision (mAP) for marine species identification by using the key deep learning frameworks, YOLOv3, YOLOv8, and Faster-RCNN. This study project not only resolves the present issues with marine animal detection, but it also lays the foundation for future studies aimed at understanding and safeguarding the delicate underwater ecosystem.

articleTitle: Code Mixed English-Malayalam Sentiment Analysis and Sarcasm Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The unparalleled use of social media has resulted in a surge of human emotional interaction creating a huge amount of data which is of high value in fields from marketing to governance. In a highly multilingual society this also creates a huge amount of unstructured code mixed data. The development of systems for sentiment analysis and sarcasm detection becomes of critical importance. In this study we collect code mixed Malayalam-English data from YouTube comments and label them for both the tasks, thereby creating a dataset of code-mixed Malayalam-English dataset. We utilize various machine learning and Deep learning techniques to analyze the sentiment and detect the sarcasm. Evaluation of the models was carried out on the metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1-Score. Among the models Support Vector Machine performed better among Supervised Machine Learning methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing Industrial Applications with LSTM-Based Predictive Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Predictive analytics in industrial applications has the potential to significantly boost productivity and enhance operational efficiency. The research intends to solve is the difficulty of traditional models to capture the detailed temporal correlations and complex non-linear patterns that are common in industrial data. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based predictive analytics are the primary focus of this research, with the primary objective being the enhancement of industrial processes. Predicting complex and ever-changing patterns within operational data is a challenge in the modern industrial environment. The allocation of resources and decision-making processes are not as ideal as they may be. The LSTM architecture enables to use of the temporal correlations of the data in order to improve ability to predict the future. LSTM-based predictive analytics are significantly more accurate than conventional models when it comes to predicting the events that will occur in industrial processes. The findings shows LSTM-based predictive analytics have the potential to revolutionize industrial decision-making, which in turn leads to improved resource management and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Adaptability of Denoising Models for Low Dose CT Images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Computed Tomography (CT) is a fundamental diagnostic imaging modality that utilizes various technologies. A CT scan involves capturing multiple X -ray images from various angles around the body and then utilizing computer algorithms to generate detailed cross-sectional images, or slices, depicting the blood vessels, tissues and bones of the patient. The imperative for enhanced imaging often necessitates exposing individuals to substantial doses of ionizing radiation, particularly in instances involving repeated CT scans or elevated radiation doses. In response to radiation-related concerns, Low Dose CT (LDCT) has emerged as a key focus of research, reducing patient exposure to merely 25 percent of the radiation associated with conventional Full Dose CT (FDCT) scans. Despite its evident advantages in radiation reduction, LDCT images tends to yield images characterized by heightened random noise and artifacts. The intrinsic challenges in LDCT images compromise their clinical utility, affecting diagnostic accuracy. Present denoising methodologies often prioritize quantitative metrics, potentially resulting in over-denoised and blurred CT images, neglecting realistic image preservation. This study evaluates contemporary general image denoising techniques alongside deep learning denoising methods specifically tailored for low-dose computed tomography, focusing on their ability to preserve high-frequency details and the realism of the resulting denoised images. The objective is highlight the state of current deep learning denoising models and find models that are able to achieve both improved metrics and produce realistic denoised image outputs.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Patterns With Deep Learning For Classification For Indian Pines
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Indian Pines test site, located primarily in north-western Indiana, is renowned for its Airborne Visible InfraRed Imaging Spectrometer (AVIRIS) scene, which has been extensively studied over the years. The hyperspectral nature of this image introduces challenges related to pixel mixture complexity, creating difficulties for supervised subpixel detection and mixed-pixel classification. Despite the prevalent use of supervised approaches for this scene due to the complexity of forming an appropriate sample pool for supervised classification, there is limited research on supervised classification for this image. The study leverages cutting-edge deep learning models and transfer learning techniques, including ResNet50 (99.68% accuracy), InceptionV3 (99.55% accuracy), DenseNet121 (99.10% accuracy), and MobileNetV3 (99.94% accuracy). These models are employed for predictive analysis, highlighting their effectiveness in handling the complexities of the Indian Pines scene and showcasing their high accuracy rates in supervised image classification. This research contributes valuable insights into the application of deep learning and transfer learning methodologies, offering a promising approach to addressing the challenges presented by complex hyperspectral imagery.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Pre-Trained Models for Hate Speech Detection on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The growing spread of hate speech across social networking is getting harder to use that demands ever further sophistication in measurement tools. This paper sought to do the same by understanding if currently available pre-trained transformer models can be effective hate speech identifiers while measuring their performance on critical metrics. In particular, the study aimed to do the same for the best available transformer-based transformers - ALBERT, BART, BERT, DistilBERT, and RoBERTa - through a comparison of their F1 Score, F1.5 Score, recall, accuracy, and precision. This made it much easier to understand the model’s strengths and weaknesses. It is RoBERTa that emerges as the top performer with an accuracy of ${0. 8 9 1 2}$ $(89 \%)$. At the same time, it is easy to see that this model can become a game-changing tool for identifying hate speech using existing infrastructure. Additionally, one can also better understand the tradeoffs this model makes between precision and recall. It makes it easier to understand how these models operate when deployed. In the end, this paper shows how it is possible to further the current discussion around AI for good by presenting a relatively unbiased view of current achievement to create safer-online-spaces. As such, this paper also aims to influence how future hate speech detection projects are developed and deployments are managed.

articleTitle: Hex-Cell Clustering Based Distributed Service Discovery Algorithm for MANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Mobile Ad-Hoc Network (MANET) is a type of wireless network consisting of mobile devices (such as laptops, smartphones, tablets, etc.) that communicate with each other without the need for a centralized infrastructure like base stations or access points. MANETs are highly dynamic and adaptable, making them suitable for scenarios where traditional infrastructure-based networks are impractical or unavailable. Service discovery remains a formidable challenge in MANETs, with the primary concern being the efficient assignment of optimal services to service requesters. This study proposes a novel Hex-cell Clustering based Distributed Service Discovery Algorithm (HC-DSDA) tailored specifically for MANETs. Utilizing a hexagonal grid structure for clustering, the algorithm appoints a Mobile Cluster Head (MCH) within each cell, tasked with coordinating with other MCHs in their respective cells. The Mscore (Mobile Score) concept were introduced to select MCH in an efficient manner which is calculated through the trust parameters of each mobile node. Extensive simulations validate the efficacy of the proposed algorithm, showcasing enhancements in precision, recall, F-measure, and time consumption. These results underscore the algorithm’s potential in improving service discovery within MANETs, thereby addressing critical challenges in dynamic network environments.

articleTitle: Fusion of Machine Learning and Deep Learning:A Hybrid Approach for Deepfake Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Deepfakes refer to artificially generated digital media designed to produce highly realistic fake videos, often with the intention of deceiving the viewer. Techniques like Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are commonly employed to achieve this goal. These methods generate content that closely resembles real visuals, making it challenging for conventional detection techniques to differentiate between real and fake content. Detection systems often rely on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based discriminators to identify such synthesized media. However, these systems mainly focus on the spatial characteristics of individual video frames and may struggle to capture temporal information from the relationships between frames. This paper employs a hybrid methodology that combines machine learning and deep learning techniques to address the issue of deepfakes. Initially, we utilized a CNN model, specifically VGG16, for extracting features. Subsequently, we employed two machine learning models, Random Forest and XGBoost, to classify the data into real and fake categories. The Random Forest-CNN model achieved a higher accuracy compared to the XGBoost-CNN model, which in turn surpassed many other techniques in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Assisted Trust Management in Vehicular Ad-Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication is crucial in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSs) for enhancing road safety, traffic efficiency, and convenience. To address the need for trust in V2X communications, a trust management system for Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) using blockchain technology has been proposed. This system calculates dynamic trust scores for vehicles based on direct communication, recommendations from other vehicles, and proximity to roadside units (RSUs). The trust scores are stored in a transparent and tamperproof blockchain, ensuring the immutability and transparency of trust scores. Simulations demonstrate that this blockchain-based trust management system significantly improves the security and reliability of V2X communications. This system is essential for the widespread acceptance of VANETs by fostering a trusted communication environment.

articleTitle: Real-Time Prediction of Patient Recovery Time using AI-driven Optimization Techniques in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Industry 4.0, or the Fourth Industrial Revolution, is revolutionizing manufacturing processes by linking traditional (AI) and modern industrial practices such as the Internet of Things (Iota) and big data analytics. Industry 4.0 aims to optimize efficiency, flexibility, and connectivity in all production processes to increase productivity while reducing costs. Industry 4.0 covers real-time automation and cloud computing as primary factors that will help achieve its complete potential RPA platform along with technology trends like AI and Iota coupled through them to help monitor and control the production processes in real-time that can give valuable data insights at a time to make instant adjustments (if necessary). The same helps improve efficiency, minimize downtime, and improve decision-making. In contrast, cloud computing helps to store and process the enormous data created by Industry 4.0 technologies. This data is then analyzed and used to identify patterns and trends, which can give invaluable information for streamlining production. When combined, cloud computing and real-time automation make a perfect platform for Industry 4.

articleTitle: Exploring the Efficacy of Mental Health Care Chatbots: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This comprehensive review paper examines the land-scape of mental health care chatbots, focusing on their design, effectiveness, ethical considerations, and future directions. Mental health care chatbots have emerged as innovative tools to support individuals in managing their mental well-being, offering a range of services from diagnosis to therapy. Furthermore, the paper discusses the importance of meeting standards, regulations, and protecting user privacy in implementing AI-based mental health interventions. It addresses the need to inform mental health providers and users about the main features and potential benefits of chatbots, while also considering the challenges of oversight and accountability. It emphasizes the importance of social and emotional aspects in chatbot design, highlighting dimensions like sociability, empathy, and understandable medical vocabulary. Ethical considerations in digital mental health care, including assessment, diagnosis, and treatment, are also addressed in the review. It discusses the educational implications of mental health care chatbots and offers research recommendations for future studies, including investigations into mobile apps for mental health and addressing challenges in digital mental health research.

articleTitle: Smart-Child Tracking System with LoRa and GPS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In response to growing concerns about child safety, there’s a rising demand for innovative child tracking systems. Combining LoRa and GPS technologies presents a solution that offers both long-range coverage and low power consumption, crucial for wearable devices. GPS ensures accurate location data, while LoRa enables energy-efficient transmission over extended distances. This system provides a cost-effective and secure alternative to cellular networks, alerting parents if a child strays from designated safe zones. The design includes wearable devices equipped with LoRa modules for transmitting location data. These devices communicate wirelessly using ESP8266 modules, with a web server retrieving and displaying real-time location data on a map. Key features like geofencing enable parents to define safe zones and receive alerts if a child enters or leaves these areas. The implementation demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of using LoRa technology for child tracking. Compared to traditional GPS systems, the LoRa and GPS approach offers advantages such as lower power consumption, longer battery life, high accuracy, and improved indoor and outdoor coverage. These features make it an ideal solution for ensuring children’s safety and security in various environments.

articleTitle: NBA MVP Prediction and Historical Analysis Using Cross-Era Comparison Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In order to understand the crucial player statistics that decide the Most Valuable Player (MVP) Trophy, this research study dives into a substantial 32-year dataset of the National Basketball Association (NBA). We build a predictive framework trained on historical player statistics and MVP voting results using a sophisticated ensemble of machine learning models, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), ElasticNet, AdaBoost, Random Forest and Back-propagation Neural Network (BP). We determine the key elements influencing this renowned award by evaluating connections between player stats and MVP picks. Our research provides insights into the MVP selection process by utilising the models’ ability to capture complex patterns and nonlinear interactions, providing stakeholders with a reliable tool for assessing player performances.This work advances the discourse surrounding the NBA MVP Trophy and enriches our comprehension of player value assessment. Also, the prediction models are used to conduct various historical analysis experiments, by finding an objective method to compare performances of players from different eras.

articleTitle: Prediction and Management of Traffic Congestion in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Efficient urban traffic congestion management is paramount for ensuring smooth vehicular flow, minimizing travel time, and reducing environmental pollution. In this context, utilizing intelligent intersection technologies emerges as a promising approach to tackling traffic challenges effectively. This paper presents an in-depth analysis of the “Intelligent Intersection” framework, a novel system designed to optimize traffic flow at intersections through advanced sensing, data processing, and control mechanisms. The research integrates the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model for urban traffic prediction, Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) for realistic traffic simulations, and adaptive traffic light control algorithms. Additionally, the integration of Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communication, particularly Dedicated Short Range Communication (DSRC), facilitates efficient coordination between vehicles and infrastructure elements. Through comprehensive experimentation and evaluation, the effectiveness of this approach in mitigating traffic congestion, reducing travel time, and promoting sustainable transportation practices is demonstrated. This research contributes to the advancement of intelligent transportation systems and lays the groundwork for future innovations in urban mobility management.

articleTitle: Secure And Energy-Efficient Multi-Objective MetaHeuristic Routing Protocol for MANET
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study introduces the Secure and Energy-Efficient Multi-Objective Meta-Heuristic Routing (SEEMOMHR) protocol, designed for mobile Adhoc networks (MANET). The protocol incorporates a hybrid optimization algorithm with trusted and optimal path selection to enhance security and energy efficiency in multi-hop routing. In this algorithm, the optimal cluster head node is selected using gray wolf optimization (GWO). However, the optimal cluster head node is selected among non-malicious nodes. For malicious node detection machine learning is used. Then after the selection of optimal nodes secure communication is performed over optimal and secure paths. For optimal path, a trust score fitness function is used by the cuckoo search algorithm. The proposed SEEMOMHR protocol aims to balance energy conservation with secure and reliable data transmission for real-world applications of MANET like disaster situation. This paper presents the result analysis in terms of energy usage, end-to-end delay, packet delivery ratio (PDR), and throughput under three cases: without attack, under attack, with attack detection and it was observed that the proposed algorithm had achieved optimal solution. The SEEMOMHR achieved 99% of average PDR, 0.46 s of average end-to-end delay, 9.3Mbps of average throughput and 0.023 J of average energy consumption with attack detection. The comparative analysis shows decrease in delay of approx. 1-2.5 sec over existing approach as well as energy consumption was also lowered from existing approach.

articleTitle: Navigating Risk: Deep Learning Approaches for Lane Change Safety and Lane Departure Warning Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the realm of road safety, the advent of advanced driver assistance systems has propelled the exploration of innovative technologies aimed at mitigating risks and preventing accidents. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into two crucial aspects of road safety: risky action recognition in lane change maneuvers and the development of effective lane departure warning systems. The first part of this study introduces a novel framework leveraging deep spatiotemporal networks with segmentation mask transfer for the recognition of risky behaviors during lane changes. By generating semantic segmentation masks from video frames and employing a CNN-LSTM network, this approach offers a promising avenue for real-time assessment of lane change safety. In the second part, a review of existing lane departure warning systems and lane line detection methods is conducted. The evolution of these systems, from traditional image processing techniques to cutting-edge semantic segmentation methods, is examined. Key considerations such as accuracy, robustness, and integration into higher- order tasks are explored, highlighting the transition towards deep learning approaches in the field. By merging insights from both domains, this paper provides a holistic perspective on leveraging deep learning innovations to enhance road safety. From proactive risk assessment during lane changes to reactive prevention strategies for lane departure incidents, this research contributes to the ongoing efforts in creating safer driving environments.

articleTitle: Evaluating Rule-Based Automated Reasoning for Complex Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Rule-primarily based automated reasoning (RBAR) is a computational venture that may be used to efficiently system complex statistics sets. RBAR is primarily based on programming regulations implemented for a given information collection, and the resulting shape of the facts is then evaluated in opposition to the shared assumptions and constraints. This reasoning has been carried out on large, complicated datasets with medical points, economic transactions, and consumer data for decision-making functions. In this paper, we discover the efficacy of RBAR for complex point processing and compare how well it plays for properly described enter-output issues. We speak of critical factors and challenges, inclusive of the selection of suitable reasoning rules and the evaluation of the ensuing output. We additionally present a case look wherein the impact of rule-primarily based reasoning is evaluated for an e-commerce dataset. Results show that RBAR can offer vast performance improvements to complex statistics processing over traditional processes.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Deep Learning Framework For NIDS
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Deep learning algorithms and frameworks have revolutionized predictive analysis over the past decade. These powerful techniques can be leveraged in the domain of Intrusion Detection to classify and predict cyber-attacks with minimal overhead. The dynamic nature of the problem along with the arise of new network attacks, make this problem highly intricate. In this paper, we aim to study the performance of a unique multi-stage deep learning models on the CICIDS-17 dataset. The dataset is a comprehensive dataset with an amalgam of real, recent and contemporary attacks which also correspond to the footprint of attacks found and encountered in the past five years. We propose a model of an LSTMAutoencoder followed by a classical ANN to classify the attacks in flow-based traffic data.

articleTitle: Botnet Attack Detection Using Deep Learning in the Internet of Things Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Botnet assaults on Internet of Things (IoT) devices are extremely harmful, yet deep learning (DL) detection requires a lot of memory and traffic on the network, and is not effective on devices with minimal memory. Dimensionality reduction techniques can be used to reduce the number of attributes in IoT network traffic. Thousands of botnet assault events classified as DDoS, DoS, reconnaissance, and information stealing are included in the publicly accessible Bot-IoT dataset. The IoT network can utilize the dataset to detect botnet traffic. Two-dimension reduction methods that might be helpful in reducing the dataset’s total feature dimensions are PCA and autoencoding. An intermediary hidden layer is used by the autoencoder, an unsupervised deep learning method, to produce a latent-space representation of the data. Deep learning techniques, such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), can detect botnet attacks using the decreased feature set. The approach’s success can be assessed using performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and a confusion matrix. In conclusion, the suggested approach is to lower the dimensionality of the features of the Bot-IoT dataset using dimensionality reduction techniques like PCA and autoencoder, enabling DL models like CNN and LSTM to detect botnet attacks. There are several performance measures available for assessing the technique.

articleTitle: Electromyography-based Hand Gesture Classification Using IGOA and DNN
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The most significant improvement in human-computer interfaces revolves around the accurate decoding of hand gestures from electromyography signals. The existing methods of doing this have a number of limitations. These include: feature redundancy and diminishing estimation accuracy for new users when pre-trained models are applied. Therefore, the current study focuses on enhancing the EMGbased recognition of hand gestures by developing a swarm intelligence based model to select features. In this model, a feature extractor, feature selector, and label classifier interface are integrated. The proposed model uses time domain (TD), frequency domain (FD), and time-frequency domain (TFD) analyses to establish the basic information of gesture recognition. Improved Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (IGOA) chooses the most discriminative features from the EMG data. It is noteworthy that a DNN classifier improves the classification result of the EMG-based gesture classification using the created feature set. It evaluates the proposed model from an 8-channel Myo Armband dataset. The proposed approach, on average improves by $2.4 \%, \mathbf{9. 6 \%, 6. 1 \%,}$ and 8% in precision, recall, F-measure, and accuracy respectively compared with a common KNN, NB, and RF estimators. Moreover, the average enhancements in recall by 7.3%, in precision by 4.9%, in accuracy by 4.1%, and in F-measure by 6.2% over popular optimization techniques like PSO, GA, and GH demonstrate the strength of the DNN and label the IGOA + DNN combination as a very effective strategy for EMG-based gesture classification.

articleTitle: Algorithmic Explorations in Webrooming: A Deep Dive into Tools and Technologies for Enhanced Consumer Engagement
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the latest tools and technologies facilitating the webrooming phenomenon, aiming to enhance the modern consumer experience. Through a systematic literature review and comparative analysis, the study identifies a diverse range of technologies, including e-commerce platforms, consumer review platforms, augmented and virtual reality, chatbots, data analytics, and omnichannel integration. Each tool and technology offer unique features and advantages, contributing to the enhancement of the webrooming experience. The study provides practical recommendations for businesses and researchers, such as adopting a holistic approach, leveraging advanced personalization techniques, exploring immersive technologies, investing in omnichannel integration solutions, investigating emerging technologies, and addressing privacy concerns. However, the rapidly evolving nature of technology may lead to the emergence of new tools and innovations not covered in this research, necessitating continuous monitoring and updating of research in this field.

articleTitle: Hate Speech Detection in Marathi Tweets using Stacked Deep Learning models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Digital platforms have revolutionized communication, but they have also led to an increase in hate speech, making it challenging to create welcoming online groups. The purpose of this study is to close this gap by using deep learning models to detect hate speech in Marathi, a regional language of India. The researchers use advanced word embeddings and DL models like Long Short-Term Memory and Bidirectional LSTM to demonstrate the efficacy of these methods. The study aims to build strong hate speech detection systems that can be extended to other low-resource languages, creating safer online spaces. The study emphasizes the importance of contextually and culturally appropriate data in enhancing model accuracy. In order to strengthen their models’ training and validation and guarantee reliable performance in real-world applications, the researchers also intend to integrate real-world social media data. The study closes a significant gap in regional language processing by concentrating on Marathi and opens the door for more inclusive and thorough hate speech detection frameworks across linguistic landscapes.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Analysis of WPA Security Protocols
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Wireless data transmission across the air is quite common. Attackers have the ability to sniff all that data. To make sure only the actual recipient could decipher its contents, wireless encryption algorithms were introduced. Now, depending on the level of security being used for data protection, attackers can replay, decrypt, or modify that data. Also, they can launch new kinds of attacks by obtaining man-in-the-middle positions or by using denial-of-service attacks as a preliminary step. This paper demonstrates how an attacker can utilize weaknesses in WPA2 and WPA3 protocols and also obtain access to a Wi-Fi network by exploiting some of those weaknesses. Also, it presents a variety of attack strategies against personal computational devices. Moreover, penetration testing was done on a personal and university network to assess the level of security being used. In the process, three distinct offline dictionary attack strategies were compared as well. Furthermore, we have discussed a number of vulnerabilities that have been addressed by new protocols and that still require the attention of the research community.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Convolutional Neural Network Architectures for Pneumonia Diagnosis from Chest X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Various viruses, bacteria, etc., are responsible for an infection called pneumonia which can be discovered by X-rays. This study will present some Convolutional Neural Network models for diagnosing pneumonia with the help of X-ray images. The dataset used contains 5856 X-ray images, which were used for training and validation. Various CNN architectures were trained to classify X-ray images into two groups: pneumonia and non-pneumonia. Some models were fine-tuned by altering parameters, hyperparameters or several convolutional layers. Four pretrained models were used: EfflcientNetB0, ResNet50, DenseNet121 and AlexNet. Among them all, the EfficientNetB6 model achieved the best validation accuracy of 84%. ResNet50 came after that at 76% while DenseNet121 had 82%. Lastly, with an accuracy score equating to 62% AlexNet performed worst among these four models. The chest X-ray dataset, comprising of 5856 images, was used for training and evaluation.

articleTitle: A Hybrid U-Net and Vision Transformer approach for Video Anomaly detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The growing dependence on surveillance videos highlights the need for automating anomalous events detection in videos, to improve real-time response and reduce manual workload. However, the diverse nature of abnormal activities across various public and private settings poses a challenge. This paper proposes integrating a U-Net-based architecture with vision transformers, leveraging their capabilities in capturing long-range dependencies, for frame-level anomaly detection in surveillance videos. The model learns inherent patterns by training on normal event videos and identifies deviations during testing for unseen video frames. Experiments on UCSD - Ped1 Dataset shows better results compared to others.

articleTitle: An Effective Path Planning Optimization in Cellular Networking Based on Key Performance Indicator: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The advancement of cellular network (CN) technologies is driven by the exponential growth of mobile users and their increasing demand for data consumption. To meet these demands, efficient Path Planning (PP) within CNs is crucial for achieving better throughput, latency, and overall network efficiency. This paper explores various PP approaches, including genetic algorithms, optimization algorithms, neural networks, and planning algorithms, utilized to find collision-free paths with minimal energy and time consumption for data transmission. Evaluation of these approaches involves analyzing Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to identify areas for improvement in network deployments. Throughput, bandwidth, latency, peak data rates, peak spectral efficiency, network resources, average transmission rate, energy efficiency, energy consumptions, accuracy, Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ), SINR, Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP), are used as KPI parameters. The effectiveness of PP methods is essential not only for enhancing network capacity but also for enabling applications such as wireless communication devices, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), and Mobile Robots (MRs) to perform preventive and corrective actions in emergency situations. This review provides insights into the significance of PP in optimizing CN performance and surveys the latest approaches aimed at reducing latency and enhancing network capacity for efficient data transmission.

articleTitle: Quantum-Inspired Differential Evolution Based Efficient IoT Service Placement in Edge Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The rise in Internet of Things (IoT) devices has led to the creation of sophisticated applications that demand various resources in real time to support a wide range of IoT services. Leveraging edge computing (EC) infrastructure, these services can be effectively placed on edge nodes (ENs). However, due to the limited computational resources of ENs, it becomes challenging to manage a large number of services while maintaining the system’s quality of service (QoS) and quality of experience (QoE). This paper introduces a quantum-inspired differential evolution method (QIDE-IoTSP) designed to optimize the placement of IoT services within EC networks. The primary objectives of QIDE-IoTSP are to maximize throughput, ensure optimal load balance, and minimize computation time. A quantum vector (QV) is utilized to develop a robust solution for the optimal deployment of IoT services in EC networks to achieve this. The effectiveness of each solution is evaluated using a formulated fitness function. Simulation results demonstrate that QIDE-IoTSP surpasses other metaheuristic techniques in terms of throughput, computation latency, and load balancing.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Contingency-Based Learning Strategies for Precision Medicine
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Contingency-based learning strategies primarily based on synthetic intelligence (AI) are being hired within the area of precision remedy to enable greater powerful selection-making when treating patients. The overall performance of such learning strategies should be evaluated to make sure they are presenting accurate and dependable outcomes. This paper aims to assess contingency-based learning strategies for precision medication to help clinicians and researchers appropriately assess the efficacy of these learning techniques and decide the first-rate method for given software., a scientific evaluation of the current literature was undertaken to identify existing assessment strategies and analyze their strengths and weaknesses. The assessment criteria used in this analysis are accuracy, interpretability, complexity, scalability, and transferability, which had been selected as they affect the performance of AI-primarily based approaches in real-international settings. Furthermore, a discussion of current equipment and frameworks that could be used to assess AI-based techniques in the area of precision remedy was performed. From this assessment, it has been discovered that most of the present assessment techniques lack the necessary accuracy and transferability essential to appropriately check the efficacy of AI-based strategies for precision medicinal drugs. But, sure, evaluation metrics, together with explain ability, may be employed to degree the overall performance of AI-primarily based techniques in order to decide the nice approach for a given application.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model For Emotion Recognition For Discrete Speech
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Human emotion recognition is recognized as essential for effective communication, understanding development, and developing meaningful connections. Its importance depends on assisting individuals in recognizing social signs, interpreting varied situations, and fostering psychological well-being. Furthermore, it helps with decision-making, conflict resolution, and general community cohesiveness. Recognizing human emotions in speech is especially important for supporting effective communication, raising awareness, and understanding complex nuances in interpersonal dynamics. This proficiency not only improves mental processes, but it also encourages deeper relationships and more compassionate reactions. The model is based on supervised deep learning principles and was particularly designed for emotion identification using discrete inputs. It employs data augmentation techniques to resolve imbalances in lower instance classes and experimentation using multiple deep learning models implemented that include CNN, LSTM and CLSTM. CLSTM Model reported the best performance with an F1-score of 0.77.

Author Keywords: Deep learning Model discrete speech emotion detection

articleTitle: Granularity-based Comparison of the Change-proneness of Micro-Clones
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Regular clones (i.e., identical or substantially equivalent code fragments greater than 4 LOC) inside a software system’s code-base have been thoroughly examined by several studies. In our research, we investigate the change-proneness of micro-clones (i.e., code clones of at most 4 LOC). In particular, we compare the change-proneness of function and block level micro-clones. An empirical study shows that micro-clones are a growing concern since the number of micro-clones is three times as much as the number of regular clones in a software system. Analyzing the impacts of function and block level micro-clones is very useful for developers because they can realize which granularity (function or block) is more important for software maintenance and evolution. When it comes to managing clones, developers should pay more attention to code clones that are subject to frequent modifications, sometimes called unstable clones, from an evolutionary perspective. They can prioritize the more change-prone micro-clones for refactoring or tracking. We investigated the micro-clone category of function level and block level for 5 diverse subject systems from the SVN repository and analyzed their change-proneness by using UNIX diff. We found that micro-clones of function granularity are generally more change-prone than micro-clones of block granularity. Thus, function level micro-clones should be prioritized more for management, such as refactoring and tracking.

articleTitle: The Transformative Impacts of Artificial Intelligence on Education through Ethical Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Innovation has surged due to the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), especially in the field of education. Traditional teaching methods are undergoing a profound transformation thanks to the influential algorithms driving AI. This technology extends far beyond the boundaries of education, penetrating various dimensions of our daily lives, enriching human activities and lifestyles. AI stimulation of human thinking and intelligence in a machine by performing tasks commonly recognized and associated with human intelligence and imagination. This research aims to synthesize diverse valuable insights of AI on educational environments. It emphasizes the ethical transition from traditional teaching and learning methods to more interactive human experiences. Furthermore, the research provides an overview of innovative elements, current challenges, concerns, and benefits of AI in education. It also highlights popular AI-powered educational tools and platforms. Remarkably, sophisticated AI platforms like ChatGPT, Squirrel AI, Google Bard (Gemini), and Grammarly take center stage. These systems, based on natural language models, can generate responses alike human interactions. The paper investigates the potential advantages of AI in education while addressing the ethical and practical considerations surrounding its implementation. By examining these technologies, the research aims to illuminate the path towards a more dynamic and effective educational landscape.

articleTitle: EEG-based Detection of Major Depressive Disorder using 2D Convolutional Neutral Network and Gated Recurrent Units
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Depression is a mood disorder that affects approximately 260 million individuals globally and is typified by feelings of hopelessness and unhappiness. Traditional diagnostic methods for depression are often inconsistent and time-consuming. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an automated technique for detecting depression utilizing Electroencephalogram (EEG) data. Our approach combines a 2D Convolutional Neural Networks (2D CNN) and a Gated Recurrent Unit Networks (GRU) to extract both temporal and spatial features from EEG signals, which facilitates the classification of signals associated with depression. The proposed method applies Independent Component Analysis (ICA) to separate underlying brain activity from background noise. The resulting signals are then converted into scalograms using the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT). These scalograms graphically depict the signal’s frequency characteristics with time, enabling the model to analyze temporal fluctuations and identify frequencies linked to depression. The approach is validated on a dataset from Universiti Sains Malaysia Hospital (HUSM), comprising 64 individuals: 30 healthy volunteers and 34 individuals with Major Depressive Disorder(MDD). We evaluate the model performance using K-fold cross-validation, attaining 98.9 % accuracy, 97.9 % precision, $99.4 \%$ recall, and $98.9 \%$ F1 score. These results confirm that our deep learning model is highly effective for the low-cost, non-invasive diagnosis of depression using EEG data.

articleTitle: Enhancing Date Fruit Classification Through Deep Learning Approaches and Real-Time User Interface Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Dates are revered as sacrosanct fruits in Middle Eastern culture due to their extraordinary nutritional value and rich flavour. In addition to their delectable flavour, these fruits have the potential to address health issues, thereby fostering overall wellness and health. People are at risk of selecting varieties that are inadequate for their taste preferences and culinary requirements if they are unable to distinguish between date classes during the purchasing process. This can result in disappointment with the flavour or texture. This study especially addresses the difficulties associated with accurately predicting various categories of dates. This study creates a classification system for nine distinct categories of dates by using a dataset that includes 1685 images. The classification performance of four deep learning models and a proposed composite model (MobileNetV2 + DenseNet201) is assessed. DenseNet201 archives as accuracy of (95.64%), followed by MobileNetV2 (92.41%), Xecption (90.62%) and VGG-19 (82.70%). The highest accuracy of 98.78% obtained by the proposed DateNet model among all algorithms with high precision and recall. DateNet model that has been proposed has the potential to provide a highly accurate and dependable classification of date fruit varieties.

articleTitle: Efficient Attitude Estimation Through a Multilayer Perceptron Neural Network Based on Multi-Data Sensor Fusion Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Inertial sensor attitude estimation is essential for many applications, ranging from self-driving cars to tracking human movement. Ambient conditions, the presence of disturbances, and motion characteristics vary throughout application scenarios. Since modern attitude estimators do not generalize across different motion features and ambient conditions, their parameters must be changed for particular motion scenarios. In order to provide precise navigational solutions, global positioning systems (GPS) and IMUs are usually combined. In signal-challenged areas, the GPS receiver will not be able to provide accurate location information. The integration system will therefore become an IMU-independent system. In order to improve the performance of the attitude estimator, this paper describes a multi-data sensor fusion system that integrates IMU data using a multi-layer perceptron neural network. When estimating a vehicle’s attitude, one of the most important factors is the multi-combination of measurements from the MARG sensor. This problem cannot be solved by classical estimators; instead, a sensor fusion method needs to be created in order to produce reliable fusion outcomes. The authors suggest utilizing a multilayer perceptron model to execute a successful prediction in order to produce a highly exact attitude estimation. The tests conducted on the sequence demonstrate that the result produced surpasses the state-of-the-art, including Madgwick, Mahony, and complementary filters, when the right dataset is used for the orientation estimation.

articleTitle: Texture Based Image and Video Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Texture-based picture and video analysis is a field of PC vision and photograph processing that explores the use of textures as visible descriptors for the characterization and analysis of virtual pictures. This consists of techniques for extraction of textural capabilities, class and segmentation of images, and synthesis of texture-based total consequences. It is useful for a myriad of programs in numerous domain names, including clinical imaging, robotic navigation, video surveillance, anomaly detection, and biometric identification. The principle strategies utilized in texture-based picture and video analysis include mathematical morphology, Gabor filters, Markov random fields, wavelets, and scaling capabilities, gray-stage co-incidence matrices (GLCMs), vicinity and shape functions, and texture synthesis. Mathematical morphology is used for processing geometrical systems in a photo by setting policies for combining pixels in a normal or irregular grid. Gabor filters are used for developing strength profiles of pixels by means of convolving a photograph with sinusoidal capabilities. Markov random fields are used for modeling the spatial interactions inside a photo with the purpose of explaining the statistical houses of the boundary pixels. Wavelets and scaling features are used for decomposing a photo into multiresolution coefficients.

articleTitle: A Study of Data-Driven Investing: Python Portfolio Analysis and Cost reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study explores the use of a data-driven investment strategy that can improve profit yield by automatically placing orders. This study examines the usefulness of using historical data to make informed investment choices. The study begins with an investigation of data fetching using the nsepy package, laying the groundwork for an extensive portfolio analysis. Examining mean daily simple returns, standard deviation (risk and return), and performance metrics for portfolios including Sharpe Ratio, predicted annual returns, cumulative returns, and annual volatility are among the significant subjects addressed in the study. The main tool used to carry out these studies is Python, which shows a detailed technique from installing required libraries to writing the whole data-fetching and analysis processes. To provide a thorough understanding of the dynamics of the portfolio, visualizations including cumulative return charts, risk box plots, correlation matrices, and stock price history plots are given with the code. In its conclusion, the project avoids making any promises of rapid money gain in favor of highlighting the material’s instructional value. Rather, our goal is to provide investors of all experience levels with the information and resources they need to support their investing choices with facts. This series of articles will cover portfolio optimization in depth in the future, guaranteeing that readers will have a thorough grasp of how to build an ideal portfolio for profitable investment.

articleTitle: Human-Centered Software Platform for Social Network of Self-Help Groups
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Designing user interfaces (UI) for marginalized rural women presents unique challenges that require a good understanding of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) principles to ensure usability. This research paper focuses on developing a contemporary UI for a social network of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in India, catering to the diverse age groups and educational backgrounds within these communities. The goal is to blend HCI principles into the design to develop an interface that is attractive, user-friendly, and easy to navigate for the users of these communities. This study tries to employ a user-centered design thinking approach to guide the development of the UI prototype. The study details the use of financial module of the application and its implementation. The software utilizes a multi-level client-server architecture using Flutter frameworks for UI design.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Comparison of Machine Learning Techniques for Heart Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Heart disease, affecting millions worldwide, poses an alarming threat to global health due to its high prevalence and significant impact on mortality rates. Despite advances in medical technology, early detection remains crucial for effective intervention and prevention strategies. Machine learning aids in heart disease detection by analyzing patient data to identify patterns and predict risk factors, facilitating early intervention and personalized treatment. In the proposed work, a comprehensive range of classifiers, including AdaBoost, SVM, Naïve Bayes, CatBoost, Random Forest, Perceptron, Decision Tree, XGBoost, kNN, Bagging, Extra Trees, Logistic Regression, Stacking, and Multi-layer Perceptron, were extensively employed to evaluate their effectiveness. Notably, Random Forest exhibited superior performance with an F1 measure of 0.98, endorsing its selection as the primary classifier in our model.

articleTitle: Enhancing AI Text Detection: Embracing Bi-LSTM and Transformer Block Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research paper introduced an innovative approach to enhance AI text detection by combining Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) with Transformer block architectures. The goal was to accurately differentiate between AIgenerated and human-written text. The proposed model utilizes an input layer, embedding layer, Bidirectional LSTM, custom Transformer block, convolutional layer, global max pooling, dense layers, and a sigmoid output layer for binary classification. By leveraging the strengths of both architectures, the model aims to address challenges related to authenticity and misuse of AIgenerated text. Evaluation metrics for instance accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are used to measure model performance. Overall, this research contributes to advancing AI text detection capabilities, fostering trust, integrity, and safety in digital communication. The study not only contributes to the academic understanding of text detection but also provides practical tools for distinguishing between AI-generated and human-written text. By leveraging a sophisticated architecture combining Bi-LSTM and Transformer Block fusion, the proposed method achieves significant advancements in text classification tasks. Through rigorous evaluation and experimentation, this research offers insights into the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately identifying AI -generated text, thereby addressing a critical need in the field of text detection. This study lays the groundwork for future research and development in AI-driven text detection systems, offering a scalable solution for detecting AIgenerated content across various digital platforms.

articleTitle: A Blockchain-Based Approach for Detecting Counterfeit Pharmaceuticals
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Nowadays, the contemplations for improving the item circulation supply structure have been expanded around the world. Simultaneously, it acquires different complexities in the inventory network and things get a lot defiled inside the production network at the hour of cataclysms. For example, alongside the false quality of items, costs to get a colossal illicit raise and unlawful cruel amassing happen to exacerbate things. Henceforth, conveyance costs are present to be uncovered and item data is to be imparted to purchasers. As it is now referenced, dispersion channels are muddled and supply chain management (SCM) is self-sufficiently accomplished in a freeway. For common sense reasons, it has been consistently called attention to that the circulation system isn’t straightforward and the dissemination edge is quite high. The motivation behind this examination is to structure a framework that vows the straightforwardness of the item dispersion structure by blockchain on inventory network the board frameworks. This methodology permits organizations just like any purchasers to follow their exchanges, items by upgrading straightforwardness in the Supply Chain Management, accordingly cursing down organizations and go-betweens from selling counterfeit drugs.

articleTitle: Denoising Ancient Epigraphical Estampages from India using Transfer Learning with Surrogate Benchmarking
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Archaeological inscriptions in India are of immense historical importance offering conclusive evidence about the reign of various dynasties. Several obsolete languages, such as the Brahmi script, have survived as inscriptions on copper plates, slabs, pillars & other artifacts. Many ancient epigraphical carvings have deteriorated due to insidious exposure to natural elements, decay, deliberate destruction, and a multitude of other factors. To facilitate computational transcription, this paper proposes the use of transfer learning methods with models such as Autoencoder and U-Net for effectively denoising degraded epigraphical estampages, supplemented by a structured image processing framework for downstream character recognition. In the absence of definitive ground truth, we rely on surrogate benchmarking to quantitatively evaluate the effectiveness of the models on alternative datasets, particularly in the context of epigraphical denoising. The proposed U-Net Model is benchmarked on the publicly available SIDD denoising dataset, obtaining an SSIM score of 0.9559. Using surrogate benchmarking to evaluate the performance of the model on denoising epigraphical images, an SSIM score of 0.85 is obtained for the output of the U-Net model, demonstrating its ability to denoise epigraphical estampages. The proposed research lays down a framework for effectively denoising epigraphical estampages sourced from India.

articleTitle: Predicting Fish Diseases Using Machine Learning Based on Water Quality Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In aquaculture, detecting fish diseases early is crucial for farmers to prevent outbreaks and financial losses. These diseases, often caused by viruses and bacteria, disrupt water quality parameters, leading to fish mortality. Inspired by recent successes in machine learning, this study utilizes cutting-edge algorithms to swiftly and accurately detect and predict water quality degradation. This research proposes the use of machine learning techniques to enable early identification of diseases in fish populations by predicting deteriorating water quality conditions. The aim is to provide stakeholders with a system that allows them to take preventive actions before disease outbreaks occur. The study evaluated the performance of several machine learning models, including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP), and Random Forest classifiers, in predicting disease occurrences. Among these techniques, the Random Forest algorithm demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy, achieving 98.97% correct classification of diseased and non-diseased cases. This integration of machine learning enhances aquaculture management, safeguarding against economic losses and fostering sector resilience. A web application utilizing machine learning predicts fish disease outbreaks based on real-time water quality data, providing early warnings to aquaculture farmers. It offers proactive measures to mitigate risks and promotes sustainable aquaculture practices.

articleTitle: Intelligent Video-Based Attendance Tracking With Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The real-time attendance management system is an innovative solution designed to record the attendance of individual students during lectures without physical contact. By utilizing multiple camera angles strategically positioned within the classroom, the system will capture a comprehensive view of the lecture space. Advanced face recognition technology will analyze real-time video feeds, identifying and matching student faces with a pre-registered database. This will ensure accurate attendance recording in real-time, eliminating the need for manual roll calls. The system will send email notifications to every registered student about their attendance. The system will be integrated with existing educational platforms and scaled to accommodate different classroom sizes and institutions. It will offer benefits such as contactless attendance tracking, time savings, and improved transparency. Overall, the real-time attendance management system will enhance safety, efficiency, and effectiveness in attendance management processes within educational institutions.

articleTitle: Recent Advancements in Online Ocular Artifacts Removal in EEG based BCI: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: EEG signals, measure brain activity, are often affected by various unwanted signals called artifacts. One major type is ocular artifacts (OAs), stemming from eye movements and blinks. Getting rid of these OAs is crucial for accurate EEG analysis, appropriate for applications requiring real-time processing, such as brain-computer interfaces (BCI). Some methods have been developed to do this online, meaning as the data comes in.Our study compares different techniques for removing OAs from EEG signals. These techniques include regression, adaptive filtering, empirical decomposition, artifact Subspace Reconstruction, blind source separation, and hybrid methods. We wanted to see which one works best for cleaning up EEG data contaminated by eye-related artifacts. By these methods with simulated EEG data, aiming to show how well each one can recover the true brain signals while maintaining the speed needed for real-time analysis. Our evaluation sheds light on the strengths and weaknesses of each approach, helping researchers choose the most effective method for their needs.In summary, our work is investigating how well different techniques can clean up EEG signals messed up by eye-related artifacts. This research is valuable for anyone working with EEG data, especially those interested in real-time processing for applications like BCIs.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive and Selective Ethanol Sensor Based on ZnO Nanorods on ITO Coated Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Nanotechnology is an emerging field in the current world that primarily focuses on nanoparticles ranging from 1 100 nm in diameter, which exhibit distinctive properties owing to their size and large surface area. Among them, zinc oxide nanostructures, are major metal oxide nanoparticles that are widely used in various fields especially in the fabrication of biosensors due to their unique structural characteristics and biological effects. In this work, ZnO nanoparticles were designed using a chemical reduction method and characterized using XRD to study the morphology and structural properties. Those nanoparticles were doped with PVA by sol-gel process and the electrode was designed using the spin coating technique on the precleaned glass slide. CV studies showed that the ZnO NPs electrode was effective in detecting ethanol with high selectivity in the presence of other substances. A high sensitivity and quick linear response were accomplished due to the large surface areas and electron transport in the corresponding reactions, which makes this electrode a very promising candidate for efficient and accurate non-enzymatic detection of ethanol ($\mathbf{C} 2 \mathrm{H} 5 \mathrm{OH})$.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Machine learning has experienced remarkable growth in recent years, largely propelled by advances in deep learning methodologies. This paper offers an in-depth exploration of the integration of deep learning into machine learning tasks across various fields, including the critical domain of malware analysis. Deep learning, a specialized branch of machine learning, leverages neural networks with multiple layers to automatically extract data representations and features. A pressing concern today is the threat posed by malicious software, which often employs methods such as generating invalid links that direct users to compromised sites or launching Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. These cyber attacks aim to steal personal and sensitive data using techniques such as 0-day exploits to facilitate rapid replication. Malware analysis is the study of various malware types, including viruses, worms, Trojans, and rootkits, to assess the potential impact of an infection. The paper delves into key deep learning architectures, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), transformers, and generative adversarial networks (GANs), and their specific roles in malware analysis. This involves both static and dynamic analysis methods, essential for understanding malware behavior and mitigating its effects. Moreover, the paper discusses the challenges associated with deep learning, such as overfitting, data availability, interpretability, and computational demands, as well as potential solutions to address these issues. Emerging trends and innovations in deep learning, including self-supervised and federated learning, are highlighted, with a focus on their impact on the future of machine learning and cybersecurity. By examining the intersection of machine learning, deep learning, and malware analysis, this paper aims to showcase the transformative potential they offer across different industries and scientific disciplines. Through these insights, the paper contributes to the ongoing development and application of machine learning in the fight against cyber threats and the pursuit of secure, efficient digital environments.

articleTitle: Smart Price Comparison Assistant: Making Shopping Smarter with Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the era of online shopping, finding the best deals on products can be a daunting task. With so many online retailers offering similar products at different prices, it can be time-consuming and overwhelming to compare prices across multiple websites manually. That’s where a smart price comparison assistant comes in handy. By utilising AI technology, this assistant can automatically search and compare prices from various online retailers, saving users time and effort. With the ability to analyse data and identify the best deals, a smart price comparison assistant can provide users with a comprehensive and unbiased view of the market. This allows users to make informed purchasing decisions and ensures that they are getting the best value for their money. By utilising AI-driven recommendation engines, this price comparison assistant can not only compare prices but also provide personalised recommendations based on user preferences and previous purchases. By using personalised shopping powered by AI, businesses can offer their customers a unique and tailored experience. This personalised experience leads to higher engagement, loyalty, and ultimately, increased revenue for businesses. In addition to personalised shopping, AIdriven product recommendations also play a significant role in creating engaging and personalised online shopping experiences. With the help of AI-powered personalization tools, the smart price comparison assistant can analyse user behaviour and preferences to personalise search results and provide relevant and accurate product recommendations.

articleTitle: A Bibliometric Study on the Interplay of Virtual Reality and Cinematic Innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: over the past decade, this highlights a substantial rise in the sphere of virtual reality and film creation. An intersection between the two has caused an immense shift that greatly affects diverse areas. The purpose of this paper is to outline this fast-growing aspect by conducting an extensive bibliometric analysis across various research outputs, established links and patterns among them in relation to the growing popularity of virtual reality as well as cinematic activities. But for a detailed profile which describes verbatim, in terms of trends, dedication, research development virtual reality and films, it would use strict bibliometric techniques. Additionally, it recognizes main actors involved with such collaborations as well as major institutions and nations supporting interdisciplinary initiatives for this merger. The examination of patterns in publications reveals a dynamic in time that underlies research topics, and gives some insight into emerging areas for further study and provides a roadmap for future research. These discoveries enrich our knowledge about the symbiotic relationship between virtual reality and film, while providing decision makers with strategic perspectives that are crucial to allocating resources in this rapidly shifting innovation-based landscape where VR converges with filmmaking. Ultimately these analyses demonstrate how VR is being adopted by many disciplines that intersect movie making.

articleTitle: Challenges in Democratizing E-commerce in India through Open Network for Digital Commerce: A Seller Network Node Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
