Through comparative analysis, we demonstrate how different FS strategies influence the ML methods’ computing efficiency and accuracy of detection. Our findings emphasize FS’s critical importance in enhancing botnet detection systems’ effectiveness within IoT infrastructure.

articleTitle: Deep Emotion Analysis: “Enhancing Emotion classification with Transformer Model”
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the era of digital technology, it becomes very critical to perceive human emotions in textual data from the point of view of many applications - sentiment analysis, mental health monitoring and user experience optimization. The investigation is on the incorporation of transformer-based models and ML techniques in order to enhance the accuracy for emotion classification. This work employs a variant of Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) that is able to preserve complex linguistic constructs and contexts. Along with this, logistic regression, decision tree, support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and gradient boosting algorithms are utilized to classify emotional aspects which are then compared for their accuracy in expressing subtleties present in text data. Fundamentally, eXplainable AI (XAI) tools such as ELI5 for random forest and LIME for BERT are employed to improve the interpretability and transparency of the emotion categorization process. These XAI tools enable users to see the feature importance and decision-making process of the model which helps in improving their understanding of the critical features that influence emotion classification. This work proposes the integration of transformer models and traditional machine learning algorithms with explanation of sentiments (XAI) to boost text-based emotion analysis.

articleTitle: The Application of Explainable AI (XAI) to Create Understanding and Trust in AI Decision-Making: A Study
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The demand for Explainable AI (XAI) has increased recently to create confidence and comprehension in AI decision-making. The goal of the AI research area known as “XAI” is to create models and algorithms something everyone can understand and utilize with ease. Making AI systems’ internal operations transparent and understandable is the aim of XAI, which can assist humans in making better decisions by enabling them to comprehend the thinking behind the decisions made by AI. This paper will examine the numerous uses of XAI in various fields, including banking, healthcare, autonomous cars, and legal and governmental decision-making. Additionally, we will go over the various XAI methodologies, including natural language explanations, model interpretability, and feature importance analysis. Lastly, we’ll look at the difficulties and potential paths for research on XAI. The purpose of this paper is to give broad examination of the XAI research field today and discuss how it can affect the development of confidence and comprehension in AI decision-making.

articleTitle: Wild Animal Recognition using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Wildlife-vehicle collisions present a significant challenge at the intersection of road networks and natural habitats, necessitating innovative solutions to enhance road safety and mitigate the impact on wildlife populations. Traditional detection methods often fall short in achieving real-time effectiveness, prompting the exploration of advanced deep learning models such as EfficientDet, Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD), and YOLOv9 for wild animal recognition. This research addresses the limitations of existing models by proposing a comprehensive recognition system that leverages the capabilities of these state-of-the-art models. EfficientDet, SSD, and YOLOv9 represent a paradigm shift in automatically extracting intricate features from raw data, offering potential for robust and adaptive recognition capabilities. Our The experimental findings illustrate that the suggested YOLOv9 model outperforms EfficientDet and SSD, showcasing superior detection accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. This discovery emphasizes the effectiveness of YOLOv9 in tasks related to detecting wild animals, underscoring its potential as a reliable and efficient solution for mitigating wildlife-vehicle collisions and enhancing road safety in natural environments.

Author Keywords: Wild Animal Recognition System, Deep Learning Models, EfficientDet, Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD), YOLOv9

articleTitle: EmoStream: Real-time Emotion Prediction through Speech with Apache Flink and Kafka Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Advancements in real-time emotion recognition systems have witnessed a surge in interest, fuelled by their potential applications in diverse fields such as human computer interaction, mental health monitoring, and user experience enhancement. Existing approaches often focus on singular modalities, such as speech analysis or facial expressions. However, a comprehensive understanding of human emotion necessitates the integration of multiple modalities. This research introduces a novel approach, a Multimodal Real-time Emotion Prediction System (MREPS), which combines speech analysis with streaming data processing. The system begins by capturing a continuous stream of audio data, which undergoes Speech-to-Text (STT) conversion using cloud-based services like Google Cloud Speech-to-Text. Simultaneously, facial expression recognition and physiological signal analysis can be integrated for a more comprehensive emotional profile. The real-time nature of the data necessitates the use of a robust streaming architecture, leveraging technologies such as Apache Kafka for data ingestion and Apache Flink for stream processing. A crucial component of the system is the Emotion Prediction API, a microservice housing a machine learning model for emotion classification. This model is trained on diverse datasets to ensure accuracy across various languages, cultures, and individual differences. The real-time API endpoint continuously processes the multimodal input, providing dynamic emotion predictions.

articleTitle: Ensemble Fusion: Skin Cancer Detection using ResNet, EfficientNet, and VGG Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Skin cancer detection is crucial for timely intervention and improved patient outcomes. This study addresses the challenge of early detection accuracy through the utilization of advanced machine learning techniques. Leveraging the HAM1000 dataset, comprising high-resolution dermatoscopic images, rigorous preprocessing techniques were applied to enhance image quality and feature extraction. Our methodology involved training an ensemble model incorporating state-of-the-art architectures such as ResNet, EfficientNet, and VGG16. This ensemble approach harnesses the diverse capabilities of these models, leveraging their strengths in feature representation and learning.Experimental results demonstrate outstanding performance, with the ensemble model achieving a remarkable accuracy of $99.1\%$ on test dataset in classifying skin lesions as malignant or benign. This achievement under-scores the effectiveness of ensemble modeling in skin cancer detection, particularly when integrating powerful architectures like ResNet, EfficientNet, and VGG16.Furthermore, our study highlights the importance of robust preprocessing techniques in optimizing model performance and ensuring reliable diagnostic outcomes. The findings of this research have significant implications for clinical practice, offering a promising avenue for improving early detection rates and ultimately enhancing patient outcomes.Future research endeavors may explore the integration of additional datasets and validation on diverse populations to further validate the efficacy and generalizability of the proposed ensemble approach.

articleTitle: Advanced Techniques for Real-Time Smoke Emission Monitoring: Color Analysis, HOG, and SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The study “Advanced Techniques for Real-Time Smoke Emission Monitoring: Color Analysis, HOG, and SVM ” addresses a critical environmental issue exacerbated by rapid urbanization and the increasing number of vehicles on the road. Images of vehicle emissions are processed to extract color and gradient features and fed into an SVM classifier for smoke detection. Additionally, the system systematically stores collected data-including SVM-HOG values, color analysis results, and vehicle plate numbers-in a database for comprehensive analysis and continuous improvement. The color analysis technique achieves an accuracy of 93.33%, a precision of 90.91%, a recall of 90.91%, and an F1-score of 90.91%. The SVM-HOG method attains an accuracy of 90.00%, a precision of 83.33%, a recall of 91%, and an F1-score of 86.96%.

articleTitle: Rice Leaf Disease Identification using Attention Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study tackles the major problem of diagnosing rice diseases in agriculture, highlighting how important early detection is to preventing large financial losses for farmers. According to the International Rice Research Institute, pests and diseases cause an average of 37% of rice harvests to be lost each year. To enable accurate AI-assisted rice illness categorization, the paper presents a novel attention network built on the ResNet152V2 architecture and featuring a channel attention mechanism. The model strategically focuses on key aspects for disease identification by using attention modules to uncover contextual relationships inside images. We performed cross-validated classification tests using a publically available rice illness dataset of 2627 photos. The suggested machine learning technique shows effectiveness in automatically identifying symptoms, making it a useful tool for farmers and improving agricultural disease management. Its test set accuracy of 96.40%, which beats out the state-of-the-art models, highlights how AI could be widely used in agricultural disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Modern Cyber Security and Advanced Machine Learning: The Future of Global Security
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The safety of networks and structures in state-of-the-art international is facing a mess of cyber-assaults, from allotted Denial-of-provider (DDoS) attacks to malware and ransomware. To protect networks and structures, modern cyber protection is the use of technologies inclusive of firewalls, antivirus software program, and encryption. In addition, advanced gadget gaining knowledge of techniques are being employed to pick out, diagnose, and save you cyber-assaults. These strategies leverage strategies such as synthetic intelligence, deep mastering, and herbal language processing to locate malicious conduct. Furthermore, device mastering-based totally cyber protection solutions are evolving and becoming an increasing number of state-of-the-art. They may be capable of come across threats quick and autonomously, adapt to new threats, and offer real-time data to safety groups.

articleTitle: Agriculture 4.0 - Integrated Smart Irrigation System
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: To combat water inefficiencies and subpar agricultural yields, Agriculture 4.0 incorporates Industry 4.0 technologies into farming methods. Examples of these solutions include smart irrigation systems. Agriculture 4.0 - Integrated Smart Irrigation system optimize water usage in real-time, encouraging conservation and soil health, by utilizing sensors and machine learning models. Farmers may monitor and control irrigation operations remotely, increasing efficiency, with technologies like web interfaces, Augmented Reality and IoT connectivity. These systems are flexible and scalable, accommodating a range of crops and local conditions. They hold great potential to transform agricultural water management and promote sustainability.

articleTitle: Improving Heart Disease Prediction: Insights from Federated Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Heart disease prediction has become an important domain in the current scenario, with numerous research efforts aimed at developing systems capable of detecting heart disease before its severe consequences occur. Machine Learning technology plays a crucial role in developing predictive models for disease prediction, but it also raises concerns about data privacy and security. To address such privacy issues, the proposed work introduces the Federated Deep Learning model training, where Deep Learning models are trained using a privacy-preserving approach known as Federated Learning. The proposed work explores the effectiveness of hybrid deep learning models combining long short-term memory networks and convolutional neural networks for classifying electrocardiogram signals and predicting heart diseases. The work utilizes a comprehensive dataset of ECG recordings and employs rigorous training and evaluation processes to assess the model’s performance. The result demonstrates the model’s proficiency in accurately classifying diverse ECG signal patterns and their potential for robust heart disease prediction. This research contributes to advancing cardiovascular health diagnostics by proposing a federated deep learning approach that combines spatial and temporal information to enhance the accuracy of heart disease prediction.

articleTitle: Harnessing Deep Learning and Hybrid Approaches for Sentiment Analysis: Exploring Positive and Negative Sentiments
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Given the sharp increase of digital content emerging from social media, it is vital to keep an eye on trends in public opinion and attitude on different subjects, events, or problems. With the primary goal of extracting feelings, views, attitudes, and emotions from a subjective text, Sentiment Analysis is one of the key subfields of natural language processing. The main objective of this research is to examine sentiment analysis in the Assamese language utilizing deep learning and hybrid architectures, with a specific focus on identifying positive and negative sentiment. Using a carefully selected dataset of 25,000 positive and negative comments from social media sites, this research compares the sentiment analysis performance of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and a hybrid CNN+LSTM model. With an accuracy of 86.34%, the hybrid CNN+LSTM model outperforms both its CNN and LSTM predecessors. These results highlight the usefulness of hybrid architectures in tasks involving sentiment prediction and open up potential options for enhancing sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Growing Agriculture: An All-encompassing Structure for Crop Disease Prediction and Ecological Handling
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Agriculture is profoundly affected by crop diseases on a global scale, which endangers food security. It is vital to detect and control these diseases as soon as possible in order to protect crop yields. This research paper presents an allencompassing framework for the detection and management of crop diseases, which integrates sophisticated image analysis, machine learning, and conventional agricultural methods. Its principal emphasis is on the timely detection and efficient control of diseases. By employing a variety of data sources, including field surveys, remote sensing, and mobile applications, the methodology detects symptoms of diseases, evaluates their severity, and proposes effective management approaches. Case studies examining a range of commodities serve to illustrate the potential of the framework in terms of enhancing global food security, promoting agricultural sustainability, and improving crop health. In brief, this research article introduces an allencompassing structure for the identification and control of crop diseases, which incorporates sophisticated image analysis, machine learning, and conventional agricultural methods. It tackles the critical matter of early disease detection and effective management through the utilization of a wide range of data sources. Case studies serve as evidence of the potential of this technology to improve agricultural sustainability, worldwide food security, and crop health through the provision of individualized disease management approaches that decrease dependence on broad-spectrum pesticides. This endeavor represents a substantial stride in the direction of transforming agriculture in order to ensure a more sustainable future for food production.

articleTitle: Innovative Approaches for Action Detection: Leveraging CNN-RF in Cricket Umpire for a Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the article, the author gives a deep analysis of the model operation. This is done by employing a lot of performance indicators that allow testing of how reliable and accurate the classification system is. This finding brings a sign of hope, with the accuracy ranging from 78.10% to 90.83% on the different lines of action. Class 3 is above the rest in terms of accuracy with a rate of 85.76%, and with a recall rate of 94.87% and an F1-score of 90.09%, it is also leading in the overall list. On the contrary, Class 4 has a surprising 74.2% recall rate and receives an F1 score of 80.7%. The macro, micro, and weighted values represent the model intermediate performance data (model averages). The mean macro results for precision, recall, and F1score are 84.96%, 85.79%, and 85.13%, respectively. The weighted average accuracy, recall, and precision measures show a slight enhancement, meeting 85.44%, 85.06%, and 84.98%. Therefore, the model showed flexibility in taking care of samples being unequally represented. Very much as often as expected, and regardless of weights, the micro-average accuracy, recall, and F1-score are all 85.06%. This points out the model’s equal observance of acknowledging umpire actions. In addition, the model is very accurate overall, achieving 85.06117% accuracy, which shows its reliability and effectiveness when it comes to sports umpire movement recognition in any environment. This section presents the abstract, which gives a summary of the statistical and practical results of the model. It explains how the model learned to differentiate cricket umpire actions and how it was helpful in improving decision-making when it came to cricket officiating.

articleTitle: An improved machine learning approach for streamline the real time analysis in Big-data applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: the contemporary digital landscape has been modified notably because of the 1992 enactment of the Copyright regulation within the United States. PC engineering has been at the leading edge of many of those adjustments, supplying software and hardware answers that enable content material creators to safeguard their works. However, the digital landscape has additionally posed a chance for unmanned laptop engineers who might need to recognize the results of the Copyright regulation and the opportunities such a gadget of laws offers. Knowledge of the virtual environment inside which copyrighted paintings are created, exploited, and shared calls for a familiarity with the Copyright law. This article will discuss the relationship between Copyright law and PC engineering by focusing on the three central rights created through the law: the right to breed, distribute, and develop spinoff works. It will offer laptop engineers a fundamental review of these concepts, describing how they’re relevant to computer engineering tasks, including software, hardware, and other digital services.

articleTitle: Precise Lake: A Feedback and Visualization System For Optimizing Code Health
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The creation of efficient and maintainable code is a crucial aspect of software development. It is a daunting task to write code that does not smell, especially for novice programmers who lack familiarity with best practices for writing clean code. Despite ongoing research into code optimization, there is a significant gap in teaching developers how to write code that minimizes runtime and memory usage. With Precise Lake, a novel code analysis tool, these challenges can be solved with the identification and optimization of latent code like unused imports, functions and variables, inefficient patterns, and much more in the form of a code health analyzer and optimizer. Obtaining an experimental average gain of 56% in terms of memory usage and 21% with respect to runtime, it aims at bridging the gap between the writing of inefficient code and the manual reviewing step done at the end by automating the process for programmers to scan their code files and receive a report on the areas of improvement.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Techniques for Corn Plant Disease Detection Using UAV Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Plant diseases have become a global concern as they pose a significant threat to food security. These diseases have the potential to cause damage to crops, reduce yields, and compromise food quality. Moreover, the rapid spread of fungi, bacteria, and viruses can lead to widespread crop failures, creating food shortages, price increases, and ultimately, the risk of hunger. However, identifying plant diseases at the early stages remains challenging and time-consuming. Traditional methods of disease identification are often time-consuming and require manual inspection, which slows down timely actions and interventions. In recent years, deep learning-based techniques have shown promising outcomes in the realm of plant disease detection. In this paper, we develop three deep-learning models for the identification of healthy and unhealthy corn plant leaves. The models include a fully convolutional auto-encoder model, and a vision transformer, along with a baseline CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) model. We acquired the data set of corn plant images from UAV drones which were used to train and validate the proposed models. The results indicate that the proposed fully convolutional auto-encoder model achieved an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 5. 0 9 \%}$ outperforming both the Vision Transformer and CNN models. By leveraging deep learning-based techniques, such as the fully convolutional auto-encoder model, the agricultural industry can benefit from improved disease detection and prevention. Early and accurate identification of plant diseases allows for timely interventions, such as crop protection measures, which can ultimately safeguard food security.

articleTitle: Waste Product Identification to assist EPR using Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With the increase in population, there has been a large increase in waste production. This has affected the environment and in turn have led to land pollution. To increase the recycling of products and increase the lifespan of raw materials, several countries of the world have implemented EPR policy. EPR requires collection of data related to the amount of non biodegradable waste generated by each company. With the recent technological advancements in machine vision, it has become possible to develop an infrastructure to easily collect such data in realtime using various object detection models like Yolo, SSD, RCNN and so on. This paper provides the details of a complete prototype that can help assist in the identification of non biodegradable waste products into their respective producers which can in turn help to implement the EPR policy and also elaborates on the model selection process for this application. The models that were used and compared in this paper includes CNN, Faster RCNN and Yolo v5

articleTitle: Automated Segmentation of Lesions Associated with Tinea Pedis Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Tinea pedis, commonly referred to as athlete’s foot, remains a prevalent dermatophytic infection affecting the feet. The use of AI-driven healthcare solutions has attracted a lot of attention lately, especially when it comes to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases. This research aims to enhance the current understanding and methods by introducing an automated segmentation technique designed to identify and outline lesions caused by Tinea pedis. Central to this study is the implementation of advanced segmentation models, including UNet and YOLOv9, to achieve accurate and efficient lesion segmentation. The research methodology encompasses the creation of comprehensive datasets through a combination of publicly available images and patient samples from skin clinic. Augmentation techniques and meticulous manual annotation procedures are employed to enhance dataset quality and facilitate model training. Our dataset will be made publicly accessible.Important stages of the study include preprocessing the data, building the model, training, evaluating, and optimizing it. Noteworthy emphasis is placed on the customization of annotation strategies tailored to the requirements of each segmentation model. Through iterative experimentation and parameter tuning, the models are refined to ensure optimal performance in lesion identification and segmentation. The outcomes of this research showcase the potential of AI-driven segmentation models in augmenting diagnostic processes for Tinea pedis. By automating lesion detection and delineation, these models offer a promising avenue for enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of disease diagnosis. The U-Net model demonstrated an IOU of 94.28% and a precision of 95.09%, whereas the YOLOv9 model achieved an IOU of 85.15% and a precision of 89.38%. Moreover, the scalability of the proposed approach lays the groundwork for its application in the broader domain of dermatological diagnostics, thereby fostering advancements in patient care and clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: DeepDerm: Elevating Precision in Dermatological Diagnosis with Enhanced CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Since human skin illnesses are among the most common dermatological conditions worldwide, visual observations are usually the first step in the diagnosis process. Accurate classification of skin biopsies and scrapings requires dermoscopic analysis and clinical screening due to medical criteria. It gets more difficult to classify skin diseases using medical photographs because of the complex forms, wide range of colors, and data security issues. In this study, we offer a dependable approach for the classification of 20 distinct types of skin illnesses, based on an improved Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. Our enhanced CNN design exceeds the standard CNN, which only achieves an accuracy of 31.38%, with an astounding accuracy of 98.21%. The accuracy of two benchmark algorithms, AlexNet and VGG19, is also not particularly high (32.14% and 52.30%, respectively). In contrast to traditional CNN models the enhanced CNN performs better, demonstrating its efficacy and dependability in accurately identifying a wide range of skin disorders. including well-known architectures like AlexNet and VGG19. Positive implications of this discovery include the development of more precise diagnostic tools for dermatology.

articleTitle: AI in Combatting Man-in-the-Middle Attacks: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of cybersecurity, Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks represent a significant and persistent threat, capable of intercepting and manipulating digital communications in a clandestine manner. This comprehensive review paper delves into the burgeoning role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in identifying, mitigating, and preventing these sophisticated cyber threats. We explore the multifaceted nature of MitM attacks, including their methodologies, targets, and potential impacts, setting the stage for a deeper understanding of the necessity for advanced countermeasures. The core of this review illuminates the innovative AI-based strategies currently being employed and developed. These strategies encompass machine learning algorithms, pattern recognition, and predictive modeling, tailored specifically to detect anomalies and patterns indicative of MitM intrusions. We further investigate the integration of AI with existing cybersecurity frameworks, highlighting enhancements in real-time threat detection, response efficiency, and adaptive learning capabilities. The paper concludes by discussing the challenges and future prospects in this domain, emphasizing the dynamic interplay between evolving AI technologies and the perpetually shifting landscape of cyber threats. In this review, our goal is to offer a thorough understanding of the present situation and possible future trends of AI applications in addressing Man-in-the-Middle attacks. This serves as an important tool for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers involved in cybersecurity.

articleTitle: Vehicle Detection in Unmanned Aerial Imagery Through Advance You Only Look Once Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The detection of vehicles by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is gaining substantial attention in the field of traffic control. In aerial images, vehicles have a unique perspective and take up less pixels than other objects in the broader data set.. This study uses the YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once version 8) deep learning architecture to propose an enhanced method of vehicle recognition in aerial photos. This work goes beyond the conventional YOLOv8 implementation by introducing new methods for data augmentation to enhance the efficiency and the model’s resiliency. To build a diverse and enriched dataset, the suggested methodology makes use of cutting-edge techniques such image cropping, contrast correction, and brightness improvement. Training the YOLOv8 model on this enhanced dataset produces encouraging results; on a different test set with ground truth annotations, a noteworthy achievement of ${7 0 \%}$ accuracy in vehicle detection was made. This accomplishment highlights the effectiveness of our strategy and shows a notable increase in accuracy over earlier approaches. The study demonstrates the potential of YOLOv8 in tackling the difficulties of aerial vehicle detection and highlights the crucial role that data augmentation plays in improving model performance and resilience.

articleTitle: Legal Considerations for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and gadgets gaining knowledge of (ML) have revolutionized organizations’ overall performance, leading to accelerated performance and productivity. This era has become a fundamental part of our daily lives, from personal assistants to self-using vehicles. However, as AI and ML continue to improve and become more pervasive, it’s crucial to undergo the prison implications that would stand up. One of the primary criminal considerations for AI and ML is record privacy and safety. With the sizeable series and processing of extensive records, the danger of fact breaches and privacy violations increases. Corporations should follow applicable legal suggestions and policies, the overall records protection law (GDPR), and the California Purchaser Privacy Act (CCPA). Another interest is a legal responsibility. As AI and ML become more impartial, questions arise about who is responsible for any damage or harm because of those structures. This trouble has become more complicated, even as a few events concern improving and deploying AI and ML technologies.

articleTitle: Exploring the Use of AI-Powered System for Human Resource Management in MNCs
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In recent years, AI-powered systems had been an increasing number of carried out to various factors of human aid (HR) control in multinational corporations (MNCs). AI-powered device in HR control can provide useful insights concerning verbal exchange, talent-set improvement, performance review, and greater. The cause of this paper is to discover how AI-powered structures can be used to enhance and enhance the HR control within MNCs. This paper will evaluation current tendencies in AI-powered HR management, examine potential advantages and disadvantages of the generation, and talk how specific challenges may be addressed. The literature examined highlights the ability of AI-powered systems to offer organizations more desirable perception and actionable effects, however also discusses how bias and other dangers may also stand up. Thru an intensive review of current developments and implications, this paper will provide valuable insights on using AI-powered structures for HR management in MNCs.

articleTitle: Designing An Energy-Efficient Flip-Flop with MTCMOS using Muller C-Element Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the contemporary landscape of electronics, the proliferation of devices has led to an exponential increase in power consumption. As electronic devices become more integrated into everyday life, the demand for energy-efficient solutions becomes paramount. This project aims to address this challenge by proposing a novel approach to minimize the number of transitions in digital circuits, thereby reducing switching activities and subsequently lowering power consumption. The project focuses on designing a low-power D flip-flop using the Muller C-element and MTCMOS technique. This circuit design aims to minimize energy consumption by reducing output transitions, making it suitable for various applications such as consumer electronics, IoT devices, embedded systems, sensor networks, medical devices, communications systems, and aerospace technology. The Muller C-element plays a pivotal role in initializing the output, resulting in a minimized transition count. Utilizing multi-threshold CMOS (MTCMOS) technology further reduction of leakage current and optimize overall performance. The design and simulation of these logic gates were executed using Dsch2.

articleTitle: Transforming Technology for Online Marketing with Focus on Artificial Intelligence: A Qualitative Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Study employs a subjective research approach to investigate the effects of artificial insight (human-generated intelligence) on computerized displays considering the view that human and mental activities can be replaced by artificial intelligence. According to a survey of 15 marketing and AI experts, artificial intelligence is influencing marketing practices and ultimately improving their efficacy. According to this argument, combining human and machine labor is the most effective way to improve results because artificial intelligence can now complete many time-consuming and pointless tasks in an advertiser’s daily life. Two major barriers to the adoption of artificial intelligence are a lack of innovation, trust, and a lack of societal readiness. These difficulties and moral responsibilities have been overcome numerous times. Given these facts, business executives and managers should prepare their teams and staff for the implementation of artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Smart Buoy Integration: Optimizing Fish Supply Chain management and Border Alert System
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The fishing industry is currently facing many challenges, such as overfishing, suboptimal resource utilization, and inadvertent border crossings. In response to these pressing issues, project Fauna Dive presents an innovative, comprehensive, and community- oriented solution: an all-encompassing fishing management application. This innovative solution employs advanced technologies and data-driven strategies to enhance fishing practices. The application incorporates Long-Range (LORA) technology in smart buoys to monitor borders in real-time to prevent international boundary breaches. By collecting and analyzing environmental data through machine learning, the app helps fishermen locate optimal fishAing zones, thereby reducing bycatch and promoting sustainable fishing methods. Additionally, the app features a robust supply chain management system that connects fishermen directly with markets, enhancing resource utilization and profitability. Key functionalities include community storage facilities, real-time market analysis, Al-powered fishery support, and seasonal breeding adjustments to safeguard marine biodiversity. The app’s architecture is modular, featuring a React. js frontend and a FastAPI-driven backend API for streamlined connectivity, leveraging its advantages in speed and efficiency. Firebase handles database management, authentication, and real-time notifications, complemented by custom LORA hardware integrated into smart buoys. Aligning with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, this initiative aims to boost economic stability and promote environmental sustainability in the fishing sector. Through this comprehensive approach, Project Fauna Dive seeks to improve fish stock management, enhance fishing efficiency, and maintain ecological balance

articleTitle: Cognitive Radio-Based Spectrum Sensing for Dynamic Spectrum Access in Sensor Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cognitive Radio-primarily based Spectrum Sensing (CRSS) is a crucial generation for permitting dynamic spectrum access in sensor ad hoc networks (SAHNs). This era allows customers to successfully make use of to be had spectrum whilst keeping off interference from existing customers. CRSS makes use of sensing and optimization strategies to identify free frequency bands to enable verbal exchange in SAHNs. Moreover, the CRSS additionally consists of protocols and techniques to locate and defend against malicious behavior, which include spectrum jamming and false sensing reports. Subsequently, CRSS may be blended with superior technology, such as multi-agent structures and system gaining knowledge of, to create an efficient and sturdy gadget for dynamic spectrum access.

articleTitle: Review of RF Energy Harvesting in 5G Networks: Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Radio frequency energy harvesting (RF-EH) stands out as a promising technique leveraging electromagnetic waves to generate energy, offering potential solutions for powering wireless devices without reliance on batteries. This cutting-edge technology holds promise as an alternative energy source for future applications. Beyond facilitating dynamic energy recharging for wireless gadgets and providing eco-friendly energy alternatives, RF-EH introduces a range of applications requiring high-quality service. This paper reviews state-of-the-art RF-EH techniques, delineating their merits, limitations, and applications. Furthermore, it explores the future prospects of RF-EH technology.

articleTitle: Bitcoin Price Predictive Dynamics Using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cryptocurrency markets, exemplified by the notable volatility in Bitcoin prices, have become pivotal arenas for financial exploration and investment. In response to this, our research undertakes a comprehensive comparison of diverse machine-learning models to predict Bitcoin prices. The models scrutinized include Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-nearest neighbors (KNN), and Neural Networks. This study evaluates and contrasts these models based on performance metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and R -squared. This work encompasses the collection and preprocessing of historical Bitcoin price data, the engineering of pertinent features, and the division of the dataset into training and test sets. Each machine learning model is meticulously trained on the training set, allowing for the tuning of hyperparameters to optimize predictive capabilities. Subsequently, the models’ performance is systematically assessed on the test set, providing valuable insights into their accuracy and reliability. The scope of this research is delimited by a specific timeframe, focusing on historical Bitcoin price data up to 15/11/2023. By addressing these objectives, this research aspires to guide investors, researchers, and analysts in navigating the intricate landscape of cryptocurrency investment decisions. The findings contribute to an enhanced understanding of the nuanced strengths and limitations inherent in different machine learning models when applied to the volatile context of Bitcoin price prediction. Ultimately, this research aims to facilitate more informed and strategic decision-making processes in the cryptocurrency market.

articleTitle: Effect of Zero Attractor in Conjugate Gradient Algorithm for Sparse Systems with Impulsive Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Wireless broadband channels are usually few in number. Gaussian noise model-based adaptive filtering techniques were introduced to take advantage of channel sparsity. Nevertheless, impulsive noises are frequently heard in many sophisticated broadband communications systems. Impulsive noise causes these conventional approaches to function less well. This work proposes robust sparse adaptive filtering techniques based on the adaptive conjugate gradient (CG) with penalty function to decrease impulsive noise. Penalty functions like reweighted zero attractors (RZA) are added to the CG method to study systems with different levels of sparsity. In a setting where impulses run high, Tukey’s biweight M-estimate function is used with CG to lower the steady-state excess mean square error (EMSE), and to identify the sparse systems, reweighted zero attractor penalty along with Tukey’s biweight M-estimate function is added as a penalty function. The suggested algorithms are validated for a different level of sparse systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Cardiovascular Disease Detection Using CNN-SVM Models Based Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In a broad sense, heart disease encompasses a variety of cardiovascular sicknesses, including coronary artery disease, arrhythmias, heart valve disorders, congenital heart problems, and heart failure. A timely and accurate diagnosis is essential in effectively treating patient illnesses. This research focuses on developing a hybrid model that simultaneously uses CNN and SVM to categorize chest radiographs, which display five unique patterns of cardiac disease pathology. This was done using a dataset of 2200 medical photos to assess the model. The performance metrics include a Macro Average Precision Score of 93. 12%, Recall of 93. For the Spam classification, the accuracy is 93%, and F1-Score is 95%. A classifying model’s precision, Recall, and F1-Score are 93. However, only about 12% of all water on this planet is fresh, while the rest is saline. 08%, respectively. The assessments of microchips (93) on these factors are consistent—12% —classes 1 and 5 potent potential to accuracy levels of 94% and 92%, respectively. However, there is room for improving the differentiation between classes 3 and 4 if the education department invests more resources in their curricula. The ROC curves have an AUC values approach of **0**. 50 signifies for classes, which are destroyed areas that cannot be improved. The model shows how powerful image analysis and machine learning algorithms are in assisting physicians in detecting cardiac abnormalities with reasonable accuracy, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and patient results.

articleTitle: Study and Analysis of Bug Propagation in Evolving Software through Micro-clones
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Code clones, identical or substantially similar code segments in a code base, have both negative and positive impacts on evolving software. Detecting code clones is important for many reasons, such as bug fixing, change suggestions, refactoring, bug replication analysis, etc. An existing study shows that a significant number of bugs are propagated through code clones. However, Micro-clones (clones of code shorter than 5 lines long) were not considered in this study. Thus, bug propagation through micro-clones is still unexplored. This research paper presents an empirical investigation of the propagation of bugs through micro-clones. In particular, two evolutionary patterns are studied that indicate the propagation of bugs by code cloning. Initially, this paper detects micro-clones that have gone through bugfix modifications by examining the history of software evolution. Subsequently, these ascertain which of these micro-clones have evolved in accordance with the patterns of bug propagation. Based on this analysis of several hundreds of commits from four Java-based open-source systems, it has been found that as many as $\mathbf{6 3 \%}$ of the micro clone segments that have gone through bugfix modifications may contain propagating bugs. Approximately 29.41% of the bugfixes encountered by the micro clones are attributed to fixing propagating bugs. This paper’s finding indicates that identical micro clones predominantly contribute to bug propagation rather than near-miss micro clones. Propagation has a greater likelihood of occurring in the clone segments that are formed during a single commit action instead of in different commits. This discovery’s significance lies in the ability to prioritize micro-clones for refactoring and monitoring in terms of bug propagation.

articleTitle: Enhanced Classification of Exoplanets Using Machine Learning: Integrating Feature Selection, Ensemble Algorithms, and Explainable AI Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research delves into employing machine learning (ML) algorithms for classifying exoplanets, focusing on enhancing classification accuracy through feature selection. By utilizing data from the KOI planet candidates, the study addresses the challenge of handling large datasets by employing feature selection techniques like the chi-square method, improving the classification process’s effectiveness. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was employed for data visualization, aiding in understanding the underlying structure and relationships within the exoplanet dataset. In the implementation phase, the study initially employed standalone classifier models such as KNN, SVM, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Decision trees and CNN. Following this, ensemble algorithms including XGBoost, GBM, CatBoost, and AdaBoost were utilized to enhance classification performance further. Among these, Random Forest emerged as the top performer, achieving an F-measure of 0.95, surpassing the others. Additionally, the study incorporates explainable AI (XAI) techniques to interpret the importance of individual features in the models’ predictions, shedding light on crucial features essential for accurately classifying KOI planets. These insights serve as a foundation for developing more advanced and dependable ML models for exoplanet classification, facilitating future research endeavors that may incorporate additional datasets and features.

articleTitle: Copy-Move image forgery detection and classification using SIFT and DBSCAN Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the digital area, images play vital role which carries important information. Therefore, identification and classification of the tampered region and genuine region from an image is a challenging field of study. Images are often altered using editing programs or editing tools such as Picasa, Photoshop, and others, intending to mislead people or conceal information. Therefore, it is essential to verify the validity of photographs to determine whether they have been altered before extracting any valuable information from them. A tampered image where an object is intentionally duplicated in the image is categorized as copymove forgery. Copy-move forgery area detection in a tampered image based on locating SIFT key points in an image has been presented in this paper. The proposed novel approach detects the tampered image and locates the genuine and fake regions. DBSCAN clustering algorithm is applied to the keypoint locations and by calculating Error Level Analysis (ELA), the original and fake regions are highlighted in the image. Tampered images from MICC-F220 and MICCF2000 datasets are used for experimentation, and the results are compared to those of previously published methods.

articleTitle: Leveraging Edge Computing for Enhancing Next Generation Network Services
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Aspect computing is quickly turning into a possible answer for augmenting and streamlining the overall performance of next era community services. Edge computing gives a disbursed computing architecture that allows computation and records storage competencies to are living closer to the edge network, rather than in, valuable records middle. This enables applications to enjoy faster reaction times and reduced latency, growing the rate of facts shipping. Side computing also presents greater scalability, simplifying the combination of IoT gadgets, permitting statistics streaming from more than one asset. As networks pass to 5G, area computing will offer the important flexibility and stability to deal with big amounts of statistics visitors securely and successfully. By leveraging the power of edge computing, corporations can create an agile and resilient service structure, imparting more advantageous safety and a variety of customizable abilities that permit them to capitalize on the success of the 5 G community.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cloud Resource Optimization for Parallel Workloads
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cloud computing has revolutionized IT infrastructure, offering scalability, flexibility, and cost efficiency. However, managing parallel workloads in diverse cloud environments poses challenges. Optimizing cloud resources in parallel computing is crucial for achieving optimal performance and resource utilization. This analysis begins by examining the current landscape of cloud computing, highlighting the challenges associated with managing parallel workloads across disparate cloud environments. It then delves into the intricacies of dynamic resource allocation, examining existing strategies and their limitations in handling complex workload scenarios. Various cloud resource optimization mechanisms and their combinations, specifically tailored for parallel workloads are examined. A comprehensive theoretical analysis is conducted and a comparative evaluation, exploring the principles, functionalities, and synergies of these mechanisms are performed based on some predefined metrics. The insights from this analysis serve as a cornerstone for crafting efficient cloud resource optimization strategies tailored to parallel computing environments. Addressing workload management and resource allocation challenges can lead to enhanced performance and scalability. These findings lay the groundwork for further research in optimizing cloud resources for evolving parallel computing demands.

articleTitle: Mitigating Annotation Burden in Active Learning with Transfer Learning and Iterative Acquisition Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In situations where there is a lack of readily available annotated data, active learning is a useful tactic. To increase the model’s generalization, it entails training a model on a constrained annotation budget and repeatedly choosing the best data points for additional annotation. Active learning in deep learning usually necessitates fine-tuning subsequent deep models. But this has drawbacks, too. Specifically, it requires an initially large batch of annotated data, which is feasible when there is a constrained budget for annotation in general. We challenge this problem with a strategy inspired by transfer learning, in which only shallow classifiers are taught during active learning iterations, when an already expert model is used, it functions as a feature extractor. We also suggest a new acquisition function that takes use of active learning’s iterative character. To improve robustness, this function chooses samples based on the largest change in uncertainty between the last two models’ predictions. To ensure representation, we incorporate a diversification stage where we select samples from various regions within the categorization space. Using balanced and imbalanced datasets, our strategy is compared to competitor approaches and shows superior performance in minimizing annotation burden while preserving good model accuracy.

articleTitle: Mitigating Racial Bias in Facial Expression Recognition Using Enhanced Data Diversification Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With countless new methods and further advancevision, applying the technology to the everyday lives of people has become inevitable. One such use of computer vision models is recognizing facial patterns and expressions. However, as recent studies have indicated, many models interpreting facial expressions have developed biases towards certain races. This is likely a result of skewed training data; the model may have been trained with more images of a certain race than others. Overall, this can cause inaccuracy when the model is presented with people from different backgrounds. To promote a diverse group of data that the model can process, I present a way to balance biases. First, I fine-tuned a hybrid facial recognition model of state-of-the-art convolutional neural network (CNN) models called DeepFace on the emotion recognition dataset FER2013 to recognize the emotions on people’s faces. Next, using FairFace, which is modeled after the large-scale CNN ResNet-34, I extrapolated the races and facial structures for each type of individual, which I then used to determine the bias and skew within the dataset. I did this by comparing the model’s accuracy when applied to different races. Then, I used a user-instructed stable diffusion model called InstructPix2Pix to modify the images and create a more well-represented and diverse dataset. With this method, I was able to balance the dataset effectively and reduce bias in the image recognition model. However, due to issues with the FER2013 dataset images, many of the transformed images were disfigured, meaning the emotion data within the images was lost. This caused the overall accuracy of the model to drop significantly. Future research can evaluate this method using InstructPix 2Pix on different computer vision tasks or with different datasets.

articleTitle: RetinAI: Beyond Retinal Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a diabetes complication that can result in blindness. It is expensive and time-consuming to manually examine color fundus images in the traditional manner in order to detect DR in its early stages. Deep learning (DL) techniques have thus been used to fundus images for automated DR screening, taking advantage of their remarkable performance in a variety of domains. An intelligent computer-aided approach for automatic fundus image DR screening is developed and presented, tackling the issues of costly and labor-intensive human screening as well as the scarcity of data for deep learning model training, which frequently results in overfitting. To improve the accuracy of DR detection, the system uses a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) in a two-stage transfer learning strategy. This strategy is a potential option for DR screening since it greatly reduces the issue of category imbalance and boosts diagnostic effectiveness. To diagnose diabetic retinopathy (DR), a convolutional neural network (CNN) model is used. From fundus images, the CNN model learns a hierarchical structure of low- to high-level characteristics. The low-level layers of the model are adjusted to enhance its ability to identify local structures of lesions and normal regions. A new completely connected (FC) layer based on principle component analysis (PCA) for unsupervised feature extraction takes the place of the fully connected (FC) layers, which encode high-level characteristics that are global and domain-specific. By using this method, discriminative characteristics are extracted from the fundus images, which can improve the precision of DR classification. Lastly, we include a classification layer that uses gradient boosting. the assessment of the suggested system using two difficult datasets (Messidor and EyePACS).

articleTitle: Detecting Retinal Damage From OCT Images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is a crucial imaging modality in ophthalmology, offering detailed retinal images essential for diagnosing various retinal disorders. In this study, we investigate the application of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning to classify retinal OCT images. We compare a custom CNN model with two pretrained models, MobileNet and VGG16, to explore their effectiveness in categorizing retinal diseases. Our study focuses on improving classification accuracy through image enhancement techniques, training methodologies, and model evaluation using confusion matrices. The results highlight the VGG16-based CNN model as the most effective, demonstrating its potential for accurate classification of retinal disorders based on OCT images. Furthermore, we delve into strategies to further enhance the performance of these models, such as data augmentation, finetuning, and hyperparameter tuning. We discuss the importance of these techniques in optimizing model performance and reducing overfitting. Additionally, we emphasize the significance of evaluating models using confusion matrices to gain insights into their performance across different classes. Overall, our findings suggest that CNNs, particularly the VGG16based model, hold promise for improving the automated diagnosis of retinal diseases using OCT imaging, which could lead to better patient outcomes in ophthalmology.

articleTitle: Comparison of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus on Foot Thermography Using Transfer Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is a metabolic illness characterized by an inability to regulate blood glucose levels in our bodies. Even though the medical industry has advanced equipment for diagnosing diabetes mellitus, early detection of the condition is extremely challenging. As a result, it is necessary to computerize the prediction cycle to eliminate related dangers and advise patients ahead of time. We apply deep learning approaches to predict diabetes mellitus with foot thermography. Initially, the study aimed to identify a categorization index such as the Thermal Change Index (TCI). Following that, we employed the deep convolutional neural network paradigm to increase picture quality and temperature pattern visibility by adopting data augmentation and improvement methods such as histogram equalization, Gamma correction, and noise reduction. The proposed study employs many models, including DenseNet121, ResNet50, MobileNet, VGG16, and Inception V3. In comparison to other models, VGG16 attained an impressive accuracy of $96.6 \%$.

articleTitle: An Investigation into YOLO-v8 Model Optimization for Small Object Detection in UAVs using Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The growth of UAV technology has led to advancements in aerial surveillance, resulting in the development of specialized algorithms for object detection in complex environments like university campuses, beaches etc. This study proposes to leverage the recent YOLOv8 model with various sophisticated attention mechanism like Spatial attention, channel attention, squeeze and excitation block attention, Efficient channel attention network, etc. to efficiently detect the tiny person objects in images captured using Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) like drones. For the purpose of this analysis, the work utilizes a recent dataset, Manipal-UAV dataset, that focuses on detecting tiny objects in the form of person. The work also provides a comprehensive comparison of recent YOLO models for model selection and provides a detailed analysis of state-of-art attention mechanism when incorporated into the best baseline YOLOv8x model. The findings from this study will suggest that tailored YOLO models are effective for UAV-based person detection tasks, potentially driving advancements in aerial surveillance technology, particularly in scenarios requiring accurate identification of small objects like individuals. The research over-all aims to highlight the importance of dataset-specific optimizations to enhance the performance of object detection models in UAV imagery with mAP50 of 50.2%, thereby, promoting more reliable surveillance applications in various real-world settings.

articleTitle: Fetal Heart Ultrasound Image Enhancement and Anatomical Feature Recognition via GAN and GradCAM
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Ultrasound, an essential component of effective prenatal care, is a primary source of valuable information concerning fetal health and development. This study presents a novel approach to solving common issues in the fetus’s heart. This study addresses the intricacies that come with biological studies concerning fetal heart ultrasound diagnosis by applying cluster analysis and the generative adversarial network, specifically the Pix2Pix Model. This study focuses on issues in fetal heart imaging, such as the small size and unclear anatomical appearance of fetal heart artifacts in ultrasound images. In addition, introducing the Grad-CAM-AI visualization significantly improves the available, interpretable assets and usability for healthcare professionals. This comprehensive approach aims to increase the quality of care for mothers and their babies using this new feature and advanced imaging technologies.

articleTitle: BUS Foot Board Control Using IOT
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Bus footboard accidents in India have emerged as a significant safety challenge within the public transportation landscape. By prioritizing passenger safety and leveraging innovative solutions, the goal is to establish a more secure environment within public transportation systems. It employs a combination of advanced technologies including PIC controller, infrared sensors, Load cell sensor and automated alert systems. Load cell sensor strategically placed on the footboard continually monitor passenger presence and weight distribution, enabling the system to detect potential instability or overcrowding situations and send the signal to the PIC16F877A. Using IoT technology, the information that the passengers travelling in the footboard can be updated in the server using the IoT technology. In response to detected risks, the system triggers automated alerts to both the driver and passengers, prompting immediate corrective measures. It aims to revolutionize footboard safety in public transportation, offering an intelligent and responsive solution to mitigate accidents and enhance the overall security of passengers during boarding and disembarking processes. It aims to reduce speed of the bus when the passengers were on the footboards which is safer for passengers. It uses sensors and smart technology to keep an eye on the footboard area where passengers stand. These sensors can detect if it’s getting too crowded or if someone is in a tricky spot. If there’s a risk of someone getting hurt, it sends alerts to the bus driver and passengers, so everyone can be careful. It is designed to reduce accidents and create a safer experience for people using public transportation.

articleTitle: IoT based Battery Precharge System for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Battery is considered to be one of the most expensive component in an electric vehicle. Vehicle owners are always in search of affordable methods for the usage of the battery in their vehicle which is not only cost effective but can also offer good battery life at the same time. The proposed system provides the users with some affordable battery subscription plans that will allow the vehicle owners to pay the price of the battery in installments based on the plan they have chosen. The battery parameters and the usage data is stored in a cloud database and the vehicle owners are notified through the user application as and when the stipulated time for the next subscription nears.

articleTitle: Advancing Machine Translation: A Comparative Analysis of Evolving Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of evolving machine translation technologies, focusing on Rule-Based, Statistical, Neural, and Hybrid approaches. The study examines the historical development, strengths, and limitations of each method, with Neural Machine Translation highlighted as the most promising due to its ability to learn translation patterns directly from data. Key recommendations for advancing machine translation include enhancing data quality, leveraging computational resources, and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration. The paper emphasizes the need for standardizing evaluation metrics and creating benchmark datasets to facilitate fair comparisons. By integrating these recommendations, the field of machine translation can move towards more accurate, efficient, and user-centric solutions for multilingual communication, ultimately bridging linguistic barriers and enhancing global interactions.

articleTitle: Latency Reduction In Industrial Iot Using Yolov8 CNN Approach For Real-Time Data Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: During the era of Industry 4.0, the incorporation of the Internet of Things (IoT) into various industrial processes has become increasingly widespread, resulting in increased levels of production and efficiency. On the other hand, while dealing with the huge amounts of data produced by Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) devices in real-time, it is particularly difficult to minimise latency in order to guarantee rapid decision-making capabilities. There has been a significant increase in the amount of data generated in industrial settings as a result of the proliferation of IIoT devices. Low-latency data processing is something that businesses that rely on timely insights need to achieve in order to improve their operational efficiency, optimise their operations, and prevent failures. Through the application of the YoLov8 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), this research introduces a novel approach to the processing of data in industrial settings in real time. The goal of this study is to find a solution to this urgent problem. The proposed approach involves utilising the YoLov8 CNN architecture to manage data in real time inside an Internet of Things environment. Through the use of simulated industrial scenarios, the study examines the latency reduction capabilities of YoLov8 in comparison to those of more conventional techniques. When it comes to processing data in real time in an industrial setting, the results demonstrate that the YoLov8 CNN approach is effective in significantly reducing the amount of latency that occurs.

articleTitle: Ensuring Data Integrity: A Strategic Approach to Reconciliation in Data Migration Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In today’s corporate landscape, mergers are increasingly prevalent, driven by various factors such as strategic expansion, cost efficiency, and technological innovation. However, post-merger, the migration of data from disparate systems becomes imperative to consolidate information and establish an efficient operational model. Despite the prominence of data migration projects, reconciliation often takes a backseat to ingestion and loading processes. This article emphasizes the critical importance of upfront consideration for reconciliation strategies, drawing from practical experience and research. Neglecting this phase can lead to chaotic testing processes and unnecessary iterations, hindering the migration process. Through this article, we present a comprehensive strategy for designing and implementing reconciliation processes, from proactive planning to meticulous execution. By prioritizing reconciliation upfront, organizations can mitigate risks and streamline their data migration endeavors for enhanced success. Our approach includes unmasking encrypted Personally Identifiable Information (PII), reconciling it with source data, and implementing a metadata-driven audit framework enriched with extensive log information. This ensures thorough oversight and accountability, safeguarding data integrity throughout the migration journey.

articleTitle: Content Based Surgical Video Retrieval using Scene and Motion Feature Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Effective clinical care increasingly relies on the ability to identify relevant details within extensive heterogeneous medical datasets, a task that becomes particularly challenging with complex media formats. Traditional keyword-based retrieval methods have limitations, and content-based retrieval techniques have gained popularity. Surgical video retrieval, a novel and largely unexplored research area, offers significant utility, especially in real-time clinical scenarios. As surgical procedures are predominantly recorded via video, these recordings are often stored on servers for subsequent access, necessitating efficient retrieval of specific footage segments by surgeons. In this work, we explore various models to extract scene and motion feature embeddings, accounting for motion intensity in videos. Accurate retrieval of similar videos or images requires precise embeddings of objects within the frames. For experimental validation, we utilized the public Cholec80 dataset, which includes cholecystectomy surgery videos. The combined scene and motion features are hashed to generate frame-level binary codes, facilitating rapid search and retrieval.

articleTitle: CLAHE - Enhanced Transfer Learning with VGG19 & DenseNet201 for Ocular Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Navigating the diverse diseases in ocular health presents a constant challenge for ophthalmologists. The complexities inherent in diagnosing these conditions demand not just expertise but also the aid of modern machinery. While traditional methods have their limitations, deep learning offers immense promise in comprehending and interpreting the intricacies of ocular diseases. This study explores the efficacy of VGG-19 and DenseNet201 models in classifying ocular diseases against healthy fundus images using the ODIR dataset, which comprises images of 5,000 patients depicting fundus scans categorized into eight distinct classes. Additionally, we utilize the Rotterdam EyePACS AIROGS dataset, a machine-learning-ready glaucoma dataset that includes a balanced subset of standardized fundus images. This dataset is split into training, validation, and test folders, which contain 2,500, 270, and 500 fundus images in each class, respectively. To address data imbalance for binary classification, we employed under sampling by limiting the number of images. Additionally, we utilized CLAHE (Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization) to enhance image quality and improve local contrast. As a result, DenseNet201 exhibited consistently high performance across multiple disease types, achieving training accuracies of 99.46% for myopia versus normal (M vs N) and 99.04% for cataract versus normal (C vs N).

articleTitle: Reliable Communication Protocols for Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs) have received tremendous concern and interest in recent years. They find many applications, from underwater exploration and monitoring to naval and marine operations. However, due to the harsh and challenging aquatic environmental conditions, the networks have to face challenges such as limited bandwidth, long latency, and packet loss, which makes the communication channel unreliable. Numerous approaches have been proposed to enhance reliable data transmission in UWSNs. These approaches range from protocol modification to specialized algorithms tailored to UWSN requirements. This paper explores UWSNs, focusing on their applications, challenges, and reliability protocols. It provides a comparative analysis of different reliability protocols, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses. Furthermore, it examines available simulators and testbeds for UWSNs and their approaches to ensuring reliable data transfer.

articleTitle: Secure Data Collection and Management in Internet of Things-Based Cloud Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Net of factors (IoT)-primarily based cloud networks are composed of more than one distributed computing gadget consisting of sensors, gateways, and edge servers that accumulate, examine, and save massive volumes of information. It is important to make certain that facts are accumulated comfortably and stored in an at-ease manner. This paper discusses diverse protection mechanisms that may be used to secure information collection and control within IoT-primarily-based cloud networks. Firstly, cozy identity management strategies along with identity authentication, token-primarily based authentication, and digital certificates are mentioned to ensure the relaxed acquisition and transmission of records. Secondly, encryption techniques such as secure encryption algorithms, key control strategies, and comfortable channel protocols are mentioned to enable storage and switching of the facts in a comfy way. Eventually, safety rules and great practices, together with identification and getting the right of entry to manipulate, data anonymization, and device logging, are supplied to ensure relaxed facts control in cloud networks. Its miles understood that comfortable facts control within IoT-based totally cloud networks is essential to guarantee confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information. As such, the security techniques discussed in this paper can assist in offering comfortable surroundings for the collection and management of facts in IoT-based totally cloud networks.

articleTitle: ANFIS-Based Crack Sealing in Concrete Pipes Using a Pipe Crack Sealing Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this paper, the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) is applied to address crack repair in pipes. The methodology involves using a pipe crack sealing manipulator (PCSM), a tree-type robot with five branches for concrete pipe repair, capable of navigating through horizontal pipes, vertical pipes and surfaces. Based on the observations and simulation studies revealed that during the repair operation, only the fifth branch is actively involved. However, when the crack trajectory is sufficiently long, more branches can navigate through horizontal pipes and surfaces.
