Making use of those layout concepts can ensure the successful layout and implementation of verbal exchange software, leading to optimized community overall performance.

articleTitle: Importance Of Developing Social Skills In Engineering Students Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Developing soft skills in undergraduate students can be challenging due to the diverse demands of various environments and the increasing complexity of social interactions. To address this, universities should be encouraged to integrate social skills development programs into their curricula. Some institutions are already taking steps in this direction by implementing programs like educational initiatives and interactive activities designed to enhance social skills. This paper reports on an initiative at a university aimed at improving the social skills of engineering students. Two methodologies were employed to achieve this goal: the PRODIP (Interpersonal Professional Development Program) and a focused academic discipline that emphasizes various social skills. The PRODIP program, which has been running for four consecutive years, involved 52 students in one of its editions. It included 15 sessions per week over a period of 4 months, combining theoretical knowledge with practical training in social interactions. The effectiveness of PRODIP was evaluated by assessing the students social skills before and during and after the program, as well as three months later. The results showed that students improved their social skills, with these gains continuing over time. The program was delivered in two formats: one with three four-hour sessions covering topics like communication and teamwork for 26 students, and another with 15 two-hour sessions. Participants reported that these courses significantly contributed to their transition from student life to professional work environments. The paper discusses the necessity of implementing strategies to enhance students’ social skills and highlights the positive impact of these programs.

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of Automated Reasoning in Big Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In large-scale data analysis, computer reasoning is an important role. This era can pull significant files from substantial statistics and in a well-timed manner. In this way, through automatic feel, facts scientists and researchers can pick styles out of your statistics or even locate anomalies that could not have been detected in records units. Additionally, it speeds up constructing decision-making models and stimulates artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence permits herculean records mining and semantic analysis methods, including device learning, ontologiesystem gaining knowledge and natural language processing. Likewise, it offers a platform for creating and monitoring valuable findings, trends or patterns. This also helped to enhance the accuracy of analytic results and provides a more efficient way for statistics scientists & researcher s to analyze large amounts of data. This generation poses a chance to enhance state-of-the-art strategies by making the correct picks.

articleTitle: An Alternative Deep Learning Approach for Early Diagnosis of Malaria
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Considering the malaria disease-related moralities prevailing mainly in underdeveloped countries, early detection and treatment of malaria must be an essential strategy for lowering morbidity and fatality rates. Detection of Malaria using traditional investigation methods through blood samples and expert judgments was found to be time-consuming. In this paper, the authors introduced a Machine Learning automated system to eliminate the need for human intervention, which in turn enables early detection of malaria. The study has used various Deep Learning techniques such as traditional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), VGG19, ConvNeXtXLarge, ConvNeXtBase, ConvNeXtSmall, ConvNeXtTiny, InceptionResnetv2, Xception, DenseNet169, EfficientNetB7, MobileNet, ResNet50, and NasNetLarge as base models. These models have been trained and tested with microscopic blood smear images dataset and observed that ConvNeXtXLarge detects malarial parasites with an accuracy of 96%. The proposed method outperforms the existing approaches in terms of both accuracy and speed. The findings of this work can contribute to the development of more accurate and efficient automated systems for early detection of Malaria.

articleTitle: Utilizing Distribution Optimization through Cloud Computing in Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cloud computing is becoming part and parcel of the optimization of wireless networks for distributed mobile applications. Thanks to the scalable, distributed nature of Kubernetes which leverages the to-be had sources to construct disbursed dynamical structures that can be moreover optimized via cloud-enabled assets. To get the best performance there is a need to have distributed systems that can sense what resources are appropriate and efficiently consume the resources that are suitable for the given application being executed. These components are managed in cloud computing and thus can be used in an eco-friendly manner. Distributed cloud computing can be used to optimize the performance of the network by using the resources currently available for distributed applications over wireless networks. Disbursed cloud computing for wi-fi networks is aimed at attaining the most efficient use of resources of the network by the least finding it suitable for distribution. Cloud computing may even offload the burden on mobile gadgets with the aid of centralizing certain factors of the network (consisting of parameters governing access to crucial components of the community), and ensuring that community resources are flippantly distributed to the ends of the network. It enhances the accuracy of network routing, paving the way for the best resources to be allocated & utilized optimally. In addition, cloud computing can enable applications to run on multiple devices concurrently, taking advantage of the distributed nature of the wireless network.

articleTitle: Assessing the Readability and Coherence in Gemini’s Triple Draft Generation: A Multi-metric Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) play a crucial role in modern society by enabling natural language understanding and generation, which enhances communication, automation, and information processing across diverse sectors, fostering innovation and efficiency. The response generated by an LLM for a given prompt is crucial as it reflects the model’s ability to understand context, convey relevant information, and maintain coherence, thereby shaping user perception and interaction. This study analyzes the coherence and readability of drafts generated by the Gemini LLM across 20 prompts. Coherence scores, assessed through semantic and cosine similarity, reveal variability across drafts, with Draft-1 generally excelling in both semantic and cosine similarity across the prompts. Readability analysis using Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) metrics indicates that Drafts 2 and 3 consistently offer higher readability compared to Draft 1. However, user interaction with Gemini’s interface reveals the potential overlook of alternative drafts, highlighting the importance of exploring all options for optimal content selection. This study underscores the significance of considering coherence and readability metrics collectively for informed decision-making in content-generation tasks.

articleTitle: Exploration of Topic Relevance in Summaries for Re-summarizing using LLM in Crisis Chronology
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The current work proposes an exploration over the topical relevance of five extractive micro-blog summary techniques i.e. LexRank, LSA, T5, ALBERT & DistilBERT in crisis timeline for situational tweets of Turkey Earthquake 2023. Here, the topic model i.e. LDA is utilized to extract the crisis topics from generated summary using each technique in crisis timeline. Then a topical relevance has been formulated a) between incoming corpus (situational tweets) and generated summaries and b) among the summary techniques at distinct time frames t in crisis timeline. The behavioral patterns of each technique at distinct time frame in terms of topical correlation are observed for $6 \boldsymbol \& 7$ February, 2023 to interpret the utility of single or multiple summary algorithms in terms of capturing crisis topics at various time frames t of the crisis. Finally, the summaries of the most suitable techniques are provided as a prompt at every time frame t to Google’s LLM i.e. Gemini AI for re-summarizing at crisis timeline. It is evident from the results that the selection of multiple summaries as a prompt and providing it to LLM has improved the lexical & syntactic relevance of crisis summaries at crisis timeline.

articleTitle: Non-Contact Blood Pressure Estimation Using Camera-Based rPPG Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Blood pressure (BP) is a primary vital sign that provides critical insights into an individual’s overall health and potential underlying conditions. Abnormal BP levels, whether elevated (hypertension) or lowered (hypotension), can indicate serious cardiovascular issues, metabolic disorders, or other systemic problems. Monitoring BP is thus essential for early detection and management of these conditions. Traditional contact-based BP measurement techniques like arm cuffs and arterial lines are accurate but obtrusive, limiting mobility and risking dermatological issues from prolonged skin contact. While smartwatches enable more convenient tracking, they still require direct skin contact which can be cumbersome and cause irritation over extended wear. There is a need for entirely non-contact, unobtrusive BP monitoring solutions to avoid constraints of contact-requiring methods. This research investigates the potential of using remote photoplethysmography (rPPG), independent component analysis (ICA), pulse transit time (PTT), and regression techniques to estimate BP values from facial video recordings. By analyzing subtle color variations in the face caused by changes in blood volume, rPPG allows contactless extraction of physiological signals like heart rate. Combining this with PTT calculated from the video can enable BP derivation via regression modeling. However, rPPG is highly susceptible to factors like ambient lighting conditions, motion artifacts, and camera distance/angle. To assess feasibility, 40 PTT readings were collected from 20 individuals aged $21-45$ years where 2 recordings were captured per individual which lasted 10 seconds long. Testing on 6 of these individuals achieved 95.6% accuracy compared to a contact reference, indicating potential but also underlying challenges. The results suggest that more advanced rPPG extraction and processing techniques may be needed to obtain BP values robustly and accurately from facial videos, especially with subject motion. Nevertheless, this unobtrusive approach holds promise for enabling continuous cardiovascular monitoring in naturalistic settings.

articleTitle: An Optimized Segmentation of Images uisng Modified Level Set Method
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Image segmentation is a crucial step in processing digital images, aimed at partitioning an image into distinct regions or segments. The Additive Bias Correction (ABC) model addresses challenges in image segmentation arising from intensity inhomogeneity. While existing models, such as multiplicative bias field correction, have made progress, they encounter limitations such as slow segmentation speeds and limited applicability. The ABC model starts by defining local regions and a local clustering criterion to address intensity inhomogeneity. This criterion is then transformed into an energy function using the level set method. During segmentation, the bias field component and reflection edge structure are estimated to minimize this energy function. Compared to traditional multiplicative models, the additive approach achieves significantly faster computation speeds. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed ABC model surpasses traditional methods in terms of robustness and speed, representing a significant advancement in image segmentation techniques.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Retinal Diseases with Fundus Images Using Deep Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Retinal health issues are serious hazards to vision that must be detected early for successful treatments. These illnesses include diabetic retinopathy, age-related macular degeneration, cataracts, glaucoma, hypertension, myopia, and others. Manual segmentation of retinal health disorders with fundus images is time-consuming, prone to human error, lacks consistency, and requires specialized expertise. It is essential to have a deep learning-based diagnostic system. Collection of labeled fundus images is acquired as part of the research methodology, and the data is pre-processed to enhance quality. Methods for improving data further strengthen the model’s robustness and applicability. The work emphasizes how important interpretability is to the model’s decision-making process, ensuring transparency and fostering trust among medical professionals. The segmentation strategy addresses the difficulty of maintaining detailed vessel structure by combining U-Net, Global transformer, and Multiheaded attention. A Discriminative Restricted Boltzmann Machine is used for classification with $94 \%$ segmentation accuracy and $98 \%$ classification accuracy. Thus, this model shows promising efficacy in diagnosis of retinal diseases.

articleTitle: Neuralink: Reclassifying the Limits of Human Insight
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: “Neuralink” is a BCI embedded and delivered by the Elon Musk organization. It is an integrated Brain-Machine Interface (BMI) developed by the Neuralink Company. The current study presents a thorough overview of Neuralink’s salient characteristics, advancements, and possible applications in addition to its underlying theoretical framework. Through this process, a neuron and the spinal cord are connected, providing our body parts with additional information to enable movement, walking, running, and other activities. By creating a link between a person’s spinal cord and other body regions, BMIs are mostly used for therapeutic purposes which can be able to create unrest in treating various human mind related diseases, for instance epilepsy, schizophrenia, loss of motion, and also brain injury. BMIs, however, can also be utilized in classroom to regulate basic routines and identify emotions. Examination of neuralink’s mechanics by testing its concepts, data conversion, and terminal design is done in this paper.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis for Optimal Project Completion Utilizing Critical Path Method and Precedence Diagram Method for Efficient Solar Power Plant Installation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This project explores the utilization of Critical Path Method (CPM) and Precedence Diagram Method (PDM) in orchestrating and executing a solar power plant installation endeavor within the domain of Operation Research. The focus is on the application of these project management methodologies to optimize the scheduling, resource allocation, and overall execution of the installation process. CPM is employed to identify the sequence of critical activities that directly impact the project timeline, highlighting the tasks that cannot be delayed without affecting the project’s completion date. On the other hand, PDM is used to establish the relationships between activities, defining various dependency types such as finish-to-start, start-to-start, finish-to-finish, and start-to-finish. By meticulously mapping out the project activities and their dependencies, the study aims to construct comprehensive network diagrams for both CPM and PDM. These diagrams serve as tools for calculating the earliest and latest start and finish times for each activity, thereby identifying the critical path and potential slack times. The comparative analysis between CPM and PDM involves examining their effectiveness in handling complex project scenarios, particularly in terms of accommodating overlapping activities and managing intricate dependencies.The ultimate goal is to ascertain the shortest duration in days required for project completion, thereby contributing to the optimization of project timelines and enhancing the efficiency of solar power plant installations.

articleTitle: DES-KNORA Model: Developing an Intelligent System for Automatic Power Mode Adjustment in Electric Bicycles
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Electric bicycles (e-bikes) have gained considerable popularity due to their environmentally friendly nature and suitability as a mode of transportation. However, they face challenges related to manual switches for power mode changes. A potential solution to this issue could be the application of machine learning to improve their performance and safety. Previous research has explored the use of machine learning for gear shifting in bicycles, but there remains a gap in the specific application of ML for automating power mode changes in electric bikes. In order to address this gap, the study proposes the design and evaluation of an intelligent system based on machine learning that can automatically adjust electric bike power modes for users. The research team utilized a Hero Lectro C7+ electric bike and designed and tested a novel ensemble model, the dynamic ensemble selection approach model (DES-KNORA), against several machine learning techniques to predict the need for power mode changes. The DES-KNORA ensemble model fit the measured data the best, with an F1-score of 0.9995 and an accuracy of 99.95%. The study’s results show that the suggested method works in real life, making the ride smoother and less annoying for riders.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction Techniques in Document Image Analysis An Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Function extraction is a vital step in file photo analysis. It enables to reduction in the size of the statistics, similar capabilities from exclusive files can be identified, and the traits of the report may be better understood. Various techniques were advanced to extract features from record pictures, such as Counting Neighboring Pixels (CNP), aspect Detection (ED), grey-stage Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM), neighborhood Binary styles (LBP), Wavelet rework (WT), and Zernike second Invariants (ZMI). Each method has its blessings and drawbacks, which makes it suitable for particular responsibilities or files. Counting Neighboring Pixels (CNP) is an easy but powerful approach for characteristic extraction. CNP works by means of counting the range of pixels that can be comparable (in phrases of brightness, color, contrast, and so forth.) to a target pixel. It is a great technique for report pictures as it can be used to pick out the structural functions of the report with no prior understanding. However, CNP could be more sturdy to photograph noise. Aspect detection (ED) is a technique for extracting features from a picture. It’s used to locate the rims or outlines of an item.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT-4 and LLaMA: Performance Evaluation on Text Summarization, Data Analysis, and Question Answering
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: ChatGPT has demonstrated the strong performance of large language models (LLMs) in natural language tasks since its November 2022 rollout by using vast datasets with trillions of parameters for training. This paper compares ChatGPT-4 and LLaMA on three NLP topics: text summarization, data analysis, and question answering using CNN/DailyMail, Airbnb Activity, and SQuAD as some of the datasets used. ChatGPT-4 outperforms LLaMA in all aspects, giving better accuracy, coherence, and relevance results, albeit with slightly higher computation costs. ChatGPT-4 performs well regarding text summarization, resulting from high BLEU scores and human evaluations for coherence, relevance, and readability. Data analyzed by ChatGPT-4 will give a more accurate insight into this topic and provide higher-quality visualizations and more precise outputs. For question answering it ranks above LLaMA in terms of precision, recall, F1 scores, correctness, and relevancy according to human ratings.

articleTitle: Ensemble-Based Network Attack Prediction in WSN
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Computer network security and integrity are severely impacted by network attacks. The ability to predict and prevent these attacks is crucial for maintaining a secure network environment. Supervised ML (Machine Learning) techniques have emerged as effective tools for network attack prediction because of their ability to analyze large amounts of network data and identify patterns indicative of malicious activity. We present a comprehensive analysis of supervised machine-learning techniques for the prediction of network attacks. We gather and preprocess the data, extracting pertinent features and converting them into a format suitable for machine learning algorithms. We assess the performance of these algorithms. We investigate the interpretability of the trained models to gain insights into the underlying patterns and characteristics of network attacks. This allows network administrators to understand the nature of attacks and develop appropriate defense strategies. Additionally, we discuss the challenges and limitations associated with the application of supervised ML techniques in the domain of network attack prediction, such as the need for real-time analysis and the emergence of sophisticated evasion techniques.

articleTitle: Realizing the Full Benefits of Data Science with AI Powered Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper specializes in the significance of utilizing synthetic Intelligence (AI) powered solutions to maximize the ability effect of facts and technological know-how in addressing actual-world troubles. It highlights the advantages of the use of AI-powered answers, which include improved accuracy, greater green time utilization, and complex analytics competencies in current enterprise problems. The paper additionally discusses various demanding situations that agencies and developers have faced even as they are trying to create meaningful AI-driven answers, and it outlines procedures for overcoming them. Additionally, a number of first-class practices for spotting and taking benefit of the full advantages of facts and technological know-how with AI-powered answers are supplied. Eventually, the paper discusses a way to construct and operate a successful AI-powered way to maximize the impact of records science at the current global enterprise.

articleTitle: 3D Channel Estimation for Millimeter Wave Networks Using Specialised Training Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Large antenna systems powered by millimeter-wave signals are a key enabling technology in 5 G and beyond systems. Exploiting the approximate sparse nature of millimeter channel matrices, compressive sensing methodologies for channel estimation have garnished a lot of interest owing to a simpler receiver algorithm but at the expense of a large training overhead. In this work, we formulate channel estimation problem as a sparse signal recovery problem in compressive sensing and invoke the usage of the existing mutually unbiased bases (MUB) based training beams. We consider three dimension beamforming by using UPAs at both the transmitter and receiver. We present detailed simulation studies using NYUSIM, an experimentally driven millimeter wave channel simulator. Our results show that the MUB-based scheme performs better than the other existing training schemes in terms of estimation error and spectral efficiency at the expense of lesser training overhead.

articleTitle: Federated Ensemble for Lung Pneumonia Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the realm of medical imaging, the detection of lung pneumonia through automated methods has garnered significant attention due to its potential to augment diagnostic processes. This study proposes a novel approach, termed Federated CNN Ensemble, aiming to enhance the accuracy and robustness of pneumonia detection from chest X -ray images through federated learning and ensemble techniques. The proposed method leverages convolutional neural networks trained locally at distributed medical institutions, thereby preserving data privacy and security while harnessing collectiveintelligence. By aggregating the learned models through an ensemble strategy, our approach achieves superior performance in pneumonia detection compared to standalone CNN models. This research contributes to the advancement of automated medical diagnosis systems, offering a promising avenue for scalable and collaborative disease detection in healthcare settings.

articleTitle: Time-Series-Based Stock Market Analysis using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The stock market is a very complex and volatile entity. Predicting it is a very challenging task but the emergence of Machine Learning and the availability of large-scale stock market data provide an opportunity to leverage data-driven approaches for improving prediction accuracy. In this paper, a framework for stock market analysis using up-to-date financial data extracted from the Yahoo Finance library and machine learning models is proposed. This paper’s approach is to capture the complex relationships and patterns in the data by using machine learning techniques. Specifically, machine learning algorithms like XGBoost, Gradient Boost, and Random Forests are employed. By analyzing diverse data sources from various companies, the aim is to extract valuable insights for stock prediction. The experiments involve processing contemporary stock data, implementing machine learning models on it, and comparing the outcomes. The predominant motives are to enhance stock prediction accuracy, manage inherent risks, enable real-time decision-making, and maximize profitability by providing valuable insights for investors that help optimize their portfolios. However, the results are real-time and the optimal algorithm for a particular stock is decided on a dynamic basis due to the stock market being volatile and unpredictable in nature.

articleTitle: Hot Spot Monitoring in Solar Arrays for Enhanced Performance with ML Predictions: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The solar energy plays a key role in our daily lives, offering various benefits including environmental, economic, and practical advantages. The role of solar energy in our daily lives continues to expand as technology improvement in technology, decrease in cost and the need for sustainable energy sources are increased more. But we also have more problems in solar as Hot spot and many more. The ‘Hot Spot’ problem of solar photovoltaic (PV) panels refers to the condition where the power performance system on the solar panel becomes extremely hot compared to the rest of the solar panel. When this happens just one zone of the solar panel reaches a very high temperature. This phenomenon can negatively impact the performance of the solar panel as the high temperatures in the affected area lower the output power. If it is not addressed, material degradation can lead to damage to the panel. Manual detection of hotspots is only possible after the negative effects become too big to ignore or when the glass turns brown due to excess heat

articleTitle: ANSAN: Data Interpretability based analysis of Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Glaucoma, an irreversible neurodegenerative disease leading to vision loss, remains a significant public health concern due to challenges in early detection and resource-intensive diagnostic procedures. Leveraging advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), presents a promising avenue for automating glaucoma detection, especially in regions lacking access to ophthalmologists. This study, explores the efficacy of glaucoma detection systems based on MobileNet architecture for mobile deployment, focusing on key factors such as dataset variability, size, and training time. This paper presents findings from two distinct datasets, namely chaksu and g1020, each trained on separate models termed the chaksu model and g1020 model, respectively. These models, evaluated against the Akshi dataset, demonstrate impressive performance, suggesting the feasibility of utilizing complete fundus images for Glaucoma detection, circumventing the complexities of segmentation tasks involving disc, cup, and blood vessels. In this study, LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) was integrated to enhance interpretability and shed light on the decision-making process of our glaucoma detection system based on MobileNet architecture. This research underscores the potential of mobile technologies coupled with AI in democratizing glaucoma screening, potentially mitigating the challenges posed in resource-constrained settings.

articleTitle: Shallow and Deep Learning Based Approaches for Malicious URL Detection: A Comprehensive Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the realm of cybersecurity, the relentless surge in cyber threats, particularly emanating from the proliferation of malicious URLs, poses a formidable challenge. This study delves into the pressing need for robust detection mechanisms to thwart these threats effectively. Through meticulous dataset curation involving 30,000 URLs, employing a diverse array of extraction methods, and leveraging advanced machine learning models this research comprehensively evaluates malicious URL detection performance. Notably, the ensemble Random Forest model emerges as the top performer, showcasing its pivotal role in cyber threat classification. Additionally, the incorporation of novel dataset creation methods and effective data preprocessing techniques, such as the Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE), underscores the significance of this research endeavor. The study’s findings underscore the efficacy of Random Forest in accurately discerning between benign and malicious URLs. Moreover, insights gleaned from model assessment metrics, including precision, recall, F1 score, and confusion matrices, shed light on the models’ generalization and stability. Overall, this research contributes to fortifying digital environments against evolving cyber threats, underscoring the pivotal role of machine learning in bolstering cybersecurity defenses.

articleTitle: Data Science Approaches for Churn Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Customer churn poses a significant challenge for subscription-based businesses, leading to revenue losses and decreased profitability. Predicting and managing churn is crucial for sustaining business growth and ensuring customer satisfaction. This paper reviews state-of-the-art machine learning techniques employed in churn prediction, ranging from traditional algorithms like logistic regression and decision trees to advanced approaches such as ensemble methods and neural networks. By exploring methodologies and practical applications, this paper provides insights for researchers and practitioners aiming to optimize churn prediction strategies. Additionally, the paper discusses the background of churn prediction, highlighting the limitations of traditional statistical models and the emergence of data science techniques. Through feature engineering, exploratory data analysis, and the utilization of various machine learning algorithms, businesses can develop effective churn prediction systems to enhance customer retention and satisfaction.

articleTitle: Resolving Design Clashes Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The construction process relies heavily on the collaborative efforts of professionals, including engineers, designers, architects, and project managers, who work together to guide projects from start to finish. This collaborative effort faces numerous challenges, such as inadequate communication among the stakeholders, budgetary constraints, and difficulties in interdisciplinary collaboration. These challenges can often lead to design clashes, where conflicting elements occupy the same space in the design. Addressing these clashes promptly is crucial to minimize rework, enhance efficiency, and ensure the smooth progression of construction projects. Failure to address these clashes in a timely manner can lead to costly rework. This paper proposes a machine learning algorithm to tackle this issue. The proposed algorithm trains multiple bagging classifiers with neural network base models, evaluates their performance, and finally creates a voting classifier using the trained models for ensemble prediction. The proposed algorithm exhibits noteworthy performance in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Gain and Bandwidth Enhanced Microstrip Patch Antenna Using a Compact and High Aperture-Efficient Metamaterial Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This work presents a compact and aperture-efficient metamaterial superstrate on the top of a microstrip patch antenna for gain and bandwidth enhancement. The compact transmissive metamaterial unit-cell is designed using the proposed dual concentric circular slots (DCCS) structure on a square patch (DCCS-SP). The proposed metasurface is designed by organizing the DCCS-SP unit cell in the form of four concentric circles named the DCCS-metasurface (DCCS-MS). The DCCSSP unit-cell’s intrinsic properties are extracted by the free space technique, which shows near-zero negative refractive index (NZRI), permittivity, and permeability in the frequency band of 9.0 - 9.50 GHz. An Inset-fed Rectangular Microstrip Antenna (IRMPA) is designed for 9.40 GHz resonance frequency with an operational frequency band from $9.15-9.63 \mathrm{GHz}$, bandwidth, 480 MHz, and a total gain of 4.7 dBi. The DCCS-SP unit-cell of size, $0.152 \lambda_{\mathrm{g}} \times 0.121 \lambda_{\mathrm{g}}$ is used to form the DCCS-MS of size $1.91 \lambda_{\mathrm{g}} \times 1.91 \lambda_{\mathrm{g}}$ is placed at the height of 19.0 mm from the ground on the top of an IRMPA to form a cavity with the IRMPA. The overall performance of the IRMPA is improved with DCCS-MS, which shows the enhancement of gain by 5.25 dBi and bandwidth by 360 MHz.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Deception Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Following decades of study proving that people cannot reliably discern dishonesty, a strong solution combining gestures, auditory characteristics, and micro-expressions is put forth. This multimodal deep learning system records verbal and nonverbal indicators linked to deceitful conduct by examining speech patterns and facial features. Different categorization models combine MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) with CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) architectures to process auditory information and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) to handle visual features. Accuracy and dependability are increased by combining predictions from many modalities using an ensemble fusion approach. The approach includes ensemble modeling, feature extraction, modality separation, and video preprocessing. With an overall accuracy of $\mathbf{9 4. 2 3 \%}$, evaluations on a carefully selected dataset of trial hearing recordings show excellent performance. The integrated technique provides a non-intrusive and dependable deception detection system by successfully separating honest from misleading remarks. The solution’s potential uses in security, human resources, and law enforcement underscore its significance and promise as a new benchmark for precise lie detection.

articleTitle: An Efficient AI and IoT Enabled System for Human Activity Monitoring and Fall Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Falls present a significant health risk, particularly among the elderly, necessitating reliable wearable fall detection systems. This paper introduces an advanced AI-powered system that integrates Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for synthetic data augmentation and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for robust fall detection and daily activity recognition. The primary challenge in developing effective fall detection systems lies in the scarcity and diversity of real-world fall data. This paper addresses this challenge innovatively by employing a GAN trained on datasets of authentic fall events to generate synthetic data. This augmentation strategy significantly expands the training dataset, enhancing the model’s capacity to generalize across various fall scenarios and daily activities. The system leverages a specialized 1D CNN architecture designed for processing accelerometer and gyroscope readings obtained from wearable devices, enabling precise feature extraction to distinguish subtle differences between falls and routine movements. The evaluation results demonstrate a notable advancement by achieving a superior accuracy of $99 \%$ for fall detection while minimizing false positives. The developed CNN model can also classify 15 kinds of falls and 19 types of daily life activities.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Cricket: A Machine Learning Approach to IPL Score Prognostication
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Indian Premier League (IPL) is a very popular and globally recognized cricket tournament, attracting many spectators worldwide. The proposed work aims to predict cumulative scores of teams in IPL using attributes such as batting and bowling team data, total runs, wickets, overs, runs scored in the last 5 overs, batting taken in the last 5 overs, and Total Score. This work employs Machine Learning (ML) techniques such as Linear Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models to predict IPL scores. The database considered in this work was carefully obtained from well-known websites such as ESPN and Cricbuzz, ensuring the reliability and credibility of the research. In addition to the prediction models, a user-friendly graphical user interface (GUI) is implemented for easy interaction with the prediction system. This GUI allows the user to enter the necessary match data and displays the predicted score. Uniquely, this system offers a range of points that can be extended up to 5 runs from the estimated score. This range recognizes the unpredictable nature of cricket matches and provides more realistic and practical predictions. The combination of various ML models and an intuitive GUI makes this system a powerful tool for IPL score prediction.

articleTitle: A Voting based Assimilation Method for the Winning Neurons in Multi-Level SOM to Cluster the Convoluted Biomarkers of a Time Varying ‘Omic Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Early detection and modelling of disease development are crucial for effective healthcare. Diseases develop over time, with changes in ‘omic expressions, leading to genotypic or phenotypic changes in the sample. These changes are unique to disease samples and can develop in various parts of the body and continue to grow, if not addressed in a timely fashion. However, due to the availability of a small population of very high dimensional ‘omic samples, this presents a significant challenge. Thus, dimensionality reduction techniques are essential to simplify the data while preserving its core structure. This work focuses on the technique of Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF), where the decomposed basis and coefficient matrices are component-wise non-negative. NMF has recently gained prominence for analyzing time-varying ‘omic data and the present work uses a contemporary variant of NMF, called flexible NMF (FNMF). In a bid to effective extract differentially expressed biomarkers using NMF, this work proposes a voting based assimilation method for factorized convoluted biomarkers obtained from FNMF using a hybrid MLSOM (Hy-MLSOM) architecture. This results in an enhanced representation of the ‘omic data, thereby facilitating more effective and precise disease detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cloud Resource Management through Predictive Neural Networks and Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Prior strategies for scaling microservices encompassed various techniques, including diverse processing approaches and mathematical models. However, these methodologies often exhibited limitations in predictive accuracy and management complexity. This study employs Reinforcement Learning as an innovative alternative, particularly the Double Deep Q-Networks Algorithm. This approach autonomously monitors and evaluates essential scaling parameters, promptly triggering on-site actions when warranted. It adeptly balances the dual aspects of environment exploitation and exploration, optimizing computational resource usage while enhancing cost-effectiveness. Empirical evaluations substantiate the superiority of this approach in dynamically scaling cloud services with precision and resource optimization. By integrating LSTM and RNN predictive capabilities with Reinforcement Learning, this research contributes to efficient cloud resource management, a vital facet of contemporary cloud computing paradigms.

articleTitle: Accent-Enhanced Automatic Speech Recognition for Multilingual Classrooms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In an increasingly interconnected world, universities face the challenge of hosting diverse students from different backgrounds. The biggest obstacle to effective communication and learning in multicultural classrooms is teacher and student diversity. To overcome this challenge, we propose the development of noise-enhanced automatic speech recognition (ASR), specifically for multilingual classrooms. The system is designed to provide instant feedback on lessons while preserving the subtleties of speech, thus improving understanding and creating a learning environment. Using the advanced capabilities of the Transformer model together with the convolutional neural network (CNN) highlight classifier, the proposed system provides powerful and accurate transcription capabilities. This article provides an overview of the design, implementation, and evaluation of voice-enhanced ASR, demonstrating its potential to transform communication and learning in a variety of educational settings.

articleTitle: IIR Filter Design Using Sparrow Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper introduces an advanced methodology for the design of an infinite impulse response (IIR) of order 8, utilizing the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA). SSA is a cuttingedge meta-heuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging and anti-predation behaviors of sparrows, renowned for its swift convergence and precision in identifying optimal solutions. This study harnesses SSA to optimize critical filter parameters, including peak stopband attenuation, transition width and normalized passband attenuation. The optimized coefficients derived through SSA are employed to develop a high-performance IIR filter. Comparative analysis and experimental results underscore the superior efficacy of the SSA-based design approach over traditional optimization techniques, demonstrating notable improvements in accuracy and efficiency. This work underscores the potential of SSA as a formidable tool for the sophisticated designing of IIR filters, offering significant advancements in the field of digital signal processing.

articleTitle: The Role of Cloud Computing in Real-Time Big Data Analytics for Smart Cities and Infrastructure Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With the enhancement of Big Data and Smart Cities, Cloud Computing has emerged as an advanced technology. Innovative city operations require real-time processing of vast volumes of data from various sources like sensors, IOT devices, or social media so that it can be analyzed and acted on in real-time with better automation for its infrastructure against different parameters. This article examines the potential of cloud computing to enable real-time big data analytics for smart cities and infrastructure automation. The cloud allows for real-time big data analytics, collecting input from disparate sources across a business ecosystem and analyzing it immediately for actionable insights. The need for large amounts of data combined with the nature of many Iota devices necessitates processing and storage at scale, a task uniquely suited to cloud computing due to its ability to provide scalability, flexibility, and lower cost essential qualities in building intelligent cities or automated infrastructure. Cloud computing offers a space for shared data and collaborative analysis, allowing the city government to open up its vast browser-based datasets so that other agencies (both within government and outside it), researchers, and even citizens can access this information, in turn driving innovation or assisting with strategic planning. Moreover, the evolution not just in cloud-based machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms but also device-side AI/ML allows for predictive analytics, which can be helpful to preemptively discern potential failures to prevent them pro-actively, thus augmenting city operations efficacy as well as resource utilization besides operational efficiency of infrastructural management. Cloud computing is integral for real-time and big data analytics and innovates cities, organizations, and infrastructure.

articleTitle: Enhancing Quality of Life: An AI-Enabled Assistive System Integrating BCI and Transformer Model for Elderly and Disabled Individuals
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Brain Computer Interface (BCI) makes it possible for a machine and human brain to communicate directly. It serves as a valuable tool for individuals facing speech disabilities, physical limitations, and cognitive disorders. BCI operates by capturing signals from the brain known as electroencephalography (EEG) waves. In this paper, an AI-based assistive system that utilizes Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technology is proposed. A non-invasive electrode band containing six electrodes is placed on the scalp. The brain signals are captured using electrodes and converted into raw EEG signals using Arduino. Filtering techniques like high-pass, low-pass, and notch filters are applied to improve signal quality by removing noise and artifacts. Power Spectral Density (PSD) analysis identifies usable frequencies. Features extracted include frequency-domain and time-frequency domain features. Transformer module convert EEG signals into characteristics using techniques like Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), teaching patterns to a Transformer-based model for anomaly detection. A translation algorithm facilitates communication between users speaking different languages. Translated text is displayed on user devices for comprehension.

articleTitle: Security for the Internet of Things: A Comprehensive Review and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is enabling unprecedented levels of automation and connectivity across industries, but it also poses significant security threats that must be addressed to preserve a stable and secure IoT ecosystem. In addition to stressing the urgent need for strong security measures at every tier of the IoT architecture, IoT security concerns and attacks are covered in detail in this article.Secure data transmission is required at the perception layer due to dangers including data insertion and eavesdropping. Strict security protocols are necessary because the network layer faces threats like packet injection and ARP poisoning. Firmware updates and secure provisioning are required by the support layer, which controls device connection and data storage. Strong security measures are crucial because the application layer, which handles client services, is vulnerable to threats like malicious code and data tampering.Throughout the IoT architecture, customized approaches are needed to address these security concerns. To ensure the reliability and durability of IoT networks, cooperative efforts are necessary for the development and application of efficient solutions. This study intends to contribute to a secure IoT environment that can meet the increasing demands of connected devices and systems by concentratingon creative security solutions at each level.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and EHR-Driven Image Processing Framework for Lung Infection Detection in Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Image processing plays a pivotal role in healthcare across various domains, revolutionizing diagnostics, treatment, and patient care. In medical imaging, such as X-rays, CT scans, MRI, and ultrasound, image processing techniques enhance image quality, aiding in the accurate interpretation of medical conditions. In healthcare, the integration of image processing with data analytics holds immense potential to revolutionize diagnostics, treatment, and patient care. By combining the power of image processing techniques with advanced analytics algorithms, healthcare providers can extract valuable insights from medical images, leading to more accurate diagnoses and personalized treatment plans. Image processing can enhance the quality of medical images, making subtle abnormalities more visible and enabling automated analysis of large datasets. Data analytics techniques, deep learning is applied to these processed images to identify patterns, predict outcomes, and assist clinicians in making informed decisions. This paper focused on the development of an effective image processing technique with a data analytics model for the detection of infection or diseases in the lung. To evaluate the characteristics of lung diseases this paper proposed point estimation centroid Deep Learning (PEC-DL). The proposed PEC-DL uses point estimation for the segmentation of images to perform the feature extraction. With the estimated points the segmentation is performed with the extraction of features in the images. Once the features are estimated deep learning is implemented for the estimation of features. Through the estimated features deep learning model performs the classification for the estimation and prediction of diseases in the lung region. Simulation analysis demonstrated that the proposed PEC-DL model achieves a higher detection rate of $\mathbf{9 8 \%}$ for the correct classification of lung diseases. The performance of the proposed model exhibits $\sim 12 \%$ improved performance than the conventional deep learning model.

articleTitle: TIPPS: Comparative Analysis of Preprocessing and Postprocessing Techniques for Tumor Images Across Different Modalities
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Tumor image analysis is essential for diagnosing and treating cancer. This study conducts a comparative analysis of preprocessing and postprocessing techniques applied to tumor images from different modalities: CT scan, MRI, and histopathological images. It investigates how these techniques enhance image quality, improve feature extraction, and aid accurate tumor classification and diagnosis. Preprocessing involves techniques like denoising techniques, unsharp masking, contrast stretching, and contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization. These techniques are applied to original dataset and new enhanced version of datasets are produced then. Further, classification algorithms such as support vector machine, decision tree, random forest, and logistic regression, enable accurate tumor categorization based on extracted features. Visualization and interpretation methods help clinicians understand complex image data. Finally, voting classifier is applied over original and new enhanced version of produced datasets acting as the post-processing technique. Through evaluating various preprocessing and postprocessing method(s) across modalities, this study aims to optimize tumor image analysis for clinical use. The findings of this study can contribute to the development of robust and effective pipelines for tumor image analysis, ultimately supporting improved diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient care.

articleTitle: ParkinSense: A Fuzzy Inference System designed to aid in diagnosing Parkinson’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Parkinson’s Disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that poses significant challenges in early detection and precise classification of its severity. This research paper introduces a machine learning and fuzzy logic based approach to address these challenges by developing a predictive model for Parkinson’s disease detection and severity classification. The study utilizes a diverse dataset comprising clinical information and speech features from individuals with and without Parkinson’s disease. Through comprehensive data preprocessing and feature engineering, the paper aims to extract relevant patterns and biomarkers associated with the disease and to predict a probability of the disease using a fuzzy approach. A variety of machine learning algorithms, including but not limited to support vector machines, random forests, and neural networks, are employed to train and evaluate the model. The focus is on achieving high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity in detecting the presence of Parkinson’s disease. Additionally, the model is designed to classify the severity levels of Parkinson’s disease, providing valuable insights into disease progression. The findings aim to enhance our understanding of the disease’s underlying mechanisms and facilitate more targeted and personalized treatment strategies. The proposed model’s performance is assessed through rigorous validation techniques, including cross-validation and independent testing. The paper aspires to bridge the gap between machine learning advancements and the pressing clinical needs in Parkinson’s disease diagnosis and severity assessment, fostering a more informed and proactive approach to patient care. This research investigates Parkinson’s disease detection through machine learning, incorporating features such as shimmer and frequency analysis. By employing advanced algorithms, the study aims to enhance diagnostic precision by examining subtle vocal and movement characteristics associated with Parkinson’s. The findings provide valuable insights into the potential of integrating multiple features for effective Parkinson’s disease diagnosis using machine learning and fuzzy based techniques.

articleTitle: kMiST: A KD-Tree Based Fast Minimum Spanning Tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Minimum Spanning Trees (MSTs) are crucial in graph theory and computer science for understanding complex networks. Their ability to efficiently connect nodes while minimizing total edge weight makes them indispensable tools in various domains. However, the quadratic time complexity of standard MST algorithms, renders them impractical for large-scale graphs, motivating the development of more efficient approaches for MST construction. A critical aspect is how to efficiently generate a intermediary graph that sufficiently encapsulates local neighborhood information with sub-quadratic time. We propose a method utilizing k-dimensional trees (kd trees) for efficient construction and connection of similarity graphs. By harnessing the spatial indexing properties of k-d trees, this approach seeks to mitigate computational challenges often encountered in graph construction. Our algorithm achieves a time complexity of $O\left(n \log ^{2} n\right)$, significantly improving upon the $O\left(n^{2}\right)$ complexity of standard MST algorithms. Experimental analyses show that intermediary graph collects shorter edges and disregards the longer edges. The proposed method’s performance was also justified through its application on several synthetic and real datasets with various characteristics, showcasing its potential to handle large-scale graphs efficiently.

articleTitle: An assessment of the effectiveness of deep learning techniques for allocating resources in 5G networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper evaluates the efficiency of deep learning strategies for aid allocation in 5G networks. 5G networks have annoying requirements, which include high statistics charge, low latency, reliability, and flexibility. Deep learning is a powerful technical device for optimizing aid allocation in 5G networks, as it can help to expect the modifications in statistics needs and examine the underlying patterns of the residents’ visitors. For you to examine the efficiency of deep getting-to-know techniques in 5G networks, the authors conducted simulations in a laboratory-scale testbed with the ability to regulate records site visitors and surroundings. The assessment covers metrics consisting of the normalized throughput, implied squared error, signal-to-noise ratio, and resource utilization. The authors determined that the usage of deep mastering techniques caused improvements in the normalized throughput and the mean squared error. The deep mastering approaches did not impact the signal-to-noise ratio and resource usage. The authors have stated that in 5G networks, resource allocation can be performed very well by using various strategies with deep knowledge, which were identified as powerful enough to apply and fulfil the requirements of resource scheduling for future generation five G networks.

Index Terms: Root Mean Square Error Of Cross-validation

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Solution for Indoor and Outdoor Floor Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Our project introduces a better solution in the quest for efficient floor cleaning: a Bluetooth-controlled floor cleaning robot, moving beyond the hand-operated sanitation methods of the past, our robot embodies a fusion of mechanical ingenuity and electronic sophistication. Imagine a sleek, agile robot equipped with a sweeping brush, mop arm, and duster arm, all harmoniously orchestrated through a user-friendly smartphone app. This paper documents our journey in conceptualizing, crafting, and validating this marvel of modern technology. At its core, our robot boasts formidable BLDC motors, enabling seamless navigation across various floor surfaces with remarkable precision. The front-mounted sweeping brush diligently gathers dust and debris, channeling them towards a concealed dust collector for efficient disposal. Meanwhile, the duster arm delicately attends to elevated surfaces, leaving no corner untouched. But the innovation doesn’t stop there. Positioned at the back, the mop arm, coupled with a water tank, ensures thorough wet mopping, enhancing the robot’s cleaning capabilities. Inside, an Arduino Mega microcontroller serves as the brain, orchestrating every movement with finesse. Bluetooth connectivity further elevates user interaction, allowing seamless control via a custom MIT App Builder application. Our robot isn’t just a cleaning tool; it’s a game-changer. Equally proficient in both indoor and outdoor settings, it promises to transform floor maintenance with its unmatched efficiency and user-centric design. From residential spaces to bustling commercial settings, our Bluetooth-controlled floor cleaning robot offers a transformative solution to modern-day cleaning challenges. Join us as we unravel the intricacies of this innovative creation, from its mechanical marvels to its digital prowess. Discover simplicity and sophistication intertwined in our mission to redefine cleanliness and convenience in automated floor cleaning. Get ready to welcome a new age of floor care with our Bluetooth-controlled floor cleaning robot at your disposal.

articleTitle: End to End Simple Indian Sign Language Sentence Translation Using Sign Transformer Network
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Sign language is a method for 6.1% of the people globally with hearing impairments to communicate as communication in spoken languages is not a viable option. Historically, Indian Sign Language (ISL) character recognition has achieved significant accuracy goals, but the work on translation of sentence-level ISL has been slow and rather inaccurate. This paper proposes a method that enables the translation of simple ISL sentences with compound signs to English sentences using the state-of-the-art Sign Transformer Network [5] [31]. We have used publicly available ISL datasets namely the ISL_CSLRT dataset [9] consisting of 1036 word level images over 700 fully annotated videos; and the INCLUDE50 dataset [28] consisting of 4287 videos over 263 words; to train the model.

articleTitle: Investigating Welded Region Stability for Thermal Analysis with YOLOV3
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology that integrates YOLOv3, a cutting-edge object identification model, with thermal analysis approaches to examine and evaluate the structural integrity of welded areas. The technology being presented utilizes the sophisticated object detection capabilities of YOLOv3 to reliably find and track specific regions of interest inside a welded structure. By incorporating this object detection model into thermal analysis tools, it becomes possible to see and study the temporal temperature distribution and thermal characteristics of the discovered locations. The study entails the collection of thermal data through the utilization of sophisticated sensors and thermal imaging technologies. This approach aims to acquire a thorough comprehension of the distribution and dissipation of heat inside the welded area under different operational circumstances. This methodology enables the continuous monitoring of operations in real-time, enabling the identification of possible concerns such as excessive heat, concentrated stress, or material distortions. These factors have the potential to undermine the integrity and security of welded structures. The findings of this study make a valuable contribution towards improving the quality control and maintenance practices of welded components.

articleTitle: Empirical Investigation on Similarity Measures used in Recommendation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Similarity measures play a crucial role in recommendation systems for quantifying the likeness between users or items within the system. These measures are fundamental in collaborative filtering, a widely used approach for generating personalized recommendations. This study analyses 29 distinct similarity measures including common one like Cosine, Jaccard, using metrics like recall, precision, and diversity on datasets like MovieLens and Bookcrossing. Findings from the result revealed that certain measures, such as PIP (Proximity Impact Popularity), CPCC (Constrained Pearson Correlation Coefficient), NHSM (New Heuristic Similarity Model), and COD (Adjusted Cosine Measure), consistently outperform others, particularly in aligning with user preferences due to consideration of rating scale differences, integration of multiple similarity aspects, and normalization of shared ratings. This paper underscores the critical role of selecting appropriate similarity measures to enhance recommendations and user satisfaction in collaborative filtering - based systems.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Genomic Data Management in the Cloud- Novel Approaches for Secure Transfer and Storage of Sequencing VCF Data in the Realm of AI and Cybersecurity - A Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Large volumes of data are generated by next-generation sequencing. Many laboratories now use AI based cloud services, especially when internal information technology infrastructure is insufficient to meet data requirements due to the complexity and data management challenges involved with next-generation sequencing. Public cloud repositories of variants are also being used more often, and their data sets are being fed by crowdsourcing contributions of human genetic variation discovered in labs. This review’s objectives are to outline the difficulties in managing genomic data on the cloud, citing the security vulnerability associated with using AI and to talk about potential solutions to these problems. The advantages and definitions of cloud computing platforms are provided. The presented algorithm and discussion is a work in progress, intended to develop an environment for genetic information sharing on cloud using AI, that includes specific regulatory considerations for laboratories and compliance procedures.

articleTitle: Natural Language Processing-Enhanced Machine Learning Framework for Comprehensive Phishing Email Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Phishing emails remain a significant cybersecurity threat, bypassing traditional rule-based detection methods. This paper proposes a novel Machine Learning (ML) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) based approach for enhanced phishing email detection. The core of the model utilizes Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) for text vectorization and a Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB) classifier. This combination facilitates the identification of semantic cues and enables dynamic adaptation to evolving phishing tactics. The model prioritizes a balance between sensitivity and specificity, ensuring accurate detection of phishing attempts while minimizing false positives. The proposed PED (Phishing Email Detection) model achieves an accuracy of ${9 7. 2 5 \%}$ demonstrating a high overall accuracy in correctly classifying both legitimate and phishing emails. High F1-scores for two email categories are indicative of the proposed model’s robust performance in balancing precision and recall. The research offers a practical solution for cybersecurity professionals, contributing to a more secure email environment.

articleTitle: Area-Delay-Power Efficient VLSI Architecture of OTFS Transceiver in Multipath Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Orthogonal Time-Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation, an innovative communication protocol designed for high-speed vehicle communication, has demonstrated its stability and efficacy. This technique works with a new delay-Doppler domain waveform, offering significant performance advantages over traditional approaches such as Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM), especially in swiftly changing wireless environments. The initial phase of our research outlines the input-output dynamics of OTFS signals inside the domain of delay-time. Additionally, using the Lower-Upper (LU) decomposition technique, we present a novel and resource-efficient Very-large-scale Integration (VLSI) architecture of the OTFS transceiver. A comparative analysis with recent state-of-the-art is done, which demonstrates our optimized transmitter’s superior performance, boasting a $1.977 \%$ faster with ${6 7 . 4 7 2 \%}$ fewer Lookup Tables (LUTs) and 66.580% less Flip-Flops (FFs), indicating optimized latency and resource utilization and ${9 . 3 9 4 5 \%}$ less power. Moreover, we present timing analysis, resource utilization, and functionality testing for our suggested optimized receiver architecture, which shows that optimized architecture uses $39.193 \%$ less LUTs and 37.295% Digital-Signal-Processing blocks (DSPs) and $35.087 \%$ less power compared to existing recent work. We checked the sanity of our architecture output with MATLAB output.

articleTitle: Enhancing Disaster Awareness using BERT-Based Analysis of Twitter Chat
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Disaster management and response are critical for minimizing the impact of natural and man-made disasters. Social media platforms, particularly Twitter, have emerged as valuable sources of real-time information during disasters. This paper presents a novel approach to enhance disaster awareness through the analysis of Twitter chat using Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT). BERT is a powerful natural language processing model that has shown remarkable performance in various text analysis tasks. This work illustrates BERT for analyzing tweets related to disasters to improve situational awareness. This work uses disaster-related tweets dataset and preprocess them for analysis and and the data is fine-tuned using pre-trained BERT model. This research demonstrate that the BERT-based approach outperforms traditional methods like BILSTM-Glove with accuracy of 84.25% and BERT-BILSTM-CNN with accuracy of 95% in classifying disaster-related tweets.

articleTitle: An Efficient Pre-trained ResNet50 Model for Driver Drowsiness Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The driver drowsiness can cause life-threatening issues, and may result in serious consequences. This drowsiness can lead to poor decision-making, impaired reaction time, decreased concentration, and lane drifting and wavering. This study presents an efficient driver drowsiness detection system that uses the ResNet50 model for the classification of the images. This is one of the effective deep learning models and is well recognized for its ability to object detection by improving the prediction capabilities. The technology uses face analysis to detect different signs of tiredness in the collected dataset and reduces the dangers related to drowsed driving. The ResNet50 model has been trained on a varied dataset collected from Kaggle. The model is implemented with different epochs and demonstrates outstanding performance by reaching an impressive test accuracy of $\mathbf{9 5. 0 2 \%}$ at epoch 20. The test loss was also identified as 0.1349 on the same value of the epoch. This work further highlights the effectiveness of the ResNet 50 model in acquiring complex characteristics from images and correctly categorising indicators of tiredness and drowsiness. This work explores the structure, training procedure, and assessment criteria, providing insights into the detailed complexities of using ResNet50 for driver drowsiness monitoring. The achieved outcomes not only confirm the effectiveness of the system but also provide opportunities for future progress in intelligent transportation systems and contribute to the continuous development of driver safety technology.

articleTitle: A Theoretical Study on Non-Leaded Sr3NCl3 Perovskite through SCAPS-1D Using DFT-Derived Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>MX<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> perovskite-like materials hold immense potential as next-generation solar cell (SC) absorbers driven by remarkable structural, electronic, and optical properties. These properties are particularly advantageous for achieving efficient and affordable SC applications. This study employed the Density Functional Theory (DFT) technique to precisely determine some critical characteristics of $\mathbf{S r}_{3} \mathbf{N C l}_{3}$. Leveraging the insights gained from DFT calculations, the derived parameters were then incorporated into the SCAPS-1D simulation framework. A novel device architecture was proposed for simulation, featuring $\mathbf{S r}_{3} \mathbf{N C l}_{3}$ as the absorber layer, $\mathbf{S n S}_{2}$ as the electron transport layer (ETL), Spiro-OMeTAD as the hole transport layer (HTL), and FTO serving as the transparent conductive oxide (TCO). To optimize device performance, a parametric sweep was conducted, systematically varying parameters like absorber thickness, defect density, parasitic resistances, temperature effects, and back contact materials. The simulation results revealed a promising device performance with an open-circuit voltage ($\mathrm{V}_{O C}$) of $\mathbf{0. 8 4} \mathbf{~ V}$, a short-circuit current density $\left(J_{S C}\right)$ of $38.39 \mathrm{~mA} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}$, a fill factor (FF) of $\mathbf{7 4. 0 9 \%}$, and an impressive power conversion efficiency (PCE) of $\mathbf{2 3. 9 6 \%}$. This combined DFT and SCAPS-1D approach lays the pathway for the advancement of $\mathbf{S r}_{3} \mathrm{NCl}_{3}$-based SCs, paving the way for improved performance and efficiency in photovoltaic technologies.

articleTitle: Innovations in Real-Time Speech Translation: Leveraging Griffin-Lim Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: At present, speech-to-speech translator systems often involve multiple intermediary steps, such as automatic speech recognition (ASR), text-to-text machine translation (MT), and text-to-speech generation (TTS), leading to latency in response time and error propagation to later stages. Furthermore, they face challenges when dealing with languages lacking text representation. This paper examines the feasibility of a direct speech-to-speech translator model trained without the use of intermediate text representations during both training and inference. Employing the Librosa library for feature extraction, our approach uses Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) in conjunction with a sequence-to-sequence Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) model for training on a dataset of German-to-English audio. Our model achieved a BLEU score of 23.5, demonstrating competitive performance. The Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality (PESQ) score of 2.9 reveals high-quality generated speech. The average time delay for translation is ${1. 5}$ seconds, significantly lower than the 2.5 to 3 seconds observed in traditional cascade models. Our experiments, including noise-free speech generation using the Griffin Lim algorithm, underline the potential of our approach for real-time applications and lay a promising foundation for future research.

articleTitle: FraudGuard Pro: An Ensemble-Based Feature Selection Algorithm for Credit Card Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In recent years, the exponential growth in data volume and sample sizes across various domains, including finance and online transactions, has presented significant challenges for machine learning and data mining algorithms. High-dimensional and imbalanced datasets, often tainted with noise, have impeded the performance and interpretability of fraud detection models. Feature selection has emerged as a pivotal technique to address these challenges by identifying the most relevant features while discarding redundant or irrelevant ones.This research explores the landscape of feature selection methods and confronts the existing challenges in credit card fraud detection. We propose the “FraudGuard Pro Ensemble Feature Selection Algorithm,” designed specifically for credit card fraud detection tasks.
