Notably, our proposed model achieves an impressive accuracy rate of 99%, outperforming traditional models such as Logistic Regression (95%), Random Forest (98%), and Support Vector Machine (94%). This substantial improvement underscores the effectiveness of our algorithm in mitigating fraud while minimizing false positives, offering a promising solution for enhanced security in online transactions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Resource Allocation in Wavelength Division Multiplexing Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper explores useful resource allocation rules inside Wavelength Department Multiplexing (WDM) Optical Networks. WDM optical networks are leveraged to provide dependable and high-capability transmission for network offerings. To accurately version the complex topologies and useful resource allocations associated with this generation, researchers are faced with combinatorial optimization and ensemble gaining knowledge of issues, amongst others. The authors of this study’s paper observe present aid project techniques within each static and dynamic scenario and outline an evaluation of metaheuristic methods that may be of help. They then introduce their proposed acyclic-based approach, which outlines a community structure based totally on the candidate dominant hyperlink (CDL) principle and explores its performance under high dynamic networks. Constructing upon their research in associated paintings, the authors then speak about the results of their method in the context of the distributed Context-conscious Computing framework. The paper culminates by discussing destiny directions for researchers to influence the development of WDM networks.

articleTitle: Enhanced Diabetic Retinopathy Grading Using a Deep Hybrid Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In recent times there have been significant achievements in deep learning methodologies, the task of classifying retinal diseases is still challenging because of their minute pathological regions. The retina’s blood vessels can be compromised by diabetic retinopathy, a complication arising from diabetes falls under the distinct category of retinal diseases. Despite many attempts with classification models such as CNN and other deep learning approaches detection encounters several challenges. These include existing deep learning models are susceptible to biases towards either local or global perspectives. These biases can impact semantic-level understanding of these representations. This work proposes a hybrid framework for Diabetic retinopathy grading. Inspired from the achievements of vision transformers in image classification and its ability to capture spatial relationships in fundus images related to Diabetic retinopathy features. Augmenting this vision transformer with traditional multiple instance learning forming a hybrid model ViT-MIL. By combining ViT’s global learning capabilities with MIL’s effective local feature extraction this hybrid model achieves enhanced performance.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Cricket: Deep Learning Solutions for accurate No-Ball Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The identification of no-balls in cricket has seen a tremendous metamorphosis because to the incorporation of innovative technology such as computer vision, augmented reality, and deep learning. This article presents a short yet thorough examination of these technical advancements and their influence on the game. It investigates the use of computer vision algorithms and deep learning models in real-time bowler analysis, as well as the use of augmented reality overlays to improve detection procedures. It also emphasises the continuous need of umpire signals, particularly in high-stakes contests, in safeguarding cricket’s integrity and fairness.

articleTitle: Microcontroller-Driven Voice-Based Smart Wheelchair Navigation with Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the field of assistive technology, it is important to give users more control. However, traditional smart wheelchairs have difficulty interacting with users, especially those with limited mobility. To address this, we developed a new approach that uses a microcontroller-driven framework with machine learning on the Arduino Nano 33 BLE. This system uses TensorFlow and Keras in Google Colaboratory and incorporates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) to efficiently extract keywords from speech signals. The model combines microcontroller-driven mechanisms with advanced machine-learning algorithms. The paper explains the technical details, highlighting the role of CNN and MFCC in feature extraction. The study shows how the hardware and software work together within the Arduino Nano 33 BLE’s constraints. This research not only advances assistive technology, but also explores the relationship between microcontrollers, machine learning, and assistive devices. The methodology is rigorous and the empirical results demonstrate the voice-based navigation system’s effectiveness and potential in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Rainfall Prediction Enhancement Using SMOTE and Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Rainfall prediction is not an easy task when utilizing conventional approaches. For many stakeholders, including people planning their daily lives, farmers caring their crop, and fishermen who depend on the weather for their livelihood, accurate rainfall forecast is essential. Predicting rainfall more accurately has been a promising use of machine learning (ML) models in recent years. Our proposed framework suggests using classification techniques like Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classifier, and Decision Tree to construct and implement an ML model for rainfall prediction. SMOTE, an efficient data-balancing technique is used for balancing the minority and majority classes of the data, as rainfall is not a uniformly distributed event, leading to an imbalanced dataset. With an astounding F1-score of around 0.91, a precision of about 0.89, a recall of about 0.94, and an accuracy of roughly 0.91, the Random Forest classifier outperformed the others. These results demonstrate how machine learning (ML) models could possibly be used in producing accurate and depewhich are effective forndable rainfall forecasts, showing significant improvements over conventional prediction techniques.

articleTitle: Dual-Attention Protein Secondary Structure Prediction (DAPSS-Pred)
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Protein secondary structure prediction is a critical task in bioinformatics, essential for understanding protein function and aiding drug discovery. Traditional methods have achieved significant milestones, but there remains a need for further accuracy and efficiency improvements. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that combines Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory BiLSTM networks and Transformer models to enhance prediction accuracy. Our dual-model strategy leverages the sequential processing strengths of BiLSTM and the robust attention mechanisms of Transformers, enabling a more comprehensive analysis of protein sequences. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that this hybrid approach achieves superior performance, with Q3 accuracy reaching 92.03% and Q8 accuracy at 85.26%, significantly surpassing existing methods. This enhancement is ascribed to the capacity of BiLSTM to capture long-range dependencies and the Transformer’s capability to focus on relevant parts of the sequence. The integration of these models provides a powerful tool for predicting protein secondary structures with high precision. The findings suggest that our approach not only advances the current state of PSSP but also offers valuable insights that can accelerate bioinformatics research and drug discovery processes. This work underscores the potential of combining deep learning models to tackle complex biological challenges more effectively.

articleTitle: Quantum Machine Learning Compiler for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The proposed work aims at designing a composite classical-quantum machine learning architecture for binary classification using VQCs. The goal is to use the power of quantum computing to enhance and improve the efficiency of classical machine learning techniques. This is done through the development of a customized compiler that maps the high-level quantum code to specific quantum circuits that are then incorporated with conventional Neural Networks into what can be termed as Quantum Machine Learning (QML) model. Goaded by the likelihood of quantum computation to enhance computational precision and speed, this proposed work presents an outline of the theoretical quantum circuits, architecture and development of this special compiler and linking of both atomic and classical models. A proof of concept is done using the Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset to compare the capabilities of the suggested model with a more profound understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of this type of hybrid strategy.

articleTitle: Prediction of Lung Cancer using Genetic Algorithm and Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: As Lung cancer is a life-threatening disease for human beings, for the sake of saving lives, early detection of lung cancer is obligatory. Many existing methods have been proposed to predict lung cancer, but there is a scope to enhance the effectiveness of the existing methods with an optimal number of features. We have proposed a method based on Machine Learning (ML) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) approaches to predict lung cancer. The dataset has been collected from data.world. In our proposed method, we optimized the features using the feature selection technique and applied the ML method to classify lung cancer patients. The GA’s fitness function and operators have been designed for feature selection. Three classifiers were employed for the classification of Decision Tree, XG Boost, and Support Vector Machine (SVM). In this study, our proposed method reached 100% accuracy, which left behind other existing methods with 13 out of 24 features. In light of the experiment’s outcomes, the proposed method outperformed the other strategies currently using the fewest features.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics for Business Decision-Making: Unleashing the Power of Data-driven Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study examines how Predictive Analytics may alter company decision-making by employing sophisticated data-driven insights to improve strategic decisions. The report examines predictive analytics’ methods, algorithms, and applications, showing how it has transformed industry decision-making. Predictive Analytics’ ability to anticipate future trends, recognize patterns, and generate accurate forecasts based on previous data is examined in corporate operations. The paper uses case studies and practical examples to show how predictive models enhance risk management, resource efficiency, and strategic planning. Business decision-making is explored in relation to predictive analytics components including machine learning algorithms, statistical modeling, and data mining. The study highlights predictive analytics’ benefits in sales forecasting, consumer behavior research, and market trend projections. The study also examines the social and economic effects of corporate predictive analytics. It examines how data-driven decision-making boosts competitiveness, innovation, and economic development, serving national interests. For a balanced and transparent deployment, ethics, data privacy, and predictive analytics are considered. This study shows how predictive analytics can help firms make smart decisions in an age of unparalleled data availability. The study shares successful applications and addresses problems to help business professionals, analysts, and researchers navigate datadriven business strategies.

articleTitle: Enhanced provably secure public key encryption with keyword search scheme for secure cloud-based keyword search
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of cloud computing, a vast amount of data is now stored on cloud platforms. Due to security concerns, data owners often encrypt their data before uploading it to the cloud, making efficient search over encrypted data a significant challenge. Despite the existence of numerous schemes, such as Public Key Encryption with Keyword Search (PEKS), many struggle to resist keyword guessing attacks. In this research, we present a PEKS scheme in the random oracle model that extends provably safe PEKS strategies. Our plan is designed to allow secure email access from an email storage’s encrypted keyword list. Notably, it provides both ciphertext and trapdoor indistinguishability qualities and effectively counters keyword-guessing attacks. To thwart keyword-guessing attacks, we utilize the client’s private key for trapdoor encryption and the data owner’s private key along with the data client’s public key during the encryption process, ensuring only the data client can decrypt it. Additionally, our proposed scheme has been rigorously tested on a real testbed, demonstrating its suitability for searching encrypted data in cloud computing environments. Our scheme is approximately 14% faster for encryption than existing schemes, offering enhanced security and compactness.

articleTitle: Entropy Aware Spatial Smoothing in Removal of Perturbation as a Defense Against Adversarial Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The vulnerability of deep neural networks to adversarial attacks constitutes a major challenge for their robustness and dependability. Various defense mechanisms such as adversarial training, input transformation, randomization and denoising have been proposed to counter such attacks. Denoising mechanisms consider the adversarial perturbations added as a type of noise and employ image processing techniques to remove the adversarial perturbations. Spatial smoothing is a denoising defense technique that aims to smooth out the image or input data spatially to reduce the influence of adversarial perturbations. In this study, we propose an entropy aware spatial smoothing technique as defense against adversarial attacks. We have implemented efficient adversarial attacks namely, DeepFool, Carlini and Wagner’s attack and Fast Gradient Sign Method attack on an EfficientNet-B0 model and have studied the effectiveness of the proposed defense mechanism. The proposed approach demonstrates its efficacy against attacks that introduce limited perturbations, while concurrently enhancing the model’s accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis of the various YOLOv8 models in Detecting Defects in PCB
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the arena of electronics, the Printed Circuit Board (PCB) forms the cornerstone of every component, extending from everyday gadgets to advanced defense equipment. The escalating pace of modern life necessitates accelerated PCB production, calling for swift and precise mechanisms to ensure defect-free output for reliable manufacturing. Though such quality control tasks were traditionally manual, the advent of machine learning and deep learning has ensured automated and reliable solutions. A standout among these is YOLO, a speedy computer vision algorithm renowned for its unmatched speed and accuracy. This paper seeks to conduct an all-encompassing study of the cutting-edge YOLOv8 sub-models, delving into their individual performance attributes. The work encapsulates the implementation of these YOLOv8 models, followed by a rigorous analysis of their results on a range of metrics like $\mathrm{mAP50}, \mathbf{m A P 5 0 - 9 5}$, precision, and recall. An integral part of this study is the preprocessing of the HRIPCB dataset, comprising six distinct defect categories, namely Missing hole, Mouse bite, Spur, Spurious copper, Open circuit, and Short. The ensuing robust methodology involves comprehensive data preprocessing, data cleansing, and standardization. Ensuring a high-level of data quality, image enhancement techniques such as Colour Balance Adjustment, Histogram Equalization, and Image Filtering - Sharpening are employed. The study shines a spotlight on the individual training and testing processes of the YOLOv8 sub-models, namely v8n, v8s, v8m, v8l, and v8x, leveraging various hyperparameters to optimize model performance. By surpassing the ${9 5. 8 \%}$ mAP50 achieved by earlier YOLO versions, this research aspires to revolutionize PCB defect detection. It paves the way for enhanced quality control mechanisms in PCB manufacturing, thus contributing to the advancement of electronics production regimes

articleTitle: Leveraging Adaptive Algorithms for Real-Time Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper proposes the use of adaptive algorithms for real-time data analysis. Adaptive algorithms are a set of practical methods used for acting information-driven optimization and studying. They have a wide variety of applications and may be implemented to a selection of facts analysis obligations. This paper offers an overview of existing adaptive algorithms and descriptions of several new programs in the area of actual-time facts analysis. In particular, the paper discusses the notion of adaptive thresholding, which allows for practical real-time evaluation of large datasets. The paper also provides a novel technique for making use of these algorithms in an online learning environment. Results from simulations illustrate the ability of the proposed method in real-international packages. Sooner or later, the paper presents numerous key lessons discovered and affords recommendations for future research and packages in this area.

articleTitle: Efficiency of Architectural Innovations in Deep Learning for Enhanced Age Prediction and Gender Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Advancements in facial recognition technology have sparked significant interest in enhancing the precision of age and gender classification, crucial for applications ranging from personalized advertising to security systems. This paper introduces a sophisticated deep learning framework, utilizing inputs of facial imagery to deploy innovative architectural methods for age and gender classification. We detail our approach from data preprocessing, model training using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Transformer models, to the evaluation of model efficacy, ultimately achieving enhanced predictive accuracy.It meticulously navigates the landscape of existing methodologies to delineate the most efficacious models, spotlighting the transformative impact of architectural ingenuity on enhancing performance in such complex classification endeavors. The culmination of this research not only illuminates the expansive capabilities of deep learning in intricate classification scenarios but also paves the way for its application in scenarios demanding unparalleled precision in age and gender predictions, such as sophisticated security protocols in access control systems. Through a comprehensive exposition of the model’s design, the intricacies of its training regimen, and the indispensable value of a heterogenous training dataset, this work enriches the existing corpus of knowledge, providing a beacon for forthcoming explorations and practical implementations in akin domains.

articleTitle: RetViT: Retentive Vision Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Attention mechanisms have traditionally served as the dominant approach for computing weighted relationships between elements in input tokens for both Natural Language Processing (NLP) and vision tasks, however a significant paradigm shift has emerged within the domain of NLP. This shift introduces “Retention” as a novel and computationally efficient alternative, consistently delivering equivalent or superior results. This research applies pure Retention directly to sequences of image patches, replacing two-dimensional attention blocks from Vision Transformers (ViT) for image classification tasks along with accelerated model training and inference speeds. Proposed model integrates retention into Compact Convolutional Transformer (CCT) to build upon CCT’s impressive $84.1 \%$ Top1-acc on ImageNet-1k, utilizing a mere 4 million parameters. Post-retention our model surpasses other models with significantly high parameters in accuracy, achieving a state-of-the-art $91.57 \%$ accuracy on ImageNet-1k with only 6.5 million parameters and only 3.65G FLOPs. Implementation code and pretrained weights for the model will be made publicly available.

articleTitle: Towards Enhanced Gym Safety and Efficiency: CNN-LSTM Models for Identifying Leg Builder Workouts
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The algorithm formulates a hybrid deep learning structure that utilizes the Convolutional layer with the LSTM network. The model underwent training and validation using a dataset consisting of 2040 photos that depict five specific exercise actions: body-weight squats, lunges, lying leg presses or hamstring curls, and calf lifts with a weight plate. In our study, we’ve found that the participants have excellent classification skills with precision scores in the range from to $97.21 \%$; and the F1-score varied from $91.53 \%$ to $\mathbf{9 4 . 9 2 \%}$. The accuracy of each class was from $92 \%$ to $97 \%$, with high accuracy noted. The confusion matrix offers a comprehensive view for the review of rightly confirmed positives with the highest level of accuracy found in Classes 4 and 5. However, difficulties in differentiation with Classes 3 and 4 surfaces, thus, become a convergent feature representation that needs to be a subject of future study. The convolutional net, coupled with extended short-term networks, showed the capability to reflect fitness modes in both spatial and time-related movement, resulting in superior precision compared to other sports and rehab application methods. The management capability of such an approach reveals that utilizing powerful machine learning tools is an efficient means of promoting an increase in the number of hours available for training and preventing fatal accidents through immaculate compliance to workouts.

articleTitle: Hate Speech Detection using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The widespread transmission of dangerous online information is one notable concern raised by the rise in internet usage among people from a variety of cultural and educational backgrounds. The main difficulty is identifying hate speech and derogatory language in the context of automatically detecting harmful text material. This research endeavor presents a meticulous and exhaustive comparative examination of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms tailored for the identification of hate speech. Its primary objective is to reveal an optimal algorithmic amalgamation characterized by simplicity, ease of implementation, efficiency, and the capacity to deliver robust detection performance. In this study, we conducted a comparative analysis of three ML techniques— Decision Tree (DT), Gradient Boosting (GB) and Random Forest (RF), and—to categorize tweets on Twitter into two distinct categories: those containing hate speech and those devoid of by applying the term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) technique. The RF model yielded the most promising results, a commendable accuracy rate of $82 \%$ and a recall rate of $84 \%$ were achieved.

articleTitle: Addressing Security in IoMT Systems: A Blockchain Consensus Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper describes about the potential of blockchain consensus models to address Internet of Things (IoT) cybersecurity challenges. Specifically, it investigates how blockchain consensus mechanisms can give a secure and good platform for IoT networks by ensuring trust, transparency, and integrity in data transactions and communication processes. The focus is primarily on consensus algorithms such as Proof of Work (PoW), Proof of Stake (PoS), Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) and Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT), among others and their applicability to IoT security. By leveraging blockchain consensus models, IoT devices can establish a tamper-resistant distributed ledger where data transactions are cryptographically secured and transparently recorded. This not only mitigates the data tampering risk and unauthorized access but also enables efficient auditing and traceability of IoT data. Furthermore, there isn’t a single point of failure because blockchain consensus is decentralized, thereby enhancing the resilience of IoT networks against cyber attacks. In this article we have discussed about the challenges and limitations, issues associated with integrating blockchain consensus models into IoT environments, such as scalability, latency, and resource constraints. Additionally, it explores potential solutions and future research directions to address these challenges effectively.

articleTitle: DRDnet22: Advanced convolutional techniques for early diabetic retinopathy detection in retinal images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a prevalent eye complication among individuals with diabetes. Early detection of DR can prevent vision loss and lower associated problems. Manual diagnosis via retinal fundus images requires the expertise of medical professionals to assess several complex characteristics, including visual acuity tests, pupil dilation, and optical consistency tomography. The process is challenging, time-consuming, and prone to errors. This paper proposes a deep learning (DL) technique, DRDnet22, to detect and categorize DR into five distinct stages. The APTOS 2019 dataset is utilized in this study, which contains 3662 images. The study employs dense block and transition layer with global average pooling (GAP) techniques, and the combination of distinct Convolutional Networks (ConvNets) results in an enhanced representation beyond the utilization of features from a single ConvNet alone. To conduct an ablation analysis, the conventional pre-trained model’s performance was compared. The performance evaluation points out that the proposed model achieved 81.6% accuracy, which is an advantage over other DCNN models. Despite facing a few inaccuracies, the model’s competence in spotting vital features underscores its diagnostic potential.

articleTitle: An Ethical Framework for Advancing Music Composition through Generative Model
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Navigating the intersection of artificial intelligence and music, this work delves into the application of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for jazz music composition. The GAN architecture, comprising a Generator and a Discriminator, is harnessed to produce original music from a jazz-specific Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) dataset. The Generator learns intricate patterns within the MIDI note rang, incorporating controlled randomness through noise, The MIDI to audio conversion is facilitated by Timidity, while pre-processing techniques include Interquartile range (IQR), box plots and cumulative distribution plots which contribute to refining the generated samples. This is done to analyze the AI capacity in the domain of music generation. It was observed after 15 epoch iterations that the accuracy turned out to be 92 percent, while still being prone to hyperparameter tuning. This process of hyperparameter tuning was carried out after multiple trial and errors to achieve this accuracy. This works provides a significant potential in the field for future research of AI generated music.

articleTitle: Identification of Fake Information from Internet Propaganda using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Social media platforms and social networking sites have made it easier for information to spread quickly, but this has also made it easier for deliberately inaccurate and unverified content to proliferate, commonly known as fake information. Such a phenomenon has far-reaching effects on many aspects of human existence and provides tremendous challenges to governments and society. Determining the authenticity of fake information accurately in the broad world of online communication is a difficult and complex task. By effectively dealing with the challenge of labelling substantial volumes of unlabelled data, the proposed methodology demonstrates to be highly effective in distinguishing between fake and real data. Deep learning techniques are particularly important when it comes to solving these challenges as they offer feasible solutions to raise the accuracy of detection systems and decrease the adverse effects of false data. Although the method combines a number of approaches, its main goal is to fully utilize the capabilities of BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), a cutting-edge deep learning model that is well-known for being effective in tasks involving natural language processing. Word2Vec approaches for feature extraction convert textual data into numerical representations that capture the semantic meanings of words within a given corpus. With the integration of BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) deep learning techniques to identify false information with a 91% accuracy rate, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and misinformation detection have advanced significantly. By leveraging BERT’s contextual embeddings alongside novel techniques such as Word2Vec, the study showcases significant advancements in fake information identification. BERT deep learning-based classification models offer a sophisticated approach to distinguishing between real and fake data in real-time scenarios.

articleTitle: Knowledge, Attitude, and Practices Regarding Screening Mammography for Breast Cancer Detection among Female Professionals in a Prominent Private University in West Bengal, India: A Cross-Sectional Questionnaire Survey.
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Breast cancer is a significant global health concern, ranking as the second most common cancer in women. Its impact is increased by late-stage detection, contributing to high cancer-related mortality rates. Early diagnosis through screening mammography is crucial for favorable outcomes, but awareness and utilization of this diagnostic tool are lacking among women. This study was designed to assess the knowledge, attitude, and practices regarding screening Mammography for breast cancer detection among female teaching and non-teaching Professionals in a Prominent Private University in West Bengal, India. This cross-sectional study involved 110 female professionals aged above 25 years as they covered a large geographic area. It consists of socio-demographic details, breast cancer awareness, screening mammography knowledge, perceptions, and practices. Descriptive statistics were utilized for data analysis and comparison. Among 106 participants, regarding screening mammography, 63% had knowledge mainly from the internet, friends and family, but only 4.7% had undergone mammographic examination. Most (55.2%) were unaware of the appropriate age for screening. Despite obstacles, over 70% believed in the curability of breast cancer when detected early through screening mammography. A key strategy for the early detection of breast cancer is screening mammography. To help people build their knowledge on the benefits of screening mammography and take preventive action for Breast cancer workshops, seminars, awareness camps, and the distribution of manual and digital posters would be beneficial.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis of Pune City’s Air Quality Index: A Machine Learning and Time Series Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The rise in pollution and global warming poses a growing threat to the environment and public health, with industries contributing to air pollution and affecting human health and ecological balance. The impact of bad air quality can be quite broad and affect different aspects of life. To address the concern, a good analysis for the air quality index is needed. This paper helps in monitoring the trends, analysis of the air quality indices for the particular areas of Pune city and helps predict the Air Quality Index (AQI). This study conducts an investigative analysis using various machine learning techniques and time series forecasting methods to predict AQI levels. Each model is trained to predict AQI values based on the pollutant concentrations. Subsequently, the predicted AQI values are categorized into six distinct levels according to a predefined scale. The experimental evaluation demonstrates that the CatBoostRegressor model outperforms the others used here, boasting an RMSE as low as 4.73 and an adjusted R-squared value of 0.98. While the ARIMA model provides a decent forecast that aligns well with the actual data, its error rate is marginally lower than that of the CatBoostRegressor.

articleTitle: Synergistic Fusion of Deep Learning Techniques for Holistic Analysis of Age Group, Gender and Emotion Prediction from Speech
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Voice-based recognition systems have garnered significant attention, owing to their versatile applications in domains such as human-computer interaction, virtual assistants, and affective computing. This research aims to address the challenges associated with concurrent processes and escalating latency in individual models by delving into the intricacies of simultaneous age-group, gender, and emotion recognition from speech data. To surmount these impediments, we present a comprehensive investigation employing three distinct modeling approaches: standalone models for age group, gender, and emotion recognition; sequential models wherein the output of one model serves as input for the next; and an integrated model proficient in concurrent detection of age-group, gender, and emotion. Drawing inspiration from video understanding techniques, the integrated model seeks to streamline recognition processes and minimize latency. Experimental datasets, including the Ryerson Audio-Visual Database of Emotional Speech (RAVDESS), Common voice dataset and Crowd-Sourced Emotional Actors Database (CREMA-D), are lever age-group for rigorous analysis. Evaluation metrics encompassing accuracy, latency, and memory usage-group are employed to compare the performance of the diverse models.

articleTitle: Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Adaptation in Dynamic Cyber Security Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This article investigates the application of meta-learning in training reinforcement learning agents for fast adaptation in rapidly changing dynamic environments. The proposed meta-learning approach demonstrates promising results in multi-agent environments, outperforming baseline algorithms and achieving stable convergence. However, in single-agent settings, the meta-algorithms exhibit similar or inferior performance compared to baseline algorithms, potentially due to overfitting. Nevertheless, the meta-learning algorithms perform well in non-dynamic single-agent environments, showcasing their ability to adapt effectively. The findings highlight the potential of incorporating meta-learning approaches in multi-agent systems to enhance adaptive behaviours and optimize performance in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: E-commerce Evolution: Unleashing the Potential of Serverless Microservices
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Microservice architecture boosts scalability and flexibility by dividing applications into independent, loosely coupled services that can be developed, deployed, and scaled separately. This structure enables teams to work on various services concurrently, speeding up development and deployment processes. Microservices also enhance fault isolation, ensuring that a failure in one service doesn’t affect the entire application. Furthermore, they support the use of diverse technologies and frameworks, allowing developers to select the most suitable tools for each service.The cloud-based architecture comprising three distinct microservices: Product, Basket, and Ordering. Each microservice is seamlessly exposed to users via AWS API Gateway, facilitating efficient interactions with their respective resources. AWS Lambda functions underpin the business logic for each microservice, enabling serverless execution and scalability, while interfacing with DynamoDB tables to ensure fast and reliable data storage. Notably, the Basket microservice triggers a checkout event, which is processed by the AWS EventBridge event bus. This eventdriven approach leverages multiple EventBridge rules to manage complex workflows and ensure timely responses to various application events. The Ordering microservice further enhances the system’s efficiency by employing an AWS SQS queue for asynchronous order processing, thereby decoupling the order submission and processing stages for improved reliability and performance. The entire infrastructure is meticulously orchestrated with AWS CDK CloudFormation, providing a framework for scalable, consistent, and automated deployments. Comprehensive monitoring and logging are facilitated by Amazon CloudWatch, offering real-time insights and operational oversight to maintain the health and performance of the application. This architecture not only supports scalability and flexibility but also ensures a seamless and responsive user experience.

articleTitle: Integrating CNN and XGBoost with Synthetic Samples for Advanced Android Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The ubiquitous presence of Android smartphones exposes users to an ever-expanding arsenal of malware threats. Existing detection methods often struggle with false positives and limited adaptability to emerging threats. This paper presents a novel hybrid deep learning approach for Android malware detection, achieving a remarkable 98.66% accuracy while minimizing false positives. By combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with XGBoost and leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for data augmentation, this method demonstrates scalability and robustness across varying dataset sizes. This approach significantly enhances user privacy, device security, and app integrity, contributing to the ongoing battle against evolving Android malware threats. Utilizing a balanced dataset of 3,000 benign and malicious APK files, our method employs feature importance techniques to ensure model interpretability and relevance. The proposed approach showcases consistent performance with 1000, 2000, and 3000 APK files, highlighting its efficacy in safeguarding Android users against an ever-expanding array of malware threats.

articleTitle: Lithium-ion (li-ion) battery with smart cars and hijacking preventions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Potential advances in security, efficiency, and connection have been made possible by the automobile industry’s revolutionary incorporation of lithium-ion, also known as Li-ion, battery technologies with smart cars. The present study investigates the potential significance of lithium-ion batteries in upgrading security protocols, with a specific focus on averting smart car-related hijacking occurrences.In order to power electric cars (EVs) and smart auto systems, the paper first describes the significance of Li-ion batteries, emphasizing their electrical power the density, time span, and rechargeability. After ins tallation, it scrambles into the current trend of putting sophisticated safety features into smart automobiles, such as remote surveillance, geo-location, and biometric identification. Furthermore, the paper examines the unique hijack prevention measures using a combination of Li-ion battery technologies, such as real time monitoring, immobility, and catastrophe communication system. These characteristics rely on Li-ion batteries’ innate capacity to offer uninterrupted power for onboard safety systems, guaranteeing an early reaction to potential attacks.Furthermore, by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) procedures with smart automobiles which operate on Li-ion batteries, research enhances the detection and reaction capabilities. Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered systems possess the capacity to recognize suspicious activity and take proactive action autonomously via analysing a multitude of inputs, such as GPS locations, driver biometrics, and vehicle behaviour. The paper proceeds by outlining the vital role that Li-ion battery technology plays in fortifying smart automobiles against incidences of hijacking. Smart vehicles with Li-ion batteries may dramatically lower their vulnerability to hijack attempts due to the amazing integration of cutting-edge safeguards and AI-driven algorithms, improving passenger security and tranquility of conscience in a world that is constantly connected.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning in Implementing Efficient Healthcare Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)

It has made big improvements in diverse areas consisting of computer imagination and prescient, natural language processing, and self-reliant driving. articleTitle: Enhancing Arrhythmia Classification: A Comparative Study of Filters and Deep Learning Models on ECG Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Arrhythmia classification using electrocardiogram (ECG) data is crucial in the treatment of cardiovascular disease. However, ECG data often includes noise, which may conceal essential facts, making categorization difficult. This paper compares a notch filter with Gaussian noise, a Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter, and an Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) filter using a 1D convolutional neural network (1DCNN) and DenseNet121. We obtained the ECG signals for this investigation from the MIT-BIH arrhythmia database. The preprocessing pipeline incorporates Gaussian noise into the notch filter at various frequency bands. The proposed IIR filter addresses baseline wander, power-line interference, and muscle artifacts, whereas FIR filters minimize high-frequency noise and baseline wander. Then, we train the 1DCNN and DenseNet-121 models on the filtered ECG data. These models classify arrhythmias as normal (N), supraventricular (S), ventricular (V), fusion (F), or unknown (Q). Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score are standard metrics used to assess model-filter combinations. Each filtering strategy increases classification performance, and 1DCNN and DenseNet-121 outperform in noisy ECG data. The IIR filter with the DenseNet-121 method achieved the best accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 9 7 \%}$, while the Gaussian noise with the notch filter using the 1DCNN method got 99%, contributing to diagnostic capabilities. These discoveries might help detect arrhythmias and improve patient outcomes in cardiovascular diagnostics.

articleTitle: Facial Emotion Recognition Using Computer Vision Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The ability to recognize facial emotions through computer vision has become a challenging yet crucial task in the field of image classification. This paper introduces a method for detecting facial emotions, focusing on the classification of seven distinct emotions which are neutral, sadness, anger, disgust, fear, happiness, and surprise. Using recent advancements in computer vision and machine learning, the proposed approach employs three distinct models: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), ResNet50, and InceptionV3. Facial expression recognition poses unique challenges in image classification, and the adoption of deep learning has gained prominence for its effectiveness in solving this complex problem. The key challenge addressed in this research is the design of architectures that balance both simplicity and effectiveness. A simple architecture ensures quick training and easy implementation, while an effective one yields high accuracy on the test data. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts in advancing computer vision applications related to human emotions and highlights the potential for practical implementation in areas like affective computing and human computer interaction. The findings offer valuable insights into designing effective and efficient deep-learning architectures for facial emotion recognition with a multiclass approach.

articleTitle: Preserving Data Integrity in Image Encryption: Comparing Deep Learning Models and integrating Gaussian Noise and Chaotic Baker Map
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the world of growing technology secure transformation and storage of visual data have become very important. Cryptographic techniques continue to play a vital role in various ways ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive and crucial information. This study talks about an image cryptosystem by using chaotic baker map and Gaussian noise. The chaotic baker map exhibits unpredictable characteristics making it very suitable for encryption processes. Instead of relying solely on chaotic maps the addition of Gaussian noise can impact the imagequality by adding unwanted artifacts or noise which simulates real-world flaws during image transmission. The main objective of the DL models is to reconstruct the original images from the noisy images. DL models can learn patterns from the noisy data as well as from the clean data based on the train and test dataset thereby improving the quality of reconstruction. This process ensures that only authorized users can recover the image accurately. This project has the potential to maintain the confidentiality and integrity of visual information.

articleTitle: Evaluating Knowledge Transfer Methods and Metrics in Zero-Shot Learning Algorithms in Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Zero-shot getting to know is an rising location of device studying that could allow a model to become aware of and classify objects without ever having seen them earlier than. A first-rate undertaking in developing successful zero-shot gaining knowledge of algorithms is attaining powerful knowledge transfer from the prevailing instructions to the unconventional ones. Moreover, we check some currently proposed 0 -shot getting to know algorithms based on verbal-visual features and examine their potential for switch from regarded training to unknown ones. articleTitle: Advancements in String-Searching Algorithms Fastrack-StringSearch: A Novel Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: String matching plays a crucial role in applications, such involving retrieval of information, data mining, natural language processing, and biology with computation. However, existing string-matching algorithms, including the Naïve Method, KMP Algorithm, Rabin-Karp Algorithm, and Suffix Array, often suffer from limitations in terms of time complexity or space complexity. Considering these shortcomings, this paper presents a novel string-searching algorithm that harnesses Merge sort and binary search techniques to optimize time complexity, while maintaining the same space complexity as traditional approaches. Drawing on compiler analysis, the proposed algorithm demonstrates a major improvement in computational time, The proposed algorithm demonstrates a major improvement in time complexity, outperforming sophisticated methods by up to 50% in the best-case scenario and matches the other algorithms in terms of speed in the worst case scenario. This advancement makes the proposed algorithm -Fastrack-StringSearch-suited for large-scale text processing.

articleTitle: MedBot – An NLP based ChatBot for Diabetes Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this age of technology, with digital devices being accessible by almost everyone, have made our lives much better. With the advent of Machine Learning and advanced algorithms at our tips, the applications are immensurate. Such an application can be found in the health-care sector. The need for better and accessible health-care is of immense precedence. In this paper, we employed Machine Learning algorithms like Logistic Regression and other state of the art techniques to predict diabetes, given patient data. Diabetes is an incessant condition that is affecting millions worldwide, every year. Early detection of diabetes and prompt diagnosis is crucial. We have addressed that using a chat-bot to predict diabetes, which we believe is a portable and accessible solution for first-level assessment. We have employed PIMA Indian Diabetes Dataset into our chat-bot, providing interactive medical advice, and enhancing patient engagement, using Telegram API, resulting in an accuracy of 77%.

articleTitle: Affordable Small Radio Telescope (ASRT) for Solar Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The goal of the project is to construct an Affordable Small Radio Telescope (ASRT) that will allow students to participate in radio astronomy. With components from Direct-to-Home (DTH) satellite systems operating in the radio frequency (RF) framework, the ASRT offers a user-friendly platform for astronomical observations, with a special emphasis on solar studies. With the help of low-noise block converters (LNBs) and parabolic dish antennas, the ASRT provides students with an inexpensive way to investigate radio astronomy methods. The project places a strong emphasis on experiential learning by letting students assemble and use the telescope under supervision. Students’ comprehension of signal capture and processing is improved by the ASRT by utilising the concepts of RF engineering and analogue communication. Through the use of the ASRT, students can conduct solar observations that provide insights into solar variability and phenomena. Overall, the ASRT project contributes to advancing education in both radio astronomy and engineering, fostering interest in scientific exploration and providing a valuable learning experience for students.

articleTitle: Classification Model for Parameteric Analysis and Water Quality Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The survival of industry and agriculture depends on freshwater resources. An essential step in managing freshwater resources is the testing of water quality. According to the World Health Organization’s annual report, a shortage of safe drinking water is killing or sickening a lot of people, especially children and pregnant women. Before using water for anything, including drinking water or the application of chemicals (pesticides, etc.), it is imperative to evaluate its cleanliness. Testing the quality of the water is one way to locate safe drinking water. For safe, clean, and sterile water, proper water monitoring is therefore essential. This research’s main objective is to measure water quality using machine learning techniques. A body of water’s potability is a numerical term used to describe its quality. Utilizing the different water quality measures, the study assessed the water’s overall potability. The water quality is represented by a feature vector that is created using these factors. To evaluate the water quality, the study used three distinct classification algorithms: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT and Random Forest (RF).

articleTitle: Community Detection and Centrality Measures in Alzheimer’s Disease Network Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This project intricately explores network analysis in the context of Alzheimer’s disease, emphasizing community detection and centrality as a pivotal facet in data research on complex networks. Community structure, an essential component of complex networks, has progressively emerged as a focus of study interest. The community detection algorithm is useful for examining the network’s true structure. The paper highlights the importance of community identification strategies in understanding network behavior and topology analysis by classifying them into non-overlapping and overlapping methods. Many ways are looked at, such as those built on different factors separation into parts, group linking, tag movement and gradual steps partitioning. The process of finding out what sicknesses, like Alzheimer’s disease someone has also highlights the advantages of knowing and working with many different abilities, skills working as a group to fix issues, and sharing what we know in a community. It present a way to look at community splits using a measure called modularity. This focuses on how it can be used to check layout, steer refinement, and comprehend network dynamics. In this paper, we look into measures of importance, especially coreness centrality. We also talk about core-periphery structures, k-shell decomposition, and extensions like the all-around score and hybrid centrality measures, which provide useful tools for determining influential nodes in complex networks.

articleTitle: MIRLR: An ensemble approach for predicting clinical trial enrollment rates
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The preclinical and medical sciences are greatly benefiting from clinical trials. However, participant recruiting issues continue to be a global barrier to their success. Insufficient enrollment is a persistent problem that has a large impact, leading to huge expenses and delaying scientific advances. Preventive methods are needed to find and prioritize trials that are likely to fall short of enrollment targets to address this problem. The study’s main aim was to examine the importance of predictive models in predicting the probability of reaching enrollment goals before a trial starts. This study aims to provide a novel prediction framework to determine the feasibility of proposed trials using data-driven approaches and statistical analyses. Embedding algorithms like GloVe and BioBERT convert textual input into vector representations. Subsequently, numerical vectors containing the top 11 features selected through correlation algorithms are combined with the existing dataset from clinicaltrials.gov. MIRLR, a novel ensemble stacking method is developed based on five models namely, M5P, IBK, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and REPTree. In MIRLR, each model’s final predictions are combined to create a new dataset. This new dataset is input into the final Random Tree Regressor (RTR) model to forecast the enrollment rate. Results revealed that the MIRLR approach achieved a root mean square error of $\mathbf{0. 3 3 4}$ patients per day on the test dataset and 0.0057 patients per day on the training dataset, following a data split of 70:30. This research showcases the MIRLR’s impressive predictive capabilities, as it performed well across a range of training and test splits in accurately predicting site enrollment rates for clinical trials.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Multi-Modal and Multi-Model API for Real-Time Sign Language Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research introduces a novel three-stream, multi-modal and multi-model architecture with a comprehensive API to advance the scalability of sign language translation systems. It integrates a sentence correction model, an emotion detection system, and a sign language recognition model. The sentence correction model ensures translations are both semantically and syntactically accurate. The emotion detection system interprets emotional nuances, which is vital for signs that look similar but have different meanings. The sign language recognition model accurately decodes gestures from video, enhancing the fidelity of translations. Preliminary results indicate a significant improvement in translation accuracy and contextual relevance, with notable reductions in semantic errors and better conveyance of emotional states. This system offers more inclusive and accessible technology, paving the way for broader communication possibilities and greatly benefiting the deaf and hard-ofhearing community.

Author Keywords: Deaf and Hard of Hearing Community

articleTitle: Enhanced Traffic Sign Recognition Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Traffic sign recognition plays a pivotal role in modern intelligent transportation systems, contributing significantly to traffic management and road safety. This thesis presents a comprehensive investigation into the utilization of deep learning techniques for enhanced traffic sign recognition. The research delves into edge detection methodologies, deep learning architectures, and classification techniques specifically tailored for the identification of traffic and road signs. A diverse range of deep learning models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), VGG19, ResNet50, ResNet101, and ResNet152, are scrutinized for their effectiveness in traffic sign classification. The evaluation is conducted on a comprehensive dataset encompassing various road signs captured under diverse environmental conditions. The classification pipeline integrates edge detection algorithms such as Canny, Sobel, and Prewitt in conjunction with the selected neural network models. Experimental results exhibit notable performance disparities among the evaluated architectures. CNN achieves the highest accuracy of 96% when combined with the Prewitt edge detection method, while VGG19 attains 95% accuracy under the same conditions. ResNet50 achieves a peak accuracy of 96% with the Prewitt edge detection technique, while ResNet101 demonstrates the capability to achieve 97% accuracy when utilizing the Canny edge detection method. Remarkably, ResNet152 emerges as the top-performing model, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 98% when employing the Sobel edge detection method, along with an exceptional F1-Score.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Ad-Hoc Wireless Networks Performance Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Advert-hoc Wi-Fi networks are characterized via decentralized verbal exchange topology and lack of any bodily infrastructure. This has made them a compelling choice in many applications which include civilian and army operations, emergency offerings, and healthcare. However, because of their decentralized nature they are prone to issues such as network congestion, frequent protocol packet drops, and vulnerable sign propagation. to triumph over those challenges, gadget gaining knowledge of strategies can be utilized that may each improve present protocol overall performance and aid in the improvement of novel routing algorithms.one of the software of device getting to know techniques is within the prediction of packet drop charge in advert-hoc wireless networks. An online or actual-time prediction of packet drop rate can be used to dynamically alter routing protocols, supplying better provider great and robustness to the network. For example, methods the use of deep getting to know together with recurrent neural networks may be trained the use of historic information series to appropriately predict the expected packet-drops within the community. This data can then be used to alter the routing protocols and/or lessen hyperlink congestion. Another instance where machine studying strategies come into play is within the improvement of novel routing protocols. Existing protocols may be used as enter statistics, and the device getting to know algorithms may be used to optimize them, study the underlying traits.

articleTitle: Real-Time Crisis Management: Deep Learning Analysis on Tweets From X
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In recent times social media platforms serve as the main source for communication, especially on public relations or on any economical crisis. During such situations, many organizations depend on tweet conversations on X platform (earlier Twitter), to know the public sentiment and reactions, and provide responsive strategies. This research mainly focuses on using machine learning and deep learning techniques for analyzing the tweet conversations on PR. The novelty in this research is to use the power of natural language processing (NLP) techniques, to analyze every word and its occurrence to know the semantic meaning and understand the sentiment of that conversation. The proposed methodology begins with preprocessing the conversation data, building deep learning models namely LSTM, BiLSTM and machine learning models like logistic regression, Naive Bayes, SVM and XGBoost, which is followed by evaluation through certain metrics. This study helps in providing automated tools for improving the organizations to know the public sentiment during crisis and respond as fast as possible with effective strategies to address the public needs.

articleTitle: Tackling Food Wastage and Hunger: Feed the Needy
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In response to the substantial wastage of food globally, this initiative proposes a solution called “Feed the Needy.” This charitable application streamlines the redistribution of excess food from various events, such as weddings and corporate parties, to orphanages and old age homes. Users input their information, including name, location, contact number, and the quantity of available food for donation. A non-governmental organization (NGO) verifies the authenticity of the provided details and coordinates the pickup and delivery process. Through this efficient system, surplus food is directed to those in need, mitigating wastage and addressing food insecurity. This application benefits both user and people with hunger. ETEX.

articleTitle: Driver Drowsiness Detection using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper endeavors to mitigate the prevalence of road accidents through the introduction of an innovative drowsiness and yawn detection system. Designed to enhance commuter safety, the system continuously monitors and evaluates an individual’s alertness in real-time, identifying instances of obtundation and yawning with remarkable precision. By analyzing blink patterns, the system calculates the Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) and employs a Yawn Threshold (YAWNTHRESH) to accurately determine reduced alertness. The empirical results exhibit substantial accuracy, triggering timely voice-based alerts. The implementation of this sophisticated system is poised to significantly diminish the risk of accidents during commuting, thereby providing a pivotal enhancement in road safety protocols. The technology’s broad applicability across a vast assortment of real-world scenarios underscores its potential to revolutionize safety measures and elevate attentiveness among drivers. Consequently, this system represents a substantial advancement in accident prevention and commuter protection.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Elevator Failure Prediction System with BigDL Time Series Forecasting Models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Predictive maintenance represents a revolutionary approach in industrial operations, aiming to predict failures before they occur, thus ensuring continuity and efficiency. Elevator systems, crucial for daily operations in numerous buildings worldwide, are particularly suited for this technology. Our research introduces an innovative Elevator Failure Prediction System that leverages Chronos, a component of the BigDL library designed for large-scale time series forecasting. In this paper, we significantly contribute to the enhancement of predictive maintenance strategies, offering a robust framework for anticipating and mitigating potential elevator malfunctions. This study mainly focuses on three sophisticated deep learning models tailored for time series prediction: Sequence-to-Sequence (Seq2Seq) Forecaster, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Forecaster, and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) Forecaster. Each model is quantitatively evaluated using Root Mean Square Error metrics across various training epochs, with a consistent lookback period of 60 and 120 time steps. This systematic assessment not only delineates the strengths and limitations of each model in predicting elevator failures but also lays the groundwork for future technological advancements in the elevator industry. Through this experimental analysis, we indicate that the Seq2Seq Forecaster performs well in terms of error rate for a look back period of 60 time steps whereas TCN Forecaster performs well in terms of error rate for a look back period of 120 time steps. However, in both the cases, the LSTM Forecaster performs well in terms of time.

Author Keywords: long short-term memory forecaster and temporal convolutional network forecaster

articleTitle: Integrating Smart Farming with AI Techniques for Crop Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Farming encompasses the act of cultivating land, growing crops, and raising animals, which is crucial for the growth of country’s economy. For every country, agriculture contributes to approximately 70% of the main source of income. Historically, farmers have used traditional agricultural methods, which though time-consuming, often yielded imprecise results, leading to decreased output. Precision agriculture stands out as a viable solution to this issue, optimizing production by accurately identifying the necessary measures at an appropriate time. Elements of precision farming include meteorological prediction, soil assessment, crop recommendation for cultivation, and determination of optimal quantity of fertilizers and pesticides. Precise farming utilizes sophisticated techniques such as Machine learning, IoT, Data analytics and Data Mining to gather data, train systems, and forecast outcomes. Precision farming utilizes technology to minimize manual effort and enhance output. Recent agriculture challenges, such as crop failures because of low rainfall and soil sterility, raise the need for further exploration. This article aims to explore efficient methods used for crop management and harvesting in response to environmental changes. Several machine learning and deep learning models have come out with encouraging results in crop disease detection, thereby enhancing crop quality and productivity..

articleTitle: Blockchain Based Architectural Model for Certification in Indian Fisheries Export
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Indian fisheries export industry grapples with challenges in establishing trust and credibility in global markets, marked by prevalent issues such as fraud and mislabelling. This research attempt to tackle these obstacles by proposing the development of a government-backed blockchain certification framework for the Indian fisheries export sector. The paper would also work on developing a user-friendly interface for stakeholders to access and verify certification details of the fisheries products easily using the developed decentralized web application. Leveraging blockchain technology’s inherent transparency and immutability, the framework aims to enhance trust, bolster product quality assurance, and bring competitiveness in international markets. Through possibility for seamless integration with existing government schemes like the Matsya Sampada Yojana, stakeholders across the supply chain can securely record and verify crucial information, ensuring transparency and trace-ability. Preliminary findings suggest that the implementation of a blockchain certification system, coupled with a user-friendly mobile application, holds promise in uplifting the livelihoods of fishermen and positioning Indian seafood products as premium commodities It is also expected that blockchain would take the 44 percent of the data management and storage in next 3 years across various fields. This research emphasises the potential of blockchain technology in revolutionizing certification processes within the fisheries industry, offering greater implications for trust-building, economic development, and the empowerment of 3,288 marginalized communities.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Power of Neural Program Synthesis in High Level Code Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In this research, we delve into a transformative exploration of the realm of code generation, unveiling three fundamental modules that constitute the backbone of our study: the Text-to-Code Generation Model, Code Autocompletion Model, and the formidable Neural Program Synthesis Model. At the forefront of our investigation, we underscore the paramount importance of Neural Program Synthesis—a dynamic force adept at crafting custom programs from input-output examples. Our exploration delves into the intricate landscape of natural language-to-code generation, offering profound insights and invaluable contributions to the field. The ability to automatically generate code from natural language instructions holds immense significance in streamlining software development processes, reducing manual effort, and enhancing productivity. Furthermore, this research addresses a pressing need within the software engineering community for efficient methods of code generation, particularly in domains where human-program interaction is prevalent. Through rigorous experimentation and meticulous analysis, we shed light on methodologies and promising avenues for future research in this burgeoning domain, paving the way for advancements in automated software development and programming assistance tools.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Coverless Information Hiding with Encrypted Images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The current coverless information hiding methods face challenges such as the requirement for large image datasets and complex adversarial networks. In order to address these issues, this paper introduces a new approach by employing the mapping rule and generating multiple hash sequences within single cover image. These hash sequences are used to hide secret information within the cover image which maps with the segments of the secret data. The sender encrypts the cover image after hiding the secret message, which the recipient decrypts to extract the hidden information. Image encryption is achieved through bitwise XOR with a pseudo-random number matrix generated using a seed value, ensuring consistency in random number generation during decryption. The proposed method achieves a high embedding capacity with low computation and encrypts the image to prevent image attacks. Further ensuring that the transmitted information remains confidential and secure. After decryption with the key and mapping information, hidden information can be retrieved along with the recovery of original images. The proposed approach enhances the hiding capacity and provides image encryption, hence increasing security against image processing attacks while maintaining low computational demands. Moreover, in terms of hiding capacity, the proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to existing coverless information-hiding techniques.

articleTitle: Human Activity Identification and Classification using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper introduces XKD, a new self-supervised system built to distill meaningful representations from unlabeled video data. XKD uses two core pseudo-goals: reconstruction of masked data to obtain modality-specific representations from both audio and visual streams, and self-supervised cross-distillation of knowledge through a teacher-student framework, enabling the assimilation of complementary information between modalities. A groundbreaking domain alignment strategy addresses domain discrepancy in audio and visual modalities, enhancing cross-modal knowledge distillation efficacy. Although our experimentation includes datasets like UCF101, Kinetics400, and Kinetics Sound, we are in the process of achieving conclusive results. Despite this, our preliminary findings show promising advancements in video action classification accuracy across benchmark datasets. Specifically, XKD improves video action classification accuracy by 85.25% on UCF101, $84.43 \%$ on Kinetics 400, and $84.4 \%$ on Kinetics Sound. Ongoing research aims to refine and validate XKD’s efficacy in diverse video understanding tasks.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Agriculture: A Transformer-based Hybrid Model for Advanced Leaf Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In modern agriculture, early and accurate detection of plant diseases is essential for maintaining crop health and maximizing yield. Traditional methods of disease identification are often labor-intensive and prone to errors, necessitating the development of automated and efficient solutions. Current research in plant disease detection has primarily focused on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which, despite their success, encounter challenges such as high computational demands and limited generalizability across diverse datasets and environments. This study addresses these challenges by proposing a hybrid model that integrates the Vision Transformer (ViT) for feature extraction with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classification. The ViT excels in capturing intricate spatial patterns in leaf images by processing them as sequences of patches. Coupled with the SVM’s robust classification capabilities, this hybrid approach enhances the model’s accuracy while reducing computational overhead. Our methodology uses the Bean Leaf Lesions Classification dataset, which contains 1,167 images. Our proposed model achieved an outstanding accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9 . 2 4 8 \%}$, with precision and recall rates of $\mathbf{0 . 9 9}$ for each class, significantly outperforming existing models. Extensive data augmentation and regularization techniques ensure that the model generalizes well across different datasets, addressing the common issue of overfitting. We also performed hyperparameter tuning to optimize model performance evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, and $\mathbf{F 1}$-score metrics. The results indicate that our hybrid model provides a highly accurate tool for leaf disease classification and offers practical benefits for deployment in resource-constrained agricultural settings due to its efficiency.

articleTitle: Dynamic V2V Network: Advancing V2V Safety with Distance, Speed, Emergency Priority, SOS, and Accident Preemption
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Road accidents on Indian National Highways (NH) pose a significant threat to public safety, with statistics indicating a high incidence rate and substantial loss of lives and property. Recognizing the urgency of the situation, current research endeavours to devise innovative solutions to mitigate these risks. This paper presents a V2V communication system tailored for Indian NHs, leveraging advanced database management and sensory data analysis techniques.
