By harnessing the power of LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) models, the system calculates crucial safety metrics such as stoppage time and distance, while also detecting road quality issues like potholes. Moreover, it integrates vehicle-specific parameters such as mass and tyre traction to evaluate the safety of vehicles ahead, providing real-time guidance on safe speeds. In the unfortunate event of an accident, the system activates an SOS feature, swiftly alerting nearby hospitals, police stations, and designated emergency contacts. Additionally, it proactively notifies approaching vehicles about ongoing accidents, helping prevent further collisions and potential casualties. From an administrative perspective, the system offers comprehensive post-analytics tools to identify accident-prone zones and analyze contributing factors. By leveraging data-driven insights, policymakers can make informed decisions and implement targeted interventions to effectively reduce accidents and enhance overall road safety on Indian NHs.

articleTitle: Novel Frontier in Brain Vasculature Analysis with Graphical Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Brain graphs provide valuable insights into neurological illnesses and disease modeling by visualizing the complex connections among different brain regions. This paper presents a novel link attribute prediction method designed specifically for brain graph analysis. In contrast to other approaches that focus only on missing link prediction, this method goes the extra length of predicting measurable vascular characteristics including vessel length, volume, radius, and several others across known connections in the brain. The approach, which has its roots in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), develops intricate representations of data that are graph structured. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in calculating vascular link properties through tests on the Open Graph Benchmark Vessel Graph dataset. The task entails developing a unique deep neural network architecture that has been optimized to forecast critical vascular characteristics from known brain network connections. Considering the mouse brain vasculature, this methodology performs exceptionally well, particularly in the prediction of various vessel attributes with $R^{2}$ values more than 0.9 when using positional features. Although there has been significant progress in generalization among various mouse strains, there are still difficulties in accurately predicting features based on shape. These findings highlight how graphical neural networks can shed light on previously undiscovered aspects of the complex vascular system in the brain, leading to revolutionary advancements in the field of neurobiological research.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Feature Selection Methods for Effective and Efficient IoT Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The growth of technology and the internet has brought significant negative impacts, especially in terms of vulnerability to cybercrime, such as malware, in the Internet of Things (IoT) environment. IoT malware is becoming an increasingly serious threat as internet-connected devices become more widespread and diverse, affecting everything from home smart devices to motor vehicles. Previous studies have introduced many malware detection models. Still, none has focused on analyzing the relationship between data features. This study aims to explore the relevance between features and improve the effectiveness of machine learning in detecting and classifying IoT malware. The proposed method employs feature selection techniques, including Chi-Square, Pearson Correlation, ANOVA, and Graph Feature Selection. The experiment shows the combination of Pearson Correlation and Gradient Boosting obtained the best result with an Accuracy of 99.98%. Thus, the result obtained optimal Precision, Recall, and F1-Score of 99.97%. Random Forest demonstrates strong performance without feature selection, achieving an Accuracy of 99.91%, Precision, Recall, and F1-Score of 99.90%.

articleTitle: Investigating the Ability of AI Algorithms to Optimize Data Access Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms’ potential to optimize information access strategies is quickly becoming a primary awareness for businesses across theglobe. AI optimizes data access, enabling swift and precise retrieval of information. AI algorithms can analyze massive numbers of statistics and perform based on the outcomes. It also allows organizations to manage and store data more efficiently resulting in improved productivity. This paper seeks to research the capability of AI algorithms to optimize records and get the right of access to techniques. It will begin by examining the different types of AI algorithms used for data analysis, their associated benefits and characteristics, and their potential to enhance data access procedures. Subsequently, it will discuss various strategies employed to enhance the efficiency of data access procedures through AI algorithms. Ultimately, it will analyze the financial and ethical implications of leveraging AI algorithms to optimize data access procedures. The goal of this paper is to provide a comprehensive evaluation of the impact of AI algorithms on data access processes.

articleTitle: Compression-Based Image Retrieval for Efficient Networked Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Compression-based total photograph retrieval (CBIR) is a method that is used to retrieve pictures from big datasets correctly. Unlike traditional photo retrieval methods, CBIR utilizes lossless or loss compression algorithms to lessen the scale of the image statistics for transmission over a network connection. That is particularly useful in programs wherein transmitting cumbersome image statistics is only sometimes viable. With the aid of compressing the facts related to a photo and sending only the compressed version, transmission instances are significantly decreased, even though nonetheless maintaining the visual first-rate and integrity of the photo. This makes CBIR a possible choice for packages consisting of streaming video, medical imaging, far-flung sensing, and massive-scale surveillance systems. CBIR also has packages in multimedia databases and different networked structures that require efficient image retrieval and viewing.

articleTitle: A Novel Zero-Knowledge Authentication Protocol for Secure Communication in VANET
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Network (VANET) is a particular subclass of the mobile ad-hoc network that raises several security challenges, notably how users authenticate the network. The work explores using zero-knowledge proofs for secure authentication while preserving user privacy and aims at encrypted information exchange between onboard units. Zero-knowledge proofs enhance security by protecting against impersonation attacks. We strive to reduce the dependence on roadside units for computational tasks by integrating the central authentication server and sub-authentication servers. We reduce modular exponentiation operations during authentication, enhancing efficiency without compromising security. We use the protocol verifier tool called Proverif to verify the security of our protocol. Simulation using the NS-2 simulator validates the protocol by varying the vehicle density. This paper advances VANET security by combining zero-knowledge authentication with encrypted information exchange, strengthening security, efficiency, and data confidentiality while reducing reliance on RSUs. Our protocol ensures secure communication in VANET with minimum computational and communication overhead.

articleTitle: Exploring Techniques and Approaches for Time Series Analysis and its Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Time series analysis is a powerful statistical technique that finds extensive use in the fields of economics, finance, healthcare, and environmental studies. This text explores both fundamental concepts and complex tactics, providing an overview of the primary methods utilized in time series analysis. The paper’s first portion covers the fundamental characteristics of time series data, such as trend, seasonality, and noise. We analyze popular time series decomposition methods, such as moving averages and exponential smoothing, highlighting their usefulness in identifying underlying patterns in raw data. The study explores more advanced techniques that go beyond simple processes, such as autoregressive integrated moving average models and seasonal-trend decomposition using losses. We review the mathematical foundations of several models, underlining their benefits and drawbacks. Additionally, the application of time series analysis to forecasting and prediction is reviewed. We give actual examples of time series models being effectively used to predict stock prices, weather, and disease outbreaks. To capture difficult temporal links, machine learning techniques such as neural networks with recurrence and long short-term memory networks have been merged and examined. However, there are several challenges associated with time series analysis, such as handling irregular patterns, missing values, and unevenly collected data.

articleTitle: A Review of AI Approaches in Combating Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) in Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of cybersecurity, Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) present a formidable challenge to organizations worldwide. These sophisticated, long-term cyberattacks are typically state-sponsored or initiated by highly organized criminal groups, targeting sensitive data and critical infrastructure. This review paper explores the emerging role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in combating APTs, offering a comprehensive analysis of recent advancements and methodologies. We begin by defining APTs and their unique characteristics, emphasizing the necessity for advanced defensive strategies. The core of the paper examines various AI-based approaches, including machine learning algorithms, deep learning frameworks, and AI-driven behavioral analytics, detailing their effectiveness in detecting, analyzing, and mitigating APT incidents. Additionally, we discuss the integration of AI in existing cybersecurity infrastructures, highlighting key challenges such as data privacy concerns, the need for large datasets, and the potential of AI being used by adversaries. Our analysis is supported by case studies and practical examples, demonstrating AI's capability in enhancing threat intelligence, anomaly detection, and predictive analytics. The paper concludes with insights into the future trajectory of AI in cybersecurity, emphasizing the importance of continuous research and collaboration among cybersecurity professionals, AI researchers, and policymakers. This review serves as a crucial resource for understanding the dynamic interplay between AI and APTs, guiding future strategies to fortify cyber defenses in an increasingly digitalized world.

articleTitle: An improved energy management model for IoT devices using deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is booming, with research showing that billions of connected devices gather data, communicate, and automate. The widespread adoption of IoT devices has been hampered by one major challenge: limited energy resources that require recharging or replacing often. Energy management strategies on these devices are essential to improve battery life. This paper presents an enhanced version of the energy management model for IoT devices using deep learning techniques in technical abstracts. The aim is to reduce energy consumption by predicting and configuring real-time device settings based on user behavior trends. A deep neural network is used as the model to learn and tailor its response variably based on different user conditions like temperature, light, and usage patterns. The model can analyze this data to predict energy demand and programmatically adjust device settings.

articleTitle: Enhancing Skin Cancer Diagnosis with Customized InceptionV3: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Skin cancer, a common and dangerous health issue, often requires accurate detection for effective treatment. Traditional machine learning techniques, while useful, involve handcrafted manual feature engineering. In contrast, deep learning methods such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) offer automated feature extraction. In this study, we utilize the Skin Cancer Detection dataset to train an image recognition model, Inception-V3, for identifying melanoma skin cancer. To enhance accuracy, we augment the Inception-V3 model with a custom top classification layer. Our proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of 96.00%.

articleTitle: An Exploratory Feature Analysis for Machine Learning-Based Human Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) has gained significant attention in recent years. Previous studies used various features from time, frequency, and wavelet domains to recognize the activities, but it is not clear how to determine the best features that can efficiently identify activities in less time. In this study, we aim to explore and elucidate the significance of the most relevant features in HAR, shedding light on their semantic meanings. We utilize different filter-based techniques like chi-square, correlation coefficient, and information gain, coupled with forward selection to find the top-ranked features. Additionally, we apply union and intersection operations on the resultant feature subsets of filtering techniques to obtain common and aggregated features. By considering these common relevant features, we observe a significant decrease in computational time by 97%, 95%, and 90%, with a reduction in memory usage by 10%, 25%, and 20% for benchmark datasets, i.e., UCI HAR and WISDM (phone accelerometer and gyroscope datasets) respectively, even though with a slight compromise in accuracy.

articleTitle: Mapping Item-wise Rating into Attribute-wise Ratings for Enhanced Personalized Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Personalization is the key to any recommendation service, as it relies heavily on analyzing user interactions with items to uncover patterns and suggest relevant items. While users provide multi-level ratings for every item in their interactions, the conventional recommendation system generally employs an average rating value. This may not be efficient in realizing personalized recommendations. To make recommendations more personalized, it is proposed to map items-wise multi-level ratings into attribute wise ratings employing the framework of Symbolic Data Analysis (SDA). This will create more informative user profiles, enabling better similarity-dissimilarity analysis between users, which ultimately generates better recommendations. The efficiency of the recommendation list is assessed using the NDCG and MRR evaluation metrics. Baseline algorithms are employed to compare the proposed model with a focus on the top-k (Top-5) recommendations to demonstrate its potential. In the evaluation, the proposed method significantly outperformed baseline algorithms. This highlights the effectiveness of utilizing attribute-wise ratings and SDA in generating personalized recommendations.

articleTitle: Malware Analysis and Classification Using Grid Search Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) technology is experiencing rapid growth, but security and privacy remain a major concern. This is because IoT devices are vulnerable to being targets of malware attacks. On the other hand, detecting malware in IoT networks is challenging. Previous research has introduced several methods for IoT malware detection using several Machine Learning algorithms. However, only a few studies discussed parameter optimization in machine learning models. Thus, this research aims to develop a malware detection model using hyperparameter optimization with grid search in several Machine Learning algorithms. Several Machine Learning algorithms are utilized, such as Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and k Nearest Neighbors (k-NN). This research aims to improve IoT network security by developing a model to mitigate and detect the presence of malware attacks. The experiment using the IoT23 dataset shows a good result with the RF model. RF obtained the best result, achieving accuracy of 99.09%, precision of 98.54%, recall of 99.05%, and an F1 score of 98.79%.

articleTitle: Electricity Theft Detection in Smart Grids using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Electricity has become an integral part of day-today life. Modern power systems are equipped with various features to enhance technical aspects like reducing line losses and improving voltage regulation in distribution. Apart from technical improvements, there are also non-technical losses caused by electricity theft that can impact the system’s efficiency and reliability. The integration of smart meters in power system operations enhances communication and energy management between utilities and customers, but it also raises concerns about the potential for electricity theft. This necessitates data analysis in addition to meter data information to detect the theft of electricity from the utility side. Most of the classification techniques are based on 1-dimensional data, and they are unable to account for the periodicity of electric consumption and detect abnormalities in them. In this work, the abnormality in electricity consumption is detected using a wide and deep convolutional neural network (CNN) based on 2-dimensional electricity data. For this, daily consumption, and weekly trend of electricity consumption through 2-D data are utilized to reliably distinguish original electricity consumption and nonperiodicity introduced due to electricity theft by deep CNN, while global characteristics of 1-D data are also captured by wide components. Thus, the wide and deep CNN model is utilized to detect electricity theft and extended the same analysis using the proposed Dilated CNN to reduce time taken while retaining same accuracy. The overall performance of the above techniques is evaluated with a set of metrics. Further it is compared with other classification models such as Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), and Support Vector Machine (SVM).

articleTitle: Investigating Scope of Real-time Data Processing for IoT in 5G Revolution
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research examines 5G-enabled IoT devices’ real-time data processing capability and constraints. A thorough literary study helps understand current technologies, application situations, and industrial difficulties. Using clear research goals, the study discovers opportunities, obstacles, and solutions. Interviews, surveys, and literature gather primary and secondary data. A use case study examines the pros and cons of 5G -enabled IoT devices in real-world data processing situations. The technical examination evaluates 5G real-time data processing capabilities, concentrating on latency, reliability, and scalability. Case studies or simulations examine implementations, successes, problems, and best practices. The results suggest architectural and efficiency methods. Simulations or prototypes test solution efficacy and feasibility. Data analysis and interpretation show 5G-enabled IoT devices’ real-time data processing capabilities and limitations. This method allows researchers to advance the area and significantly affect industry and academic research and practice. We will analyse the design, implementation, and optimisation of 5G-enabled IoT systems for real-time data processing. This technology has tremendous possibilities and problems, which we shall study. We wish to promote innovation and enable the next generation of networked applications and services. The prior model employed conventional methods and had 89.1 % accuracy and 11.9 % inaccuracy. When employing the hybrid Bert model, accuracy climbed to 92.3% and error rate reduced to 7.7%.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Survey on Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) - Applications and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) is changing healthcare through the use of the Internet to connect medical devices, apps, and systems. This helps improve patient care, makes healthcare more efficient, and improves health outcomes. This paper deals with the edge-fog-cloud computing architectures for Internet of Health applications. Remote patient monitoring is done by collecting the data from wearable health devices, processing at different communication levels, applying intelligent algorithms and providing insights to the patient and healthcare professionals. This paper reviews the IoMT architecture and how the entire workflow is managed at device, edge, fog, and cloud levels. The paper also discusses IoMT challenges, such as data security and privacy concerns due to the interconnectedness and interoperability of devices at each layer and hurdles for seamless data integration within healthcare networks.

articleTitle: YouMatter: A Conversational AI Powered Mental Health Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In many regions globally, the shortage of trained mental health professionals leaves countless individuals without the support they desperately need. This deficiency, highlighted by the world health organization, underscores the pressing need for innovative solutions to bridge this gap. Chatbots emerged as a scalable intervention, offering an interactive platform for mental health solutions. These systems, adept in spoken, written, and visual languages, hold significant potential, particularly for individuals hesitant to seek traditional mental health services. Even though there are some chatbots already available, like SERMO and Aapka Chikitsak, they still have some problems such as the absence of analyzed reports and graphical data. This paper proposed a new chatbot referred to as YouMatter, to tackle these challenges. Developed on a foundation of advanced natural language processing, and Large Language Model (LLM), YouMatter serves as a mental health care chatbot, extending support and resources to those navigating mental well-being. Leveraging WebSockets, YouMatter facilitates real-time interactions, ensuring assistance is available around the clock. With the capability to analyze users’ mental health trends and present graphical insights, YouMatter empowers individuals to track their progress and receive tailored support. Through personalized email tips and accessible chatbot assistance, YouMatter strives to democratize mental health care, removing barriers and fostering happier, healthier lives for all.

articleTitle: An Investigation into Robust Video Watermarking Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: this paper investigates techniques for ensuring the robustness of video watermarking algorithms. Many watermarking strategies awareness of performance measures like protection and imperceptibility; however frequently need to remember robustness, which is a vital element in creating a robust watermark that can preserve diverse types of signal noise and intentional attacks. The authors proposed an adaptive technique for the usage of movement estimation-primarily based watermark encoding and interpreting to assure robustness towards diverse noise and alteration assaults, along with white noise, contrast less noise, image filtering, JPEG compression, and video cropping. The authors in comparison the proposed algorithm with existing methods in phrases of height sign-to-noise ratio (PSNR), normalized correlation (NC), and robustness evaluation with four reference points (RP4). Effects showed that the proposed set of rules carried out higher in terms of PSNR, NC, and RP4, providing robust evidence of its robustness in comparison to present algorithms. Usual, the consequences from this paper recommended that the proposed adaptive method is a promising solution for robust video watermarking. The algorithm presents a strong overall performance in phrases of security, imperceptibility, and robustness towards various sorts of noise and intentional attacks. Future studies could discover the utility of this method to a much wider variety of video watermarking situations.

articleTitle: Using Existing CCTV Networks for Crowd Management and Crime Prevention using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The Indian Railways is one of the largest railway networks in the world, serving millions of passengers daily. However, with the increasing number of passengers and trains, challenges like High passenger volume and increase in crime rate. RailEye is a cutting-edge railway crime detection solution leveraging AI for crowd management and safety in railway stations. Comprising three integral modules, it ensures comprehensive surveillance and prevention. The Crowd Management module incorporates Crowd Count, Monitoring, and Human Trajectory Prediction, optimizing station operations. Anomaly Detection and Crime Classification employ advanced techniques like 3D CNN and SlowFast Action Recognition to swiftly identify and classify suspicious activities, enhancing security measures. Lastly, the Person Tracking and Re-Identification module utilizes OpenPose and DeepSort algorithms for accurate tracking and re-identification, facilitating efficient monitoring and response. RailEye stands as a beacon of safety, revolutionizing railway security through advanced AI technology.

articleTitle: Automatic Running Notes Generation from Audio Lecture using NLP for Comprehensive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Taking notes is vital for students as it provide a condensed what they learn during classes sessions. Good notetaking helps students understand better and remember more. Notes help students engage more deeply with the material. However, note-taking is difficult because it requires listening, understanding, and writing simultaneousely, especially when lectures are fast-paced. Students also need to learn how to decide what information is important to note down. Automatic note generation solves these problems by using technology to make note-taking easier. It means students don’t have to write everything down as they listen and lets them focus more on understanding the lecture. Thus, the proposed work presents a comprehensive solution for automatic notes generation from audio lectures, facilitating access to summarized content in both English and Telugu languages. Leveraging advanced techniques including Google’s Web Speech API employing a combination of Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), system accurately transcribes spoken content with a Word Error Rate (WER) of 8% and a Word Accuracy Rate (WAR) of ${9 2 \%}$. Subsequently, employing the TextRank algorithm, the system extracts key information and generates structured notes with precision of 0.82, recall of 0.9649, and an F1 score of 0.886. Furthermore, employing a neural machine translation (NMT) approach, the system achieves a BLEU score of 0.5789, enabling seamless translation of the generated notes into Telugu. The system provides users with the flexibility to download both English and Telugu notes in Microsoft Word format, thus offering versatile tool for accessible knowledge dissemination from audio lectures.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Methods for Video Segmentation and Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Deep mastering strategies for video segmentation and tracking involve using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to pick out gadgets or areas of hobby in the body of a video. Such fashions may be used to extract spatial statistics, which include an item’s role, movement, and velocity from the video. Moreover, they are able to help locate changes in the environment, hit upon appearances of recent items, and tune multiple objects within the identical body. It is an effective device for video forensics and movement evaluation, permitting computerized tracking and identity of objects in a scene. Maximum contemporary procedures observe CNNs for single-frame item segmentation and monitoring, which is predicated on the excessive-stage shape and look facts of interested items. Furthermore, CNNs may be used for temporal analysis and fusion of the collection of frames for extra robust object detection and tracking. Such an approach is regularly employed for multi-item monitoring and hard item segmentation duties. In the end, using CNNs in video segmentation and monitoring can result in advanced accuracy and robustness of video information.

articleTitle: Evaluating Data Poisoning Vulnerability in Selective Reincarnation within c-MARL to Salt and Pepper Noise Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In the domain of cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (c-MARL), the deployment in safety-critical applications necessitates rigorous robustness testing. Despite the advancements in c-MARL algorithms facilitated by deep neural networks (DNN), the susceptibility of agent policies to adversarial examples poses significant risks. This study focuses on the susceptibility of selective reincarnation, a method leveraging historical agent experiences to expedite learning, in c-MARL systems against data poisoning attack targeting the offline teacher dataset, which consists of curated experiences collected during tabula rasa training. We tested the influence of salt and pepper noise on selective reincarnation and employed Hamming distance to quantify ranking disruptions. Our results reveal significant performance declines, with top-performing agent combinations (configurations) under clean conditions experiencing up to a $\mathbf{5 0 \%}$ decrease in performance under adversarial conditions. Furthermore, configurations with three or more agents exhibited a $\mathbf{1 0 0 \%}$ Hamming distance, signaling complete ranking reversals that critically affect reincarnation decisions. Our research not only enhances the understanding of the effects of data poisoning on c-MARL selective reincarnation but also contributes to the advancement of more secure multi-agent learning algorithms, ensuring robustness in critical applications.

articleTitle: Unleashing power of Vision Transformers for disease prediction in Chest X ray images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This work develops and evaluates a deep learning model to properly categorise chest X-ray pictures into three categories: normal, pneumonia, and COVID-19. The main idea is to help physicians diagnose illnesses at an early stage and provide accurate treatment, which eventually leads to critical patient care and enhanced healthcare system efficiency. Hence, this research work makes use of various state-of-the-art architectures like Vision Transformers, InceptionNetV3, EfficientNetV2, MobileNetV2, NasnetMobile, ConvNext and DenseNet169, to fully evaluate their performance on the dataset of Chest-Xray-14. These models have shown good results and their usefulness in detecting chronic chest conditions thereby, proving their efficient applicability in the medical field. This study has great reported efficient results with Vision Transformers clearly to be the best model for diagnosing chest diseases like Pneumonia and COVID-19 speedily and effectively.

articleTitle: Automated Weed Identification And Classification Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In contemporary agriculture, effective weed management is paramount for maximizing crop yield and mitigating environmental impact. This paper introduces an innovative automated solution for weed identification and classification, utilizing the YOLOv8m algorithm (You Only Look Once version 8 with mobile architecture). Recognized for its real-time object detection capabilities YOLOv8m has been specifically designed and refined to enable quick and precise identification of weeds in agricultural areas. The system employs a comprehensive dataset encompassing diverse weed species, growth stages, and environmental conditions to train the YOLOv8m model. Its real-time image processing capability enhances its suitability for dynamic agricultural settings. The YOLOv8m architecture is fine-tuned to identify and classify weeds rapidly, providing a reliable on-the-fly decision-making solution. The workflow includes image acquisition with various sensors, pre-processing for noise reduction, and training the model to recognize intricate features associated with different weed species. The resulting model seamlessly integrates into a user-friendly application compatible with precision agriculture technologies, empowering farmers to make informed decisions about weed management. Field trials attest to the YOLOv8mbased system’s efficacy in accurately identifying weeds and distinguishing them from crops. The algorithm’s versatility makes it adaptable for deployment across diverse agricultural landscapes. Integrating this automated weed identification system into precision farming practices not only reduces reliance on manual labor but also promotes sustainable agriculture by minimizing herbicide use. The research findings underscore YOLOv8m’s potential as a potent tool for automated weed identification, paving the way for advanced, technology-driven solutions in precision agriculture. Its application in weed management signifies a significant stride toward optimizing resource utilization and fostering sustainable farming practices amidst evolving agricultural needs.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of YOLO Models for Detecting Bangladeshi License Plates
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This research paper presents a comprehensive investigation into the effectiveness of YOLO (You Only Look Once) models, namely YOLOv5, YOLOv7, and YOLOv8, in the domain of Bangladeshi license plate detection. With the escalating demand for precise license plate recognition systems to facilitate efficient traffic management and bolster law enforcement efforts, this study conducts an in-depth evaluation of these models. Central to our methodology is the development of a specialized dataset comprising Bangladeshi license plate images, reflecting the unique characteristics and challenges prevalent in this geographical context. Through meticulous dataset curation, model training, and rigorous testing procedures, we ascertain the performance metrics of each YOLO variant. Notably, our findings reveal YOLOv8 as the most proficient model, achieving a remarkable mean average precision (mAP) score of 0.934 with precision 0.93 and recall 0.906. The insights gleaned from this research contribute significantly to the advancement of intelligent transportation systems and public safety initiatives in Bangladesh, offering tailored solutions for license plate detection challenges in this specific locale.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Travel and Parking Ticket Pass for the United Arab Emirates Transport Services
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The transportation and parking systems field has been rapidly evolving in recent times. However, in the United Arab Emirates, the state of transportation and parking systems still has a long way to go. Some areas still use traditional paper ticketing systems that require physical cash, which is not optimal in today’s digital age. Other systems, such as those that require payment through messaging services, are not convenient for most users as they lack the option of using different payment methods. In addition, some systems do not support foreign credit cards, while others do not allow wallet sharing with family members. To address these issues, a project was undertaken to design and develop a website-based application for integrating travel and parking ticket systems in the UAE using RFID. The team used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build the website and integrated the RFID system using a Raspberry Pi. The result obtained for the project is a complete website that provides all traveling services in one platform while providing a secure user experience, where users can easily share their wallet with family members. The benefits of this system include increased automation, greater convenience, and efficiency, as well as the ability to access all services in one platform with a secure system protected by blockchain technology.

articleTitle: Optimizing Distributed Communication: A Comparison of Load Balancing Strategies in gRPC and Apache Thrift
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Efficient load balancing is essential for distributed systems to have outstanding performance and scalability. This study compares the load balancing strategies of two popular distributed application frameworks, gRPC and Apache Thrift. The features of each algorithm are examined, along with their advantages and disadvantages. To give a helpful evaluation, the performance of these algorithms is tested using key factors like throughput, latency, resource utilisation, and scalability. The comparison looks at the trade-offs involved in selecting different algorithms for distributed system load balancing and identifies the scenarios in which one method might be more suitable.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques for Identifying Child Abusive Texts in Online Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This study addresses the critical issue of child abuse in digital communications by developing advanced machine learning and deep learning models for detecting child abusive texts in the Bengali language on online platforms. The primary goal of this research is to contribute to child abuse prevention by creating an effective tool for accurately identifying abusive content. Utilizing a combination of natural language processing (NLP) techniques and deep learning algorithms, this model distinguishes between abusive and non-abusive text. The dataset, comprising manually collected and labeled comments and posts from social media sites, is categorized into Positive, Neutral, and Negative classes. For model development, a variety of machine learning algorithms including RF, DT, and SVM, alongside deep learning approaches such as LSTM and CNN, were tested. The performance of the proposed model was assessed using precision, recall, and F1 score metrics. The findings reveal that the model performs with high accuracy in classifying abusive text in Bengali, offering significant potential as a tool for effective child abuse identification and prevention.

articleTitle: Enhanced Community Identification Based on Spider Ant Colony Relative Feature Mining Algorithm Using Dense Net Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Community detection is essential for identifying related groups in online social networks. Internet Communication Technology (ICT) makes e-learning and technology necessary in education. In addition, ICT plays an important role, from providing distance education and identifying interest groups to providing services to social interaction groups. Also, social realities, relative adversaries, groups to be served, etc., may be determined based on vested interests. Therefore, it is necessary to enable active researchers in social networks and identify communities to discover more, mainly behaviour-based groups. However, not any comment can be copied in terms of social associations. It is demonstrated that most machine learning algorithms using absolute mean ratios can derive interest scores based on social group organizations. However, these can reduce accuracy due to random correlations and lead to poor analysis. To solve this problem, we can implement deep learning-based social recognition and improve recognition accuracy. An improved community identification based on Spider Ant Colony Relative Feature Mining Algorithm (SACR-FMA) using Dense Net Convolution Neural Network (DNCNN) can be proposed. The online Community dataset is collected based on learner search features. The Learners Impact Behavioural Rate (LIBR) is initially estimated to find the learner’s interest. Then Edge Graph Semantic Subset Group Mining (EGSSGM) is used to marginalize the feature rate. Depending on the learner community rate, the Spider Ant Colony Relative Feature Mining Algorithm (SACR-FMA). The selected features are trained into Dense Net Layers (DNL) to create relative subgroup identity mining. Then the features are introduced into an optimistic Dense Net Convolution Neural Network (DNCNN) to identify the community interest class by category. The proposed method performs very well in detecting related subgroups in social networks compared to other systems. It provides accuracy, higher precision, recall and F-measure with less time complexity.

articleTitle: Efficient Source Coding for Narrowband Wireless Voice Communication: Development and Simulation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This paper explores different encoding methods for speech signals and provides a methodology for a narrowband speech waveform with a targeted bandwidth of less than 25 kHz. This waveform could be used in any standard reconfigurable radio system. The paper also explores the effectiveness of different source encoding techniques for speech and audio signals, and also considering effects of different source coding techniques on signal quality and bandwidth utilization. The proposed methodology for the narrowband speech waveform emphasizes on optimizing resources while maintaining a targeted bandwidth requirement under $25 \mathbf{k H z}$. Different encoding schemes for speech have been studied and different parameters such as SNR, compression ratio and encoding decoding time has been calculated using mathematical simulation software. Few of the promising schemes have been simulated with entire narrowband waveform and their performance within the specified targeted bandwidth has been assessed at different bit error rate introduced by channel.

articleTitle: Image Caption Generator Using Resnet50 and Lstm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Image captioning is an advanced technique used to generate textual descriptions that can describe the content and context of an image. This process involves both NLP and computer vision to automatically generating detailed description of image that explain the content visually depicted in an image. These descriptions are valuable in many domains, providing insights into image content and aiding in a deeper understanding of visual data. Image captioning is applicable in various fields, including analyzing large collections of unlabeled images. By automatically generating descriptions, image captioning helps extract meaningful information and identify patterns in these images. In machine learning, image captioning is useful for guiding autonomous systems like self-driving cars. By providing contextual descriptions of the environment captured by cameras, image captioning helps in navigation and decision-making. Additionally, image captioning enhances accessibility for visually impaired individuals by providing narrations that enable them to understand visual content and interact with digital media effectively. The implementation of image captioning typically involves deep learning models. A ConvolutionalNeuralNetwork (CNN) serves as the encoder, extracting relevant features from input images. Architectures like ResNet50 (Residual Network) are commonly used for their effectiveness in extracting hierarchical features from images. The decoder, on the other hand, uses the LongShort-TermMemory (LSTM) variant, to generate textual descriptions. The LSTM architecture is well-suited for processing sequential data, making it effective in generating coherent and contextually relevant captions. Overall, the integration of neural network models for image captioning represents a significant advancement in computer vision and NLP. By harnessing the power of deep learning image captioning systems can accurately describe visual content, leading to enhanced understanding and utilization of images across various domains and applications.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Fog-Cloud Framework for Smart Refrigerator Inventory Management
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Technological advances have led to the proliferation of smart home applications, which rely on sensors. The sensors used in smart home applications generate vast amounts of data. Typically, this data gets transmitted to distant cloud data centers for analysis and storage, significantly impacting device performance and user experience. However, introducing the fog nodes at intermediate layers can alleviate the aforesaid issues by conducting most data processing operations locally and offloading only the resource-intensive tasks to the cloud. This paper proposes to showcase the efficacy of the hybrid fog-cloud-based framework for the smart refrigerator inventory management. Using a simulation tool, we evaluated the framework’s efficiency against a conventional cloud-based system. The results demonstrate the clear advantages of our proposed framework with respect to network usage, power consumption and delay.

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: In an increasingly digital and interconnected world, the need for speech emotion classification has become imperative. The classification of emotions within audio using advanced technology holds the promise of transforming various domains. Emotion recognition from speech is pivotal in applications ranging from enhancing human-computer interactions to facilitating mental health assessments. This discussion leverages deep learning techniques, specifically RNNs (Recurrent Neural Network), with a focus on LSTM(Long Short Term Memory) cells known as their prowess in capturing sequential data pattern. The proposed method encompasses a comprehensive framework, including data preprocessing, feature extraction, and LSTM-based model training, with a spotlight on acoustic feature representations such as spectrograms or Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs). Beyond its foundational applications, speech emotion classification holds the potential to revolutionize domains such as personalized content recommendation systems, adaptive education methods, and emotionally resonant entertainment experiences. The experimental results, evaluated on publicly available emotion databases, underscore the effectiveness of this deep learning approach in speech emotion classification, thereby opening doors to improved human-computer interactions, sentiment analysis, mental health assessment, and transformative applications across various industries.

articleTitle: Automatic Braking System and Driver Safety Using Arduino Uno Atmega 328p
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This project addresses one of the primary causes of vehicle accidents: the sudden appearance of obstacles while driving. Drivers’ varying response times often lead to accidents due to delayed braking or inability to stop in time. To mitigate this, an Autonomous Braking system is proposed, leveraging intelligent mechatronic technology. The system employs an Ultrasonic wave emitter at the front of the vehicle to emit Ultrasonic waves, coupled with a corresponding Ultrasonic receiver that detects reflected signals. By analyzing these signals, the system calculates the distance between the vehicle and any obstacles, enabling the microprocessor to adjust the vehicle’s speed accordingly. In emergencies, the microcontroller activates the braking system to apply brakes swiftly and decisively, enhancing safety. A significant upgrade to the system is the integration of a Python-based application using Flask, which dynamically determines the incident’s location and communicates with the nearest emergency services based on real-time geographical data. This is facilitated through GSM technology, which transmits alarm signals and the vehicle’s GPS location to the appropriate authorities, ensuring prompt response and assistance. Additionally, the system’s potential expansion includes inter-vehicle communication capabilities, allowing cars to share information about their locations and speeds, thus enhancing road cooperation and awareness. This not only leads to fewer collisions but also smoother traffic flow. The models used in this project, including the ultrasonic sensor and GPS modules, have demonstrated an accuracy rate of over $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ in obstacle detection and emergency alert transmission. Overall, the Autonomous Braking system aims to enhance road safety by reducing response times and stopping distances, thereby preventing accidents and significantly improving emergency response capabilities.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of EEG Feature Fusion Techniques for Emotion Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) system-based emotion classification is an intriguing topic for research. Feature extraction is an essential step in these systems, usually carried out by a deep neural network or hand-crafted features. Studies in this area frequently highlight the significance of a small set of features; a precise comparison of different proposed features is still necessary. To classify emotions from EEG data, we attempt an exploratory evaluation of a number of EEG features, including those in the time domain, frequency domain, auto-encoded, and deep features, using the DENS dataset. Baseline techniques like Random Forest (RF), XgBoost (XGB), and KNN are used to compare feature performance. The results of this study shed light on the possibility of using these EEG features to identify emotional states. Compared to the previous results on the same dataset, our results show accuracies of 82.10% and 81.33% for valence and arousal, an increase of 29.63% and 18.82%, respectively.

articleTitle: Advancing Tourism Chatbots: Understanding Irony, Sarcasm, and Negative Emotions of Users
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The recent trend in chatbots for several application areas shows their potential to act as a support system to assist users with their needs. However, there is a need to direct efforts to build emotional intelligence into this software to enhance its usability and user experience. Building emotionally intelligent chatbots helps to interpret and respond to users according to their emotions, resulting in rich and healthy user experiences. Understanding irony, sarcasm and Negative emotions of the user are important aspects of sentimental analysis as they largely affect the emotional tone. This research utilises Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, to enhance chatbot sentiment analysis. In our experimentation, we leverage a dataset comprising over a million comments from Reddit, distinguishing between sarcastic and non-sarcastic expressions, to train and test our LSTM model. Along with the utilization of LSTMs Networks for sentiment analysis in the chatbot, the experiment incorporates BERT, a Transformer model architecture, to further enhance the chatbot’s capacity to recognize and react to sarcasm and satire. Using BERT’s capacity for contextual comprehension and pre-trained languages, the conversational agent can resonate with the user’s input tone and intent, whether they are sarcastic or not.

articleTitle: News Topic Categorization on Telugu Dataset Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The digital age has ushered in an unprecedented era of data proliferation across various domains, with the news sector being no exception, accumulating vast amounts of information, often measured in petabytes. Manual classification of such voluminous data is impractical, particularly considering the complexity of languages like Telugu, belonging to the Dravidian family, renowned for its intricate morphological characteristics. Natural Language Processing (NLP) offers a promising avenue for tackling textual data, leveraging diverse word embedding techniques to enrich model representations. Notably, prior research in this domain has predominantly relied on count-based algorithms for word embeddings. However, in this investigation, we explore alternative approaches, specifically custom-built Deep Learning models integrated with word embeddings, to optimize the classification of newspaper articles. Through a series of methodical experiments, we endeavor to identify the most effective model architecture for this task, aiming to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of article categorization in Telugu. The proposed model has experimented with word embeddings such as FastText and GloVE with deep learning models like LSTM, Bi-LSTM, CNN. Among the models experimented, FastText in combination with CNN have reported the highest F1-Score of 0.93.

articleTitle: Incorporating Knowledge Graphs in Semantic Search
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Information Graphs are a powerful mechanism for incorporating dependent facts into semantic search. They are a form of graph database that represents standards and their relationships, as opposed to just information and their attributes. This additional layer of abstraction enables greater and a sophisticated inferencing and querying, making them perfect to be used in semantic search. Incorporating knowledge Graphs into semantic search entails numerous technical steps: 1. Information Extraction: The first step is to pick out and extract applicable facts from various resources, such as databases, text documents, and APIs. This fact can encompass entities, relationships, and their attributes. 2. Information Alignment: Once the records have been extracted, it needs to be aligned with the ideas in the knowledge graph. This includes mapping the extracted records to the suitable entities and their relationships in the graph. 3. Information Enrichment: To improve the first-class and completeness of the knowledge graph, the extracted statistics may additionally need to be enriched with additional statistics. This will involve incorporating information from external sources or leveraging device mastering techniques to deduce lacking facts. 4. Entity Disambiguation: Considering that entities in the understanding graph may additionally have comparable or ambiguous names, it is very much essential to disambiguate them to ensure correct search outcomes. This can be done through strategies inclusive of named entity recognition.

articleTitle: Media Bias Monitor: Quantifying Biases of Indian Print Media
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Throughout history, mass media has significantly influenced societal thoughts, affecting areas such as religion, politics, and gender equality. This influence, whether intentional or not, highlights the critical need for unbiased media to prevent misinformation. Media bias, seen in inconsistent or duplicated reporting, significantly shapes public thoughts and emotions. This article aims to uncover the subtleties of media bias, understanding its impact on social perceptions, and recommending strategies to reduce bias, thereby promoting equity, inclusion, and informed discourse. Sentiment analysis within NLP evaluates the emotional tone of text, categorizing it as positive, negative, or neutral. In this study, we use the VANDER and RoBERTa models for sentiment analysis. For web scraping, we use various APIs for scraping the news articles from various news media houses. Our results show the presence of various types of biases such as gender, religion, and political bias in the news articles published by mainstream Indian media. Overall, in the dataset, the news articles are more biased towards male in gender, Hindu in religion, and BJP in political parties.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of Brain Tumor Categorization on MR Images using various Deep Learning models
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Neural Network algorithms have demonstrated notable capability in effectively analyzing human body image datasets obtained from MRI or CT with sufficient efficiency to direct medical operations. Although clinicians and radiologists can adeptly detect the presence of tumors and general abnormalities in brain scans, differentiating between specific tumor types typically requires significant time and effort. This study introduces an approach employing Convolution Neural Network (CNN) algorithms for precise classification of brain tumor into four distinct classes, leveraging deep learning models such as VGG16, VGG19, Efficient Net B5, Customized CNN. Prior to classification, the dataset undergoes preprocessing using Adaptive Median Filter (AMF) and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) for denoising and contrast enhancement. The classification task involves categorizing images into four classes namely Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary and Tumorless. The proposed methodology aims to streamline the analysis process by minimizing complexity while maximizing accuracy rates when compared to previous developments.

articleTitle: Transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence in Education
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Artificial intelligence’s (AI) capacity to transform education has acquired a lot of attention, particularly because of COVID-19. It is comprehensively changing the way traditional educational methods are applied in classrooms. The author synthesizes current research findings, examines emerging trends, and focuses on finding out the multifaceted impact of applying AI technologies to the education system. The study explores how AI is enabling educators to customize instructional content to fit the different requirements of students, support specialized learning pathways, and develop critical thinking abilities by using AI-driven tools such as virtual mentors, intelligent tutoring systems, and personalized learning systems. How the analytics capabilities of AI help educators make data-driven decisions. The study sheds light on some of the ethical concerns. The challenges of the digital divide, which emerges because of the adoption of AI in education, are that not all institutions will be able to implement it. The study proposes recommendations for harnessing the transformative power of AI to promote equitable and inclusive educational practices in the digital age.

articleTitle: Measuring Electromagnetic Performance and Configuration of Networks in High Interference Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Measuring the electromagnetic overall performance and configuration of networks in high-interference environments can be challenging. In those environments, the indicators of hobby can be infected with unwanted heritage indicators, i.e., noise, leading to degraded overall performance and misguided size readings. This paper investigates the most reliable techniques for measuring networks’ electromagnetic performance and configuration in these problematic environments, utilizing introducing a unique multistage framework that combines sign-processing strategies with some community parameters. In particular, the framework includes four degrees: sign reception, sensitivity analysis, pass-correlation, and community configuration optimization-an analysis of the results of varying environmental conditions on sign reception and sensitivity change into conduct. A cross-correlation approach has evolved to decide the extent of correlation among one-of-a-kind alerts and to locate the specific configurations of the particular networks. Sooner or later, an optimization set of rules was carried out to locate the network’s optimum configuration. The final result of this research is a reliable method for measuring the electromagnetic performance and configuration of networks in high-interference environments. The proposed technique is anticipated to help researchers and engineers better understand the electromagnetic behaviors of complicated networks in actual-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Image Segmentation Techniques: Applications, Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Digital image processing is the class of methods that is used in all research domain. With the help of a computer algorithm, the manipulation of an image is done that provides the required information about the image which includes the sharpness and blurriness of an image, identification of edges, and many more. Digital image processing follows fundamental steps like image acquisition, image enhancement & restoration, color image processing, wavelets, multi-resolution processing, image compression, morphological processing, and image segmentation. In this paper, we reviewed various types of image segmentation and their application based on latest technology. We reviewed mathematical equation of some of the techniques to understand the working more accurately. Depending upon the review we provide conclusion about the advantage and limitation of the segmentation technique.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Network-Based Voice Synthesis from Spectrograms for Low-Resource Speech Recognition in Mismatched Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The use of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has been increasing in speech recognition tasks but there has been significant hurdle due to limited availability. The use of GAN have shown promise in speech synthesis tasks, yet their application in low-resource speech systems faces a significant hurdle owing to limited data availability. The progress of effective Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems faces multiple challenges due to a limited range of options and scarcity, resulting in decreased adaptability and efficiency. This article proposes an innovative approach for integrating Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to create speech for both adults and children. Experiments have been conducted on using Mel-Spectrograms for synthetic augmentation to address the problem of limited data availability, particularly for low-resource languages and children. The experiments were conducted under both matched and mismatched conditions. The results demonstrate a noteworthy decrease in the Word Error Rate (WER), showcasing the potential of the GAN-based Vocoder model. This leads to an overall Relative Improvement (RI) of $\mathbf{1 2. 7 4 \%}$ and $\mathbf{1 3. 9 5 \%}$ for the adult and children ASR system, respectively. The research has yielded useful insights on the advancement of ASR systems, particularly in relation to the potential benefits of using GAN-based augmentation in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Ventricular Dysfunction and Organ Transplant Rejection Determinant Biomarker Recognition in Serum via Charge Deduction Method
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: This manuscript highlights ventricular dysfunction and organ transplant rejection determinant biomarker detection in serum for well and infected persons and the pertinent sensitivity investigation with a dielectric modulated (DM) single-sided charge plasma (CP) $\mathrm{I n}_{0.53} \mathrm{G a}_{0.47} \mathrm{A s} / \mathrm{I n}_{0.52} \mathrm{A l}_{0.48} \mathrm{A s} \quad$ hetero-structure TFET supported biosensor (DM-SCP-HTFET). Here, indirect N ${ }^{+}$type pocket having varying electronic concentration ($\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{E}}$) has been recognized by the tuning of source-region-channel (SRC) length ($\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{SRC}}$) under the gate region. The charge deduction dependent scheme has been employed. Device optimization for advanced sensitivity is attained by using Silvaco ATLAS TCAD device simulator. An utmost 96% sensitivity concerning sub-threshold swing ($\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{ss}}$) has been achieved while presume repulsive steric hindrance (RSH) during the concentration variations. Finally, an error estimation table is arranged to approximate deviations in sensitivity ($\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{D}}$) by the RSH method. Thus, RSH must be included throughout the lessons of label-free biosensing.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Brain Tumor Detection using Data Augmentation with CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The accurate detection of brain tumors is critical for effective treatment planning and patient outcomes. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have emerged as powerful tools for medical image analysis, particularly in tumor detection. However, the performance of CNNs can be limited by the availability of annotated medical images, which are often scarce and expensive to obtain. This research explores the enhancement of brain tumor detection through the application of data augmentation techniques to CNNs. By artificially expanding the training dataset with transformed versions of existing images, the model’s ability to generalize improves significantly. Various augmentation methods, such as rotations, flips, and intensity variations, were implemented to enrich the dataset. The augmented data facilitated the CNN in learning more robust and diverse features, thereby improving its detection accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional methods, underscoring the potential of data augmentation to enhance CNN-based brain tumor detection systems.

articleTitle: CyberSentry: Machine Learning Algorithms for Early Detection of Cyberbullying on Twitter
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Cyberbullying, a great trouble enabled by using virtual communique systems, offers massive barriers to the intellectual and emotional fitness of people, particularly young adults and teenagers. The rise of social media and the potential to stay anonymous on line has substantially elevated its presence and have an effect on global. As a reaction, researchers have resorted to employing device gaining knowledge of techniques for the motive of identifying and reducing the impact of the problem. This takes a look at examines cutting-edge research on the detection of cyberbullying, with a selected emphasis on the utilization of device studying strategies for analyzing Twitter facts. The facts pretreatment tiers, which contain the removal of stop words, stemming, and lemmatization, are defined intensive. The analysis of the dataset provides valuable insights into the distribution and properties of the accrued statistics. Following the cleansing process, any duplicate values are removed, and the length of the textual content is chosen for education functions. The dataset is partitioned into separate education and trying out sets, and the elegance distribution is equalized the usage of SMOTE. The overall performance of 4 system mastering algorithms-Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Naïve Bayes, and Random Forest-become compared. Random Forest outperformed the other methods in terms of precision, recall, F1 score, and accuracy. Confusion matrices offer further understanding into the performance of a model. In summary, this work emphasizes the significance of machine learning in tackling cyberbullying and proposes potential areas for further investigation.

articleTitle: Enhancing COVID-19 and Pneumonia Detection with a Hybrid ACGAN-CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Corona Virus caused a pandemic outbreak all over the world during 2020-2021. Identification of such diseases in the X-ray images needs help of deep learning methodologies involving classifiers. Achieving proficiency in training convolutional neural networks requires a considerable volume of data. Higher accuracy is needed while dealing with medical fieldrelated problems especially. When dealing with small datasets, networks tend to exhibit overfitting problems. In order to get larger dataset, techniques for data augmentation serve to enhance the neural networks’ capacity for generalization by expanding existing training data more efficiently. While conventional data augmentation methods do enhance performance, their scope remains restricted. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have proven instrumental in producing fresh data, thereby elevating the performance of CNNs. Methodologies for augmenting data with the help of GAN’s is not as much notable in Convolutional neural networks. In this research study, a GAN architecture is used for augmenting X -ray images of chest in order to expand the dataset. Auxiliary Classifier Generative Adversarial Network model has been used to produce images. It consists of a generator that produces new images with random noise and a discriminator whose job is to identify fake & real images. The results showcase that the new image generated is fine-tuned over each epoch and the significance can be seen in the output images. We compare the quality of our ACGAN images with the conventionally augmented images.

articleTitle: Analysing Mutual Fund Performance: A Hybrid Approach Using LSTM with explainable AI Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Mutual fund performance analysis holds paramount importance for investors aiming to optimize their investment strategies. Conventional methods often falter in capturing intricate temporal dependencies ingrained within financial data, resulting in less than optimal predictions. Prevailing methods typically hinge on simplistic models or lack interpretability, constraining their efficacy in grasping the nuanced patterns prevalent in financial time series data. A pioneering hybrid approach integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with explainable AI techniques is introduced to enrich mutual fund performance analysis. The proposed approach surmounts this impediment by harnessing the sequential learning process of LSTM networks while furnishing insights into the model’s process of determining decisions through explainable AI techniques. The initial step involves pre-processing historical mutual fund data and extracting pertinent features. Subsequently, an LSTM network is trained to discern the temporal dynamics of the data and forecast future fund performance. Augmenting interpretability, explainable AI techniques like feature importance analysis and partial dependence plots are employed to elucidate the determinants steering the model’s predictions. Empirical findings on real-world mutual fund datasets underscore the efficacy of the proposed approach. The hybrid LSTM model, with an MSE value of 0.0023, surpasses traditional methods and offers valuable insights into mutual fund performance, empowering investors and analysts with actionable insights.

articleTitle: Pioneering Early Glaucoma Identification Through Deep Learning Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Glaucoma, a degenerative eye condition causing irreversible vision loss, often goes undiagnosed until it is advanced due to its asymptomatic early stages. Timely intervention and the prevention of visual impairment depend heavily on early detection. The innovative use of deep learning methods, in particular convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to transform the early detection of glaucoma is examined in this research. Fundus scans of the retina can be used to identify distinctive morphological changes that are suggestive of glaucoma, especially in the Optic Nerve Head (ONH). This research attempts to create very precise and effective algorithms that can identify glaucoma in its early stages by utilizing insights from deep learning. These developments might revolutionize the diagnosis of glaucoma, allowing for early intervention and greatly enhancing patient outcomes in the fight against visual loss.

articleTitle: Security and Privacy Preserving GDPR-Compliant Scheme Resisting in Rendering False Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The protection of personal data has grown to be a top priority around the world. The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) enables the data subjects (DS) to get back the control of their personal information, which is usually managed and processed by Service Providers (SP). Therefore, it is to check whether a service by SP is GDPR compliant. Manual verification is not feasible as a lot of data are being generated over time by a DS. An automated process may help. We explored a recent such automated tool, which allows the SP to provide requested data to a User (U) only if the DS has the consent for this transaction. However, a malicious SP can alter the data as the correctness of the received data is not being verified. In this paper, we have addressed this problem and proposed a GDPR compliant scheme that ensures the correctness of the received data. We simulate our proposed scheme using the well-known Automated Verification of Internet Security Protocols and Application (AVISPA) verification tool, which illustrates that the proposed scheme is safe. We compare the performance of our proposed scheme with the existing scheme to ensure its acceptance in real life.

articleTitle: VANET Congestion Control and Stability Performance Analysis using Seagull Optimization Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Significant matters in VANET environment include high vehicle versatility, changing vehicle thickness and dynamics between vehicle separating. Therefore, improved routing protocol enhances overall performance of VANET through intermittent service availability. In this regard, a group-based AI technique is implemented to predict VANET mobility. Effective routing based on a hybrid metaheuristic algorithm combined with Ensemble Learning produces significantly improved results. Vehicle Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) are currently used in various applications such as transportation using vehicle-to-vehicle multi hop wireless communication since they offer scalable and cost-effective solutions for it. On the other side, multi-hop communication development is regarded as a challenging task in VANET conditions due to rapid alterations of periodic and topological network breakdowns. In general, mobile ad hoc routing protocols, this leads to failure of routing or its invalidation. In order to solve the problem of routing and get multi-constrained QoS (quality of service) measures in VANETs, numerous research works have been conducted on it. Another aspect for application is traffic collision control. Unfortunately, there are hardly any sensors anywhere which make it basically impossible to obtain continuous information about traffic states. Accurate predictions about traffic flow are difficult because road accidents and public events cannot be predicted in advance and both these can essentially affect the traffic flow. This article reports the framework of Seagull Optimization Deep Learning for predicting accuracy and experiments various nodes. This framework exhibition focuses on different vehicle flows, position rates, and road organization typologies. Our framework effectively reduces the general waiting time of vehicles during aggregation and shortens the vehicle travel season even when the location rate is low.
